plan.planOverview:
Nine perspectives converged on one diagnosis: the engine is disciplined and the pedagogy is genuinely good, but every load-bearing invariant that spans a boundary — between collections, between disk and the live Anki collection, between a cached LLM artifact and the prompt that outranks it, between prose rules and code — is enforced by nothing, and an absent check reads exactly like a passing one. Five reviewers independently found the same artifact on disk (`.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json`, plus four 4-byte `CLIP` stubs in `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/`, both confirmed by me): `npm test` writes into the durable library the daily deck is built from. I also confirmed the course's shipping `.apkg` (13 Aug 11:35) is stale against two units edited 14 Aug, that a foreign 11 MB `japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana.apkg` sits inside the course directory, that `reopen` exists nowhere in `src/`, that `preflight` walks only `epubs`/`courses`, and that BOTH `/output` (422 MB, 29 hand-reviewed units) and `/.anki-builder` (292 MB, the dedup library) are gitignored AND untracked with no backup anywhere.

That last fact reorders everything. Roughly forty of this review's recommendations mutate or delete inside unbacked state, so WS0 (snapshot the few MB of irreplaceable JSON, then stop the test suite writing into it) is a hard prerequisite, not a parallel track. WS1 then builds the verification substrate — a shared scope model with unit/collection/workspace tiers, a FAIL/ACK/INFO severity policy, and the first tests scripts/ has ever had — because ~15 of the proposed checks all land on preflight, and dumping them onto a tool whose two report-only lines have never once been zero would convert the one deterministic gate into wallpaper. WS2 is the owner's stated priority, EPUB ingestion, and it is deliberately almost all diagnostics: the parser is proven on exactly one book and its failures on a second are silent on every axis at once (0/35 nav entries classified as lessons on the probed hostile book, spine files absorbed with no log, inverted ranges, undecoded entities flowing into live Anki deck names, and a probed image-filename collision that hands the extraction model the wrong picture). Making those loud at `--list-lessons` time costs one read-only command and no LLM spend.

Everything after that is ordered by evidence and by cost-of-being-wrong. The prompt work (WS3) carries the only proven content loss in the set — chapter 32's あります/います paradigm produced zero cards because a 14 Jul cached conventions file silently outranks a 9 Aug extraction prompt — and is cheap, reversible and squarely inside the agentic core's support layer. Card/learner quality (WS4) and audio (WS5) rank above delivery plumbing per principle 2, but every change that reaches the live note type is gated behind WS1's model-diff guard, because the deliverer force-syncs a language-wide model, cannot add a template at all, and never re-files a note between decks. The skill doc (WS7) is treated as a prompt with a critical bug: it prescribes a Reopen button that does not exist for recovering a mis-clicked Mark done on a delivered unit. Models (WS8) gets the per-pass scope split everyone wanted plus the timeout fix nobody costed, and its eval fixtures are now justified as regression coverage for WS3's prompt rewrites rather than as a precondition for downgrades the plan rejects.

Three rounds of red-team review then caught ten places where THIS PLAN would have caused the damage it exists to prevent. Rounds 1-2 (all fixed in place, objections preserved as dissent): narrowing `byAbid` would have broken the durable delivery key; a pre-push hook would have coupled `git push` to unversioned deck state; WS5's audio hash delivered zero coverage without a backfill and would have been the first-ever block on Mark done; WS4's build-side direction suppression was inert on the AnkiConnect path and self-reversing on the .apkg path; WS6's changeDeck re-file was an unflagged mutation of live deck membership; WS2's image-path fix was ambiguous between archive-mirroring (correct) and flattening (silently breaks the model's relative Read).

Round 3 upheld three more, each verified by reading live files. (h) WS6's re-keyed fail-closed assertion referenced data that does not exist: I read both live `anki-delivered.json` files and each contains exactly `{note, ankiParent, lastDeliveredAt}` — no card ids, no counts — and `writeDeliveredMarker` (deliver.js:172-190) writes only those three keys inside a `try` whose catch is empty ("The marker is advisory; a failed write must not fail the deliver."). The item now ADDS the delivered key set, makes that write fail-loud, and states an explicit bootstrap rule so the gate arms from the second deliver rather than false-aborting the first; WS0's rationale for protecting the marker is corrected to say it is protected because of what it will hold, not what it holds. (i) WS1's import verifier conflated a headless `.apkg` harness with live-AnkiConnect behaviour probes — `DEFAULT_ENDPOINT` is pinned to `http://127.0.0.1:8765`, which on this machine is the collection the owner studies daily, and `references/deliver.md` never mentions a profile — so the probes are split into their own item, run against a purpose-made second Anki profile, with a hard refusal when the reachable collection contains a delivered deck. (j) WS4's suspend-at-delivery was held to the standard the plan itself set for changeDeck: unconditional only for notes this deliver creates, opt-in and `--dry`-previewed for already-delivered notes, a human-unsuspend override that is reported and never silently re-suspended, and a filtered-deck (`odid`) question added to the behaviour probes. Seven non-blocking concerns are folded in, most consequentially: WS2's image work splits into a detector (M) and a layout change (L), WS8's eval fixtures are re-justified and re-sequenced ahead of WS3's prompt edits, WS0 states plainly that audio recovery rests on sibling `.orig.mp3` files (and pulls the seven flagged clips plus their originals into the snapshot), and the git option in WS0 now names the exact `.gitignore` mechanics, because `/output` is a directory exclusion and a naive `!/output/**/cards.json` negation silently matches nothing.

Nothing in this plan mechanizes a judgment. Every new script proposes candidates and reports; the extraction, cue-wording, merge-vs-cue and keep-vs-fix decisions stay exactly where they are.

workstreams.name: WS0 — Stop the bleeding: protect irreplaceable state (do first, blocks everything destructive)
workstreams.goal: Make the owner's 714 MB of unbacked, unversioned human review recoverable, and make it impossible for the test suite to write into the state the daily deck is built from. Every deletion, --apply sweep, migration AND content regeneration in a delivered unit elsewhere in this plan waits behind this. Cannot start until the snapshot-mechanism open question is answered.

items.title: Version-control or snapshot the irreplaceable JSON under output/ and .anki-builder/
items.description:
Verified: .gitignore excludes both /output and /.anki-builder as DIRECTORIES, and `git ls-files` returns nothing for either. The unrecoverable half is small — output/**/{cards.json,corpus.json,book.json,course.json,anki-delivered.json} plus .anki-builder/epubs/*/{corpora/,conventions.md,taught-index.json} — a few MB of JSON representing months of human review. Either un-ignore exactly those globs or add scripts/snapshot-state.mjs writing a timestamped tarball beside anki-backups/ with the same prune policy deliver.js already implements. Pick one; do not do both.

MECHANICS CORRECTION (round 3, non-blocking concern 2): 'un-ignore exactly those globs' does NOT work as written. Git does not descend into an excluded directory, so with `/output` present a `!/output/**/cards.json` line silently matches nothing. The git option requires converting the entry to `/output/**` plus a `!/output/**/` DIRECTORY re-include placed before any file re-include (same for `/.anki-builder`). If the git option is chosen, verify with `git status --porcelain` and `git check-ignore -v` on one real cards.json before relying on it — a rule that appears applied and quietly is not, on the item every other item depends on, is this project's signature failure mode.

PROTECTED SET, explicitly: (a) the JSON globs above; (b) `<collectionDir>/.preflight-accepted.json` (WS1 item 2) — the acknowledgement state is what makes the ACK tier mean anything; (c) `<collectionDir>/anki-delivered.json`. RATIONALE CORRECTED (round 3): the marker is protected NOT for what it holds today — I read both live markers and each contains exactly {note, ankiParent, lastDeliveredAt} — but because WS6 item 3 adds a delivered-key baseline to it that becomes irreplaceable the moment it is first written (it cannot be reconstructed from disk; it is a record of what the live collection received).

AUDIO HONESTY (non-blocking concern 1): this item is JSON-only by design (audio/, images/, *.apkg, *.bak stay ignored), so it protects NOTHING that an audio regeneration could destroy. State that plainly in the item and in WS5: audio recovery rests on the sibling `<clip>.orig.mp3` in the unit dir, which I confirmed exists for the flagged clips — not on WS0. Cheap mitigation, do it: pull the seven WS5-item-2 clips plus their `.orig.mp3` siblings into the snapshot explicitly (a few hundred KB). Note also that WS0 item 3 deletes inside .anki-builder/audio (140 MB, 3,610 paid clips) while that tree stays unbacked by design — which is exactly why that deletion names its two targets literally.

This is gated on the first open question and blocks every other item in the plan that deletes, mutates or regenerates content in a delivered unit.
items.rationale: Red line 2 is about not losing the owner's daily-study work. The corpora/ dedup library and 29 reviewed units ARE that work, they exist on one disk in no version control, and this review proposes ~40 mutations and several deletions inside them. Cost of being wrong is unbounded and irreversible.

items.title: Make libraryHome() refuse or redirect the real library under a test runner
items.description:
src/model/index.js:365 resolves REPO_ROOT/.anki-builder with no test override, and src/server/adapters/applyCards.js defaults BOTH saveChapterCorpus and the rmSync-ing removeChapterCorpus to the real implementations, so safety depends on every test author remembering a stub. Make libraryHome() return a per-process tmpdir under the test runner unless an explicit env escape is set, mirroring the assertExternalCallAllowed idiom the repo already invented for the same class of problem. Add the guard at libraryHome() itself, not at each writer, since saveChapterCorpus, removeChapterCorpus, registerEpub and the audio cache all resolve through it. CORRECTION to the pre-review draft: this does NOT keep every existing test green — test/model/index.test.js:479 ('libraryHome - resolves to <repo-root>/.anki-builder') asserts the un-redirected path and must be updated.

DECIDED UP FRONT (non-blocking concern 7, no longer an in-item caveat): gate the redirect on NODE_TEST_CONTEXT ONLY, not on isTestEnv(). I confirmed src/util/testEnv.js:8 also returns true for NODE_ENV === 'test', and a real run under a shell profile that sets NODE_ENV=test would silently write its library into a tmpdir and appear to have lost the dedup registry — a worse failure than the one being fixed. Covering the NODE_ENV=test case is a separate follow-up, not part of this item.

CLEANUP, specified: `node --test` runs ~75 processes, so a naive per-process tmpdir leaves 75 directories per suite run — create them under one suite-scoped parent (os.tmpdir()/anki-builder-test-<runner pid>) or register a process exit handler that removes its own.
items.rationale: Five reviewers found the same artifact independently. I confirmed .anki-builder/epubs/h1/ and four 4-byte CLIP files in .anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/ sitting beside three REAL voice caches. getDefaultVoice returns real voice ids and the cache key is (voice, model, textHash) with no provenance, so one test omitting --voice poisons a real voice's cache; clean-audio.mjs would faithfully re-derive the poisoned .orig.mp3 into a shipped card.

items.title: Add a suite-wide durable-write guard, then delete the two named stray artifacts
items.description: Snapshot a manifest of .anki-builder/, output/ and anki-backups/ and fail the run naming any path that changed. IMPLEMENTATION CORRECTION: node:test has no cross-process global hook and `node --test` runs 75 files in separate processes, and stat-ing ~13,000 files (8,464 under output/, 4,419 under .anki-builder/, 67 under anki-backups/) per process is ~1M stat calls per run — so implement it as a wrapper around `node --test` (snapshot once before, diff once after) or as a per-process --import that stats only directory mtimes. Also add assertExternalCallAllowed to fetchElevenLabsTts, the one API that bills per character and has no guard. Only after item 1 lands, delete exactly two paths, named literally: the directory `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/`, and the VOICE-ID directory literally named `.anki-builder/audio/v1/` (4 stub files) — NOT any other audio subdirectory. The three real voice caches are 3JDquces8E8bkmvbh6Bc (2,842 clips), gPPH6SLdL8XSX6GNJ40G (384) and xHIzJ4zBhlGcvJscsdON (384); 'v1' reads like a cache-version namespace and this plan proposes a CACHE_VERSION elsewhere, so the literal naming is load-bearing against a plausible misreading that would rm 3,610 paid clips off unbacked state.
items.rationale: Fixing only libraryHome() closes today's instance and leaves the class open; the defect sat in the tree with npm test green throughout because nothing makes a claim about WHERE a command writes. The guard catches every future variant, including a test that writes into output/.

items.title: Route every scripts/ --apply write through atomic write + backup + validate, and stamp .bak filenames
items.description: scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs:90 and scripts/extras-order.mjs:69/78 write with bare writeFileSync — no writeFileAtomic, no backupFileOnce, no post-write validateCards — while all of src/ uses that discipline. Retrofit them. Separately, stamp backups as <file>.pre-<reason>-<YYYYMMDDHHmm>.bak so a second run of a tool cannot clobber the first run's restore point (card-authoring-rules.md already documents that enhance-card-notes.mjs does exactly that), and add scripts/prune-baks.mjs keeping newest N per unit (330 .bak files / ~10 MB today).
items.rationale: These scripts can mutate reviewed and (under --force) done units that are in the live collection, using the least safe write path in the repo, against state with no backup. The restore point the .bak convention exists to create is currently destroyed by re-running the same tool.

items.title: Add excludedBy/excludedReason provenance to the card schema
items.description: src/model/index.js:82 and :204 declare `excluded: { type: "boolean" }` inside additionalProperties:false objects, so a script's --apply exclusion is byte-identical to a human's reviewed decision. Add optional `excludedBy` ("human" | "<script name>") and `excludedReason` (absent = human/legacy, backward compatible), stamp them from every --apply writer, render them in the dashboard and the corpus-review artifact, and have preflight report script-authored exclusion counts per unit.
items.rationale: 95 cards are excluded today. Combined with the extras-duplicate-check false-positive rate (~a third of groups) and the fact that a post-delivery exclusion leaves a live orphan nobody suspends, an unattributable exclusion is an unauditable content loss. This is the minimum that makes any --apply survivable.

workstreams.name: WS1 — Verification substrate: make the deterministic gate a gate
workstreams.goal: Give preflight a scope model, a severity policy, an acknowledgement mechanism and tests BEFORE the ~15 proposed checks land on it, then land the checks that close silent-corruption paths. Includes the first real-Anki verification the repo has ever had — now split into a headless .apkg harness and a separately-profiled live-AnkiConnect probe — plus the model-diff guard that gates every WS4 card-face change. Standing rule: a check promoted to FAIL ships in the same commit as the fix or the ACK for its live instance.

items.title: Introduce src/audit/ with one unit loader and unit/collection/workspace scopes
items.description: Export a single UNIT_DIR_PATTERN / listUnitDirs that knows all three shapes (chapter|lesson-N, -extras, and templates/<name>/<lang>/), replacing four independently re-typed copies (scripts/preflight.mjs:46, extras-collision-audit.mjs:27, extras-duplicate-check.mjs:31, src/deck/deckFileName.js:24 — whose comment already names two more in rebuild.js and adapters/stage.js). Add a check registry where each check declares scope: `unit`, `collection`, or `workspace`. scripts/preflight.mjs becomes arg parsing plus a scope filter; validate-decks folds in as --schema-only once templates are covered. A unit-shaped dir that matches no known shape is a REPORT line, promoted to FAIL only after all three shapes are recognised. ALSO (otherwise homeless, codeexpert-12): pin the undocumented invariant that `chapterNumber` means 'the lesson's FIRST spine index' in one place next to the loader — it is the join key for corpora/<n>.json, runDirOrderContext, loadPriorChapterItems and chapterCachePath, and three checks in this workstream key on it; drop the dead `flags.book` term in assemble.js:99 in the same commit. SPLIT: land (1a) the shared loader + chapterNumber invariant first, then (1b) the scope registry and the validate-decks fold — items 3-6 depend on 1a only. PREREQUISITE: answer the 'is the bundled-template source path alive?' open question BEFORE starting — if it is dead, the template shape and the templates half of the fold both evaporate and 1b shrinks materially.
items.rationale: Verified: preflight's collectionDirs() walks only epubs/courses and its loadUnits regex cannot match a template unit, yet it prints 'preflight clean'. Three separate findings (cross-collection ids, cross-deck collisions, dedup-library completeness) are homeless because every checker takes one book dir. No shared scope model is also why the regex is triplicated.

items.title: Define FAIL / ACK / INFO tiers with a per-collection acknowledgement file
items.description: Three declared tiers: FAIL blocks handing over a review link; ACK reports against a <collectionDir>/.preflight-accepted.json written only by an explicit `preflight --accept`, so the printed number is UNREVIEWED instances; INFO is coverage/shape reporting that never fails. Print a coverage header (collections, units, unmatched dirs seen) so 'clean' can never mean 'I did not look'. Each check declares its tier in one line. DEPENDENCY: .preflight-accepted.json lives inside the same gitignored, untracked tree WS0 protects — it is in WS0 item 1's protected set explicitly, or the acknowledgement state is itself unbacked and a disk loss silently re-reds every accepted check.
items.rationale: A read-only run today prints '· duplicates 17 target group(s)' and '· audio 7 clip(s) flagged marker-audible' followed by 'preflight clean' — both lines have been non-zero on every run since they were written, so the 18th duplicate group will render identically to noise the operator has learned to scroll past. Adding fifteen more report lines without this converts the one deterministic gate into wallpaper.

items.title: Land the silent-corruption guards: -extras epubHash, dedup-library completeness, 〜-in-target
items.description: (a) Refuse the library save in markCardsReviewed when the run dir basename ends -extras (src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:107-124 keys purely on (epubHash, chapterNumber); chapter-13 and chapter-13-extras both carry chapterNumber 33 today, so one copied field silently overwrites the base chapter's dedup entry), plus the mirror preflight assertion. (b) For every unit with meta.epubHash and meta.reviewed, assert .anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/corpora/<n>.json exists — and report the reverse, which would have surfaced the h1 leak on day one. (c) Assert /[〜～~]/ never appears in a shipped target. NOTE: (c) is red on live data today (one survivor, だれも…〜ません) — fix or ACK that card in the same commit that promotes the check to FAIL.
items.rationale: All three are two-to-twenty-line deterministic guards on paths whose failure mode is silent and whose historical cost is documented (3 lessons missing from the dedup library → 12 unflagged repeats). The extras rule and the placeholder rule are both stated as absolutes in prose and enforced by nothing.

items.title: Add workspace-scope checks: cross-collection ids, cross-deck collisions, stray .apkg — and delete the stray package in the same commit
items.description: (a) Cross-check card ids across every collection whose marker resolves guidNamespace to null, classifying identical-content collisions as a note and differing-content ones as a FAIL — of the 10 shared ids, nine are byte-identical and only `scarf` differs (スカーフ vs マフラー, both glossed 'Scarf'), so an unclassified check ships 90% noise on its first run. (b) Run findCollisions over every delivered collection at once, reporting the shared-ENGLISH class (10 uncued ambiguous prompts) more loudly than the shared-target class, and normalizing case/trailing-period/abbreviation variants first. (c) Assert the only *.apkg in a collection dir is deckFileNameForDir(dir). The check is red on live data the day it lands — I confirmed a foreign 11 MB japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana.apkg (28 Jul) in output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/ — so delete that one literally-named file in the same commit that promotes the check; the deletion needs nothing but WS0's snapshot.
items.rationale: The collision doctrine is correct and holds at zero uncued members within a book; only its scope is wrong, because Anki interleaves every deck studied that day and matches guids collection-wide. All three are pure reads over data preflight already loads.

items.title: Add a package-freshness check and fix the false rebuild comments
items.description: For each collection, resolve the package with resolveDeckPathForDir (never a hand-typed slug) and FAIL when any done unit's cards.json is newer than it. I confirmed this is live right now: nihongo-101-course-n5.apkg is 13 Aug 11:35 while lesson-0 (14 Aug 11:29) and lesson-3 (14 Aug 11:23) were written today — so this check MUST land in the same commit as a rebuild of that package, or the first run of the new gate is one the owner has to override. Root cause: rebuildGroupQuiet has exactly one caller (src/server/index.js:286, handleLessonDone — re-verified), while src/deck/rebuild.js:6-8 and src/server/index.js:423-425 both assert an edit to a done lesson keeps the package in step. Either call it from the exclude/edit/audio handlers for a done unit, or delete both comments and surface staleness in the dashboard — but fix the false claim either way. NOTE the interaction with WS4 item 6: once direction suspension exists, the .apkg deliberately no longer reproduces the delivered deck card-for-card (see that item), so 'fresh' here means 'rebuilt from current cards.json', not 'identical to Anki'.
items.rationale: This single check covers three separate findings at once (post-done dashboard edits, an improvised hand edit of meta.done because Reopen does not exist, and any scripts/ --apply mutation) and makes SKILL.md's hand-typed gate-2 shell fragment redundant. A false safety claim in the two files a future maintainer trusts is worse than the missing rebuild.

items.title: Bound the model-wide blast radius of a deliver (hard prerequisite for WS4 item 5)
items.description: The note type is keyed on language alone (src/deck/collection.js:80, `AnkiBuilder ${label}`), so delivering any ja deck rewrites templates and CSS for BOTH the book and the course simultaneously, and flips schemaChanged (forcing a one-way full AnkiWeb sync the user must complete by hand). Keep the sharing — it is correct — but make --dry print a unified diff of live qfmt/afmt/CSS vs spec plus every deck using that model, and require an explicit --allow-model-change when tmplChanged || cssChanged. This was WS6 item 4 with only a note to 'consider pulling it forward'; it is sized S, it hard-blocks an entire WS4 item, and a suggestion is not an ordering constraint — so it is scheduled here, and WS6 item 1's modelTemplateAdd must route through this same guard rather than relying on its own warning (a template add is also a schema-modifying write on the shared model and forces the same manual one-way sync).
items.rationale: Four separate WS4 recommendations step on this without noticing, and WS6's own template-add item does too. The restore side already exists (models.json is snapshotted into the backup dir); only the pre-change warning is missing. Landing it here removes the only cross-workstream stall in the plan.

items.title: Make extras-duplicate-check report-only on the documented path
items.description: Edit references/extras-pass.md:206-228 to drop --apply from the happy path. If --apply survives, gate it on english similarity as well as target equality and refuse any group whose glosses differ beyond a threshold, printing them for the agent instead. I reproduced the false positives read-only: the keeper for に is chapter-2/num-2 (the NUMBER 2), and --apply would exclude all five genuine particle senses; さん keeps num-3 over the honorific; ご keeps num-5.
items.rationale: preflight.mjs:129-130 argues in writing that this exact judgment must never be auto-applied, while extras-pass.md:210 advertises --apply as a normal step. Roughly a third of this book's 17 groups are genuinely distinct cards LIMITATIONS.md itself names. Only the reviewed/done guard prevents damage today, and an in-flight chapter is unreviewed by definition.

items.title: First tests for scripts/ and the dashboard's rebuild-failure signal, plus the substrate rule for new ones
items.description: Add test/scripts/ with a tmpdir fixture root (book + course + template + one deliberately broken unit of each kind) asserting exit codes and which units each check reported. Adopt the rule the codebase already half-follows: any script that MUTATES output/ keeps its logic in src/ behind a unit-tested function and the .mjs is arg parsing plus reporting (extras-order.mjs already delegates to orderExtrasUnit; extras-duplicate-check.mjs does not). Split scripts/migrations/ from standing tools with a `// SPENT: <date>` header. ALSO pick up the one otherwise-homeless thread: two cheap tests for src/review/clientScripts.js (659 lines, zero tests, and the only surface that renders the rebuild-FAILED string SKILL.md's gate-2 procedure depends on) — assert the Mark-done response carries rebuildError for a non-benign throw and null for each benign message (pinning the broad /directories found/ regex), and assert the ' — but deck rebuild FAILED' branch exists in the rendered page source. Add one test that pins the WS6 item 3 scope split apart (book-wide abid query vs unit-scoped target indexes), per the dissent recorded in that ruling.
items.rationale: scripts/ is 13 files / 1,653 LOC with zero tests, and it is where this review wants to add ~10 new tools. Commit 82e77b9 fixed a shipped arg-parsing bug with a defensive comment rather than a test. The dashboard is where both human gates are clicked and it is untested; WS1's package-freshness check largely subsumes the gate-2 need, but the FAILED string is still the only in-band signal.

items.title: Headless .apkg import verifier, and `npm run check` as a MANUAL gate
items.description: SPLIT from the former single item after a verified round-3 objection (see item 10 for the live-Anki half). scripts/verify-apkg-import.mjs shells out to a pinned `anki` Python package and imports a built .apkg into a THROWAWAY collection it creates itself in a tmpdir — no running Anki, no AnkiConnect, nothing on :8765. Assertions: note count, media playability, and the two package-format questions this plan currently refuses to assume — (1) what happens to a dconf preset with id 1 named 'Default' on import; (2) what happens to a note whose guid already exists (guid-match-update vs duplicate — the two live markers' own text disagrees, which is why qa-2 is ranked HIGH not critical). Keep the whole script out of `npm run ci` (output/ is gitignored) and make it a documented Definition-of-Done step for a first-ever build of any new source type. Separately: make preflight and validate-decks exit 0 with '(no collections found)' on an empty output/, and add `npm run check` = ci && validate:decks && preflight. Do NOT point .githooks/pre-push at it — the hook today runs `npm run ci` only (format:check, lint, test, build, all tracked-state assertions that pass in a fresh clone), while preflight/validate-decks assert on gitignored, untracked deck state; wiring them in couples `git push` to unversioned decks, is a no-op in CI and fresh clones by construction, and on day one of WS1 would block a README typo behind a deck rebuild whose only escape is --no-verify. Document `npm run check` where SKILL.md already puts preflight: before handing over a review link, and before a deliver. If hook coverage is wanted later, make the validate:decks/preflight half advisory — print, never contribute a non-zero exit.
items.rationale: LIMITATIONS.md records three .apkg format bugs that 'all passed npm test and every synthetic check' because nothing ran a real import — and that is still true. Today the entire two-week 'catch it before the review gate' frontier is enforced by one sentence of prose. Splitting the headless half out means it can land immediately, without waiting on the second-profile setup the live probes need.

items.title: Live-AnkiConnect behaviour probes — against a SEPARATE Anki profile, never the owner's
items.description:
NEW ITEM, split out after a verified round-3 objection. Three of the questions the plan defers are not answerable headlessly: they are about what AnkiConnect does to a live collection. Verified: src/anki/ankiConnect.js pins DEFAULT_ENDPOINT to `http://127.0.0.1:8765`, AnkiConnect only talks to the running Anki instance, and on this machine that instance is the collection the owner studies daily; I grepped references/deliver.md and it never mentions a profile, 8765 or localhost, so the obvious execution of these probes performs experimental schema-modifying writes, deck moves and filtered-deck manipulation against ~4,300 live cards.

SETUP, mandatory and documented in references/deliver.md before any probe runs: create a SECOND Anki profile purely for this, install AnkiConnect in that profile, close the owner's profile (only one instance can hold :8765), run the probes, then a documented 'switch back' step. The probe script must REFUSE to run when the reachable collection contains any deck matching a delivered marker's ankiParent ('Japanese for Busy People Book 1: Kana', 'Nihongo 101 Course (N5)') — a fail-closed check on the one machine where the wrong profile is one click away.

PROBES: (1) does modelTemplateAdd / updateModelTemplates regenerate a card row omitted by the .apkg writer, and does it UNSUSPEND anything (the fact WS4 item 6 turns on); (2) what does changeDeck do to a card sitting in a FILTERED deck (odid/odue) — WS6's --refile must not ship until this passes; (3) ADDED in round 3: what does `suspend` do to a card with non-zero odid, and does Check Database or a template update unsuspend — WS4 item 6's opt-in half must not ship until this passes.

Until this item is specified and built this way, NO other item may cite 'the WS1 behaviour test' as its safety prerequisite.
items.rationale: This is the gate that unblocks four deferred decisions, and as originally written it would have run them against the exact collection red line 2 exists to protect — the plan causing the damage it exists to prevent. The separation costs one profile and a paragraph of runbook; the alternative is experimenting on the owner's scheduling.

workstreams.name: WS2 — EPUB ingestion robustness (owner's stated priority)
workstreams.goal: Make the second book's failures LOUD without touching the agentic core. Almost every item here is a log line, a warning, or a shape report at --list-lessons time — before any paid pass — plus the hostile fixtures that pin them.

items.title: Ship scripts/epub-probe.mjs and fold its shape report into --list-lessons
items.description: One read-only command printing: nav source (nav vs ncx), spine count, per-entry spine RANGE with how many files in that range the TOC actually named, spine files falling before the first nav entry ('unreachable via --lesson'), duplicate-href collapses, classifyLesson type as an annotation, unitDeckSegments(label) for every label, per-file stripped-text length vs count, total bytes and image count with a WARN above JBP-derived thresholds, and the image-filename collision count from item 3. The log callback is already threaded through listLessons/resolveLesson to ctx.log, so these land in front of the human at the decision point.
items.rationale: On the probed hostile EPUB, nothing throws and everything degrades: 0/35 entries classify as lesson, spine 1 is unreachable, three entries silently swallow files the nav never named, and describeChapter(1) collides with nav entry [1]'s label. On the PROVEN book, entry [56] already swallows spine 57 and file 11 is 94 chars of text with 7 images. This is the cheapest way to fire the five dormant 'revisit at the second real book' triggers, and it answers 'will this book work' in five seconds for zero LLM or TTS spend.

items.title: Make the silent parser drops loud: NCX labels, comments/CDATA, non-monotonic nav
items.description: (a) Tolerate attributes and nested markup on <navLabel>/<text> (the live path for EPUB2 books — the probed book resolved source 'ncx') and route every skipped navPoint through the existing log callback. (b) Strip <!--...--> and <![CDATA[...]]> spans before every scanner, so a commented-out nav anchor cannot become a phantom lesson that shifts every ordinal, and a commented <item> cannot be selected as the nav document. (c) Detect non-monotonic nav: clamp lastChapterNumber to >= first and warn loudly, and assert the invariant in resolveLesson so it fails at the gate rather than 20 minutes into extraction. (d) Warn when the toc <nav> block contains more <a> occurrences than parsed entries.
items.rationale: Each is a pure function over an in-memory zip with a silent failure mode. The non-monotonic case is the worst: a probe returned a 5-2 range, which assemble silently degrades to single-file extraction AND which then makes flagForwardConcerns treat the lesson's own spine files as 'later chapters'. Today the only log that fires covers hrefs that fail to resolve, not entries that never parsed.

items.title: Image-extraction detectors: collision byte-compare, zip-slip containment, SVG wrappers
items.description: SPLIT from the layout change (non-blocking concern 4) — this half is pure detection and ships this cycle. (a) THE COLLISION, confirmed in code: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:637 computes `join(destDir, src)` where destDir = dirname(destPath) and chapterCachePath is `/chapters/.xhtml` — so EVERY chapter shares one `chapters/` directory, which is simultaneously why relative `` resolution works (the comment at :577-588 states the extraction prompt tells the model to resolve each src relative to the chapter file it just Read and open it directly) and why two chapters in different archive directories referencing the same relative filename overwrite each other's image. Ship a byte-compare on write that LOGS the collision loudly, naming both chapter hrefs and the shared dest, and surface the count in the item-1 shape report. Changes no path; makes the failure loud, which is this workstream's whole thesis. (b) Resolve the destination and reject anything escaping .anki-builder/epubs// — src is archive-supplied and ../ is not filtered, so a crafted zip can overwrite repo source. (c) When a copied asset is an .svg, re-scan it and copy what it references, or log every copied .svg so the shape report can flag 'these images are SVG wrappers'.
items.rationale: The image path is not decorative: the extraction prompt instructs the model to open these files and epubArchive exists to make that resolution work, so a swapped image is swapped card content, silently. OEBPS/Text + OEBPS/Images is the standard Sigil/InDesign layout; the one proven book is flat, which is why this has never fired.

items.title: Mirror the archive layout under chapters/ so image collisions are impossible by construction (AFTER the fixture suite)
items.description: SPLIT OUT and resized to L (non-blocking concern 4): this half moves chapterCachePath, interacts with isCachedChapterFile, and forces the item-5 CACHE_VERSION bump — it is not the same size as a detector. Sequenced strictly after item 7's fixtures exist. MECHANISM: mirror the archive layout under the book's chapters/ root (chapter at `chapters/<archive dir>/<file>.xhtml`, images written to their own mirrored archive paths), which preserves every relative relationship EXACTLY and is isomorphic to the zip, so no src can resolve differently. A per-chapter subdirectory (`chapters/<n>/`) is an acceptable simpler variant but note it does NOT close the case where two chapters in different dirs both reference `../images/foo.png` resolving to different archive entries — item 3's byte-compare detector stays in either case. EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN: any flattening, hashing or archive-path-keyed FILENAME scheme that changes an image's path relative to its chapter file without also rewriting the cached xhtml's src attributes. That failure is invisible — extractReferencedImages logs only missing ARCHIVE entries, isCachedChapterFile then treats the chapter as a complete extraction forever, and no test exercises image reading because it only happens inside a paid LLM pass. The layout change invalidates only the free zip-inflate chapter cache, never an LLM artifact.
items.rationale: Sequencing the layout change behind the detector and the fixtures respects the plan's own cautionary tale — the last obviously-reasonable change to a media-path scheme produced an .apkg Anki rejected while passing every test — while still closing the collision by construction rather than leaving it as a log line forever.

items.title: Version the EPUB cache and ship a guarded clear command
items.description: Add a CACHE_VERSION (bumped whenever extraction or image resolution changes — including the item-4 layout change) into the chapter cache path or a sidecar, and ship `anki-builder epub cache --clear <hash> [--chapters|--conventions|--taught-index]` that REFUSES to touch corpora/. Print the cache's provenance (generated-at, parser version, prompt hash) in the shape report.
items.rationale: Every parser and prompt fix in this plan is inert for the existing book: cached chapters are treated as complete extractions and re-read forever, conventions.md and taught-index.json are written once and never re-derived. Today the only way to force a re-derive is an improvised rm -rf directly beside the dedup registry the owner must not delete — the exact adjacency that already cost 12 unflagged repeats.

items.title: Decode HTML entities properly — NEW BOOKS ONLY as scheduled
items.description: Replace decodeHtmlEntities (5 named entities today) with one handling &#NNNN;, &#xHHHH; and the ~10 common named entities, and insert a space when stripping inline elements so Lesson5 does not become 'Lesson5' (which also defeats deckPath's GROUPED_LABEL regex). Ruby handling is demoted to nav labels only. SCOPE DECISION, not an either/or: chapterLabel flows to unitDeckSegments to the live Anki deck name, and the deliverer's re-file path does not exist (and is now opt-in behind --refile) until WS6. So as scheduled this ships NEW-BOOKS-ONLY: gate the new decoder on a book-marker flag set at registration, and freeze the existing book's labels. Whether to come back and migrate once WS6's --refile is proven is an open question. Do NOT apply it to the delivered book on the strength of 'WS6 will add changeDeck'.
items.rationale: A probed label 'Lesson 1 — Greetings' produces the deck segment verbatim. The one book uses literal UTF-8, so this has never fired — but a deck name change in Anki is not a rename, it is a new deck, and the existing notes stay in the old one with all their scheduling.

items.title: Detect real DRM and widen nav discovery
items.description: Parse META-INF/encryption.xml and throw a clear 'DRM-protected' error ONLY when an encrypted <CipherReference URI> names a spine document (font obfuscation uses the same file on perfectly readable books and must not false-positive). Separately, add a last-resort nav sweep: any XHTML manifest item containing a <nav> whose *:type token list includes toc (prefix-agnostic) or whose role is doc-toc, after the current tiers so proven behaviour is unchanged.
items.rationale: The current check covers only zip-level encryption; Adobe ADEPT leaves the zip unencrypted, so a retail book parses 'successfully' into ciphertext and hands 40+ files of garbage to a whole-book paid pass. On the other side, a conformant book with a differently-bound namespace gets the confidently wrong message 'no navigation document found', pushing the user onto raw spine indices for a book that has a perfectly good TOC.

items.title: Add the hostile-EPUB fixture suite
items.description: One fixture case per silent shape: ruby labels, numeric/hex entities, comments/CDATA, NCX labels with attributes, duplicate-href nav entries, non-monotonic nav, unnamed spine files inside a range, path-escaping image srcs, colliding image filenames across directories, non-UTF-8 chapters, an SVG-wrapper page. All are pure functions over in-memory zips — fast and deterministic. This suite is the stated prerequisite for item 4 (the chapters/ layout change).
items.rationale: The only two adversarial EPUB tests that exist cover the two paths that already fail LOUDLY (ZIP64, zip encryption), so test coverage is currently inversely correlated with silent-degradation risk. This is the highest value per line of test code anywhere in the repo, and it is what makes every other WS2 item safe to land.

workstreams.name: WS3 — Extraction & prompt quality
workstreams.goal: Close the one proven content-loss path, remove the impossible constraints and unstated branches the model is currently resolving by inference, and mechanize the two coverage checks SKILL.md already defines deterministically but never wrote. Sequencing: WS8's eval fixtures for the extraction pass should exist BEFORE the prompt rewrites here land (see WS8 item 3's re-justification), and the romanization-prompt MOVE lands before WS4's Hepburn injection and WS5's per-language fragments, which edit the same file.

items.title: Fix the conventions-vs-extraction precedence conflict and link cached artifacts to prompt versions
items.description: (a) Move the {{BOOK_CONVENTIONS}} block AFTER the extraction rules and add an explicit precedence sentence: conventions are authoritative about MARKUP and where things are, never about WHAT to extract; on any conflict the rules above win. (b) Reword docs/epub-book-conventions-prompt.md so it describes drill markup structurally without prescribing skip/extract policy, and classifies reference tables inside EXERCISES as reference. (c) Write a sibling <artifact>.meta.json (prompt path + sha256 of the rendered template, model, effort, timestamp, chapter count) when caching conventions.md and taught-index.json, and WARN at assemble time when the current prompt hash differs — never block, never auto-regenerate, since a rebuild is a paid pass and a judgment call.
items.rationale: The only demonstrated CARD LOSS in the entire review: conventions.md (14 Jul) names chapter 32's あります/います paradigm image as exercise material to skip, while the extraction prompt (9 Aug) uses that exact shape as its worked example of 'reference material, extract in full' — and chapter-12/cards.json ships zero of those eight forms. This is the failure class SKILL.md itself calls structurally invisible, and its cause is an undated cached artifact silently outranking a prompt edited a month later.

items.title: Resolve the dialogue ban vs worked-example contradiction
items.description: Narrow the absolute ban ('treat the whole dialogue as off-limits') to 'do not extract the dialogue wholesale as a script', and add a stated exception: a dialogue line MAY be extracted when it is the only in-chapter demonstration of a function word required by Step 2, marked with a reviewNote naming the form it illustrates. Delete the misleading Step-2 clause claiming a dialogue line satisfies the requirement (it only does if the exception exists).
items.rationale: The two rules are mutually unsatisfiable and the corpus shows the model breaking the ban to satisfy Step 2 (にほんのスパですよ is a verbatim dialogue line, extracted to serve the particle よ) — while the extras pass re-mines the same dialogue anyway. Function words without a demonstrating sentence are exactly the cards a learner can recite and cannot use, so the ban is what must give.

items.title: Write the two coverage scripts SKILL.md already specifies
items.description: scripts/vocab-coverage.mjs <chapterFile> <unitDir>: parse <table class="voca"> rows including td.sub sub-rows, report glosses whose target appears in no card's target, normalize away the optional-prefix class ((お)てら vs おてら), and emit the near-match that explains each false positive. scripts/paradigm-grid.mjs <bookDir> --grid <spec.json>: the grid spec is authored per chapter by the agent, but the matching implements the predicate-position (after が/は/も/に or string start) and longer-form-exclusion rules that currently live only as ~15 lines of prose. Put the matching logic in src/cards/ behind tests; wire vocab-coverage into preflight for EPUB units.
items.rationale: SKILL.md:299-310 and extras-pass.md:153-169 both say explicitly 'the check is a script, not a read-through' — the doc has already ruled this is mechanism, not judgment — and neither script exists, so a throwaway with different matching rules is re-derived every chapter. It guards the failure mode the skill itself calls structurally invisible, which is the worst possible place for per-chapter variance.

items.title: Give extraction a coverage back-channel and add the missing content-class rules
items.description: (a) Change the extraction contract to an envelope — {items, coverage:{imagesOpened, imagesSkippedAsDecorative, concerns}} — with the parser accepting both shapes, then diff the referenced-image set assemble already knows against imagesOpened and WARN on any image the model never accounted for. (b) Add a third placeholder branch for discontinuous patterns (X…〜Y): resolve BOTH slots into one natural utterance and record the source spelling in reviewNote; state that '…' is a placeholder marker too. (c) Add a rule for numbered picture-caption lists (WORD POWER): extract every label, supply the gloss where the voc-box omits it, set uncertain and name the list in reviewNote. (d) Add the ruby rule ahead of the second book: <rt> content is the publisher's authoritative reading — copy it into `reading`, never into `target`.
items.rationale: Today a chapter the model could not read produces the same output shape as an empty one — taught-index.json records `teaches: []` for the two image-only kana chapters, indistinguishable from 'read it, nothing taught'. The taught-index pass already proves an envelope with a mechanically-checked coverage requirement works. The three content rules each convert an inference that a stronger model happened to get right into an instruction a deployed Sonnet-medium can follow.

items.title: Move the code-embedded prompts into docs/ templates (do this BEFORE WS4 and WS5 touch them)
items.description: Move buildRomanizationPrompt and the translation prompts into docs/romanization-prompt.md / docs/translate-prompt.md rendered through renderPromptTemplate, injecting per-language LANGUAGE_PROMPT_RULES fragments as placeholders exactly as fill-in-blank already injects {{COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE}}. This brings them under test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js. If deferred, the minimum is a test asserting docs/translate-prompts.md contains the string the builder actually emits. ORDERING: three workstreams edit the romanization prompt — this move, WS4's pinned-Hepburn injection, and WS5's per-language failure-mode fragments. This item lands first or the other two are rewrites of a file that just moved.
items.rationale: Translation and romanization touch EVERY card in every deck and are the only prompts a human cannot edit without a code change, the only ones with no automated contract, and the only ones whose documentation is a hand-maintained transcript — which has already drifted (the doc documents a counter-hyphen paragraph and `rok-kai`; the shipped prompt has neither and outputs `rokkai`). This one move is the enabler for three separate romanization findings.

items.title: Show the authoring model what a card actually looks like, and fix the taxonomy drift
items.description: Add a compact {{CARD_FACES}} block generated from CARD_TEMPLATES (not retyped) to the extraction and FIB prompts, showing both fronts and both backs with a filled example, so the leak rule becomes operational ('if you can guess the answer from the Recognition front alone, the scene leaks'). Fix the concrete drift: 'Three note fields' → Four; the FIB prompt's rule-7 cross-reference → rule 10; its "Travel" example → "Travel & Tourism"; the pedagogical-sort prompt's documented `notes` input → the `hint`/`scene` it actually receives; add the CATEGORIES enum to the cards schema; state which category a Step-2 worked example takes.
items.rationale: The field semantics are defined entirely by prose about a rendering the model has never seen, which is why Reading is populated by one pass and rendered by neither template, and why the leaky-scene class on particle cards is obvious on a face and invisible in a JSON row. The category ambiguity is the direct cause of 44 sentence-length cards sitting in Grammar & Function Words while Other is the second-largest bucket.

workstreams.name: WS4 — Card & learner quality
workstreams.goal: Pin the styles that currently coin-flip per batch, make the rendered card face visible to the reviewer for the first time, and land the card-model changes that are safe to reach a live collection. GATE: every item that mutates the note type, its templates or its CSS is blocked on the model-diff/--allow-model-change guard in WS1 item 6, which is scheduled there precisely so this workstream cannot stall.

items.title: Pin one Hepburn spec and lint it
items.description: Export a single style constant (macrons; ii/ei exceptions; n-before-b/p; を as o; no terminal ASCII punctuation; proper-noun casing; -san attachment; counter hyphenation) from src/translate/languageRules.js and inject it into the romanization prompt, the number-reading prompt, the FIB prompt and references/card-authoring-rules.md so hand-authored extras inherit it. Make JA_COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE the single source (the shipped romanization prompt currently teaches the opposite of its own documentation), regenerate docs/translate-prompts.md §3 from real code, and fix docs/number-reading-prompt.md's example, which violates the rule it injects. Then add a WARN-level preflight romaji lint. Lands AFTER WS3's prompt-template move.
items.rationale: pronunciation is a learner-facing field on 2,250 delivered cards rendered on the back of BOTH directions, and it drifts per batch: trailing periods 100% in chapter-2/3/4-extras and 0% in chapters 6-13; -san 32/32 hyphenated in one unit and 40/40 spaced in the next; kombini vs konbini; 209 cards hyphenate a counter while others fuse it. A worked example contradicting an injected rule is the most reliable way to make a model ignore the rule.

items.title: Audit the 1,847 inline romanizations against the deck's own pronunciation field
items.description: Extract <kana> (roman) pairs from note/hint/scene/reviewNote, look the kana up in the collection's own card targets, and WARN on every case where the inline spelling differs from that card's audited pronunciation after case/space normalization. At least 36 disagreements are already measurable (note 'ohayou gozaimasu' vs field 'ohayō gozaimasu'; 'sayounara' vs 'sayōnara'; 'chuugokujin' vs 'chūgokujin').
items.rationale: The extraction prompt MANDATES a parenthetical romanization whenever a note quotes non-Roman text, and none of them passes through the romanization pipeline — only the pronunciation FIELD does. This is the cheapest romanization check available anywhere in the repo because ground truth lives in the same file, with no new judgment and no new model call.

items.title: Render the real card face for the reviewer
items.description: Add a card-face preview — a per-card flip toggle in the dashboard and/or a review-faces.html artifact — that renders the real qfmt/afmt with the real CSS for BOTH directions from cards.json. The templates are already single-source in src/deck/collection.js, so this is a render, not a reimplementation. This item is READ-ONLY with respect to the note type and is NOT gated on the model-diff guard.
items.rationale: The three most valuable rules in card-authoring-rules.md ('answerable alone', 'a scene must not reveal the answer', 'hint on the Production front only') are all claims about a rendered FRONT that no surface in the pipeline ever shows anyone. Highest card-quality return per line in the repo: it turns doctrine the agent must simulate into something the human sees at Gate 1.

items.title: Add the answerable-alone audit and the FIB length ceiling
items.description: (a) Preflight check 7, WARN-level: list cards whose English starts with a pronoun stand-in ('It's', 'That's', 'They're') and carry no scene — the audit card-authoring-rules.md itself names, which returns 27 live hits including 'It's the 3rd floor.' and 'It's about ten minutes.' Some hits are legitimately producible, so this must never hard-fail. (b) A length ceiling on the Production face (31 live cards have English ≥60 chars, one is a three-sentence self-introduction): split, or ship Recognition-only once the direction mechanism in item 6 exists. (c) A near-sibling check restricted to frames whose members differ SOLELY in a proper noun or digit — not a blanket 3+-member warning, which would fire on the deck's best minimal-pair drills.
items.rationale: These are mechanical detections of rules the docs already state, keeping the keep-vs-fix decision with the reviewer. The narrowed sibling check is the difference between a signal and another permanent report line.

items.title: Fix the card face: prompt sizing, contrast, Reading, category chip, scene/hint distinction — GATED ON WS1 ITEM 6
items.description: Single-source edits in src/deck/collection.js: wrap both prompts in .prompt at the same 26px/600 weight the answer already gets (today the string the learner must decode is 20px while the same string as an ANSWER is 26px bold) and scope the Japanese webfont to the target rather than .card; darken .note-back (~3.9:1) and .hint-front (~3.1:1) to clear WCAG AA in light mode; render {{Reading}} on the BACK of both templates (136 cards populate it and neither template shows it); drop {{Category}} from the RECOGNITION qfmt only; give scene and hint distinct treatment instead of two identical unlabeled grey lines. EXPLICIT GATE: every one of these force-syncs a note type keyed on language alone, hitting BOTH delivered collections and marking the schema modified, which forces a one-way full AnkiWeb sync the owner must complete by hand. Do not ship before WS1 item 6's --dry unified diff and --allow-model-change guard exist. SECOND-ORDER NOTE: an updateModelTemplates on the live model is one of the events that may regenerate missing cards and is a probe question in WS1 item 10 — see item 6.
items.rationale: All are reversible, all reach the live collection through the field/CSS/template sync that already works (unlike template ADDITION), and each is a defect on the surface the owner sees every day. The category chip in particular is an uncontrolled answer cue on 2,150 Recognition fronts — stronger than any scene the collision doctrine would permit — while 86% of those fronts have no scene at all.

items.title: Per-card direction control via SUSPEND-AT-DELIVERY — unconditional only for NEW notes, opt-in and previewed for delivered ones
items.description:
RESPECIFIED TWICE. Two mechanisms are struck outright: (i) gating an existing template's qfmt on a new field — an empty front is not a skipped card, it is an EMPTY card, and Tools → Empty Cards deletes it with its interval and revlog; (ii) 'honour the flag where cards are generated (src/deck/collection.js:526)' — I confirmed that loop sits inside the .apkg SQLite writer, while the owner's actual delivery path (src/anki/deliver.js:426-433) calls `client.addNote(...)` and ANKI generates one card per template, so a build-side omission is INERT for every AnkiConnect-delivered note, and on the .apkg side a note with a non-empty front but a missing card row is regenerated by Check Database and by any template update.

MECHANISM: keep a per-card direction flag in the card schema as the authoring surface; keep the .apkg builder emitting BOTH card rows; SUSPEND the unwanted ord at delivery. This requires adding `suspend`/`unsuspend` to src/anki/ankiConnect.js — I verified it exposes findCards, cardsInfo, notesInfo and addTags but NEITHER suspend NOR changeDeck.

ROUND-3 SCOPING (objection upheld — hold suspend to the standard this plan set for changeDeck): (1) UNCONDITIONAL only for notes created by THIS deliver (the addNote path) — a card that has never been studied has no scheduling to disturb; report the set exactly like `createdDecks`. (2) For already-delivered abid-matched notes, suspension is OPT-IN behind an explicit flag, with `--dry` printing every proposed change (note id, card id, ordinal, from-state, to-state) for inspection first. A card the owner has been studying for months must not silently stop appearing because of a flag in cards.json. (3) HUMAN-OVERRIDE RULE: a card that is currently unsuspended AND already carries the `dir-suspended` tag is treated as a deliberate human unsuspend — report it, never silently re-suspend, unless a distinct second flag is passed. Without this the pipeline overrides a one-click human decision on a schedule, which is the drift open question 7 already concedes. (4) PREREQUISITE for (2): WS1 item 10 must first establish what AnkiConnect `suspend` does to a card with non-zero odid (filtered deck / custom study), and whether Check Database or a template update unsuspends.

STATED CONSEQUENCE (non-blocking concern 6): because the .apkg keeps emitting both card rows while the AnkiConnect path suspends one, the .apkg deliberately no longer reproduces the delivered deck card-for-card. That is the right trade (the two builders must not drift structurally), but it must be written down here, because WS6 item 1 is simultaneously correcting the src/deck/collection.js:162-166 overclaim that the two paths cannot drift, and WS1 item 5 treats the .apkg as the freshness target.
items.rationale: The need is real — に ships six cards whose Recognition fronts are the bare string に, disambiguated by scenes that paraphrase their own answers — and suspension is the only per-note direction suppression in Anki that survives routine housekeeping. But an unconditional suspend on every deliver is a new live write path that alters scheduling, and the plan already ruled that reporting such a change after the fact is not consent.

items.title: Expand the category taxonomy and add the notes truth-check to Gate 1
items.description: (a) Add 'Descriptions & Qualities', 'Everyday Objects' and optionally 'Actions & Verbs' to absorb the observed Other mass (222 cards, the second-largest bucket, containing a coherent adjective class and an everyday-objects class); enum additions are backward-compatible. Settle the Step-2 worked-example category rule first so the new buckets do not inherit the same ambiguity. (b) Add a Gate-1 checklist item listing every note that asserts a decomposition ('+', 'form of', 'distinct from') and verifying each against the deck's own cards — a deterministic helper produces the list, the verdict stays human. (c) State the parenthetical convention: a parenthetical restoring a subject the target also drops stays in english; one describing the situation moves to scene.
items.rationale: A shipped note currently teaches a false morphological analysis (なんじ and なんにん described as instances of なんの) that survived extraction, the cross-lesson note pass, corpus review and Mark done — every existing note check is structural, none checks whether a claim is true.

items.title: Cue the scarf pair and the other genuine cross-deck ambiguities by hand
items.description: Immediate content fix ahead of any tooling: マフラー (winter neck scarf) vs スカーフ (light/head scarf) both glossed 'Scarf' with no cue, plus the 10 uncued shared-English prompts ('Nice to meet you.' → はじめまして vs よろしくおねがいします; 'Yes' → ええ vs はい; 'Bag' → ふくろ vs かばん). Two-line edits to cards.json entries that reach the collection on the next deliver. Behind WS0's snapshot like every other edit to a delivered unit.
items.rationale: These are live daily-review failures the learner is guaranteed to get wrong on one side, and the fix does not need to wait for the workspace-scope audit that will find future instances. The register cueing already works within a book (はい 'the standard, neutral yes' vs ええ 'the softer, more conversational yes'), which proves the doctrine — only its scope failed.

workstreams.name: WS5 — Audio
workstreams.goal: Close the staleness hole that exempts every clip a human touched — including the ~200 that already exist — triage the clips already shipping broken, and make the Japanese-quality and non-Japanese-language gaps explicit rather than latent. Nothing here blocks the owner's daily Mark done until the badge population is measured.

items.title: Record a text hash for every take, BACKFILLED from audioOriginal, badge-only first, with a human 'keep this clip' accept
items.description: REVISED TWICE. (a) Add audioTextHash alongside AUDIO_FIELDS whenever a clip is installed (generated, picked, trimmed or uploaded) AND backfill it for existing clips by parsing the text-hash prefix off audioOriginal — `<hashTerm(ttsText)>.orig.mp3` for stage takes, `<hashTerm(ttsText)>-gen-<sha>.orig.mp3` / `-genkanji-<sha>.orig.mp3` for picked variants (src/audio/index.js:167-178, generateVariants.js:68, generateKanjiVariants.js:65). Measured on the live tree: audioOriginal is present on 100% of audio-bearing cards, and the prefix is derivable for 1,912 of 1,932 (1,765 plain + 70 gen + 77 genkanji); of the 109 audioManual cards, 95 are derivable and 14 are not. (b) It must NEVER be BULK-backfilled from current card text — that would permanently certify the drift this item exists to detect. (c) A clip with no derivable prefix (the 20 hand-named uploads) yields an INFO 'unverifiable' line and never blocks anything. (d) SHIP BADGE-ONLY FIRST: I confirmed handleLessonDone (src/server/index.js:277-287) has no gate of any kind today, so a block here would be the first ever on the owner's daily critical path — and the analogy to findUnreadableNumbers does not hold, because src/cards/readiness.js:61-65 argues explicitly that THAT block is clearable in place with nothing to re-run, whereas a hash mismatch under rules (b) and (d) has no exit except destroying the human's trim or pick. Badge in the audio review, do not regenerate over the human's work, do not block. Run the backfill, report the live badge count, and only then decide whether to promote. (e) ADD the missing exit regardless: a per-card 'keep this clip for the current text' action in the audio review that re-stamps audioTextHash from CURRENT card text and records provenance (audioTextHashAcceptedBy: "human" + timestamp). The prohibition in (b) is scoped to automated/bulk backfill only. (f) The comparison must consult the same per-unit kanji-TTS meta flag that gates defaultClipText (next item), or flipping that flag badges every card in the unit at once.
items.rationale: clipIsCurrent short-circuits to 'current' whenever isStageOwnedCard is false, which it is for every audioManual or hand-picked clip — roughly 200 cards in the live book are exempt from the text-changed check forever, while editCard freely rewrites target/reading. The backfill takes coverage from 0% to 99% on day one. Badge-first respects the plan's own standing rule that a gate red on live data on landing day teaches an override habit — and here the override would be destroying hand-tuned audio.

items.title: Triage the 7 marker-audible clips and make the count an acknowledged one
items.description: Audit and fix the seven named clips currently shipping flagged (chapter-9-extras/p9-iie-zenzen-yomimasen, chapter-9-extras/v9-otosan-ni-denwa, chapter-10/hontouni-samui-ne, chapter-12/nihon-no-supa-desu-yo, chapter-13-extras/koko-ni-imasu-a, chapter-14/kuremasu-exception, chapter-14/karimasendeshita), then move marker-stuck to the ACK tier so preflight prints 'N accepted, M new' and fails only on M > 0. RECOVERY, stated honestly (non-blocking concern 1): WS0's snapshot is JSON-only and protects nothing an audio re-trim could destroy — the recoverable artifact is each clip's sibling `.orig.mp3` in the unit dir, which I confirmed exists for these clips. WS0 item 1 additionally pulls these seven clips plus their `.orig.mp3` into the snapshot (a few hundred KB), so the claim 'this sits behind WS0' is true rather than decorative.
items.rationale: The prose says regenerate or hand-trim rather than ship audible nonsense; these are in the live collection now. A heuristic with a non-zero false-positive rate must not hard-fail a gate — that is how a --force habit starts — but a permanently non-zero report line carries no information either.

items.title: Make the kanji TTS path an opt-in default for NEW units, behind an A/B
items.description: Generate the kanji orthography for ja and surface it in the audio review automatically (rather than behind a per-card button), but gate its use as TTS input on a per-unit meta flag set at unit creation so existing units keep their kana clips. Run a blind A/B on ~20-30 cards drawn from the flagged/re-rolled set first, and measure mis-conversion on the homophone-bearing class (はし, いま, かみ, きます) before flipping any default. Keep the human veto in the review modal. The flag is the same one the text-hash comparison above must read.
items.rationale: The codebase itself says kanji orthography voices more naturally, and ~13% of clips needed human intervention. But defaultClipText feeds the ElevenLabs cache key AND the staleness filename, so changing it for ja re-hashes every ja card: ~1,700 paid refetches, discarded trim/marker tuning, and — because hand-touched clips are exempt from regeneration — a silently MIXED-orthography deck. Kana→kanji is also one-to-many, so it introduces a new wrong-word channel into audio for a kana deck where the learner cannot detect the error.

items.title: Triage the ar/hi/he romanization adapters and de-Japanify the correction prompt
items.description: (a) Move the failure-mode paragraph, the Important bullets and the Example Input/Output pair into per-language entries in languageRules.js with a neutral fallback — today a Hindi or Arabic run is shown two Japanese exemplars (ろっかい/こんにちは) and told about kana. (b) For ar and he, either drop them from ROMANIZATION_LIBRARIES so they take the LLM-only path, or keep the library as a consonant-skeleton hint with a mandatory 'supply full vocalization' instruction. (c) For hi, add explicit schwa-deletion and nukta handling. (d) Record in docs and LIMITATIONS that only ja/zh/ko are library-proven. Lands AFTER WS3's prompt-template move and after WS4's Hepburn injection, since all three edit the same prompt.
items.rationale: Empirically the adapters emit unusable output (كتاب→ktab, कमल→kamala, सड़क→saḍa़ka with a leaked raw nukta) while the prompt frames it as a trustworthy starting point and tells the model to keep the library's value when it is already right. Few-shot examples dominate a short instruction, so the model is anchored on the wrong task. Nothing but ja/zh/ko has ever been run end to end.

items.title: Record the end-marker's scope, and trial か-question prosody on new cards only
items.description: Document in LIMITATIONS.md that end-marker protection is ja-only, so a Spanish or Korean deck's clipped endings are a known unhandled condition. Separately, generate a handful of NEW か-final cards as ですか？。ででで and audition for a rising contour, measuring the end gap against the current trim tolerance — never as a bulk regeneration of the 328 delivered question cards.
items.rationale: The marker's 。 is load-bearing for trim detection (1.12s gap vs 0.24s without) and 7 clips are already flagged marker-audible, so inserting punctuation before it is a trim-regression risk for an unproven prosody gain. A new-cards trial costs almost nothing; a bulk re-hash costs money and re-opens tuned clips.

workstreams.name: WS6 — Delivery integrity
workstreams.goal: Make the AnkiConnect path able to express the changes the rest of this plan needs, and close the paths where a rename, a re-import or a routine deliver can silently damage the live collection. The model-diff guard formerly here now lands in WS1 item 6.

items.title: Give the deliverer a template-add path — or make it fail loudly — routed through the WS1 model-diff guard
items.description: Either add modelTemplateAdd, guarded and reported like addedFields, with a loud warning that N new cards will be generated for every existing note (new cards only; existing scheduling untouched), or detect a spec template with no live counterpart and FAIL with 'this note type gained a card template; add it by hand in Anki first'. Do not leave updateModelTemplates being called with a name AnkiConnect will not create. Fix the overclaiming comment at src/deck/collection.js:162-166 either way — and note that WS4 item 6 deliberately introduces a card-level difference between the two paths, so the corrected comment should say the two builders share the note-type SPEC, not that the delivered decks are card-for-card identical. modelTemplateAdd is a schema-modifying write on a note type shared by BOTH delivered collections, so route it through WS1 item 6's guard (--dry diff + --allow-model-change) rather than relying only on its own warning. Interaction with WS4 item 6: adding a template regenerates cards on every existing note, so any direction suspensions must be re-applied afterwards; make that a reported step, not an assumption (and confirm the regeneration behaviour in WS1 item 10 first).
items.rationale: tmplChanged includes the !live case and then pushes an update whose behaviour is undefined — a no-op that reports success on a live-collection write, the class this project keeps getting burned by. It also silently blocks every card-design change in WS4 that ADDS a direction (a listening card, a picture-prompt card).

items.title: Add an OPT-IN, previewed note re-file step and a rename guard
items.description: (a) The re-file is real and needed — it is the only way a chapterLabel fix can land on an existing book without splitting a chapter across two decks — but as originally written it was an unconditional, unflagged mutation of live deck membership on EVERY routine deliver. Verified: deliver.js today never reads a note's deck (findNotes/notesInfo/updateNoteFields/addNote only) and src/anki/ankiConnect.js exposes no changeDeck, so this is a new write path. SHIP IT AS: an explicit `--refile` flag, off by default; `--dry` prints every proposed move (note id, card ids, from-deck, to-deck) for inspection before anything runs; SKIP any card whose current deck is a filtered deck (non-zero odid) or any deck outside the managed set, reporting those as untouched. Anki's `deck:` search matches a filtered card by its HOME deck while cardsInfo reports the FILTERED deck, so without that skip a card in a custom-study session reads as 'deck differs' and gets yanked out mid-session. Deck membership also selects the options preset — the very scheduling parameters item 4 is about. PREREQUISITE: WS1 item 10's behaviour probes must first establish what changeDeck does to odid/odue on a filtered card, on a second profile. (b) SCOPE CORRECTION (non-blocking concern 3): 'record the delivered ankiParent in anki-delivered.json' ALREADY SHIPS — writeDeliveredMarker (deliver.js:172-190) writes it and I confirmed both live markers carry it. Only the NEW half is work: if the marker exists and the bootstrap query returns 0 notes, ABORT naming the likely cause (the book title changed). (c) Treat a falsy exportPackage result as a failure so the pre-delivery backup is genuinely fail-closed. (d) Add an add-count ceiling requiring an explicit flag.
items.rationale: ankiParent is a human-editable title, so a title change makes the lookup return nothing and re-inserts the entire book as fresh notes with no scheduling — while the backup that should catch it records a false success, because AnkiConnect returns result:false without an error for a deck that does not exist. This is the single largest unbounded-damage path in the delivery layer. Making the re-file opt-in and previewed keeps that fix without adding a second unbounded path.

items.title: Split the bootstrap index families (do NOT narrow the abid query), and make the fail-closed baseline real
items.description:
src/anki/deliver.js:350-366 builds byAbid, byTarget and byTargetEnglish from ONE book-wide findNotes(deck:"<ankiParent>" note:"<model>"). (a) Keep that book-wide query as the SOLE source of byAbid, and state in a code comment that the abid lookup is deliberately NOT narrowed — abid is the durable delivery key, and a delivered note whose cards no longer sit in unit.ankiDeck must remain findable or the loop falls through to addNote({allowDuplicate:true}) with a fresh guid and fresh scheduling while merely printing the old one under r.orphaned. (b) Scope ONLY the first-run bootstrap indexes byTarget and byTargetEnglish to unit.ankiDeck, which closes the cross-bind on the 17 confirmed repeated targets without touching the durable key; drop or unit-scope the startsWith prefix fallback that would pick 'No' for 'No, not at all'.

(c) FULLY RESPECIFIED IN ROUND 3 — the previous phrasing keyed the fail-closed assertion on 'previously-delivered card ids recorded in anki-delivered.json', and that data does not exist. I read both live markers: each contains exactly {note, ankiParent, lastDeliveredAt}, and writeDeliveredMarker (deliver.js:172-190) writes only those three keys inside a try whose catch is empty ('The marker is advisory; a failed write must not fail the deliver'). So the work is: (c1) ADD the delivered key set to the marker — `deliveredCardIds` (or a count plus a stable hash of the sorted id list, if size matters), written by writeDeliveredMarker on every real deliver; (c2) make THAT write fail-loud — a gate on the largest unbounded-damage path in the delivery layer must not inherit an error-swallowing advisory writer, so either give the marker write its own non-swallowing path or have the deliver report a prominent warning and skip arming the gate rather than silently trusting a stale baseline; (c3) state the BOOTSTRAP RULE explicitly — on a marker with no delivered-key field (which is both live collections today), the first deliver RECORDS the baseline and the assertion is INACTIVE; it arms from the second run. Then: ABORT when a materially large fraction of the recorded ids fails to resolve by abid. Without (c3) the gate has no baseline for the two already-delivered collections and lands in exactly the 'red on day one, or tuned so loose it never fires' trap the round-2 fix existed to avoid.

(d) Add an opt-in --suspend-orphans that suspends and tags abid-tagged notes whose card id left the corpus, reported exactly as today's list — this shares the `suspend` primitive WS4 item 6 adds to ankiConnect.js, and inherits its --dry preview requirement.
items.rationale: The cross-bind is real and worth fixing, but the obvious fix breaks the delivery key and makes item 2(a)'s re-file unimplementable. Separately, 95 cards are excluded today and any excluded after delivery is a card the learner keeps drilling forever; suspending preserves the card, its interval and its revlog and is one click to reverse.

items.title: De-collide the shipped deck preset and document the bury setting
items.description: Rename and re-id the .apkg's deck-options preset (currently id 1, name 'Default') to something deck-scoped like 'anki-builder', so it can never collide by id or name with the owner's collection-wide Default, and note in references/deliver.md that the .apkg's deck options are informational because the AnkiConnect path never applies dconf. Add the one line that actually reaches the live decks: enable 'Bury new siblings' and 'Bury review siblings' on the preset the book decks use. Interleave new-card positions so a note's two directions are not adjacent (fresh-import hygiene only). Verify the preset's actual import behaviour as an assertion of the WS1 item 9 headless import test before touching it further.
items.rationale: Recognition and Production of the same note currently land back-to-back with burying off, so the second direction is answered from working memory — that is real daily-study damage, but the fix that reaches the owner's already-imported, AnkiConnect-updated decks is the doc line, not the dconf edit.

items.title: Settle guid namespacing and the .apkg import runbook
items.description: Decide and record whether the two delivered collections should acquire guidNamespace values going forward (a namespace change on an already-delivered deck creates new notes, so this is new-books-only unless the WS1 item 9 import test proves otherwise), and add to the deliver runbook that a bare-guid deck must never be .apkg-imported into a collection holding another bare-guid deck. Also add the second-profile runbook WS1 item 10 depends on (create profile, install AnkiConnect there, close the owner's profile, switch back) — references/deliver.md currently never mentions a profile at all. NOTE: the stray foreign package deletion moved to WS1 item 4 so its preflight check is not red on the day it lands.
items.rationale: Both live markers resolve guidNamespace to null, so both ship bare guids and 10 ids overlap. AnkiConnect delivery is deck-scoped and safe; the .apkg drag-and-drop path is not, and the marker file's own text contradicts the guid-match-updates model — nobody in this review knows which happens, which is why the import test decides it.

workstreams.name: WS7 — Skill doc & process hygiene
workstreams.goal: SKILL.md is the only file the agent executes; treat it as a prompt with a critical bug. Then mechanize the two procedures that are retyped every unit and every chapter, and stop the docs drifting again.

items.title: SKILL.md truth sweep, as one commit
