items.description: (a) Remove the Reopen flow (verified absent from src/): a done lesson stays fully editable, there is no Reopen and no un-done control, and pulling a delivered unit out of the shipping deck means clearing meta.done plus a rebuild. (b) deck.apkg → <slug>.apkg in all nine places, and fix the State & artifacts tree (unit dirs hold no package; one package per group). (c) Correct the false 'every stage reads stripped-out plain text / the pipeline never sees images' claim in SKILL.md AND extras-pass.md. (d) Resolve the Step-3b timing contradiction. (e) Document the fifth prepare pass (number readings) — and close the other half of that finding in the same commit: the pass sets `uncertain` on machine-filled cards, so at Gate 1 that badge means either 'the extractor thinks this may be premature' or 'check this counter reading' with no way to tell them apart; have the pass write a distinguishing reviewNote (one line, matching how semanticDedup already explains itself). (f) Present ALL nav entries with classifyLesson type as an annotation, never as a filter, and say that on a non-English book every entry will read 'other'. (g) Say that stale review-*.html files may exist in older unit dirs and must never be read as current state.
items.rationale: The Reopen drift lands squarely on red line 2: the documented recovery path for a mis-clicked Mark done on a delivered, daily-studied unit is literally impossible, so an agent following the doc will improvise a hand edit of live state — and the most recent commit in that area ADDED Reopen prose after the button was removed. The classifyLesson item is the most likely first-five-minutes failure of book #2 (0/35 entries qualify on the probed book).

items.title: Replace the review watcher prose with scripts/await-review.mjs
items.description: anki-builder watch / await-review <runDir> --gate 1|2 [--timeout 30m]: resolves the run dir to an absolute path itself, fails loud if cards.json is unreadable (no 2>/dev/null), polls meta.reviewed/meta.done, for gate 2 compares resolveDeckPathForDir(bookDir) mtime against cards.json (so the slug can never be typed wrong), prints a sparse heartbeat, exits with the semantics the prose defines. Ship scripts/undone-unit.mjs alongside it: back up, clear meta.done, rebuild.
items.rationale: ~50 lines of shell reproduced four times per chapter (~60 hand transcriptions for the book already built), encoding four rules each learned from a real incident, and its own gate-2 snippet already contradicts Step 6 six screens later. It contains zero judgment — it observes a flag a human sets. undone-unit turns the one operation that touches a shipped unit from an improvisation into a reviewed script.

items.title: Add a docs-integrity test and declare doc precedence
items.description: One ~20-line test asserting every scripts/*.mjs path mentioned in docs/, README.md, .claude/skills/ or LIMITATIONS.md exists on disk, every file in scripts/ is referenced by at least one doc, and the string 'deck.apkg' appears nowhere outside an explicitly-marked legacy note. Declare SKILL.md normative for operator procedure and PIPELINE.md strictly 'how the code is wired, no procedure', stated at the top of each. Fix the stale Haiku claims in src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js:83 and LIMITATIONS.md.
items.rationale: Four prose surfaces (~4k lines) describe a 14.7k-LOC system with no stated precedence, and drift is already measurable: LIMITATIONS.md documents a deleted script, README/PIPELINE never mention preflight, and the Haiku comment describes a model no pass runs. This test catches the whole class mechanically, which matters because this plan adds ~10 new scripts.

items.title: Replace the per-chapter image sweep with the artifacts that already exist
items.description: Rewrite SKILL.md's grep+unzip recipe to point at .anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/images/ (727 files already extracted and cached) and at conventions.md's per-chapter 'Image-Embedded Content' list. Optionally ship scripts/chapter-images.mjs <hash> <n> printing each referenced image's resolved cache path and whether conventions.md names it. The judgment — load-bearing vs decoration, by position not filename — stays exactly where it is. If WS2 item 4's layout change lands, this script is also the natural place to surface the new mirrored path.
items.rationale: The mandated chore re-extracts by hand, from the archive, information the pipeline already produced and paid for, on every chapter of every book — and its stated justification is false. Do this together with the precedence fix in WS3, or the sweep keeps compensating for a cause that is never addressed.

items.title: Ship finalize-extras and check-done as commands
items.description: anki-builder finalize-extras --run <dir>: prepare → duplicate check (report) → collision audit → order --apply with a fresh seed → validate → preflight, in the correct order, printing every report for the agent to read and judge. scripts/check-done.mjs <runDir>: imports resolveDeckPathForDir, reads meta.done, compares mtimes, exits 0/1/3 (subsumed by await-review --gate 2 if that lands first). All authoring — two waves of subagents, cue wording, which reported duplicate is real — stays agentic.
items.rationale: The extras tail is a seven-command hand-sequenced procedure with real ordering constraints, and two of its steps have already been forgotten in production and patched into prose rather than code (commits 7d7e8db and 0ef7850). Same shape as the assemble→prepare chaining SKILL.md says was created for exactly this reason.

items.title: Give LIMITATIONS.md a status field and retire the dead harness loop
items.description: Add `**Status:** open | resolved <commit> | superseded by <entry>` and, for entries asserting a live-data fact, `**Verified by:** <command>` naming the script that re-derives it instead of freezing a count. Fix the three known-rotten entries (the deleted backfill script; the three 'still uncued' pairs, two of which no longer exist and the third is now cued; the Haiku claim). Mark the harness loop retired and state in CLAUDE.md that LIMITATIONS.md + IDEAS.jsonl are the planning loop — but TRANSPLANT T011's content into LIMITATIONS.md as a when-to-revisit entry rather than dropping it, and reconcile the six IDEAS rows that have already shipped before any convert sweep.
items.rationale: LIMITATIONS.md is the artifact that actually steers the work (83 commits, newest 2026-08-13) while the harness ledger stopped 2026-07-13 across 535 commits. Entries that assert live-data facts are the ones that rot, and a false entry is worse than a missing one because it closes a question that is open. T011 is the only written pointer at the template path, which is simultaneously the path with zero worked examples, no preflight coverage and a readiness-gate exemption.

items.title: Make invisible states visible: readiness exemptions, unit/marker disagreement, corpus drift
items.description: Report-only preflight lines: (a) any unit that is done but lacks the full readiness marker set, and any unit carrying meta.prepareDegraded — two of the three shipped course lessons carry no markers at all and are permanently exempt; (b) any unit whose meta.courseSlug/epubHash disagrees with the containing collection's marker (lesson-0 carries courseSlug 'intensive-japanese-1' inside nihongo-101-course-n5), plus gaps or duplicates in the chapterNumber sequence (keyed on the invariant pinned in WS1 item 1); (c) ids present in corpus.json but not cards.json (chapter-6 already has one) and relative-order mismatches. Also have extras-duplicate-check mirror exclusions into corpus.json the way extras-order already mirrors ordering. Introduce one unitState()/collectionState() returning {authored, reviewed, done, packaged, delivered} and make it the single input to every guard, so --force on a DELIVERED collection needs a distinct second flag.
items.rationale: Keep the readiness carve-outs (removing them would retroactively unreview signed-off work) but stop them being unknowable. And 'delivered' — the state that literally means red line 2 applies — is currently written by the deliverer, read only by a dashboard badge, and consulted by no guard; every mutation guard keys on a weaker proxy instead.

workstreams.name: WS8 — Models, pinning and pass mechanics
workstreams.goal: Give each pass its own knob (and its own timeout), raise the one pass whose failures are structurally invisible, and build the eval fixtures that make WS3's prompt rewrites measurable rather than hopeful.

items.title: Split the two env scopes into per-pass scopes, with per-scope timeouts
items.description: Give each runClaude wrapper its own scopeEnvPrefix (one line per call site; keep ANKI_BUILDER_TRANSLATE and ANKI_BUILDER_EPUB_LLM as fallbacks so nothing breaks), and make timeoutMs part of the same per-scope resolution (<SCOPE>_TIMEOUT_MS). Document the result as one table in PIPELINE.md: pass → module → prompt file → model/effort → env override → batched? → typical wall clock.
items.rationale: Today one knob covers chapter extraction — the pass whose misses SKILL.md itself calls structurally invisible — and the pedagogical sort, which is mechanically validated and fails open. Their blast radii are not comparable. The timeout must move with the scope: a single 10-minute spawnSync ceiling with one same-budget retry already caps the 57-file conventions pass, so raising effort without raising the timeout converts a quality knob into a hard mid-chapter abort with a misleading error.

items.title: Build per-pass eval fixtures — as regression coverage for the WS3 prompt rewrites (do this BEFORE WS3 lands)
items.description: RE-JUSTIFIED AND RE-SEQUENCED (non-blocking concern 5). This was sized L and justified entirely as a precondition for model downgrades the plan then explicitly rejects, for a saving described as cents — an L-sized item with no claimed payoff. Its real use is the one that went unclaimed: WS3 rewrites the extraction prompt's precedence rule, narrows the dialogue ban, adds three content-class rules and changes the output contract to an envelope, with NO way to tell whether card output improved, stayed level or regressed. So: check in one reviewed lesson per pass as input → human-approved reference output (extraction items, dedup exclusion set, sort ordering, category assignment, forward flags), and run it before and after each WS3 prompt edit, comparing item sets and diffing what changed for a human to judge (never auto-pass/fail on an exact match — extraction is generative and a diff is evidence, not a verdict). START with the extraction fixture, since that is the pass WS3 changes most and the only one whose misses are unrecoverable. The downgrade use survives as a secondary benefit: only downgrade a pass whose cheaper run matches within tolerance, starting with forward flags and the pedagogical sort; semanticDedup and lesson-word categorization stay NOT downgradeable until measured. If this item is dropped, record the downgrades as permanently deferred rather than 'pending a fixture'.
items.rationale: There is no eval harness anywhere in the repo, so both a prompt rewrite's improvement and a downgrade's damage are unmeasurable by construction. The prompt rewrites are landing regardless and are the higher-value thing to measure — and putting the fixture before them turns WS3 from a set of plausible edits into a set of observed ones.

items.title: Raise chapter extraction (and batch the conventions pass before touching it)
items.description: Set extraction to effort high once per-scope timeouts exist. For the whole-book conventions pass, first batch it over chapter ranges with a merge step, and add a taught-index-style coverage assertion: require a per-chapter line quoting a deterministic anchor (the chapter's <title>) and verify each quote against the cached xhtml. Normalize whitespace and entities before comparing, and REPORT the per-chapter shortfall rather than aborting — the anchor can legitimately be absent, duplicated across chapters, or entity-escaped, and hard-failing the one pass that onboards a book on a fragile anchor trades a silent gap for a hard block.
items.rationale: Extraction is the only pass whose failure mode is silent and unrecoverable, and it is agentic, which is where effort buys reading discipline. The conventions pass currently self-certifies ('All 57 chapter files were read in full') inside a 10-minute ceiling with no partial-progress path — the exact silent-degradation signature, in the artifact that then steers every chapter extraction.

items.title: Fix the two pass mechanics that lose work on failure or concurrency
items.description: (a) On translate retry, halve the failed set instead of re-sending the identical unbatched prompt — with BATCH_SIZE = Infinity a truncated response makes the retry deterministically identical to the first attempt. (b) Apply audio.js's merge pattern to prepare and crossLessonNotes: re-read cards.json after the multi-minute model call and write back only the fields the pass owns, instead of writing a whole-file snapshot taken before it. Factor the merge into a shared mergeIntoCardsFile(path, byId, ownedFields).
items.rationale: Both are silent-loss seams: the retry burns a second full-size call to fail the same way, and a concurrent dashboard edit during a 10-minute pass is silently overwritten. audio.js already documents and defends against exactly this hazard, so the pattern exists and is proven in-repo.

items.title: Add the EOCD entry-count throw (and keep media memoization deferred)
items.description: Throw when entries.length > 0xffff in buildZip rather than emitting a structurally corrupt central directory. Do NOT memoize media entries by item.audio until the headless import verifier from WS1 item 9 exists and passes on a memoized package.
items.rationale: The throw is unambiguously right and converts silent corruption into an error. The memoization saves 22 redundant zip entries out of 1,914 (~1%) in exchange for re-entering the exact code path whose last obviously-reasonable change produced an .apkg that Anki rejected while passing every test and every synthetic check.

rulings.topic: ROUND-3 OBJECTION H — the re-keyed fail-closed abid assertion references data that does not exist (WS6 item 3c, and the WS0 item 1 amendment)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD in full; the item is respecified and WS0's rationale corrected. I read both live markers: output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana/anki-delivered.json and output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/anki-delivered.json each contain exactly {note, ankiParent, lastDeliveredAt} — no card ids, no note ids, no counts. writeDeliveredMarker (src/anki/deliver.js:172-190) writes only those three keys, and its catch block is empty with the comment 'The marker is advisory; a failed write must not fail the deliver.' So the round-2 phrasing was unimplementable as written, and the WS0 amendment protected the file on a false premise about its contents. FIX AS SPECIFIED, three parts: (1) ADD the delivered key set to the marker (deliveredCardIds, or a count plus a stable hash of the sorted list), written by writeDeliveredMarker on every real deliver; (2) make that write FAIL-LOUD rather than inheriting the advisory swallow — a gate on the largest unbounded-damage path in the delivery layer must not silently depend on a best-effort writer, so either give it a non-swallowing path or have the deliver warn prominently and decline to arm the gate rather than trust a stale baseline; (3) state the BOOTSTRAP RULE explicitly — on a marker with no delivered-key field (which is BOTH live collections today), the first deliver RECORDS the baseline and the assertion is inactive, arming from the second run. WS0 item 1's rationale is corrected to say the marker is protected for what it will hold, not what it holds.
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is that the round-2 re-key was itself a correction of a worse bug (comparing abid matches against the current spec card count, which false-aborts every legitimate incremental deliver), and that piling a schema addition, a writer-semantics change and a bootstrap rule onto it grows a fix that was supposed to be a one-line comparison. There is also a fair worry that recording delivered card ids in an unversioned marker creates a new piece of irreplaceable state — which is precisely why it joins WS0's protected set. Both are accepted costs: a gate whose baseline does not exist is not a gate, and the alternative (deriving the baseline from Anki at deliver time) is circular, since the whole point is to detect that Anki no longer matches.

rulings.topic: ROUND-3 OBJECTION I — the import verifier's live-Anki assertions would run against the owner's daily collection (WS1 item 9)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; the item is SPLIT and the target collection named for each half. Verified: src/anki/ankiConnect.js:7 pins DEFAULT_ENDPOINT to http://127.0.0.1:8765, AnkiConnect talks only to the running Anki instance, and I grepped references/deliver.md for 'profile', '8765' and 'localhost' — zero hits, so nothing anywhere tells the operator which Anki these probes hit. Assertions (1) and (2) of the original item (dconf preset id 1, guid-match-on-import) are genuinely headless via the pinned anki Python package against a throwaway collection — those stay as WS1 item 9 and can land immediately. Assertions (3) and (4) (what modelTemplateAdd/updateModelTemplates does to card rows; what changeDeck does to a card with non-zero odid) are AnkiConnect behaviour and become WS1 item 10, which must: run against a SEPARATE Anki profile created for the purpose with AnkiConnect installed in it, require the owner's profile closed (only one instance can hold :8765), document a switch-back step in references/deliver.md, and REFUSE to run when the reachable collection contains any deck matching a delivered marker's ankiParent. Until item 10 is built that way, no item may cite 'the WS1 behaviour test' as its safety prerequisite. Round-3 objection J adds a third probe (suspend on a filtered card) to the same item.
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is friction: the second-profile dance (close Anki, switch profile, install the add-on, run, switch back) is enough ceremony that the probes may simply never be run, which strands four deferred decisions indefinitely — whereas running them on the live collection with a fresh pre-probe backup (deliver.js already snapshots before every deliver) would be quick and, on the optimistic reading, recoverable. That is rejected under principle 1: a backup makes damage recoverable, not absent, and the specific damage here (a forced one-way AnkiWeb sync, cards yanked out of a custom-study session, schema flags flipped mid-study-day) is exactly the class the plan spends a whole workstream avoiding. Friction on an experiment run once is the correct price.

rulings.topic: ROUND-3 OBJECTION J — suspend-at-delivery held to a weaker standard than changeDeck (WS4 item 6)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; suspend is held to the standard the plan set for changeDeck in round-2 objection C. Verified again that `suspend` is absent from src/anki/ankiConnect.js, so this is a genuinely new live write path with no existing behaviour to lean on — the same footing as changeDeck, which the plan made opt-in, --dry-previewed, filtered-deck-skipping and test-gated on the reasoning that 'reporting a move after the fact is not consent'. Every clause transfers. SHIP AS: (1) unconditional suspension ONLY for notes created by THIS deliver (the addNote path — a card that has never been studied has no scheduling to disturb), reported like createdDecks; (2) for already-delivered abid-matched notes, OPT-IN behind an explicit flag with a --dry list of note id, card id, ordinal, from-state and to-state; (3) a card that is currently unsuspended AND already carries the `dir-suspended` tag is treated as a human override — reported, never silently re-suspended, unless a distinct second flag is passed; (4) add 'what does AnkiConnect suspend do to a card with non-zero odid, and do Check Database or a template update unsuspend' to the WS1 item 10 probes, as a prerequisite for (2). Also stated in the item, per non-blocking concern 6: the .apkg keeps emitting both card rows while delivery suspends one, so the package deliberately no longer reproduces the delivered deck card-for-card.
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is that the direction flag in cards.json is supposed to be the authoring surface, and a mechanism that only applies to newly-created notes unless a flag is passed means the flag is decorative for the 2,150 already-delivered notes where the leaky-scene problem actually lives — に's six identical fronts are all delivered. Making the fix opt-in risks it never being applied, exactly as the parallel dissent on --refile records. Answered the same way: an opt-in path the owner runs deliberately once, with a dry-run diff in front of them, is strictly better than one that silently stops a matured card appearing tomorrow because of a JSON field; and the human-override rule means the owner's own unsuspend in Anki wins permanently rather than being re-fought on every deliver.

rulings.topic: ROUND-2 OBJECTION A — the mechanism for per-card direction control (WS4 item 6)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; the item was fully respecified and the plan's own earlier substitute struck. I verified both halves in code. (1) The `for (let ord = 0; ord < 2; ord++) { insertCard.run(...) }` at src/deck/collection.js:526 sits inside the .apkg SQLite writer. (2) src/anki/deliver.js:426-433 delivers with client.addNote(...), and Anki generates one card per template from that note — so a build-side card omission is INERT for every note delivered the way the owner's decks actually are, and on the .apkg side it is self-reversing (a missing card row is regenerated by Check Database and by a template update, i.e. WS4 item 5 would undo WS4 item 6). NEW MECHANISM: suspend-at-delivery, sharing the `suspend` primitive with WS6 item 3(d); the .apkg builder keeps emitting both card rows so the two paths cannot drift structurally. Round 3 then scoped WHEN that suspend may run (see objection J).
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is the original item's build-side simplicity: not generating a card is conceptually cleaner than generating one and immediately suspending it, it needs no new AnkiConnect write path, and it keeps the deck free of suspended clutter in browse views and card counts. There is also a legitimate worry that suspension is a per-CARD state a human can flip in Anki without the pipeline knowing, so cards.json and live state can diverge — the same provenance-drift shape as isStageOwnedCard. Both are real; they lose because a mechanism that is inert on the primary delivery path and reverted by Check Database is not a mechanism at all. The drift worry is now answered concretely by round 3's human-override rule.

rulings.topic: ROUND-2 OBJECTION B — audio text-hash mismatch blocking Mark done (WS5 item 1d)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; the block is removed for now and the missing exit added. Verified: handleLessonDone (src/server/index.js:277-287) does setLessonDone then rebuildGroupQuiet — no gate of any kind today, so this would have been the first ever block on the owner's daily critical path. The analogy to findUnreadableNumbers does not survive src/cards/readiness.js:61-65, which argues explicitly that THAT gate is clearable in place ('the offending cards are on screen … fixing it clears the block on the next render, with nothing to re-run'). A hash mismatch had no such exit: clause (b) forbade re-stamping from current text and clause (d) forbade regenerating over the human's clip, so the only escape for the ~200 hand-touched cards this item exists to protect was destroying the hand trim or hand pick. FIX: (i) ship badge-only, run the backfill, report the live badge count, decide about promotion afterwards; (ii) add a per-card 'keep this clip for the current text' action that re-stamps from CURRENT text with provenance (audioTextHashAcceptedBy + timestamp), and scope the never-backfill-from-card-text prohibition to AUTOMATED/BULK backfill only.
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is codeexpert-3's original framing, which is sound: a badge with no teeth is exactly the wallpaper class this plan spends WS1 item 2 fixing, and the whole point of the finding is that a text edit silently invalidates a clip the deck then ships forever. A per-card human accept also creates a one-click path to certifying drift, which is what (b) was written to prevent. That cost is answered by recording WHO accepted and WHEN — auditable in a way today's silence is not — and by leaving promotion-to-block on the table once the badge count is measured.

rulings.topic: ROUND-2 OBJECTION C — unconditional changeDeck re-file on every deliver (WS6 item 2a)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; the re-file becomes opt-in and previewed. Verified: deliver.js reads notes via findNotes/notesInfo and writes via updateNoteFields/addNote/addTags only — it never reads a note's deck — and ankiConnect.js has no changeDeck, so this is a wholly new write path. Two hazards stand: deck membership selects the options preset (the same limits and burying WS6 item 4 is about), so a silent re-file changes scheduling behaviour while this plan demands an explicit --allow-model-change for a cosmetic CSS edit; and Anki's `deck:` search matches a filtered card by its HOME deck while cardsInfo reports the FILTERED deck, so a card in a custom-study session reads as 'deck differs' and would be yanked mid-session. SHIP AS: `--refile` off by default; `--dry` prints every proposed move; skip any card with non-zero odid or outside the managed set and report it untouched; and the filtered-deck question goes to the WS1 item 10 probes. Reporting a move after the fact is not consent.
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is that the re-file is the ONLY way a chapterLabel correction can reach an existing book without splitting a chapter across two decks — a deck rename in Anki is a new deck — so without an automatic re-file the WS2 entity fix is permanently new-books-only, and the existing book's labels likely freeze by inertia. Accepted: an opt-in path run deliberately once, with a dry-run diff in front of the owner, is strictly better than an automatic one that runs on every deliver forever.

rulings.topic: ROUND-2 OBJECTION D — 'key the destination on the archive path' for colliding image filenames (WS2 item 3a)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD in substance; the mechanism is disambiguated, flattening forbidden, sequencing inverted — and in round 3 the two halves are split into separate items (non-blocking concern 4), with the layout change resized to L. I verified the mechanism: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:637 computes join(destDir, src) with destDir = dirname(destPath), and chapterCachePath is `/chapters/.xhtml`, so ALL chapters share one chapters/ directory — simultaneously why relative resolution works (comment at :577-588: the extraction prompt tells the model to resolve each src relative to the chapter file it Read and open it directly) and why the collision exists. Any scheme that changes an image's path RELATIVE to its chapter file without rewriting the cached xhtml's src attributes breaks the model's Read invisibly. SHIP FIRST: byte-compare and log loudly, plus a count in the shape report. SHIP SECOND, behind the fixture suite: mirror the ARCHIVE layout under chapters/, which is isomorphic to the zip. One correction to the objection's own proposal: a per-chapter subdirectory does NOT fully close it — two chapters in different archive dirs both referencing ../images/foo.png still collide — so the byte-compare detector stays in either design.
rulings.dissent: The objection argued for fixing by construction immediately, on the grounds that a detector that only logs still ships the wrong image into a paid extraction pass, and that the layout change invalidates only the free zip-inflate cache. That is largely right and is why the layout change is scheduled rather than rejected. It loses the ordering argument to principle 4 and to the project's own cautionary tale: this is the code path whose last obviously-reasonable change produced an artifact the real consumer rejected while every test passed, and the real consumer here (a model opening a file by relative path) is exercised nowhere in the test suite.

rulings.topic: BLOCKING OBJECTION 1 — scoping the AnkiConnect bootstrap query (codeexpert-5, WS6 item 3)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; the item is rewritten. src/anki/deliver.js:350-366 populates byAbid, byTarget and byTargetEnglish from the same single book-wide findNotes. Narrowing that query narrows the durable delivery key, so an already-delivered abid-tagged note whose cards no longer sit in unit.ankiDeck misses byAbid, misses the now-unit-scoped target index, and falls through to addNote({allowDuplicate:true}) with a fresh guid and fresh scheduling — while merely being appended to r.orphaned. That is red line 2, introduced by the plan itself, and it makes WS6 item 2(a)'s re-file unimplementable. FIX: keep the book-wide query as the sole source of byAbid with an explicit comment; scope only byTarget/byTargetEnglish to unit.ankiDeck; add a fail-closed assertion — whose baseline round 3 then had to construct, since the marker holds no delivered ids (see objection H).
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is the original item's simplicity: one findNotes per unit is a smaller, more obviously-correct diff than two index families fed by two differently-scoped reads, and the cross-bind is a real observed hazard (17 targets repeat across units; the startsWith fallback would pick 'No' for 'No, not at all'). The split leaves a book-wide read a future maintainer may 'simplify' back. Answered by the fail-closed assertion, an explicit comment at the query, and the pinning test in WS1 item 8.

rulings.topic: BLOCKING OBJECTION 2 — wiring preflight/validate-decks into .githooks/pre-push
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; the pre-push clause is struck. Verified: .githooks/pre-push runs `npm run ci` only, and ci = format:check && lint && test && build — all assertions about tracked state that pass in a fresh clone. preflight and validate:decks assert on /output and /.anki-builder, both gitignored AND untracked. Wiring them in couples git push to unversioned deck state; in CI and a fresh clone the hook is a no-op by construction, so the coupling buys nothing and costs the push path. At least two of WS1's new FAIL-tier checks are red on live data the day they land, so the first push after WS1 would require --no-verify. KEEP `npm run check` = ci && validate:decks && preflight as a MANUAL documented gate before handing over a review link and before a deliver.
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is that a gate nobody is forced to run is not a gate: this project's entire failure catalogue is 'the check existed and was skipped', and pre-push is the one enforcement point an orchestrating agent cannot forget. The compromise stands if the owner wants hook coverage later — make the validate:decks/preflight half ADVISORY inside the hook (print, never contribute a non-zero exit).

rulings.topic: BLOCKING OBJECTION 3 — audio text hash coverage and the absent case (codeexpert-3, WS5 item 1)
rulings.decision: OBJECTION UPHELD; the item is respecified and the numbers back it. As written it stamped audioTextHash only on install, delivering ZERO coverage for the ~200 hand-touched clips the finding is about. Probed the live tree: audioOriginal is present on every audio-bearing card, and its prefix is derivable for 1,765 plain + 70 -gen- + 77 -genkanji- = 1,912 of 1,932; 20 are hand-named uploads; of the 109 audioManual cards 95 are derivable. So: BACKFILL from the audioOriginal filename prefix; NEVER bulk-backfill from current card text; an underivable clip yields an INFO 'unverifiable' line that never blocks; and the comparison must consult the same per-unit kanji-TTS meta flag that gates defaultClipText.
rulings.dissent: The losing argument is that deriving a text hash from a FILENAME infers provenance from a name — precisely the mistake isStageOwnedCard already made once, when it judged stage-ownership from `audio` until cleanup renamed everything and provenance had to move onto audioOriginal. A stamp-on-install-only rule is unimpeachable at the cost of covering nothing today. That is why the backfill is one-way and why the 20 underivable clips degrade to INFO rather than being guessed at.

rulings.topic: Severity and ordering of the test-suite library leak (qa-1 / techlead-1 / codeexpert-1 / generalist-3 / adversarial-14)
rulings.decision: CRITICAL, and the second thing fixed after the state snapshot. Merge all five into qa-1's framing, the only one carrying both channels (dedup library AND audio cache) and the escalation through real voice ids. Implement the guard at libraryHome() itself — returning a per-process tmpdir under the test runner — not at each writer, and add the suite-wide write guard so the CLASS is closed. I confirmed .anki-builder/epubs/h1/ and four 4-byte files in .anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/ beside three real voice directories. Round-3 refinement (non-blocking concern 7): the redirect is gated on NODE_TEST_CONTEXT ONLY, decided up front rather than left as an in-item caveat — src/util/testEnv.js:8 also returns true for NODE_ENV=test, and a real run under that env would appear to have lost the dedup registry, a worse failure than the one being fixed. Tmpdir cleanup for ~75 processes is specified in the item.
rulings.dissent: QA itself retracted to HIGH on re-probe: the escalation needs two simultaneous omissions and no current test supplies both, so realized damage today is zero. Adversarial originally filed it LOW because 'h1' is a fake hash. Both arguments are about current fixture values, not about the code — which is why the majority position won under principle 4: the defect is a missing injection, and safety depends on every future test author remembering a stub, the exact reasoning assertExternalCallAllowed already rejects for the LLM spawn.

rulings.topic: Severity of the cross-deck card-id / bare-guid collision (qa-2)
rulings.decision: HIGH, not critical — but ship both preflight checks now and classify collisions by content. Of the 10 shared ids, nine are byte-identical in target and english and only `scarf` differs, so the realistic worst case is a small number of notes acquiring the wrong book's field values (loud, recoverable from the pre-delivery backup) plus a foreign book landing in the course tree — not the silent scheduling loss 'critical' is reserved for. Establish the actual import behaviour as an assertion of the WS1 item 9 HEADLESS import test (not the live probes) and let that evidence re-rank it. The stray-package DELETION lives in WS1 item 4 so the check is not red on landing day.
rulings.dissent: QA ranked it critical on the strength of a loaded gun: both markers resolve guidNamespace to null, a foreign 11 MB .apkg physically sits in the course directory (confirmed), LIMITATIONS.md predicted this exact hazard with the trigger 'before importing a second book's .apkg' which is now TRUE, and the .apkg is what a human reaches for when AnkiConnect is not running. QA also notes the marker file's own text claims a re-import 'creates duplicate notes', contradicting the guid-match-updates model — so nobody in this review knows which happens, and ranking on the more optimistic model is a bet.

rulings.topic: Mechanism for per-card direction control (learner-3) — the empty-front rejection
rulings.decision: REJECT the template-conditional mechanism outright. A conditionally-empty front does not suppress a card in Anki — it creates an empty card, which Tools → Empty Cards deletes along with its interval and revlog. That is red-line-2 scheduling loss on 2,150 delivered notes triggered by routine housekeeping, not reversible by re-delivering. Three reviewers reached this independently. The GOAL is retained; its mechanism is suspend-at-delivery, scoped per round-3 objection J.
rulings.dissent: Learner's underlying case is strong and stands: に ships six cards whose Recognition fronts are the bare string に, disambiguated by scenes that paraphrase their own answers, and the fixed two-cards-per-note model is what makes the accepted leaky-scene tension cost real daily reps. Learner did say 'ship it with a suspend path, not silently' — which rounds 2 and 3 vindicated: the suspend path was the right half of the finding all along.

rulings.topic: How the sibling-burying fix reaches the live collection (learner-2)
rulings.decision: The doc line is primary; the dconf edit is fresh-import hygiene only. The owner's decks were delivered via AnkiConnect, which never writes dconf and never sets due positions, so flipping bury in buildDconf changes nothing for the decks this finding is about — and aiming a modified preset named 'Default' at the owner's collection-wide Default is an unknown write to scheduling parameters. Ship: one line in references/deliver.md, the preset rename/re-id, and the position interleave as .apkg hygiene. Downgrade to medium as a code item; the study insight itself is high-value.
rulings.dissent: Learner ranked it high as the single biggest study-quality gain per line of code, and that framing is right about the SYMPTOM: Recognition and Production of one note land back-to-back with burying off, so the second direction is answered from working memory, converting a two-direction note into roughly one direction of learning. Learner then retracted the dconf half themselves during discussion; the retraction is what this ruling follows.

rulings.topic: Kanji-orthography TTS as the Japanese default (linguist-4)
rulings.decision: Opt-in for NEW units behind a meta flag, gated on an A/B and a mis-conversion measurement, with the generated kanji surfaced automatically in the audio review for veto. Do not flip the global default. defaultClipText feeds both the ElevenLabs cache key and the staleness filename, so changing it for ja invalidates ~1,700 clips (paid refetches, discarded trim tuning) while the ~200 hand-touched clips are exempt from regeneration — producing a silently mixed-orthography deck. Kana→kanji is also one-to-many, adding a wrong-word channel the learner cannot detect from a kana card face. The WS5 text-hash comparison must read the same per-unit flag.
rulings.dissent: Linguist's evidence stands and linguist self-downgraded to medium during discussion: the codebase itself says kanji voices more naturally, ~13% of clips needed human audio intervention, and all-kana input strips the word-boundary and homograph cues a Japanese TTS front-end relies on. The pedagogy is not in dispute — only the rollout.

rulings.topic: Per-pass model tiers (promptengineer-4) and the purpose of the eval fixtures
rulings.decision: ADOPT the scope split and the extraction raise; ADD the per-scope timeout as a hard prerequisite; REJECT the downgrades until eval fixtures exist. Round-3 amendment (non-blocking concern 5): the fixtures are RE-JUSTIFIED as regression coverage for WS3's prompt rewrites and RE-SEQUENCED ahead of them, starting with the extraction fixture. As previously written, an L-sized item was justified solely as a precondition for downgrades this plan rejects, for a saving described as cents — that is not a payoff, and it left WS3's five prompt edits with no way to tell improvement from regression. The downgrade use survives as secondary. If the item is dropped entirely, the downgrades are recorded as permanently deferred rather than 'pending a fixture'.
rulings.dissent: PromptEngineer's cost argument is sound and the blast-radius analysis is the sharpest model-layer thinking in the review: forward flags are explicitly prompt-biased toward cheap false positives, the sort is a mechanically validated permutation, and paying Sonnet-medium for all of them is real waste. Learner separately objects that even the sort should not drop, since a degraded ordering is a valid permutation that no tool diffs and that changes the teaching sequence the owner experiences. Re-purposing the fixture does not settle that argument — it makes it measurable, which is the point.

rulings.topic: Whether preflight should hard-fail on an unrecognised unit-shaped directory (qa-3) and on marker-stuck clips (generalist-6)
rulings.decision: Both start as REPORT/ACK, not FAIL. The unmatched-dir check becomes a failure only after the shared loader knows all three unit shapes — otherwise the first person to build a template unit gets a red preflight for a legitimate layout and learns to ignore it. Marker-stuck stays a heuristic behind an acknowledgement file: FAIL only on unacknowledged instances. Triage the 7 live clips as content work regardless. Generalised: any check promoted to FAIL lands in the same commit as the fix or the ACK for its live instance — which is why the stray-.apkg deletion moved into WS1.
rulings.dissent: QA argues 'a unit-shaped folder this tool cannot see' is a strictly more useful error than silence, and the silent-skip is the project's signature failure mode. Generalist argues the prose already says a marker-stuck clip should be regenerated rather than shipped. Both are right that the end state is a failure; the ruling is about ordering, since a red gate the operator learns to override is worse than no gate.

rulings.topic: Hand-rolled EPUB stack vs a library (techlead-10)
rulings.decision: KEEP the hand-rolled stack. Only container walking is hand-rolled (~200 lines over zlib.inflateRawSync), its two rejections are explicit and loud with 35 tests behind them, and the genuine cliff is downstream convention-bound code (deckPath's GROUPED_LABEL, classifyLesson) that no parser swap touches. Spend the effort on the probe, the diagnostics and the hostile fixtures instead.
rulings.dissent: None recorded — every perspective that examined the parser reached the same conclusion. Adversarial's evidence strengthens it: the failures are silence, not incorrect parsing, and a library would trade specific loud rejections for generic ones.

rulings.topic: Where the ~15 proposed new checks live (techlead-14 vs 'add it to preflight')
rulings.decision: Build the scope model and the severity policy FIRST, then land checks. preflight today has six checks and two report lines that have never once been zero, no tests, and no way to distinguish a check that matched nothing from one that passed. Adding fifteen more report lines to that base destroys the one deterministic gate. Same rule for scripts/ generally: a script that mutates output/ keeps its logic in src/ behind a test. WS1 item 1 is sized L and split (shared loader first, scope/severity registry second) because items 3-6 depend only on the loader half.
rulings.dissent: The competing view, implicit in most findings, is that each check is 15-20 lines and waiting on a substrate delays cheap safety wins. That is true for the three two-line guards (extras epubHash, 〜-in-target, dedup completeness), which is why they are scheduled inside WS1 rather than after it — the policy work gates the volume, not the urgent minority.

rulings.topic: When the extras pass runs (promptengineer-7)
rulings.decision: AFTER Gate 2 (Mark done), and say it once. SKILL.md's own arc diagram and its watcher instructions already say gate 2; only the section that owns the step says gate 1. The technical argument is decisive: exclusions at gate 2 change the base card set that the extras duplicate and collision audits diff against, so authoring extras at gate 1 silently invalidates those audits. Delete the losing phrasing rather than softening it.
rulings.dissent: SKILL.md:367 states gate 1 emphatically, and there is a real workflow argument for it — extras authoring is slow and starting it earlier overlaps with the audio stage. If the owner prefers gate 1, the doc must then say explicitly that extras are re-audited whenever the base unit changes during gate 2.

rulings.topic: Retiring the harness loop and the fate of T011 (techlead-7)
rulings.decision: Retire the loop, TRANSPLANT T011. The ledger stopped 2026-07-13 across 535 commits while LIMITATIONS.md has 83 and steers the actual work, so the pretence should end — but T011 is the only written pointer at the intersection of three confirmed blind spots (no real-Anki-import test, output/templates/ empty, sourceType 'template' exempt from the readiness gate). Move its content into LIMITATIONS.md as a when-to-revisit entry with the import-smoke-test scope attached, and reconcile the six already-shipped IDEAS rows before any convert sweep.
rulings.dissent: TechLead's position is that a stale T011 pointing at the one path with zero worked examples is itself the dishonesty, and the honest move is to drop it. QA and Generalist both objected that dropping it erases the record of the highest-risk untested path — the same silent-degradation shape the rest of the review is about.

rulings.topic: Deleting stale artifacts, and what WS0 actually protects
rulings.decision: All deletions wait behind the WS0 snapshot — and so do content REGENERATIONS inside delivered units (WS5's 7 marker-audible clips, WS4's hand cue edits), which mutate the same unbacked tree. Verified: both /output and /.anki-builder are gitignored AND untracked. ROUND-3 HONESTY AMENDMENT (non-blocking concern 1): WS0's protected set is JSON-only by design, so for AUDIO the gate was empty — the plan asserted a safety net that protects nothing an audio re-trim could destroy, which is the exact class of false safety claim WS1 item 5's own rationale calls worse than a missing mechanism. Fix both ways, cheaply: state plainly in WS0 and WS5 that audio recovery rests on the sibling .orig.mp3 (confirmed present for the flagged clips), AND pull those seven clips plus their originals into the snapshot. Also note that WS0 item 3 deletes inside .anki-builder/audio (140 MB, 3,610 paid clips) while that tree stays unbacked by design — which is why that deletion names its two targets literally rather than by pattern. Fix the review-*.html doc claim now; delete later.
rulings.dissent: Generalist originally recommended deleting the stale review-*.html outright to make SKILL.md's claim true, then retracted — those files are unversioned forensic snapshots of what a reviewer actually signed off on. The counter-argument, that leaving falsifiable claims in the doc invites an agent to read months-old card sets, is addressed by the doc fix rather than the deletion. On the audio half, the competing view is that snapshotting any audio at all invites scope creep into a 140 MB tree the plan deliberately leaves unbacked; that is why the addition is scoped to seven named clips.

rulings.topic: Ruby handling severity (adversarial-4)
rulings.decision: Demote ruby to a nav-LABEL concern (medium); keep entity decoding at high. Adversarial's own retraction is decisive: extractChapterToFile writes the RAW xhtml and the extraction model reads the file directly, so <ruby>…<rt>…</rt></ruby> reaches the model intact. The load-bearing half is the entity decoder, because a label flows verbatim into a live Anki deck name — and as SCHEDULED it ships new-books-only, since WS6's re-file path does not exist until later and is now opt-in.
rulings.dissent: Linguist argues the ruby half deserves more weight going forward: the one proven book contains zero <ruby> while ruby is near-universal in kanji-bearing Japanese textbooks, and the interleaving failure (漢かん字じ) would be silent. That concern is carried instead as the WS3 prompt rule making <rt> the authoritative reading source, which is the higher-value response to the same fact.

rulings.topic: Media-key memoization in the .apkg builder (codeexpert-11)
rulings.decision: SPLIT: ship the EOCD uint16 throw now; defer the memoization until the headless import verifier (WS1 item 9) exists and passes on a memoized package. The payoff is 22 redundant zip entries out of 1,914 (~1%), against re-entering the one code path whose last reasonable-looking change produced a package Anki rejected while passing every test and every synthetic check.
rulings.dissent: CodeExpert's observation is correct and the fix is small; the memoization also keeps the integer-sequential-key invariant intact by construction if written carefully. QA and Generalist both objected on sequencing grounds, and the deferral costs nothing because the verifier is scheduled in WS1 — and after the round-3 split, the headless half of it can land without waiting on any Anki-profile setup.

openQuestions: Snapshot mechanism for the unbacked state (WS0): un-ignore the few MB of JSON under output/ and .anki-builder/*/corpora so it lives in git history, or keep everything ignored and write timestamped tarballs beside anki-backups/? Git gives real history and diffs and makes a bad --apply sweep trivially revertible; tarballs keep the repo clean and match the existing anki-backups precedent. MECHANICS, so the git option is not chosen on a false premise: .gitignore excludes `/output` and `/.anki-builder` as DIRECTORIES, and git does not descend into an excluded directory — so `!/output/**/cards.json` silently matches nothing. The git option requires converting to `/output/**` plus a `!/output/**/` directory re-include placed before any file re-include, verified with `git check-ignore -v` on a real file before being relied on. Either way the protected set must include .preflight-accepted.json, anki-delivered.json (for the delivered-key baseline WS6 item 3 adds to it), and the seven WS5 marker-audible clips plus their .orig.mp3 siblings. One of these must be chosen before ANY work begins.

Is the bundled-template source path alive? output/templates/ is empty, preflight never enumerates it, prepare skips both enrichment passes for it and readiness exempts it from the gate entirely — so it is simultaneously the least-exercised and least-guarded path in the repo. ANSWER THIS BEFORE STARTING WS1 ITEM 1, not at the end: if it is dead, say so and delete the template branches, and WS1 item 1 plus the templates half of the validate-decks fold both shrink materially (which is what makes its L sizing tolerable). If it is alive, the first template deck doubles as the headless import verifier's fixture.

Reading vs furigana policy before the second book: render {{Reading}} on the answer side and widen the extraction prompt to emit it for any kanji-bearing target, or add a separate furigana/kana field and keep `reading` as the TTS-spoken form only? The schema and the prompt currently define `reading` two incompatible ways (general kanji disambiguation vs numerals-only), 136 cards populate it, neither template renders it, and this is the decision that determines whether a normal kanji textbook produces studiable cards at all.

Should the deck gain new card DIRECTIONS at all — a listening card (front = the ~1,900 already-auditioned clips, which today are never the question) and/or picture-prompt cards for concrete nouns (the Image field is declared, rendered on the back, and populated on zero cards while 729 book images sit cached)? Both are genuine pedagogical upgrades and both roughly scale the daily load on an already ~4,300-card collection. A study-time budget call only the owner can make. Adding a direction needs WS6 item 1's template-add path routed through the model-diff guard; REMOVING a direction per-card is settled (suspend-at-delivery, unconditional only for newly-created notes).

How aggressively should the category taxonomy change? Adding 'Descriptions & Qualities' / 'Everyday Objects' absorbs most of the 222-card Other bucket, but existing cards keep their value until re-reviewed, so the deck spends a period with two conventions live. Related and unresolvable from the outside: does a Step-2 worked-example sentence take the category of the FORM it demonstrates (findable next to the particle card it serves) or of its content topic? Both are defensible; the prompt currently states neither, which is why 44 sentence cards sit in Grammar & Function Words.

Timing of the chapterLabel decoder fix relative to the existing book: as scheduled, WS2 ships it NEW-BOOKS-ONLY. The open call is whether to come back afterwards and run WS6's opt-in `--refile` once (with its --dry diff in front of you) to migrate the existing book's deck names, or freeze them permanently. Review made the migration safer but also made it something you choose deliberately rather than something a routine deliver does — so inertia now favours freezing. Nobody outside can weigh how much the current deck names bother you.

How much suspended clutter is acceptable in the live collection? Both WS4 item 6 (direction suppression) and WS6 item 3(d) (--suspend-orphans) express content decisions as suspended cards rather than absent ones. That is the only housekeeping-proof mechanism Anki offers short of a second note type, and it is one click to reverse — but suspended cards still appear in browse views and card counts. The pipeline now respects a human unsuspend permanently (a card that is unsuspended while still tagged dir-suspended is reported, never silently re-suspended), so the drift is one-way in your favour; the remaining question is purely aesthetic. If you would rather keep the collection visually clean, the alternative is a separate single-template note type for one-directional cards — a much larger change that splits the model the deliverer force-syncs.

NEW: are you willing to maintain a second Anki profile for behaviour probes (WS1 item 10)? The four deferred delivery decisions (template-add card regeneration, changeDeck on a filtered card, suspend on a filtered card, unsuspend-on-housekeeping) can only be answered by talking to a running Anki, and this plan now forbids doing that against your daily collection. That means: create a throwaway profile, install AnkiConnect in it, close your real profile while probing, switch back. If you would rather not, say so — the honest alternative is to leave WS6's --refile, WS4 item 6's opt-in half and WS6 item 1's template-add permanently unshipped rather than shipped on assumptions, and the plan should record them as deferred rather than pending.

explicitlyRejected.findingId: learner-3 (two proposed mechanisms — the finding's goal is in WS4 item 6)
explicitlyRejected.why: Both the template-conditional AND the build-side card omission are rejected and must not be built. (i) Gating an existing template's qfmt on a new field so the front renders empty does not skip a card in Anki — it creates an EMPTY card, and Tools → Empty Cards deletes it together with its interval and revlog: red-line-2 scheduling loss on 2,150 delivered notes from routine maintenance. (ii) 'Honour the flag at src/deck/collection.js:526' is rejected after verification: that loop is inside the .apkg SQLite writer, while the owner's decks are AnkiConnect-delivered via addNote (deliver.js:426-433) where ANKI generates one card per template, so it is inert on the primary path; and on the .apkg path a missing card row is regenerated by Check Database and by any template update, which WS4 item 5 performs. The goal survives as suspend-at-delivery, requiring `suspend` in ankiConnect.js (verified absent), and scoped per round-3 objection J.

explicitlyRejected.findingId: WS4 item 6 as previously specified — unconditional suspend-at-delivery on already-delivered notes
explicitlyRejected.why: Rejected in round 3 as a new live write path applied without consent to cards with real scheduling. The plan had already ruled (round-2 objection C) that a brand-new AnkiConnect write path affecting scheduling must be opt-in, --dry-previewed, filtered-deck-aware and test-gated; every clause applies to suspend, which is equally absent from ankiConnect.js. As written, a card studied for months with a mature interval would stop appearing tomorrow because of a flag in cards.json, on every routine deliver, with a human's manual unsuspend silently re-suspended on the next run. Retained as: unconditional ONLY for notes this deliver creates; opt-in + --dry for already-delivered notes; a `dir-suspended`-tagged-but-unsuspended card treated as a permanent human override; and the odid/filtered-deck behaviour added to WS1 item 10's probes as a prerequisite.

explicitlyRejected.findingId: WS1 item 9 as previously specified — AnkiConnect behaviour assertions with no named target collection
explicitlyRejected.why: Rejected in round 3. The item designated as the prerequisite unblocking five deferred decisions would itself have performed experimental schema-modifying writes, deck moves and filtered-deck manipulation against the owner's live 4,300-card collection: DEFAULT_ENDPOINT is pinned to 127.0.0.1:8765, AnkiConnect only talks to the running instance, and references/deliver.md never mentions a profile (grepped: zero hits for profile, 8765, localhost). Split into a headless .apkg verifier (throwaway collection via the pinned anki Python package — keeps assertions 1 and 2 and can land immediately) and WS1 item 10, live probes against a purpose-made second Anki profile with a hard refusal when the reachable collection contains a delivered deck. No item may cite 'the WS1 behaviour test' until item 10 exists in that form.

explicitlyRejected.findingId: WS6 item 3(c) as previously specified — fail-closed assertion keyed on delivered card ids in anki-delivered.json
explicitlyRejected.why: Rejected in round 3 as unimplementable on a false premise. I read both live markers: each contains exactly {note, ankiParent, lastDeliveredAt}; writeDeliveredMarker (deliver.js:172-190) writes only those three keys, and its catch is empty by deliberate design ('The marker is advisory; a failed write must not fail the deliver'). Retained only with the three additions that make it real: add the delivered key set to the marker, make that write fail-loud rather than inheriting the advisory swallow, and state the bootstrap rule (first deliver records the baseline, the gate arms from the second run) so it neither false-aborts nor sits permanently disarmed on the two already-delivered collections.

explicitlyRejected.findingId: promptengineer-4 (the 'lower toward Haiku' half only — the scope split is in WS8)
explicitlyRejected.why: Rejected as written, pending eval fixtures. There is no golden corpus or regression test for any pass, so a downgrade's quality cost is unmeasurable by construction — and two of the four named passes do not fail open in any sense that protects content: semanticDedup sets excluded:true (a silent drop indistinguishable at Gate 1 from a human decision, on a script whose sibling has a measured ~1-in-3 false-positive rate) and lesson-word categorization renders a visible chip on the card front. Forward flags and the pedagogical sort remain the legitimate candidates once the fixture exists — and note the fixture is now justified primarily as regression coverage for WS3's prompt rewrites, so if it is dropped the downgrades are permanently deferred, not merely waiting.

An already-delivered, abid-tagged note whose cards no longer sit in unit.ankiDeck would miss byAbid, miss the now-unit-scoped target index, and fall through to addNote({allowDuplicate:true}) with a fresh guid and fresh scheduling — while WS6's own re-file step becomes unimplementable. explicitlyRejected.findingId: codeexpert-3 (the 'block Mark done on mismatch' half — the hash and badge ship in WS5)
explicitlyRejected.why: Rejected as a landing-day behaviour. handleLessonDone (src/server/index.js:277-287) has no gate today, so this would be the first ever block on the owner's daily critical path — and unlike findUnreadableNumbers, which src/cards/readiness.js:61-65 argues is clearable in place with nothing to re-run, a hash mismatch had NO exit: the item forbade re-stamping and forbade regenerating, leaving 'destroy the hand trim' as the only escape on exactly the ~200 cards where a human already made a deliberate call. Ships badge-only plus a per-card human accept; promotion to a block stays available once the live badge count is measured.

explicitlyRejected.findingId: codeexpert-14 / adversarial-4 (the unconditional changeDeck re-file — the opt-in --refile is in WS6)
explicitlyRejected.why: Rejected as an unflagged mutation on every routine deliver. Verified: deliver.js never reads a note's deck today and ankiConnect.js exposes no changeDeck, so this is a brand-new live write path. Deck membership selects the options preset (the scheduling parameters WS6 item 4 is about), and Anki's `deck:` search matches a filtered card by its HOME deck while cardsInfo reports the FILTERED one — so a card in a custom-study session would read as 'deck differs' and be yanked out mid-session, with odid/odue behaviour under AnkiConnect uncharacterised. Reporting moves after the fact is not consent. Retained as opt-in, --dry-previewed, filtered-deck-skipping, and gated on WS1 item 10's probes.

explicitlyRejected.findingId: adversarial-15 (the 'key the destination on the archive path' mechanism — the collision detector and the mirrored layout are in WS2)
explicitlyRejected.why: Rejected in its flattening/hashing reading, and forbidden explicitly in the item text. src/corpus/epubArchive.js:637 writes join(destDir, src) precisely so the on-disk layout mirrors the relative relationship baked into the chapter HTML, because the extraction prompt tells the model to resolve each relative to the chapter file it just Read and open it directly (comment at :577-588). Any scheme that changes an image's path relative to its chapter file without rewriting the cached xhtml's src attributes breaks the model's Read INVISIBLY — extractReferencedImages logs only missing archive entries, isCachedChapterFile then treats the chapter as complete forever, and no test covers image reading because it happens only inside a paid pass. The collision is closed by a byte-compare detector now (WS2 item 3) and an archive-MIRRORING layout after the fixture suite (WS2 item 4, sized L).

blockingObjections.target: WS6 item 3(c) — the re-keyed fail-closed abid assertion (and the WS0 item 1 amendment that protects anki-delivered.json "which WS6's fail-closed assertion now keys on")
blockingObjections.argument: The round-2 fix re-keys the assertion to "the count of PREVIOUSLY-DELIVERED card ids recorded in anki-delivered.json". That data does not exist. I read both live markers: output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana/anki-delivered.json and output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/anki-delivered.json each contain exactly {note, ankiParent, lastDeliveredAt} — no card ids, no note ids, no counts. src/anki/deliver.js:172-186 writeDeliveredMarker writes only those three keys, and its catch block is empty with the comment "The marker is advisory; a failed write must not fail the deliver." So as specified the assertion cannot be implemented at all, and the WS0 amendment adds a file to the protected set on a false premise about its contents. Two consequences the plan does not account for: (a) the new field has no baseline for the two ALREADY-delivered collections, so the first run after landing has nothing to compare against — the same "red on landing day / tuned so loose it never fires" trap the round-2 fix existed to avoid, just moved; (b) a fail-closed gate on the single largest unbounded-damage path in the delivery layer would inherit a best-effort, error-swallowing writer, so one silently failed marker write leaves a stale or absent baseline that either false-aborts or disables the gate.
blockingObjections.requiredFix: Respecify the item to (1) ADD the delivered key set to the marker (e.g. deliveredCardIds or a count + hash, written by writeDeliveredMarker), (2) make that write fail-loud rather than inheriting the advisory catch, and (3) state the bootstrap rule explicitly: on a marker with no delivered-key field, the first deliver RECORDS the baseline and the assertion is inactive; it arms from the second run. Also correct the WS0 item 1 rationale, which currently justifies protecting the marker on the strength of contents it does not have.

blockingObjections.target: WS1 item 9 — scripts/verify-apkg-import.mjs and its four "first assertions"
blockingObjections.argument: The item conflates two harnesses with different risk profiles and specifies a safe collection for only one of them. The .apkg import half ("import a built .apkg into a throwaway collection") is genuinely headless via the pinned anki Python package. But assertions (3) and (4) are not: (3) is about what an AnkiConnect modelTemplateAdd/updateModelTemplates does to card rows, and (4) is about what AnkiConnect changeDeck does to a card with non-zero odid. AnkiConnect only talks to the running Anki instance — src/anki/ankiConnect.js pins DEFAULT_ENDPOINT to http://127.0.0.1:8765 — and on this machine the running instance is the collection the owner studies daily. Nothing in the item, in references/deliver.md (I grepped: zero mentions of profile, 8765 or localhost), or anywhere else in the plan says which Anki these probes run against. The obvious execution — run the script while Anki is open — performs experimental schema-modifying writes, deck moves and filtered-deck manipulation against 4,300 live cards. That is red line 2, introduced by the very item the plan designates as the prerequisite that unblocks five deferred decisions (media memoization, the dconf preset, the guid question, WS4 item 6's regeneration question, WS6's --refile).
blockingObjections.requiredFix: Split the item and name the target collection for each half. (a) Headless .apkg assertions via the anki Python package against a temp collection — automatable, keep as specified. (b) Live-Anki behaviour probes — state that they run against a SEPARATE Anki profile created for the purpose, with AnkiConnect installed in that profile, the owner's profile closed (only one instance can hold :8765), and a documented "switch back" step; add an explicit refusal in the script when the reachable collection contains any deck matching a delivered marker's ankiParent. Until (b) is specified this way, no item may cite "the WS1 behaviour test" as its safety prerequisite.

blockingObjections.target: WS4 item 6 — suspend-at-delivery, specifically its application to already-delivered abid-matched notes
blockingObjections.argument: The plan applied a strict standard to changeDeck in round-2 objection C — opt-in --refile, --dry preview of every move, skip filtered decks, and a behaviour test as a prerequisite — on the reasoning that it is a new live write path that alters scheduling and that "reporting a move after the fact is not consent." Every clause of that reasoning applies to suspend, and the plan does not apply them. As written, suspend runs on every routine deliver, for already-delivered notes as well as new ones, gated only by --dry being available. Three gaps follow. (i) A card the owner has been studying for months with a mature interval stops appearing tomorrow because of a flag in cards.json, with no opt-in and no preview requirement. (ii) The plan's own open question 7 concedes "a human can unsuspend one in Anki without the pipeline noticing, so cards.json and live state can drift" — but nothing stops the next deliver silently re-suspending exactly that card, which converts a one-click human decision into something the pipeline overrides on a schedule. (iii) The WS1 behaviour test gained a filtered-deck question for changeDeck and none for suspend, even though suspending a card sitting in a filtered deck / custom-study session is the same uncharacterised odid interaction the plan refuses to assume elsewhere. I confirmed suspend is absent from ankiConnect.js, so this is a genuinely new write path with no existing behaviour to lean on.
blockingObjections.requiredFix: Hold suspend to the standard the plan set for changeDeck: (1) apply it unconditionally only to notes created by THIS deliver (addNote path); (2) for already-delivered abid-matched notes make it opt-in behind an explicit flag with a --dry list of note/card ids, from-state and to-state; (3) add a rule that a card currently unsuspended and already carrying the dir-suspended tag is treated as a human override and reported, never silently re-suspended, unless a distinct flag is passed; (4) add "what does AnkiConnect suspend do to a card with non-zero odid" to the WS1 behaviour test alongside the changeDeck question, as a prerequisite for (2).

nonBlockingConcerns: WS0's protected set is explicitly JSON-only ("keeping audio/, images/, *.apkg, *.bak ignored"), yet WS5 item 2 says its re-trims "sit behind WS0's snapshot exactly like a deletion" and the deletions ruling extends WS0 to "content REGENERATIONS inside delivered units". For audio the gate is empty — WS0 protects nothing an audio regeneration could destroy. The practical risk is small (the 7 named clips each keep a sibling .orig.mp3 in the unit dir, which I confirmed), but this is a false safety claim of exactly the class WS1 item 5's own rationale calls worse than the missing mechanism. Either say plainly that audio recovery rests on .orig.mp3 and not on WS0, or pull the 7 clips plus their .orig into the snapshot. Related: WS0 item 3 deletes inside .anki-builder/audio (140 MB, 3,610 paid clips) while that tree stays unbacked by design.

The git option in WS0 item 1 is stated as "un-ignore exactly those globs", which does not work as written. .gitignore currently excludes the directory `/output`, and git will not descend into an excluded directory, so `!/output/**/cards.json` silently matches nothing. Making it work requires converting the entry to `/output/**` plus a `!/output/**/` directory re-include before any file re-include. A rule that appears to be applied and quietly is not, on the one item every other item depends on, is the plan's own signature failure mode. Name the exact mechanics in the open question, or the reader will pick the option that fails silently.

WS6 item 2(b) says "Record the delivered ankiParent in anki-delivered.json" — that half already ships (writeDeliveredMarker, deliver.js:172-186, and both live markers carry it). Only the abort-on-zero-notes half is new. Worth correcting so the item is not sized for work that exists.

WS2 item 3 is sized M but carries a byte-compare detector, the archive-mirroring chapters/ layout change, zip-slip containment and SVG re-scan. The layout half alone moves chapterCachePath, interacts with isCachedChapterFile and forces the WS2 item 4 CACHE_VERSION bump. Since the plan already sequences the two halves apart (detector now, layout after the fixtures), split them into two items and size the layout half L.

WS8 item 3 (per-pass eval fixtures, L) is justified entirely as a precondition for model downgrades the plan then explicitly rejects, for a saving it describes as cents. Its strongest actual use goes unclaimed: WS3 rewrites the extraction prompt's precedence, the dialogue rule and three content rules with no way to measure whether output improved. Re-justify it as regression coverage for WS3's prompt edits (which also fixes the ordering — fixtures would want to exist before WS3 lands, not after), or drop it and record the downgrades as permanently deferred.

WS4 item 6 keeps the .apkg writer emitting both card rows while the AnkiConnect path suspends one, so the .apkg — the restore artifact and the gate-2 freshness target — no longer reproduces the delivered deck. That is a deliberate, defensible choice, but it should be stated in the item, since WS6 item 1 is simultaneously correcting the collection.js:162-166 overclaim that the two paths cannot drift.

WS0 item 2 leaves a live decision inside the plan's second-most-blocking item: whether to gate the libraryHome redirect on NODE_TEST_CONTEXT only or on isTestEnv() (which I confirmed at src/util/testEnv.js:8 also returns true for NODE_ENV=test). Since a wrong answer makes a REAL run write its library to a tmpdir and appear to lose the dedup registry, decide it up front — NODE_TEST_CONTEXT only, with NODE_ENV coverage as a separate follow-up — rather than leaving it as an in-item caveat.

evaluationSummaries.summary: The project's deterministic-check layer (preflight.mjs, validate-decks.mjs, the three extras audits) is genuinely good and correctly aimed at the "catch it before the review gate" frontier — but it checks a per-collection, per-unit slice of the world and is blind to every invariant that spans collections, spans the on-disk library, or is only written down in prose. I found two live, reproducible instances of the project's signature failure mode. First, the test suite escapes its tmpdirs and writes into the owner's durable `.anki-builder/` library: the stray `epubs/h1` directory is `test/server/index.test.js`'s readiness fixture landing in the real dedup registry (mtime today), and `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/*.mp3` are 4-byte `CLIP` stubs from `test/cli/index.test.js` sitting in the real audio cache — the same code path, one missing `--voice`, poisons a real voice's cache with a permanent `.orig.mp3` that `clean-audio.mjs` would faithfully re-derive into a shipped card. Second, the two decks delivered into the live collection share 10 identical card ids and both ship bare (un-namespaced) guids, while a stray `japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana.apkg` physically sits inside the nihongo course directory — the AnkiConnect path is deck-scoped and safe, the `.apkg` drag-and-drop path is not, and nothing checks either. Beyond those, several load-bearing invariants are enforced only by skill-doc prose (extras units must carry no `epubHash`; the unit-dir regex; dedup-library completeness), the `scripts/*.mjs` `--apply` writers bypass the atomic-write/backup/validate discipline that all of `src/` uses while being allowed to mutate `done` units, and readiness markers remain a "the pass ran" claim with two of the live course's three shipped lessons carrying no markers at all. The highest-leverage fixes are all mechanizable and none of them touch the agentic core.

The pedagogical *design* here is genuinely strong — the four-field note model (scene/hint/note/reviewNote), the collision-cue asymmetry (only a `scene` renders before the answer on both faces), the "answer card must be answerable alone" rule, the backward-only cross-reference constraint, the number-run jumble, and the extras pass's minimal-pair particle drills are all real, correct language pedagogy, and the delivered JBP cards mostly read like a competent human wrote them. The weaknesses are all in *enforcement and generalization*, not in the rules. The single biggest defect is that `pronunciation` — a learner-facing field on 2,250 delivered cards — has no pinned orthographic style and no lint, so Hepburn conventions coin-flip per LLM batch: trailing periods are 100% in chapter-2/3/4-extras and 0% in chapters 6–13; `-san` is hyphenated 32/32 in chapter-7-extras and spaced 40/40 in chapter-8-extras; counter hyphenation, macron-vs-double-vowel, and `konbini`/`kombini` all drift the same way, and the three passes that touch romanization each carry a *different* version of the counter-hyphen rule (one of which the shipped code doesn't actually contain). Generalization beyond Japanese is weaker than the docs claim: the romanization-correction prompt hardcodes sokuon/kana failure modes for every language, and the Arabic and Hindi adapters empirically emit unusable output (`كتاب`→`ktab`, `कमल`→`kamala`, `सड़क`→`saḍa़ka`) while the prompt frames that output as a trustworthy starting point. On audio, the pipeline knowingly has a better Japanese path (kanji-orthography TTS) and leaves it behind a manual per-card button. None of this touches scheduling or deck integrity, so nothing is critical under the owner's red lines — but the romanization and ar/hi findings degrade every card silently, which is this project's documented recurring failure signature.

Architecturally this is a healthy, unusually disciplined codebase: the src/ layering is clean, the CLI layer is well tested (test/cli/index.test.js is 2436 lines, contrary to the briefing), the two runClaude modules are a deliberate core+scoped-wrapper pair rather than duplication, and load-bearing invariants (unitDeckSegments as the single deck-path authority, rebuildBookDir's no-yield property, atomic writes) are documented at their definition sites. The code-vs-judgment boundary is mostly drawn well, and the last two weeks of commits show the right instinct — mechanizing prose rules into preflight. But the boundary is drawn inconsistently in two directions: preflight explicitly refuses to auto-apply a duplicate judgment while extras-duplicate-check.mjs --apply does exactly that (and a read-only probe shows ~a third of this book's 17 "duplicate" groups are genuinely distinct cards LIMITATIONS.md itself names), and the two checks SKILL.md most insists on — the vocabulary diff and the paradigm audit — tell the agent to "write a script" that has never been written, so a throwaway is re-derived every chapter. The single sharpest defect I found is not a design one: `npm test` writes into the live `.anki-builder/` library home (`.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json`, mtime today), because the test guard covers the LLM spawn but not filesystem writes to state that decides which cards get built. Process-wise the harness backlog is dead (last loop outcome 2026-07-13) while LIMITATIONS.md is the real planning artifact with 83 commits — the honest move is to retire TASKS.json rather than keep a stale T011 pointing at the one path with zero worked examples.

I read the EPUB parser, lesson resolution, assemble/prepare/translate, the audio staleness chain, the .apkg builders and the AnkiConnect deliverer, and probed the live outputs and a synthetic EPUB read-only. The code is unusually well-reasoned per-function — most comments are honest and the invariants (media-key integers, no-await rebuild, guid namespacing, shippableCards) are real and enforced. The defects that remain are almost all of the repo's own stated failure signature: SILENT DEGRADATION at seams between modules, where each side is individually correct. Two are live-collection-adjacent and confirmed on disk: `npm test` writes into the real `.anki-builder` dedup library (I found the artifact, written today, from a fixture that forgot to inject `saveChapterCorpus`), and post-`done` dashboard edits never rebuild the `.apkg` despite two comments asserting they do. Two more are hard "next book" cliffs I confirmed empirically with a synthetic EPUB: a nav document that isn't strictly spine-monotonic yields inverted lesson ranges (`5-2`) that silently truncate extraction and poison the forward-flag pass, and numeric HTML entities survive undecoded into Anki deck names. The audio staleness hole is real and not closed: a card the reviewer hand-trimmed or hand-picked is exempt from the text-changed check forever.

The engine is in better shape than its operating manual. README.md and (mostly) docs/PIPELINE.md were updated when features changed; SKILL.md — the only file the agent actually executes — was not, and it now documents two removed features as live: a **Reopen** button (deleted in commit 289f64b, recorded in LIMITATIONS.md:1360) and `deck.apkg` filenames (renamed by src/deck/deckFileName.js). Both drifts land squarely on the owner's red line #2: the documented recovery path for a mis-clicked **Mark done** on a delivered, daily-studied unit is literally impossible, so an agent following SKILL.md will improvise a hand edit of `meta.done`.
