The second theme is that the recent "catch it before the gate" frontier is real and good but only half-wired: `npm run preflight` silently skips `output/templates/` entirely while printing "preflight clean", its report-only lines have never been zero (7 marker-audible clips and 17 duplicate-target groups sit in the shipped deck), and nothing in `scripts/` has a single test. Third, the test suite writes into the live `.anki-builder/epubs/` library (`h1/corpora/2.json`, mtime today) — benign by luck of the fixture hash, one collision away from corrupting the dedup library the daily deck reads. If I could fix only five: (1) the Reopen/`deck.apkg` drift in SKILL.md, (2) sandbox the epub-library writes in tests, (3) an `-extras` guard in `markCardsReviewed`, (4) preflight covering templates + failing on marker-stuck, (5) turn the 40-line prose review watcher into `scripts/await-review.mjs`. All five are mechanizations at the edges; none touches the agentic core.

The card model is unusually well-reasoned for a hand-rolled deck: the scene/hint asymmetry (scene on both fronts, hint on the Production front only) is exactly right, the collision doctrine in card-authoring-rules.md is better than most published SRS advice, and it holds up empirically — across 1,914 live JBP cards I found zero English-collision members and zero target-collision members lacking a cue. The weak points are not content, they are (a) the boundaries the audits cannot see, (b) the fixed 2-cards-per-note model, and (c) the rendered card face, which no surface in the pipeline ever shows the reviewer. The single worst daily-study defect is cross-DECK collisions: the JBP book and the nihongo-101 course sit in one Anki collection and share 47 identical targets with differing glosses plus 10 uncued ambiguous English prompts ("Nice to meet you." → はじめまして vs よろしくおねがいします; "Yes" → ええ vs はい), and both preflight.mjs and extras-collision-audit.mjs are structurally per-book so neither can ever see them. Second worst is scheduling ergonomics: the two directions of a note get consecutive due positions and the shipped deck config sets new.bury/rev.bury false, so Recognition and Production of the same note land back-to-back and the second is answered from working memory. Third, every note unconditionally emits both directions with no per-card opt-out, which is what makes the leaky-scene tension on particle/counter cards cost real daily reps — and the deliverer has no path to add a template, so any card-design change that adds or removes a direction cannot reach the live collection at all.

The prompt corpus is unusually good — incident-grounded, specific, and mostly self-consistent — but it has accumulated three classes of defect that the pinning strategy amplifies. First, cross-prompt conflicts: the cached BOOK_CONVENTIONS text (generated by a prompt whose framing predates the extraction prompt's current EXERCISES policy) countermands the extraction rules with no precedence statement, and I verified a concrete content loss from it (chapter 32's あります/います paradigm image produced zero cards despite matching the extraction prompt's own worked example of "reference material, extract in full"). Second, the Step-1 dialogue ban and the Step-2 "every function word needs a worked example" requirement are mutually unsatisfiable, and the reviewed corpus shows the model breaking the ban to satisfy Step 2 — while the extras pass re-mines the same dialogue anyway. Third, model pinning offers exactly two env scopes (TRANSLATE, EPUB_LLM), each bundling passes of wildly different difficulty and blast radius: chapter extraction — the one pass whose misses are structurally invisible, as SKILL.md itself says — shares a knob with the pedagogical sort, which is mechanically validated and fails open. I ran the extraction prompt myself against chapter 32 and diffed against the reviewed corpus; agreement was high (all vocabulary blocks, sub-rows, placeholder resolution, key sentences, correct skipping of substitution alternatives), but I am a much stronger model than deployed Sonnet-medium, so every "the model recovered by inference" case below should be read as an upper bound on deployed fidelity. SKILL.md is a strong orchestrator prompt whose main flaws are a factually wrong claim about image handling (repeated in extras-pass.md), a Step-3b timing contradiction, and a prescribed "script" that does not exist.

I probed both books directly. On the proven book (JBP) the nav path works exactly as documented — 56 nav entries, correct ranges, `source: "nav"`. On the hostile book (Black Library "Betrayer", libgen, EPUB2/NCX) nothing throws, which is the problem: it degrades silently on every axis at once. 35 nav entries resolve, ZERO classify as `lesson` (32/35 are `other`), spine file 1 is unreachable by `--lesson` at all because nav starts at spine 2, three separate entries silently swallow spine files the nav never named, and `describeChapter(1)` returns the same string "Cover" as nav entry [1] — a deck-name collision. A user following SKILL.md Step 1 literally ("offer the `lesson`-typed entries as options") would be offered nothing. The deeper pattern: the EPUB layer's error handling is excellent for the two LOUD failures it has tests for (ZIP64, zip-level encryption) and absent for every silent one — regex fragility in the NCX/nav scanners drops entries with no log, unnamed spine files get absorbed into neighbouring lessons with no log, duplicate-href nav entries collapse with no log, and label defects (undecoded numeric entities, ruby mangling, `<span>` concatenation) flow uninspected into `corpus.meta.chapterLabel` → `unitDeckSegments` → the live Anki deck name. Almost all of this can be made loud without touching the agentic core: the fixes are logs, warnings and a shape report at `--list-lessons` time, not gates.

allFindings.title: The test suite writes into the production .anki-builder/ library — the stray `h1` dir and 4-byte `CLIP` mp3s prove it
allFindings.evidence: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json` (mtime 14 Aug 12:10 — today) contains `{epubHash:"h1", chapterNumber:2, chapterLabel:"Uch", enriched:true, notesEnhanced:true, reviewed:true}`, byte-for-byte the fixture in test/server/index.test.js:1234-1254 (`unpreparedFixture`) as consumed by the test "a prepared lesson passes the gate and signs off normally" (test/server/index.test.js:1318). That test passes `editDeps` (test/server/index.test.js:60-68), which stubs `getDefaultVoice`/`fetchTts`/`trim` but NOT `saveChapterCorpus`, so src/server/index.js:268 → src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:123 calls the real `saveChapterCorpus`, which resolves `libraryHome()` = `resolve(REPO_ROOT/.anki-builder)` (src/model/index.js:365-367). Independently: `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/{6dde65c7439b036b,6ce47560ba160669}{,.orig}.mp3` are each 4 bytes containing the literal string `CLIP`, written by test/cli/index.test.js:2242/2278/2420 (`audio --run <tmpdir> --voice v1`) because src/cli/commands/audio.js:114 passes `ctx.libraryHome()` and no test injects it. Only test/corpus/epubLibrary.test.js threads `libraryHomeDir` (test/corpus/epubLibrary.test.js:22-27); every server and CLI test does not. Escalation path is concrete: `getDefaultVoice` returns REAL voice ids (src/audio/voiceLibrary.js:6-7 → `3JDquces8E8bkmvbh6Bc`), and the cache key is (voice, model, textHash) with no provenance, so one test that omits `--voice` on a `ja` lesson writes stub bytes into the live cache; a later real `audio` run gets a cache HIT and ships it. The `.orig.mp3` is poisoned too, so `scripts/clean-audio.mjs --apply --force` (the documented repair, LIMITATIONS.md:420-425) would faithfully re-derive garbage. The mirror path is worse: src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:153 `removeChapterCorpus(epubHash, chapterNumber)` DELETES a real chapter's dedup entry. I verified the real voice caches are currently clean (smallest real clip 3,846 bytes), so this has not fired yet.
allFindings.recommendation: Mechanize, exactly mirroring the precedent this repo already invented for money-spending calls. src/util/testEnv.js:19 `assertExternalCallAllowed` exists because 'forgetting to inject a stub is silent' — the same argument applies verbatim to durable-state writes. Make `libraryHome()` (src/model/index.js:365) throw under `isTestEnv()` unless `ANKI_BUILDER_ALLOW_REAL_LIBRARY_IN_TESTS=1`, or better, return a per-process tmpdir so existing tests keep passing while their writes go nowhere real. Add the same guard inside `saveChapterCorpus`/`removeChapterCorpus`/`registerEpub` for defence in depth. Then delete `.anki-builder/epubs/h1` and `.anki-builder/audio/v1` by hand. Fully deterministic; zero impact on the agentic core.

allFindings.title: Ten real card-id collisions between the two live decks, both shipping bare guids, with a foreign .apkg sitting in one of their directories
allFindings.evidence: Probe over the two delivered collections: 10 ids appear in BOTH `output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana` and `output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5` as non-excluded, done cards — `pen`, `file` (chapter-2 | lesson-2); `beef`, `beer`, `small`, `white`, `black`, `restroom`, `camera` (chapter-5 | lesson-3); `scarf` (chapter-14 | lesson-3). `output/epubs/.../book.json` has `"guidNamespace": null` and `output/courses/.../course.json` has no `guidNamespace` field at all, so `readGuidNamespace` (src/deck/rebuild.js:149-165) returns null for both — both packages ship BARE ids as Anki note guids, and Anki matches guids COLLECTION-wide on import. Both dirs carry `anki-delivered.json`, i.e. both are in the owner's live collection. LIMITATIONS.md:1343-1358 predicted this exact hazard and set the trigger as 'before importing a second book's .apkg, check for id overlaps' — the condition is now TRUE and nothing checks it. Compounding it: `output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana.apkg` (11 MB, 28 Jul) sits inside the course directory next to the legitimate `nihongo-101-course-n5.apkg` — a foreign package one drag-and-drop away from overwriting 10 live notes and their scheduling. The AnkiConnect path is safe (src/anki/deliver.js:350 scopes findNotes by `deck:"${ankiParent}"`), so this is purely an .apkg-import hazard — but the .apkg is what a human reaches for when AnkiConnect isn't running.
allFindings.recommendation: Two cheap preflight checks. (1) In `--all` mode, after the per-collection `assertUniqueCardIds`, cross-check ids across every collection whose marker resolves `guidNamespace` to null, and FAIL naming the pairs — this is ~15 lines reusing the existing `seen` map shape from src/deck/shippableCards.js:33. (2) Assert the only `*.apkg` in a collection dir is `deckFileNameForDir(dir)` (or the `LEGACY_DECK_FILENAME` fallback, src/deck/deckFileName.js:18/46) and fail on any other — that catches the stray JBP package and any future mis-copy. Separately, add to the deliver/import runbook that a bare-guid deck must never be .apkg-imported into a collection holding another bare-guid deck.

allFindings.title: Every audit script silently skips a unit directory whose name doesn't match its own copy of the unit-dir regex
allFindings.evidence: The same pattern `/^(chapter|lesson)-(\d+)(-extras)?$/` is re-typed independently in scripts/preflight.mjs:46, scripts/extras-collision-audit.mjs:27, scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs:31, and a fourth variant `UNIT_DIR_PATTERN` lives in src/deck/deckFileName.js:24 with a comment ('Keep this in step with the same pattern in src/deck/rebuild.js and src/server/adapters/stage.js') that admits at least three more copies. A directory that fails the match is not reported — it is filtered out and the run prints a clean bill of health for the units that remain. `preflight` prints `✓ schema 29 unit(s) valid` and never prints how many unit-shaped directories it saw, so a typo'd, zero-padded, or copied dir (`chapter-15 copy`, `lesson-01`) drops out of duplicate-id, collision, spacing and audio checks with no output difference at all. This is the project's exact signature: an absent check reads identically to a passing one. scripts/validate-decks.mjs walks recursively (validate-decks.mjs:33-40) and would still schema-check such a dir, which means the two tools disagree about what a unit is with no reconciliation.
allFindings.recommendation: Export one `UNIT_DIR_PATTERN` / `listUnitDirs(dir)` from src/model (or src/deck/deckFileName.js, which already owns a copy) and have all four scripts plus rebuild.js and adapters/stage.js import it. Then make preflight FAIL on any directory that contains a `cards.json` or `corpus.json` but does not match — 'a unit-shaped folder this tool cannot see' is a strictly more useful error than silence. Purely mechanical.

allFindings.title: 'Extras units carry no epubHash' is a prose-only invariant guarding the dedup library from being overwritten by its own extras unit
allFindings.evidence: extras-pass.md:64 mandates that an extras unit carry `chapterNumber` identical to its base lesson, and extras-pass.md:71 mandates '**NO `epubHash`.** The dedup library is keyed by `(epubHash, chapterNumber)`'. src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:107-124 acts on exactly that pair with no other discriminator: `if (epubHash && chapterNumber != null) saveChapterCorpus(epubHash, chapterNumber, {...})`. The only enforcement is a comment at applyCards.js:131-134 ('An extras unit carries no epubHash, so its unreview can never touch its base lesson's library entry'). I verified the collision is real in live data: `output/epubs/.../chapter-13/cards.json` and `chapter-13-extras/cards.json` BOTH have `chapterNumber: 33`, and the extras unit is the one that happens to lack `epubHash`. If an extras unit ever acquires an `epubHash` — a hand-edit, a copy-paste of the base meta (which extras-pass.md:75-80 already warns agents do reflexively for `corpus.meta`), or a future assemble path — then clicking Mark reviewed on the extras unit overwrites the BASE chapter's dedup-library entry with the extras' item list. Backward dedup for every later chapter then silently mines the wrong vocabulary, with no error and nothing in preflight to notice. That is precisely the shape of the documented '3 lessons missing from the dedup library cost 12 unflagged repeats' incident.
allFindings.recommendation: Two assertions in preflight, both trivial: (a) no two units in a collection share a `(meta.epubHash, meta.chapterNumber)` pair when `epubHash` is set; (b) any unit whose directory ends in `-extras` must have no `meta.epubHash`. Optionally also refuse in `markCardsReviewed` itself (src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:107) when the runDir basename ends `-extras` — that turns the prose rule into a server-side gate that no hand-edit can route around.

allFindings.title: Nothing verifies the dedup library actually covers every reviewed chapter — the exact historical failure has no detector
allFindings.evidence: `.anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/corpora/` holds 15 files (11,14,15,17,18,19,22,23,25,26,29,30,32,33,34) and I confirmed those match the 15 base chapters' `meta.chapterNumber` exactly — so the library is complete TODAY. But that completeness is an accident of history, not an invariant anyone checks: entries are written only as a side effect of clicking Mark reviewed (src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:107-124) and are DELETED by Mark-unreviewed (src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:150-154), which is reachable for any not-yet-done unit. A reviewer who un-reviews to fix a card and then completes the chapter by any route that doesn't re-click Mark reviewed leaves a permanent hole; `loadPriorChapterItems` (src/corpus/epubLibrary.js:147) simply reads whatever directory entries exist and reports nothing about the ones missing. The observable symptom is repeats that reach the learner — the documented incident cost 12 unflagged repeats — and it is invisible to preflight, to validate-decks, and to both review gates.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a preflight check for EPUB collections: for every unit with `meta.epubHash` and `meta.reviewed === true`, assert `.anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/corpora/<chapterNumber>.json` exists, and report any that don't with the runDir to re-mark. Report the reverse too (a corpora entry with no reviewed unit behind it — that would have surfaced the `h1` leak in qa-1 immediately). Deterministic, ~20 lines, and it converts the project's most expensive past incident into a pre-gate line of output.

allFindings.title: The --apply scripts bypass the atomic-write/backup/validate discipline that all of src/ uses, and --force lets them mutate a done unit that is already in the live collection
allFindings.evidence: scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs:90 writes with bare `writeFileSync(unit.path, JSON.stringify(unit.data, null, 2))`; scripts/extras-order.mjs:69 and :78 do the same for cards.json and corpus.json. Nothing in `scripts/` imports `writeFileAtomic`/`backupFileOnce` from src/util/atomicWrite.js, which every writer in src/ uses (src/cli/commands/shared.js:12-14, src/cards/crossLessonNotes.js:26), and neither script runs `validateCards` after mutating. Both accept `--force` to override their reviewed/done guard (extras-duplicate-check.mjs:64-69, extras-order.mjs:35-42) — and a `done` unit is by definition in the shipping `.apkg` and delivered to the collection the owner studies daily. Excluding a card in a done unit under `--force` removes it from the package while src/anki/deliver.js never deletes, leaving a permanent 'orphaned in Anki (kept)' note the learner keeps studying against text that no longer exists on disk. There are zero tests for anything under `scripts/` (`grep -rln "scripts/" test/` returns nothing), despite scripts/extras-order.mjs having already shipped and needed a fix for an argument-parsing bug that made its documented default form unusable (commit 82e77b9, 14 Aug).
allFindings.recommendation: Route every `--apply` write through `writeFileAtomic` + `backupFileOnce` + the matching `validateCards`/`validateCorpus`, so a crash or a bad edit is recoverable and schema-checked the same way the pipeline's writes are. Add a small `test/scripts/` suite driving each `--apply` script over a tmpdir fixture (the fixture builders in test/support/ and the epub fixture pattern already show the shape) — these are pure file-in/file-out programs, the cheapest possible tests. Consider making `--force` on a `done` unit require a second explicit flag, given the live-collection consequence.

allFindings.title: Readiness markers assert 'the pass ran', cover only 2 of the 5+ pre-review passes, and two of the three shipped course lessons carry none at all
allFindings.evidence: src/cards/readiness.js:22-31 defines `REQUIRED_PASSES` as exactly `enriched` and `notesEnhanced`. The number-readings pass, the audio stage and the whole extras pass sit outside the gate. The markers are set on completion regardless of output — src/cli/commands/prepare.js:189-196 documents this deliberately ('Marked even when nothing was mined'), which is defensible, but it means a chapter whose drill mining returned zero cards is indistinguishable at the gate from one that produced a full block. More telling, readiness.js:50 short-circuits on `meta.reviewed === true || meta.sourceType === 'template'`, and live data shows what that carve-out permits: `output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/lesson-0` (`{sourceType:"manual", reviewed:true, done:true}`) and `lesson-2` (same) have NO `enriched` and NO `notesEnhanced` markers at all, yet are reviewed, done, and delivered — only `lesson-3` carries them. Those two lessons were signed off before the gate existed and are now permanently exempt from it, and no tool anywhere reports that. `prepareDegraded` (prepare.js:17-26, readiness.js:73-75) is the one breadcrumb that survives, and it surfaces only in the dashboard banner, never in preflight.
allFindings.recommendation: Keep both carve-outs (removing them would retroactively unreview signed-off work — correct as written). Instead make the exemption VISIBLE: have preflight print, per collection, any unit that is `done` but lacks the full marker set, and any unit carrying `meta.prepareDegraded`. That is a report line, not a failure, and it turns 'this lesson was never gated' from an unknowable into one line of output before the next review link is handed over.

allFindings.title: The gate-2 'watch the artifact, not the checkbox' guard is copy-paste shell prose that recomputes a filename the codebase already owns
allFindings.evidence: SKILL.md:99-118 documents the hardest-won lesson in the project — 'Mark done does two things... a watcher polling only meta.done reports success on the first even when the second FAILED' — and then ships it as a shell fragment the agent must fill in by hand: `APKG=<bookDir>/<book-slug>.apkg` followed by `[ "$APKG" -nt "$RUN/cards.json" ]`. The book slug is exactly what src/deck/deckFileName.js:46 `deckFileNameForDir` and :63 `resolveDeckPathForDir` exist to compute — deckFileName.js:11-16 explicitly argues that writer and reader must derive the name independently from the PATH so they cannot disagree, and this watcher is a reader that derives it from a hand-typed guess instead. If the agent types the slug wrong the `-nt` test is false against a nonexistent file, which reports 'rebuild FAILED' — a false alarm, so the failure mode here is noise rather than silence. But the same fragment is retyped per unit, twice per chapter, across a 15-chapter book.
allFindings.recommendation: Ship `scripts/check-done.mjs <runDir>` that imports `resolveDeckPathForDir`, reads `meta.done`, compares mtimes, and exits 0/1/3 with the same messages. SKILL.md's snippet then becomes one line, the slug derivation is shared with the builder, and the check becomes unit-testable. This is a pure mechanization of an already-mechanical step — the judgment (whether to proceed) stays with the agent.

allFindings.title: clientScripts.js is the sole surface for the rebuild-failure signal and has zero tests
allFindings.evidence: src/server/index.js:283-288 threads `rebuildError` back on the Mark-done response with a comment naming the incident it prevents ('reporting success while the shipping .apkg stayed stale is exactly the divergence the auto-rebuild exists to prevent'), and src/server/index.js:421-431 `rebuildGroupQuiet` carefully distinguishes benign from real failures. The ONLY consumer is src/review/clientScripts.js:561-564, which appends ' — but deck rebuild FAILED: ' to the status text. That file is 659 lines of inline browser JS with no test file anywhere under test/ (test/review/ contains only deckViewChrome.test.js and renderDeckViewPage.test.js). SKILL.md:99-104 explicitly builds the gate-2 procedure on top of that string being rendered. A refactor that drops or renames that branch silently reverts the dashboard to reporting a green Mark done over a stale shipping package — and `npm test` would stay green. The benign-error regex at src/server/index.js:429 (`/no finished lessons|no chapter-\*\/|directories found/`) is also broad enough that an unrelated message containing 'directories found' would be swallowed as benign, and nothing pins it.
allFindings.recommendation: Two cheap tests: (a) a server test asserting the Mark-done JSON response carries a non-null `rebuildError` when `adapter.rebuild` throws a non-benign error, and null for each benign message (this also pins the regex); (b) a string-level assertion over the rendered page source that the `rebuildError` branch and its ' — but deck rebuild FAILED' text are present, in the same style test/review/deckViewChrome.test.js already uses for markup. Neither needs a DOM.

allFindings.title: Two overlapping blind spots meet in the template path: no real-Anki-import test, no worked template example, and templates are exempt from the readiness gate
allFindings.evidence: LIMITATIONS.md:423-447 records three .apkg format bugs (media manifest keys, `col.crt` units, `csum` range) that 'all passed npm test and every synthetic check, because nothing in the test suite actually ran a real Anki import', and states plainly 'There is still no automated test that runs a real Anki import'. Independently, `output/templates/` contains nothing but a `.DS_Store` — the bundled-template path has zero worked examples on disk — while src/cards/readiness.js:50 exempts `sourceType === 'template'` from the readiness gate entirely and src/cli/commands/prepare.js:96-99 skips both enrichment passes for it. So the one source type with no gate is also the one with no exercised example. The only open backlog item, T011 'End-to-end: build a real travel deck + verify in Anki', targets exactly this intersection, which is the right instinct.
allFindings.recommendation: Scope T011 to close both at once: build one real template deck end to end (which populates `output/templates/` with the first worked example the skill can point at), and land the result as a checked-in `scripts/verify-apkg-import.mjs` that shells out to a pinned `anki` Python package to import a built `.apkg` and assert the note count. Keep it OUT of `npm run ci` (output/ is gitignored, and LIMITATIONS.md already reasons through why) — make it a documented Definition-of-Done step for a first-ever build of any new source type. That is the only check that would have caught the media-key class of bug.

allFindings.title: The nihongo course's lesson-1 gap is a stale unit folded in from an abandoned course, and nothing checks a unit's own meta against the directory holding it
allFindings.evidence: `output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/` holds lesson-0, lesson-2, lesson-3 — no lesson-1. lesson-0's meta is `{sourceType:"manual", chapterNumber:1, chapterLabel:"Lesson 1", courseSlug:"intensive-japanese-1", reviewed:true, done:true}` — a courseSlug naming a DIFFERENT course from the containing dir (`nihongo-101-course-n5`), while lesson-2 and lesson-3 both correctly carry `courseSlug:"nihongo-101-course-n5"`. So lesson-0 is a survivor of a renamed or abandoned course, carried into this one, and the directory index (0) no longer tracks `chapterNumber` (1) the way it does for lesson-2 and lesson-3. Functionally the passes are fine — `lessonSiblings` orders by `meta.chapterNumber ?? 0` (src/cards/crossLessonNotes.js:72, :80), not by folder name — but every human-facing surface (folder listing, dashboard ordering, the SKILL's 'which lesson comes next' question) reads a gap that means nothing, and lesson-0 also carries the stale `.pre-*.bak` set from a different course's pipeline. Nothing anywhere validates that `meta.courseSlug` / `meta.epubHash` agrees with the containing collection's marker file, nor that unit numbering is contiguous. Combined with qa-2 (the foreign .apkg in the same directory), this dir is accumulating cross-course debris unnoticed.
allFindings.recommendation: Add two preflight report lines (notes, not failures — a legitimate gap can exist): (a) any unit whose `meta.courseSlug` disagrees with the dir's `course.json`, or whose `meta.epubHash` disagrees with the dir's `book.json`; (b) a gap or duplicate in the units' `chapterNumber` sequence, and any unit whose folder index disagrees with its `chapterNumber`. Both are pure reads of data preflight already loads in `loadUnits`.

allFindings.title: corpus.json and cards.json can drift apart and no tool compares them — one live chapter already has
allFindings.evidence: Probe across both collections: `output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana/chapter-6` has 1 item id present in corpus.json but absent from cards.json (the reverse direction, 12 ids only in cards.json, is expected — those are mined drills). scripts/validate-decks.mjs validates each file against its own schema independently (validate-decks.mjs:15-18, :43-52) and scripts/preflight.mjs:82-98 does the same; neither ever compares the two files' item sets or ordering. scripts/extras-order.mjs:64-77 goes out of its way to keep both in the same order ('corpus.json must follow, or the reviews and the deck disagree on order'), but scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs:88-92 writes cards.json ONLY, so an `--apply` there guarantees drift by construction. corpus.json is what the corpus-review artifact renders, so drift means a reviewer signs off against a slightly different set than the one that ships.
allFindings.recommendation: One preflight note per unit: ids present in corpus.json but not in cards.json, and (where both exist) a relative-order mismatch over the shared ids. Report-only — a legitimate drop can happen — but it makes the divergence visible instead of latent. Separately, have extras-duplicate-check.mjs mirror its exclusions into corpus.json the way extras-order.mjs already mirrors ordering.

allFindings.title: The money/time guard covers `claude -p` but not ElevenLabs, and a stale comment misstates which model runs the only categorization pass for --words courses
allFindings.evidence: src/util/testEnv.js:19 `assertExternalCallAllowed` is called in exactly two places, both in src/util/runClaude.js (lines 40 and 97). src/audio/elevenLabsTts.js:45 `fetchElevenLabsTts` has no equivalent guard — it is injectable everywhere and `generateAudio` throws without an explicit `fetchTts` (src/audio/index.js:216, :224-226), so the current exposure is small, but the asymmetry means the one API that bills per character is the one without the 'the refusal lives in the code rather than in the discipline of whoever writes the next test' protection the repo argues for. Separately, src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js:83 documents `assembleCorpusFromLessonWords` as categorizing 'via a small batched Haiku pass', and LIMITATIONS.md:495-517 repeats the claim across four lines — but src/util/runClaude.js:7-8 pins `claude-sonnet-5` / effort `medium` for EVERY call, with no Haiku override anywhere. So the documented cost/quality profile of the ONLY categorization pass on the `--words` course path is wrong in both the code comment and the institutional-memory doc.
allFindings.recommendation: Add `assertExternalCallAllowed('call ElevenLabs')` at the top of `fetchElevenLabsTts` — it costs nothing and closes the symmetric hole before a future test forgets to inject. Fix the lessonCorpus.js:83 comment and the LIMITATIONS.md:495 entry to say Sonnet-medium (or, if Haiku really is wanted there for cost, wire a scoped `ANKI_BUILDER_LESSONWORDS_*` prefix — `runClaudeWithPrompt` already supports scoped prefixes at runClaude.js:43-53 — and make the comment true again).

allFindings.title: Romanization style is unpinned and coin-flips per unit across the whole delivered deck
allFindings.evidence: Probe over all 2,250 cards in output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana + output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5. Per-unit drift (trailing ASCII period in `pronunciation` / `-san` hyphenated / `-san` spaced): chapter-2-extras 58 of 60 dotted, chapter-3-extras 57/59, chapter-4-extras 56/56, vs chapters 6–13 all 0. `-san`: chapter-7-extras 32 hyphenated / 1 spaced; chapter-8-extras 0 hyphenated / 40 spaced; chapter-9 2/16; chapter-9-extras 29/0. Long vowels: `yūmei` (ch-10) vs `yuubinkyoku` (ch-12-extras), `kyoukai`/`biichi` (ch-12) vs `kōen`/`chīzukēki` elsewhere; `iie` (ch-10) vs `īe` (ch-4-extras). Also `kombini` (ch-12) vs `konbini` (ch-12-extras, 6x), one `wo` for を against 227 `o`, and mid-string capitals (`iie, chotto tōi desu. Basu de …`, `Tōkyōshisha`). Cause: src/translate/romanizationEval.js:29 makes the model "the final authority" with only 4 style bullets, and normalizeRomaji (romanizationEval.js:105) only fixes spaces; extras units are hand-authored and skip the pass entirely. src/model/index.js:132 does not constrain the field.
allFindings.recommendation: Pin ONE Hepburn style spec (macrons; ii/ei exceptions; n-before-b/p as `n`; を as `o`; no terminal ASCII punctuation; proper-noun casing; `-san` attachment) as a single exported constant in src/translate/languageRules.js and inject it into romanizationEval's §3 prompt, the number-reading prompt, the FIB prompt, and references/card-authoring-rules.md so hand-authored extras inherit it. Then MECHANIZE the check: add a preflight.mjs romaji lint (terminal [.?!], `[a-z] san`, `ou|uu|oo` outside a whitelist, digits in `pronunciation`, capitals after position 0 not on a known proper-noun list) as a WARN, not a hard fail — the judgment about a genuine exception stays with the agent/reviewer.

allFindings.title: The romanization-correction prompt hardcodes Japanese failure modes for every configured language
allFindings.evidence: src/translate/romanizationEval.js:20-89 is the ONLY correction prompt and runs for every language in src/translate/romanizationLibraries.js (ja, zh, ko, ru, he, hi, ar). Its Overview (lines 26-28) tells the model the library "mishandles the Japanese small っ (sokuon)" and "falls back to spelling out unfamiliar kana letter-by-letter"; its Example Input/Output (lines 42-54, 75-82) are ろっかい/こんにちは; its `Important` bullet (line 68-69) is a sokuon rule. A Hindi or Arabic run is therefore shown two Japanese exemplars and told about kana. This is exactly the leak src/translate/languageRules.js:1-6 says the plug-in layer exists to prevent ("never Japanese prose leaking into a Spanish run").
allFindings.recommendation: Move the failure-mode paragraph, the Important bullets, and the Example Input/Output pair into per-language entries in languageRules.js (e.g. `romanizationCorrectionRules`, `romanizationExamples`) and have buildRomanizationPrompt inject them, with a neutral fallback when a language has none. Per language the real failure modes differ and must be stated: pinyin tone-sandhi and polyphone choice for zh; Revised-Romanization assimilation for ko; vowel supply for ar/he; schwa deletion for hi.

allFindings.title: Three different counter-hyphenation conventions coexist; the docs describe a rule the code does not contain
allFindings.evidence: src/translate/languageRules.js:12-16 defines JA_COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE (`jūni-nichi`, `go-ji`, `nijūgo-nen`, `ip-pon`) and injects it into the number-reading pass and the FIB pass. docs/translate-prompts.md:370-375 documents a matching paragraph plus the example `{"id":"sixth-floor","pronunciation":"rok-kai"}` in the §3 correction prompt — but the actual code at src/translate/romanizationEval.js:66-82 has NO hyphenation bullet at all and its example output is `"rokkai"`, i.e. the shipped prompt teaches the opposite convention to the documented one. Separately docs/number-reading-prompt.md:44-48 shows `"pronunciation": "nisen nijūgonen ni"` as its own worked example, directly violating the `nijūgo-nen` case spelled out in the rule it injects at line 27. Delivered result: 209 cards hyphenate a counter (`go-kai`, `ni-mai`, `jūichi-ji`, `jup-pon`, `nijup-pun`) while others fuse it (`gofun`, `gomai`, `sanji`, `hachijikan`, `gohyakunin`, `sanjuppun`, `hyakunanajūen`), and 3つ is `mit-tsu` while 2つ/4つ/6つ are `futatsu`/`yottsu`/`muttsu` — all in one book.
allFindings.recommendation: Make JA_COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE the single source: inject it into buildRomanizationPrompt too, regenerate docs/translate-prompts.md §3 from the real code (the promptTemplates test pins placeholders, not this prose — extend it to assert the rule string appears in the built prompt), and fix docs/number-reading-prompt.md's example to `nisen nijūgo-nen ni`. Decide explicitly whether みっつ-type native numerals hyphenate and state it, since the current rule is silent and the model guessed both ways.

allFindings.title: Japanese TTS is fed all-kana by default even though the codebase knows kanji orthography voices better
allFindings.evidence: src/audio/ttsText.js only strips whitespace for ja; the audio stage sends `reading ?? target`, which for this kana deck is always all-kana. src/audio/generateKanjiVariants.js:15-17 states the opposite is better — "a kanji orthography is generated from the card's kana reading … (which ElevenLabs voices more naturally than all-kana)" — but it is Japanese-only, on-demand, one card at a time, behind the dashboard's Generate (kanji) button. Delivered evidence of the cost: 81 cards ship a `-genkanji-` clip, 86 ship a `-gen-` re-roll, 109 carry a manual trim, 4 are human uploads and 7 are flagged audioMarkerStuck — ~13% of 2,173 clips needed human audio intervention. All-kana input strips the word-boundary and homograph cues a Japanese TTS front-end relies on (はし, いま vs い間, 1じ readings), which is precisely what the kanji path fixes.
allFindings.recommendation: Make kanji-normalized spoken text the DEFAULT for ja in the audio stage: generate the kanji orthography once per card (kanjiOrthography.js already exists) and use it as the TTS input while `target`/`reading` stay kana for display. Keep it agentic where it matters — surface the generated kanji in the audio review so the human can veto a wrong reading (the modal already does this) — and keep the kana text as the automatic fallback when generation fails. This also removes most of the manual Generate-(kanji) clicking from the per-chapter loop.

allFindings.title: Arabic and Hindi romanization adapters emit output that is not a usable pronunciation guide, and the prompt anchors the model to it
allFindings.evidence: Empirical probe of the installed packages. Arabic (src/translate/romanization/ar.js, IJMES via arabic-transliterate): كتاب→`ktab` (should be kitāb), مرحبا→`mrḥba` (marḥaban), شكرا→`shkra` (shukran), السلام عليكم→`al-sal-m ʿlykm` (as-salāmu ʿalaykum) — unvocalized Arabic has no short vowels to transliterate, so the library returns consonant skeletons plus a stray hyphen. Hindi (romanization/indic.js, IAST via sanscript): कमल→`kamala` (spoken kamal), राम→`rāma` (Rām), दोस्त→`dosta` (dost) — IAST is an orthographic Sanskrit standard and applies no Hindi schwa deletion; सड़क→`saḍa़ka` leaks the raw nukta U+093C. he.js's own comment concedes the same vowel problem for consonant-only Hebrew. Meanwhile src/translate/romanizationEval.js:29 tells the model to "keep the library's value when it is already right" and lists only Japanese failure modes, so nothing signals that the entire ar/hi/he output class is systematically wrong. docs/translate-prompts.md:12 advertises all seven languages as equivalently supported.
allFindings.recommendation: Per-language triage rather than a blanket registry: (a) for ar and he, either drop them from ROMANIZATION_LIBRARIES so they take the LLM-only pronunciation path, or keep the library only as a consonant-skeleton hint and add a mandatory per-language instruction "the library omits short vowels — supply full vocalization"; (b) for hi, add an explicit schwa-deletion + nukta instruction (and consider `iast`→a phonetic scheme); (c) note in docs/translate-prompts.md and LIMITATIONS.md that only ja/zh/ko are library-proven, since none of ar/he/hi/ru has ever been run end-to-end. Also reconcile the goal conflict: prompts 1/2 ask for something "readable by an English speaker unfamiliar with the language", while IJMES/SBL/IAST are diacritic-heavy academic systems.

allFindings.title: The category taxonomy misfits real textbook content: 10% of cards land in "Other" and sentence cards get grammatical, not topical, categories
allFindings.evidence: src/model/categories.js is a 25-value topical list, self-described as "First-cut list — revisit if it proves too coarse or fine in practice". Across 2,250 delivered cards `Other` is the SECOND largest bucket at 222 (Time 272, Travel & Tourism 200). Its contents are two coherent missing classes: everyday personal objects (かばん, めがね, さいふ, かぎ, かさ, ところ, え) and the entire descriptive-adjective class plus its sentences (きれい, おもしろい, べんり, ふるい, にぎやか, しずか, おおきい, このほんはおもしろいです, このかばんはおおきくないです). Because src/deck/collection.js:173,183 renders the category chip on the FRONT of BOTH templates, `Other` is a visible, contentless chip on ~10% of reviews. Separately, docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:180 says to pick by topic "not its grammatical role", yet 44 sentence-length cards are categorized `Grammar & Function Words` (これはペンですか, これはわたしのペンです, いいえ、ちがいます, ちょっとまってください) — the rule is stated and not followed.
allFindings.recommendation: Add three categories that absorb the observed Other mass — "Descriptions & Qualities" (adjectives and adjective sentences), "Everyday Objects" (bag/keys/wallet/umbrella class), and optionally "Actions & Verbs" — and re-state in the extraction prompt that a full sentence takes the topic of its content noun, with これはペンです → the pen's category as a worked counter-example. Adding enum values is backward-compatible (corpus schema enum at src/model/index.js:50); existing cards keep their value until re-reviewed.

allFindings.title: LLM-authored notes carry unverified morphological claims that ship to the live deck
allFindings.evidence: output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana/chapter-8/cards.json, card なに: note reads "Plain 'what,' distinct from なんの (nan no) 'what kind of' seen with なんじ (nanji, 'what time') and なんにん (nannin, 'how many people')". なんじ and なんにん are なん + counter; they contain no の and are not instances of なんの. The note teaches a false analysis of the exact contrast it is trying to draw, and it survived the extraction pass, the cross-lesson note pass (docs/cross-lesson-note-prompt.md), the corpus review and the Mark-done gate. The same note also writes `nannin` where the collision rules (references/card-authoring-rules.md:238) write `nan-nin`. Every existing note check is structural — enhance-card-notes deletes restatements, strip-restatement-notes.mjs clears echoes — none checks whether a claim is TRUE.
allFindings.recommendation: Keep this agentic but give it a place to happen: add an explicit instruction to docs/cross-lesson-note-prompt.md and docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md that a note may only make a morphological claim it can point at in the card set ("name the other card by its target"), and add a cheap per-chapter linguistic spot-check to the Gate-1 checklist in SKILL.md — list every note that asserts a decomposition (contains '+', 'form of', 'distinct from', 'same … as') and verify each against the deck's own cards. A deterministic helper can extract that candidate list; the verdict must stay human/agent.

allFindings.title: `reading` is defined two incompatible ways and is never rendered — no furigana path exists for a kanji-bearing source
allFindings.evidence: src/model/index.js:141-145 (cards schema) documents `reading` as the spoken form "e.g. kanji 二十一 … reading (にじゅういち), sidestepping ambiguous readings of logographic scripts" — a general kanji-disambiguation field. docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:30,44 restricts it to "include ONLY when target contains a numeral", and references/card-authoring-rules.md:91-101 states it as the numbers rule only. Real data agrees with the narrow reading: 136 of 2,250 cards have one, all numeric. Meanwhile src/deck/collection.js registers a "Reading" field (line 28, populated at line 463) that appears in NEITHER template's qfmt/afmt (lines 173-188) — it is stored and never shown. Consequence: the moment a source is a normal kanji textbook rather than this kana edition, cards show kanji + romaji with no kana anywhere, which is not how a Japanese deck is studied; and the one field that could carry furigana is both restricted by prompt and invisible by template.
allFindings.recommendation: Decide and document the policy before the second book: either (a) render `{{Reading}}` on the answer side of both templates and widen the extraction prompt to emit it for any kanji-bearing target, or (b) add a separate `furigana`/`kana` field and keep `reading` as the TTS-spoken form only. Note the deck-template change is a note-type field/template edit against a live collection — route it through the existing template-migration path in references/deliver.md rather than a fresh model.

allFindings.title: FIB prompt teaches an invalid category, and the cards-side schema drops the enum so a wrong one is silently rewritten
allFindings.evidence: docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md:93 shows `"category": "Travel"` in its Output Format example; "Travel" is not in src/model/categories.js (the value is "Travel & Tourism"). src/model/index.js:50 enforces the enum on the corpus side but line 132 declares `category: { type: "string" }` on the cards side — no enum — so nothing downstream rejects it. src/cards/fillInBlank.js:170 then snaps any unrecognized category to `items[0]?.category` ("snap an unrecognized one back to a category this lesson actually has"), i.e. a wrong category becomes silently plausible rather than surfacing. Two smaller staleness bugs in the same prompt: rule 8 (line 66) says "no trailing 。 (the audio stage adds one itself where the language wants it)" — false since the 。 moved inside the end marker (references/audio-pipeline.md:45-49), and rule 11 (line 111) cross-references "rule 7" for readings when the readings rule is 10.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the example to "Travel & Tourism" (or inject {{CATEGORY_LIST}} as the extraction prompt does), add the CATEGORIES enum to the cards schema so hand-authored extras units are checked by `npm run validate:decks`, change fillInBlank's snap to also log the rewrite, and correct the two stale sentences.

allFindings.title: The "an answer card must be answerable alone" rule is stated three times and enforced by no tool
allFindings.evidence: The rule is in references/card-authoring-rules.md:263-282, docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:202 and docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md rules 4-5, and card-authoring-rules.md:282 even names the mechanical audit ("listing cards whose English starts with a pronoun stand-in ('It's', 'That's', 'They're') and checking each for a scene"). src/cards/fillInBlank.js only logs a warning. scripts/preflight.mjs runs six checks (schema, duplicate ids, collisions, duplicate targets, display normalization, audio markers) and this is not one of them. Applying the doc's own heuristic to the 2,150 non-excluded delivered cards returns 27 hits with no scene, including FIB output the rule was written for: 13,000えんです "It's 13,000 yen.", さんがいです "It's the 3rd floor.", じゅっぷんぐらいです "It's about ten minutes.", いまくじです "It's 9:00 now.", とてもおいしいです "It's very delicious."
allFindings.recommendation: Add the audit to scripts/preflight.mjs as check 7, WARN-level (some hits are legitimately producible, e.g. きょうはさむいですね where the target also states きょうは — so this must not hard-fail). Matching the project's stated frontier of "catch X before the review gate, not at Mark done", this is cheap and purely mechanical; the keep/fix decision stays with the reviewer.

allFindings.title: The 。ででで end marker imposes declarative prosody on every card including questions, and covers only Japanese
allFindings.evidence: src/audio/ttsMarker.js appends `。ででで` to every ja utterance, and the module comment is explicit that the 。 is load-bearing for trim detection (「はちじ。ででで」 leaves a 1.12s gap vs 0.24s without). But display targets never carry 。 or ？ (references/card-authoring-rules.md:21-29), so a か-final question is voiced as a full stop followed by a second utterance: 328 delivered cards have an English gloss ending in ?. ElevenLabs v3 is punctuation-driven for prosody, so these likely get flat/falling rather than the rising contour a real か question takes. Separately MARKED_LANGUAGES is `{ja}` only, and the module concedes the で choice "does not transfer automatically to another language" — so every non-Japanese deck still has the end-clipping problem the marker exists to solve, undocumented as a gap.
allFindings.recommendation: Cheap experiment before changing anything: generate a few か-final cards as `…ですか？。ででで` vs today's `…ですか。ででで` and audition — if the rising contour appears and the marker still strips (the gap comes from the 。, which is retained), make it the ja default for か-final text. Independently, record in LIMITATIONS.md that end-marker protection is ja-only so a Spanish/Korean deck's clipped endings are a known, unhandled condition rather than a surprise.

allFindings.title: Glosses use parenthetical ellipsis markers where the rules say the context belongs in `scene`
allFindings.evidence: references/card-authoring-rules.md:197-198 and docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:36 both say contextual parentheticals move out of `english` into `scene` ("Excuse me. (said when entering a room)" → english + scene). 37 delivered cards keep a mid-gloss parenthetical instead, and they mix two different jobs: ellipsis restoration (chapter-1 "Yes, (he is) American." / chapter-14-extras "(She) will give it to a colleague.") and genuine scene content (chapter-12 "There is a bank and a convenience store on the first floor (and nothing else).", chapter-14 "I'm sorry (for what I did a while ago)."). Four of the chapter-1 pair even have a proper `scene` AND the parenthetical. On the Production front the learner must guess whether the parenthesized words are to be produced — for 「はい、アメリカじんです」 they are not, for 「ちちはいつわたしにおかねをくれますか」/"When does (my) father give me money?" they arguably are.
allFindings.recommendation: State the distinction once in card-authoring-rules.md: a parenthetical that restores a subject the TARGET also drops is the deck's convention and stays in `english` (it tells the learner not to produce it); a parenthetical that describes the situation or adds nuance moves to `scene`/`note`. Then apply it in the extraction prompt with one worked example of each. Mechanizable only as a listing pass (find mid-gloss parentheticals for review), not as an auto-fix.

allFindings.title: `npm test` writes into the live .anki-builder library home — the test guard covers the LLM spawn but not state writes
allFindings.evidence: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json` exists with mtime today (14 Aug 12:10) and contains exactly the `unpreparedFixture` payload from test/server/index.test.js:1233-1256 (`epubHash: "h1"`, `chapterNumber: 2`, `chapterLabel: "Uch"`, one item english "one" / target いち, `reviewed: true`). The producer is the test "a prepared lesson passes the gate and signs off normally" (test/server/index.test.js:~1317), which passes `editDeps` (test/server/index.test.js:60-68) — that stub set covers fonts, TTS and ffmpeg but NOT `saveChapterCorpus`, unlike the test at :540 which does inject it. `libraryHome()` (src/model/index.js:365) is repo-relative with no test override, and `assertExternalCallAllowed` (src/util/testEnv.js) only guards `spawn claude -p`. The dedup library keyed by (epubHash, chapterNumber) is precisely what decides which cards a later chapter builds for a deck studied daily.
allFindings.recommendation: Two mechanical fixes, both cheap: (a) extend the testEnv guard to a `assertLibraryWriteAllowed()` called from `bookDir()`/`saveChapterCorpus` in src/corpus/epubLibrary.js, so any un-injected library write throws under NODE_TEST_CONTEXT the same way an un-stubbed model call does; (b) have `libraryHome()` honour an `ANKI_BUILDER_HOME` env var and set it to a temp dir for the whole suite. Then delete the stray `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/` tree. Fully mechanizable, no judgment involved.

allFindings.title: extras-duplicate-check.mjs --apply automates a judgment preflight explicitly refuses to automate, and false-positives on this book's own data
allFindings.evidence: preflight.mjs:129-130 states the policy: "Duplicate targets — reported, never auto-applied: whether a pair is one word taught twice or two senses that share a spelling is a judgment about the source material." But extras-pass.md:210 advertises `node scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs <book> --apply   # exclude later copies` as a normal step. A read-only run of that script on output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana shows the keeper for target に is `chapter-2/num-2` (the NUMBER "2"), and --apply would exclude `chapter-6/ni-particle`, `chapter-7/ni-particle-time`, `chapter-9/ni-particle-target`, `chapter-12/ni-particle-location`, `chapter-14/ni-from-particle`; similarly さん keeps `chapter-1/san-suffix-ch14` and would drop `chapter-2/num-3` ("3"), and ご keeps `num-5` over the honorific prefix. LIMITATIONS.md:~1218 independently names yasumi (break/vacation), the と particle and the に particle as genuinely different cards that collided. Only the reviewed/done refusal is stopping this today; a NEW chapter in flight is unreviewed and would be mutated.
allFindings.recommendation: Make report-only the canonical documented path (edit extras-pass.md:206-228 to drop --apply from the happy path). If --apply survives at all, gate it on `english` similarity as well as `target` equality and refuse any group whose members' glosses differ beyond a threshold, printing them for the agent instead. This is the correct code-vs-judgment line: the script enumerates candidates, the agent decides — exactly what preflight already does.

allFindings.title: The two checks SKILL.md most insists on (vocabulary diff, paradigm audit) are documented as scripts that do not exist
allFindings.evidence: SKILL.md:299-310 — "Also diff the chapter's VOCABULARY entries against the built cards… The check is a script, not a read-through: pull every `Japanese word` + `English gloss` pair out of the chapter text and report any whose word appears in no card's `target`." extras-pass.md:153-169 — "Write the check as a script over all `chapter-*/cards.json` targets rather than reading tables by eye", plus ~15 lines of prose encoding real matching rules (predicate position after が/は/も/に or string start, exclude longer forms of the same paradigm when testing a shorter one). `grep -rl paradigm scripts/ src/` returns nothing; no vocabulary-coverage script exists in scripts/ (13 files listed). So the agent re-derives both throwaways every chapter, and the matching rules that exist only as prose are re-implemented from memory each time — the exact provenance of the project's own "3 lessons missing from the dedup library" and "naive substring audit reports full coverage" incidents.
allFindings.recommendation: Ship `scripts/vocab-coverage.mjs <chapterFile> <unitDir>` (emit candidate misses + the near-match that explains each false positive, e.g. `(お)てら` vs `おてら`) and `scripts/paradigm-grid.mjs <bookDir> --grid <spec.json>`, where the grid spec (which cells exist, which forms fill them) is authored by the agent per chapter but the matching implements the predicate-position and longer-form-exclusion rules in code. Both respect red line 1: the script proposes candidates, the agent judges every hit. Put the matching logic in src/cards/ behind tests, per techlead-11.

allFindings.title: preflight does NOT subsume validate-decks (templates are invisible to it), and the unit-loading block is triplicated verbatim
allFindings.evidence: scripts/preflight.mjs:29-40 `collectionDirs()` only walks `output/epubs` and `output/courses`; :46-49 `loadUnits()` only matches `/^(chapter|lesson)-(\d+)(-extras)?$/`. So `output/templates/<name>/<lang>/` — a real on-disk unit shape documented in SKILL.md:644-646 — is never schema-checked by preflight, while scripts/validate-decks.mjs:29-38 walks the whole root recursively and does check it. The identical `readdirSync → /^(chapter|lesson)-(\d+)(-extras)?$/ → sort → load cards.json` block appears verbatim at preflight.mjs:46-63, extras-collision-audit.mjs:24-37 and extras-duplicate-check.mjs:30-44. A future unit type has to be added in three places or two of the three audits silently skip it — the project's own signature failure mode.
allFindings.recommendation: Do not retire validate-decks until preflight learns the templates layout (add a templates branch to collectionDirs + a template unit shape to loadUnits); then fold validate-decks into `preflight --schema-only` and delete it. Independently, move the unit loader into src/cards/extrasTools.js (already the shared home for findCollisions/findCrossChapterDuplicates/orderExtrasUnit) and have all three scripts import it.

allFindings.title: No lifecycle policy for scripts/: spent one-shot migrations sit beside pipeline tools, and LIMITATIONS.md documents a script that was deleted
allFindings.evidence: scripts/ mixes standing tools (preflight, validate-decks, extras-*, deliver-to-anki, restore-anki-backup) with spent one-shots whose own headers say "One-off" / "Migration": clean-audio.mjs, jumble-number-runs.mjs, split-front-hint.mjs, strip-restatement-notes.mjs, migrate-deck-numbering.mjs (28 Jul – 13 Aug). Nothing marks them as already applied, and two of them (jumble-number-runs.mjs:13, split-front-hint.mjs:11) spend LLM credits and rewrite reviewed units in bulk — jumble's bare form "scans output/" and split-front-hint's rewrites every lesson of a book. Meanwhile LIMITATIONS.md:905 still carries a full What/Why/Impact entry for `scripts/backfill-dedup-library.mjs`, which was deleted in commit 991d0cb; a maintainer reading the institutional memory is told to reach for a file that isn't there.
allFindings.recommendation: Adopt a two-tier policy: `scripts/` = standing tools referenced by SKILL.md; `scripts/migrations/` = one-shots, each with a `// SPENT: <date>, applied to <collection>` header line, or deleted outright and recovered from git when a second book needs them. Delete the LIMITATIONS.md:900-916 backfill entry (or rewrite it as "the dedup library has no recovery path", which is the durable lesson). Mechanizable as a CI test — see techlead-9.

allFindings.title: The review watcher is pure mechanism reproduced by hand as ~50 lines of SKILL.md shell — the highest-value mechanization in the skill, and it has already shipped a bug
allFindings.evidence: SKILL.md:70-84 and :106-113 are two shell snippets the agent must reproduce byte-correct twice per unit, four times per chapter, including a readability probe, an absolute-path rule, a heartbeat modulus, a timeout bound, and a gate-2 `[ "$APKG" -nt "$RUN/cards.json" ]` artifact check. SKILL.md:90-98 records that this already failed in production (relative RUN after a `cd`, `2>/dev/null` swallowing MODULE_NOT_FOUND, so "cannot read" looked like "not signed off"), costing the user exactly the message the watcher exists to save; commit 597a6e6 "Stop the review watcher from failing silently" is the fix, applied to the prose. `src/cli/index.js:114-123` COMMANDS = {assemble, prepare, translate, audio, deck, restyle-font, view-deck, serve} — there is no watch command. This step contains zero judgment: it observes a flag a human sets.
allFindings.recommendation: Add `anki-builder watch --run <dir> --gate {1|2} [--timeout 30m]` implementing the readability probe, the poll, the gate-2 artifact-freshness check and the same emoji heartbeat lines on stdout. SKILL.md then collapses ~50 lines to "run it under Monitor", and the failure class disappears from prose into a tested function. Strictly additive to the agentic design — the agent still decides when to arm it and what to do when it fires.

allFindings.title: The harness backlog is dead while LIMITATIONS.md is the real planning loop; T011 points at the one path with zero worked examples
allFindings.evidence: .harness/ledgers/outcomes.jsonl last entry is T010 at 2026-07-13T13:46:22Z — the loop has not run since day 1, while `git log --oneline | wc -l` = 535 commits. TASKS.json holds T001–T011, all done except T011 "End-to-end: build a real travel deck + verify in Anki" (status pending, gate needs-human) — the template path, and `output/templates/` is empty, i.e. the only open task targets the only source type with no worked example. IDEAS.jsonl (13 rows) was last appended 2026-07-20; at least six have shipped since: #1 image sweep (now SKILL.md:280-297), #6 numbers template (templates/numbers.json exists), #9 bracket-free variants, #10 FIB extraction (src/cards/fillInBlank.js), #13 per-step prompt files (docs/*.md + test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js). By contrast LIMITATIONS.md has 83 commits, most recent 2026-08-13 — it is the artifact that actually steers the work.
allFindings.recommendation: Retire the pretence rather than revive it: mark T011 dropped (or re-scope it to the real gap — a second EPUB conformance run, see techlead-10), state in CLAUDE.md that this project is hand-driven and that LIMITATIONS.md + IDEAS.jsonl are the planning loop, and keep .harness/ only for the LIMITATIONS overlay and the CLAUDE.md conventions. If instead the loop is to be revived, one convert-ideas sweep must close the six shipped ideas first, or every future sweep re-proposes them. This is a judgment call for the owner, not something to mechanize.

allFindings.title: preflight's non-failing '·' notices are permanent wallpaper — a count that never reaches zero cannot signal a new instance
allFindings.evidence: A read-only `node scripts/preflight.mjs --all` right now prints for japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana: "· duplicates 17 target group(s) spanning units" and "· audio 7 clip(s) flagged marker-audible: chapter-9-extras/…, chapter-10/hontouni-samui-ne, chapter-12/…, chapter-14/karimasendeshita" — then "preflight clean". All 29 units are reviewed and done, so those 24 notices are accepted, permanent, and shipped into the live collection. The 18th duplicate group or the 8th stuck marker introduced by chapter 15 will render identically to the noise the operator has already learned to scroll past. This is the same silent-degradation signature as isStageOwnedCard claiming all 1,179 clips were hand-picked.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a per-collection acknowledgement file (`<bookDir>/.preflight-accepted.json` holding accepted duplicate group keys and accepted audioMarkerStuck ids, written only by an explicit `preflight --accept`). preflight then prints "duplicates: 17 accepted, 0 new" and FAILS on anything unaccepted. Cheap, fully deterministic, and it converts a wallpaper channel back into a signal — which is the stated goal of the current frontier ("catch X before the review gate").

allFindings.title: Doc ownership is unassigned: README.md and PIPELINE.md never mention the newest safety mechanism, and a pinned-model comment is stale
allFindings.evidence: `grep -c preflight docs/PIPELINE.md README.md` → 0 and 0; neither mentions validate-decks or any extras-* script either, though both were last committed 2026-08-10 and preflight landed 2026-08-14 (commits 853ad23, 271a872). So four prose surfaces now describe the system — README.md (23 KB), docs/PIPELINE.md (844 L), SKILL.md (670 L) + 5 reference files (953 L), LIMITATIONS.md (1430 L) ≈ 4k lines of prose against 14.7k LOC — with no stated precedence. Drift is already measurable: src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js:83 claims category assignment runs "via a small batched Haiku pass" while src/util/runClaude.js:7 pins `claude-sonnet-5` for every call and lessonCorpus imports the default translate runner; LIMITATIONS.md:905 documents a deleted script (techlead-5).
allFindings.recommendation: Declare SKILL.md normative for operator procedure and PIPELINE.md strictly "how the code is wired, no procedure", stated at the top of each. Then add a docs-integrity test alongside the existing test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js: assert every file in scripts/ is referenced by at least one doc, and every `scripts/*.mjs` path mentioned in docs/, README.md, .claude/skills/ or LIMITATIONS.md exists on disk. That one ~20-line test catches both the backfill-dedup-library drift and the next undocumented script. Fix the lessonCorpus Haiku comment.

allFindings.title: Keep the hand-rolled EPUB stack — the real cliff is convention-bound downstream code, which no library fixes; spend the effort on a second-book probe instead
allFindings.evidence: The zip layer is thinner than it looks: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:3 uses `zlib.inflateRawSync`, so only container walking is hand-rolled (~200 L), and its two rejections are explicit and loud — ZIP64 at :24-30 and :56-60, encrypted/DRM entries at :48-54 with a message naming the cause. 35 tests cover it, and the project has a documented precedent for a bounded dependency exception (LIMITATIONS.md:315, the romanization libraries). The genuine single-book risk sits downstream of any parser: src/corpus/epubLessons.js:18-31 classifies with English-only regexes (mitigated — it's display-only and never a gate, per its own comment), while src/deck/deckPath.js:29 `/^(Lesson|Chapter|Unit)\s+(\d+)\s*:\s*(.+)$/` IS load-bearing and silently degrades a differently-labelled book to one flat level (LIMITATIONS.md:1287-1305 says so). LIMITATIONS.md:144, :204, :565, :1324, :1339 all carry "revisit at the second real book" triggers that have not fired because there is no second book.
allFindings.recommendation: Do not swap in an EPUB library — it would trade explicit, loud rejections for generic ones and buy nothing against the actual failure mode. Instead ship `scripts/epub-probe.mjs `: print nav entries with classifyLesson types, spine ranges, `` counts per lesson, and `unitDeckSegments(label)` for every label, so "will this book work, and will its decks group" is answered in five seconds before any LLM or TTS credits are spent. That is the cheapest way to fire the five dormant second-book triggers, and it is pure mechanism.

allFindings.title: scripts/ has zero tests, and mutating scripts split unevenly between tested src/ logic and inline logic
allFindings.evidence: `find test -path '*script*'` returns only test/model/scriptSpacing.test.js — nothing exercises scripts/. The pattern is inconsistent: extras-order.mjs correctly delegates to `orderExtrasUnit` (src/cards/extrasTools.js:151, covered by test/cards/extrasTools.test.js, 159 L) and preflight delegates to validateCards/assertUniqueCardIds/findCollisions; but extras-duplicate-check.mjs performs its exclusion mutation inline in the .mjs, and jumble-number-runs.mjs / split-front-hint.mjs / strip-restatement-notes.mjs each hold their own LLM prompt + rewrite logic in the script. Commit 82e77b9 ("Fix extras-order.mjs dropping the run dir when --seed is omitted") is a shipped bug in exactly the untested arg-parsing layer, and its fix is now a defensive comment at extras-order.mjs:22-24 rather than a test.
allFindings.recommendation: Adopt the rule the codebase half-follows already: any script that MUTATES anything under output/ keeps its logic in src/ behind a unit-tested function, and the .mjs is arg parsing + reporting only. Retrofit extras-duplicate-check.mjs first (its --apply is the riskiest mutation — techlead-2). Add a tiny test/scripts/argParsing.test.js importing each script's parser, or extract parsing into a shared helper; that alone would have caught 82e77b9.

allFindings.title: The extras pass's deterministic tail is a 6-step hand-sequenced procedure whose steps have already been forgotten in practice
allFindings.evidence: extras-pass.md prescribes, in order and by hand: audits (:206-245) → extras-order.mjs --apply (:249-258) → `anki-builder prepare --run <dir>` (:291-301) → re-run the duplicate check and collision audit on the grown unit → re-run extras-order.mjs with a NEW seed (:308-310) → validate-decks (:92-96) → preflight (SKILL.md:119-125). Seven commands with real ordering constraints and no single entry point. Two of them have already been forgotten in production and patched into prose rather than code: commit 7d7e8db "Extras pass docs: run prepare on the unit or the review gate stays shut" and commit 0ef7850 "Add validate:decks, and stop extras units writing invalid corpus.json".
allFindings.recommendation: Add `anki-builder finalize-extras --run <dir>` running prepare → duplicate check (report) → collision audit → order --apply (fresh seed) → validate → preflight in the correct order, printing every report for the agent to read and judge. The authoring (two waves of subagents, wave-2 briefs, cue wording, which reported duplicate is real) stays entirely agentic — only the fixed sequence and its ordering constraints move into code. Same shape as the existing `assemble → prepare` chaining, which SKILL.md:270-277 says was created for exactly this reason ("those steps used to be separate commands, which is exactly why they got skipped").

allFindings.title: Module health is good and two briefing claims are wrong — record the correction so effort isn't misallocated
allFindings.evidence: The CLI layer IS covered: test/cli/index.test.js is 2436 lines with per-command dispatch, resumability, gate-refusal and --output-root resolution tests (test/cli/ totals 3504 L). The two runClaude files are not duplication but a deliberate core + scoped-wrapper trio: src/util/runClaude.js (sync + async cores, model/effort resolution, timeout, one retry) with src/translate/runClaude.js and src/corpus/epubLlmRunClaude.js as thin scope wrappers — 16 call sites all import a wrapper, and test/util/testEnv.test.js pins that neither will spawn under the runner. The largest modules (epubArchive 714, review/clientScripts 659, deck/collection 655, translate/index 623, anki/deliver 613) are each single-concern. The genuinely untested surface is src/review/clientScripts.js (659 L of inline browser JS, no harness) and scripts/ (techlead-11).
allFindings.recommendation: No refactor warranted; do not spend effort on module splitting or on CLI test coverage. If any testing effort is spent, put it on src/review/clientScripts.js — the dashboard is where the human gates are clicked, and a broken Mark reviewed/Mark done button is a red-line-2 path with no automated coverage at all. A jsdom-free approach (extract the pure state transitions out of the inline script into an importable module) is probably enough.

allFindings.title: npm test writes into the owner's real .anki-builder dedup library (artifact present on disk)
allFindings.evidence: src/model/index.js:365 `libraryHome()` is hardcoded to `REPO_ROOT/.anki-builder` with no test/env override. src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:89 defaults `saveChapterCorpus` to the real one and applyCards.js:136 defaults `removeChapterCorpus` to the real one (which `rmSync`s). test/server/index.test.js:1320 uses `unpreparedFixture({enriched:true, notesEnhanced:true})` and hits `POST .../review/reviewed` with `editDeps` that does NOT inject `saveChapterCorpus`. Proof it fires: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json` exists (mtime today 12:10) containing `"chapterLabel": "Uch"` — verbatim from that fixture. `src/util/testEnv.js` already has exactly the right guard shape (`assertExternalCallAllowed`) but it only covers spawning `claude`, not library writes.
allFindings.recommendation: Mechanize: add `assertLibraryWriteAllowed()` (same shape as `assertExternalCallAllowed`) inside `libraryHome()`, or have `libraryHome()` return a per-process tmpdir when `isTestEnv()` and `ANKI_BUILDER_ALLOW_LIBRARY_WRITES` is unset. Today only the accident of fixtures using `epubHash: "h1"` keeps this from overwriting/deleting `.anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/corpora/<n>.json` — a signed-off chapter's dedup corpus, whose loss is silent and only shows up as unflagged repeats many lessons later. Also delete the stray `.anki-builder/epubs/h1` tree.

allFindings.title: A nav document that isn't spine-monotonic produces inverted lesson ranges, silently truncating extraction and inverting the forward-flag window
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:529-534 computes `lastChapterNumber = deduped[i+1].spinePosition - 1` with no check that the next entry's spine position is greater. Probe (synthetic EPUB, nav listing c2, c5, c3, c6 over a 6-file spine) returned: `[{label:"Lesson 1…",first:2,last:4},{label:"Lesson 2",first:5,last:2},{label:"Appendix A",first:3,last:5},{label:"Lesson 3",first:6,last:6}]`. Downstream, src/cli/commands/assemble.js:289-304 tests `lastChapterNumber > chapterNumber`, so `5-2` falls to single-file extraction (the rest of the lesson is dropped and `meta.lastChapterNumber` is never set, so prepare.js:141-145 also mines drills from the wrong file); assemble.js:339 then passes `chapterNumber: lastChapterNumber` (=2) to `flagForwardConcerns`, so src/corpus/epubForwardFlags.js:162 treats the lesson's OWN spine file 5 as a "later chapter".
allFindings.recommendation: In `listExternalChapters`, detect non-monotonic nav order: either clamp (`lastChapterNumber = max(firstChapterNumber, next-1)`) and `log()` loudly, or drop the range semantics for such books and fall back to single-file. Mechanizable and cheap. Also assert `lastChapterNumber >= firstChapterNumber` in `resolveLesson`/`--list-lessons` so it fails at the gate rather than 20 minutes into extraction. `--list-lessons` currently prints `spine 5` for a `5-2` range (assemble.js:148-152), hiding the corruption from the human.

allFindings.title: Text edits never invalidate a hand-trimmed or hand-picked clip — the card ships the old spoken words forever
allFindings.evidence: src/cli/commands/audio.js:74-78: `clipIsCurrent = (item) => !isStageOwnedCard(item) || (…hash comparison…)`. src/audio/index.js:204-208: `isStageOwnedCard` returns false whenever `item.audioManual` is set, or `audioOriginal` isn't `<hash>.orig.mp3` (a picked `-gen-` variant or a Replace upload). So the entire content-hash staleness check is short-circuited to "current" for exactly the cards a human touched. src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:160-172 `editCard` writes `target`/`reading` (both feed `speechText`) and touches none of `AUDIO_FIELDS`, and audio.js:267 `handPicked` makes `generateAudio` skip such a card entirely ("no fetch … no annotation").
allFindings.recommendation: Record the clip's source text hash when ANY take is installed (add e.g. `audioTextHash` alongside `AUDIO_FIELDS` in applyCardAudio.js) and compare it to `hashTerm(defaultClipText(item, lang))` regardless of ownership. On mismatch, do NOT regenerate over the human's work — badge it in the audio review and block Mark done, the way `findUnreadableNumbers` already blocks the corpus gate. This is exactly the "catch it before the gate" pattern the recent commits are pursuing and it can be fully mechanized.

allFindings.title: Dashboard edits to a done lesson never rebuild the .apkg — and two comments claim they do
allFindings.evidence: `rebuildGroupQuiet` is called from exactly one place: src/server/index.js:286, inside `handleLessonDone`. `handleReviewExclude` (index.js:290-301), `handleReviewEdit` (index.js:303-315), `handleSelect`, `handleTrim` and `handleReclean` all return without rebuilding. Yet src/deck/rebuild.js:6-8 says the module is shared by "the dashboard's automatic rebuilds (Mark done, and an audio or exclude edit on an already-done lesson)", and src/server/index.js:421-424 says the quiet rebuild exists so "marking a lesson done (or an edit to a done lesson) keeps the on-disk package in step". Both are false.
allFindings.recommendation: Either call `rebuildGroupQuiet` from the exclude/edit/audio handlers for a `meta.done === true` unit (cheap — `buildBookDeck` is sync and already re-entrant by the no-await invariant), or delete the two comments and surface "package is stale — rebuild" in the dashboard. Leaving a false safety claim in the two files a future reader will trust is the worse half of this bug. Note the practical impact is bounded because AnkiConnect delivery reads `cards.json` directly — but the `.apkg` is the restore artifact and the two delivery paths silently disagree, which is the exact class of divergence `src/deck/shippableCards.js` was written to prevent.

allFindings.title: AnkiConnect bootstrap matches untagged notes book-wide, not unit-wide; re-id'ing a card (which the code itself instructs) creates a permanent duplicate note
allFindings.evidence: src/anki/deliver.js:350 queries `deck:"<ankiParent>" note:"<model>"` — the WHOLE book — and builds `byTarget`/`byTargetEnglish` from it; deliver.js:381-405 then matches a corpus card to any free note with the same Target regardless of which unit deck it sits in, stamps `abid:` on it, and updates it in place. I confirmed 17 targets that repeat across units in the live JBP deck (`いいえ`, `じかん`, `に` ×6, `から`, `ご`, …). The `free` guard (deliver.js:380, 448) only helps once a note is already abid-tagged. Separately, the prefix fallback at deliver.js:391-396 (`ne.startsWith(ce) || ce.startsWith(ne)`) will pick "No" for "No, not at all". And src/deck/shippableCards.js:44-46 instructs the human to "give the later one its own id" on a duplicate-id clash — doing so leaves the old note tagged `abid:<oldid>`, so the re-id'd card is ADDED as a brand-new note and the old one is only reported in `r.orphaned` (deliver.js:442-444) and never reconciled; scripts/deliver-to-anki.mjs:93 just prints it.
allFindings.recommendation: Scope the bootstrap indexes to the unit's own `unit.ankiDeck` (one `findNotes` per unit) so a Target repeat across lessons can never cross-bind, and drop or unit-scope the prefix fallback. Separately, make `orphaned` actionable: offer a `--retag <old> <new>` on the deliver script rather than only printing it, so the re-id remedy the error message prescribes doesn't quietly double a note the owner studies daily.

allFindings.title: prepare and cross-lesson-notes write back a whole-file snapshot taken before a multi-minute LLM call, losing concurrent dashboard edits
allFindings.evidence: src/cards/crossLessonNotes.js:190 loads every unit's `cards.json` into memory, line 222 runs `runClaude` (10-min timeout per src/util/runClaude.js:13), line 260-261 then `writeJson(current.file, current.data)` from the pre-call snapshot. src/cli/commands/prepare.js:63 `readJson(paths.cards)` → line 148 `mineFillInBlankCards` (another `claude -p`) → line 195 `writeJson(paths.cards, cards)`. src/cli/commands/audio.js:139-149 documents this exact hazard and defends against it by re-reading (`const fresh = readJson(paths.cards)`) and merging only the fields that stage owns; these two paths do not.
allFindings.recommendation: Apply audio.js's merge pattern: re-read `cards.json` after the model call and write back only the fields the pass owns (`note`/`hint` for cross-lesson notes; appended `fillInBlank` items + `meta` markers for prepare). Mechanizable — factor audio.js:149-169 into a shared `mergeIntoCardsFile(path, byId, ownedFields)` helper.

allFindings.title: Only 5 named HTML entities are decoded — numeric and common named entities survive into Anki deck names
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:272-276: `HTML_ENTITIES = {amp, lt, gt, quot, #39}` and the regex `/&(amp|lt|gt|quot|#39);/g`. Probe with a nav label `Lesson 1 — Greetings & Farewells` returned `"Lesson 1 — Greetings & Farewells"` from `listExternalChapters`, `listLessons` and `describeChapter`. That label flows to `corpus.meta.chapterLabel` (assemble.js:311-312) → `selectDoneChapterDecks` (rebuild.js:69) → `unitDeckSegments` → the literal Anki deck name, and to `crossLessonNotes.js:73` as the citable lesson name the model is told to quote. The one book in the tree happens to use literal UTF-8 curly quotes, so this has never fired.
allFindings.recommendation: Replace `decodeHtmlEntities` with a decoder that handles `&#NNNN;`, `&#xHHHH;` and the ~10 common named entities (`nbsp`, `rsquo`, `lsquo`, `ldquo`, `rdquo`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`). Purely mechanical, ~10 lines, and directly protects a load-bearing identifier (a deck name change is not a rename in Anki — it's a new deck).

allFindings.title: Image extraction writes to an unvalidated archive-supplied relative path (zip-slip)
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:637 `const localDest = join(destDir, src);` where `src` comes straight from `` / `` in archive content (line 617-622), filtered only by `isLocalRelativePath` (line 613-615), which rejects schemes and `data:` but not `../`. `destDir` is `.anki-builder/epubs//chapters/`, so `src="../../../../src/deck/index.js"` overwrites repo source with image bytes via `writeFileAtomic`. The `../`-relative case is deliberately supported (see the comment at 577-588), so it can't just be banned outright.
