allFindings.recommendation: Resolve `localDest` and refuse anything that doesn't stay under the book's library dir (`.anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/`), logging the skip the same way a dangling ref is logged at line 633. Two lines; no behavior change for real books. Low likelihood, but the blast radius is arbitrary file overwrite in a repo whose `output/` holds a year of reviewed work.

allFindings.title: Regex XML scanning breaks on '>' inside attribute values and on commented-out markup — a lesson disappears with no diagnostic
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:103 `new RegExp('<'+tagName+'\\b([^>]*)>')` and :337 `NAV_A_TAG_PATTERN` both use `[^>]*`. A nav entry `Lesson 3` fails to match, so that entry vanishes from `parseNavXhtmlToc`; because `listExternalChapters` derives `lastChapterNumber` from the NEXT surviving entry (line 532), the missing lesson's spine files are silently folded into the previous lesson's range — no log line fires (the `log()` at line 507 only covers hrefs that fail to RESOLVE, not entries that never parsed). Symmetrically, `findTags(opfXml, "item")` at line 154 will happily pick up an `` inside an XML comment, which `findManifestItemByProperty(… "nav")` (line 412) could then select as the navigation document. Neither case has a test (test/corpus/epubArchive.test.js, epubExternalChapters.test.js).
allFindings.recommendation: Keep the hand-rolled scanner (a real XML parser is a dependency the project has deliberately refused), but (a) strip `<!--…-->` spans before scanning the OPF/nav, and (b) add a sanity check to `listExternalChapters`: if the toc `<nav>` block contains more `<a ` occurrences than parsed entries, `log()` the shortfall. That converts a silent lesson loss into a visible one, which is the whole point of the two-gate design.

allFindings.title: Translate retry re-sends the identical unbatched prompt, so a size-driven failure fails twice deterministically
allFindings.evidence: src/translate/index.js:17 `BATCH_SIZE = Infinity`; :428-435 `attempt(group)` then `attempt(firstAttemptErrors.map(({item}) => item))` — if the whole response was unparseable, `firstAttemptErrors` is the entire group, so the retry rebuilds the SAME prompt over the SAME items. `parseBatch` (:276-288) throws "model response was not valid JSON" for a merely TRUNCATED array, and `runClaude` already burned its own internal retry (src/util/runClaude.js:56-63) plus a 20 MB `maxBuffer` cap. The same unbatched-with-no-fallback shape is in src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js:10.
allFindings.recommendation: On retry, halve: `chunk(failedItems, Math.max(1, Math.ceil(failedItems.length/2)))`. Preserves the "one call keeps translations self-consistent" rationale for the happy path while making the failure path actually different from the first attempt. Also fix the stale comment at lessonCorpus.js:83 ("a small batched Haiku pass" — it runs the Sonnet default).

allFindings.title: Media entries are emitted per card rather than per unique clip, and the zip EOCD entry count is an unguarded uint16
allFindings.evidence: src/deck/index.js:39-57 `resolveChapterAudio` pushes one `mediaEntries` row per CARD with an unconditional `counter.next++`, so two cards sharing a content-addressed clip produce two zip entries and two `media` keys pointing at the same filename. Measured on the live book: 1914 audio-bearing cards, 1892 distinct clip names → 22 redundant entries. src/deck/zip.js:95-96 writes `entries.length` into the EOCD's two uint16 count fields with no range check, so a package exceeding 65,535 entries emits a structurally corrupt central directory rather than an error.
allFindings.recommendation: Memoize by `item.audio` in `resolveChapterAudio` (reuse the existing key when the filename is already in `media`) — this keeps the integer-sequential-key invariant intact, which the comment at index.js:30-38 rightly guards. And add `if (entries.length > 0xffff) throw` in `buildZip`. Both are small and testable, and given the media-key bug's history ("passed all tests and broke real import"), the entry-count cliff deserves an explicit throw rather than silence.

allFindings.title: assemble's out-of-order warning cannot fire for the --book path it most needs to cover
allFindings.evidence: src/cli/commands/assemble.js:99 `const ordered = flags["output-root"] && (flags.epub || flags.book || flags.words);` — but lines 121-130 desugar `--book <slug>` into `flags.epub` BEFORE this runs, so `flags.book` in the disjunction is dead code. Harmless today (the `flags.epub` arm covers it), but line 102 `Number(flags["chapter-number"] ?? flags["lesson-number"])` runs before `--lesson` desugaring only in the `--words` case — for `--lesson`, `flags["chapter-number"]` was set at line 164, so `ownNumber` is the lesson's FIRST spine index, which `runDirOrderContext` compares against siblings' `meta.chapterNumber` (also first-spine). Consistent, but only by coincidence of both sides keying on the first spine file rather than the nav ordinal.
allFindings.recommendation: Drop the dead `flags.book` term and add a comment (or an assertion) pinning that `chapterNumber` means "the lesson's FIRST spine index" everywhere — it is the join key for `corpora/<n>.json`, `runDirOrderContext`, `loadPriorChapterItems` and `chapterCachePath`, and nothing states it once. This is documentation of an invariant that four modules already depend on.

allFindings.title: SKILL.md documents a Reopen flow that no longer exists; the recovery path for a mis-clicked Mark done is impossible
allFindings.evidence: .claude/skills/build-anki-deck/SKILL.md:362-363 ("It refuses while the lesson is `done` … **Reopen** first, then Unreview"), :428-429 ("A **done** lesson opens read-only (a VIEW … only action **Reopen**); the edit path for a shipped lesson is Reopen → change → Mark done"), :611 ("rebuilds are automatic on Mark done / Reopen"), :612 ("A spot-check is: Reopen a done lesson → …"), and references/audio-pipeline.md ("a done lesson opens as a read-only view whose only action is **Reopen**"). Reality: `grep -rni reopen src/` returns nothing. src/server/pages.js:344-348 — a done lesson renders only `✓ done`, with the code comment "a done lesson stays fully editable; the badge just names its state"; the Unreview button is rendered ONLY when NOT done. src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:56-58 "The clearing form has no UI (done lessons stay editable)" and :141-145 — `unmarkCardsReviewed` hard-refuses while done. Removed in commit 289f64b "Remove the reopen flow: done lessons stay fully editable"; recorded in .harness/custom/docs/LIMITATIONS.md:1358-1372 ("No un-done control in the dashboard"). README.md:95-98 states the CORRECT behaviour ("Marking a lesson done never locks it"). Worse, the most recent SKILL.md commit touching this area (aa1d150, "Document the direct-edit path for field-only fixes on done units") ADDED Reopen prose after the button was already gone.
allFindings.recommendation: Rewrite SKILL.md Step 3's Unreview paragraph and Step 4's done-lesson paragraph against the code: a done lesson stays fully editable, there is no Reopen and no un-done control, and pulling a unit out of the shipping deck means deleting `meta.done` from cards.json by hand plus a rebuild (LIMITATIONS.md:1367-1370 already has the wording). Also move the Unreview button's real location (audio stage, not-done only) into Step 3. Mechanizable follow-up, not agentic: either add the guarded un-done control LIMITATIONS.md's "when to revisit" already anticipates, or add `scripts/undone-unit.mjs <runDir>` that clears `meta.done`, backs up, and rebuilds — so the one operation that touches a delivered unit is a reviewed script rather than an improvised hand edit.

allFindings.title: SKILL.md still names every package `deck.apkg`; the code renamed them, and SKILL.md contradicts itself
allFindings.evidence: src/deck/deckFileName.js:45-47 `deckFileNameForDir` = `<slugified dir identity>.apkg`; `LEGACY_DECK_FILENAME = "deck.apkg"` is only a read fallback (:58-66). On disk there is no `deck.apkg` anywhere: `find output -name '*.apkg'` returns only `japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana.apkg` and `nihongo-101-course-n5.apkg`. SKILL.md still says `deck.apkg` at :456 (Step 5), :467 (Step 6), :475 (Step 7 — "select the book/course-level `deck.apkg`"), :591, :622, :632, :636, :642, :645 (the State & artifacts tree). SKILL.md contradicts ITSELF: its own gate-2 watcher snippet at :108-109 uses `APKG=<bookDir>/<book-slug>.apkg`, and its serve section at :611 says "there is one `.apkg` per group" while the tree at :632/:645 shows a `deck.apkg` in every unit dir (none exist). docs/PIPELINE.md:506,524 and README.md:107 both document the rename correctly — SKILL.md is the only stale file.
allFindings.recommendation: Sweep all nine `deck.apkg` occurrences in SKILL.md to `<slug>.apkg` and fix the State & artifacts tree (unit dirs hold no package by default; there is one package per group). Cheap mechanization: a docs lint in `npm run ci` that greps the skill + docs for `deck.apkg` outside an explicitly-marked legacy note, since this exact string is what the gate-2 watcher and Step 7 hand-off both depend on.

allFindings.title: The test suite writes into the live .anki-builder EPUB library that the daily deck's backward-dedup reads from
allFindings.evidence: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json` exists alongside the real book `1fab0f99d1195ad9`, mtime 14 Aug 12:10 (today). Its content is a unit-test fixture verbatim: `{"epubHash":"h1","chapterNumber":2,"chapterLabel":"Uch","items":[{"id":"a","english":"one","target":"いち"}]}`. Source: test/server/index.test.js:1233-1255 `unpreparedFixture` + the test at :1319 ("a prepared lesson passes the gate and signs off normally") which POSTs `/review/reviewed` with `editDeps` — and `editDeps` (test/server/index.test.js:60-68) stubs fonts, TTS, API key and trim but NOT `saveChapterCorpus`. src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:109-123 therefore calls the real `saveChapterCorpus`, which with no `libraryHomeDir` override writes to the developer's real library (src/corpus/epubLibrary.js:15,107,115). Only one other test (:563-564) bothers to stub it.
allFindings.recommendation: Point the whole suite at a temp library home: give `startDeckServer` a required-in-tests `libraryHomeDir` (or set `ANKI_BUILDER_HOME` in a `node --test` setup file) and add the stub to the shared `editDeps`. Then add a guard in src/corpus/epubLibrary.js that refuses a write to the default home when `NODE_ENV=test`/`node:test` is active — src/util/testEnv.js already has `assertExternalCallAllowed`, so the idiom exists. Today's leak is benign because `h1` is not a real hash; a fixture that ever reuses `1fab0f99d1195ad9`, or a test exercising `removeChapterCorpus`, would silently rewrite the dedup library every later chapter of the live book reads.

allFindings.title: Nothing in code stops an extras unit's epubHash from overwriting its base lesson's dedup-library entry — the guard is prose only
allFindings.evidence: references/extras-pass.md:71-73 states the rule and its consequence ("**NO `epubHash`.** The dedup library is keyed by `(epubHash, chapterNumber)`, so an extras unit carrying one would overwrite its base lesson's entry the moment it is marked reviewed, corrupting every later chapter's backward-dedup"), and :75-82 notes that copying `cards.meta` wholesale "is the obvious thing to do and nothing ever complained". But src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:109-124 (`markCardsReviewed`) does exactly `const { epubHash, chapterNumber } = data.meta; if (epubHash && chapterNumber != null) saveChapterCorpus(...)` with no check of the unit's identity. All 14 shipped extras units currently comply (probe: every `chapter-*-extras/cards.json` has `'epubHash' in meta === false`), and each shares its base lesson's `chapterNumber` (14, 15, 17, …) — so a single copied field would collide exactly as described. Preflight (scripts/preflight.mjs) does not check it either.
allFindings.recommendation: Mechanize: in `markCardsReviewed`, skip (or throw) the library save when the run dir basename matches `-extras$` — the same `UNIT_DIR_PATTERN` regex already lives in src/deck/deckFileName.js:24 and is duplicated in rebuild.js and adapters/stage.js, so factor it once. Add the mirror check to scripts/preflight.mjs ("no `-extras` unit carries an epubHash"), which already loads every unit's meta. This is a two-line deterministic guard on a silent-corruption path; it does not constrain any judgment the agentic pass makes.

allFindings.title: `npm run preflight` silently skips output/templates entirely, then prints "preflight clean"
allFindings.evidence: scripts/preflight.mjs:31 `for (const group of ["epubs", "courses"])` — templates are never enumerated; and even if they were, `loadUnits` (:45-49) only matches `^(chapter|lesson)-\d+(-extras)?$`, whereas a template unit lives at `templates/<name>/<lang>/`. Verified by running it read-only: output covered only `japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana` and `nihongo-101-course-n5`, then printed `preflight clean` with no mention that a third source type exists. SKILL.md:119-125 states the rule unconditionally ("**Run `npm run preflight` BEFORE you hand over a review link**") and :546 describes it as "every book + course", so the doc is honest but the workflow rule is not scoped. This is the path with zero worked examples (`output/templates/` is empty) and the only open backlog task (.harness/tracking/TASKS.json — T011 "End-to-end: build a real travel deck + verify in Anki", the sole non-done task of 11). By contrast scripts/validate-decks.mjs:30-38 walks recursively and DOES cover templates.
allFindings.recommendation: Either extend `collectionDirs()`/`loadUnits` to the `templates/<name>/<lang>` shape (validate-decks.mjs's `unitDirs` generator is the working precedent to reuse), or — minimum — make `--all` print an explicit `(templates: N unit(s) not covered by preflight)` line so "preflight clean" never means "I did not look". Same silent-degradation signature the repo's own LIMITATIONS.md catalogs repeatedly.

allFindings.title: Preflight's report-only lines have never been zero: 7 marker-audible clips and 17 duplicate-target groups are in the shipped, daily-studied deck
allFindings.evidence: Read-only run of `node scripts/preflight.mjs --all` on the live tree reports for `japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana`: `· duplicates 17 target group(s) spanning units` and `· audio 7 clip(s) flagged marker-audible: chapter-9-extras/p9-iie-zenzen-yomimasen, chapter-9-extras/v9-otosan-ni-denwa, chapter-10/hontouni-samui-ne, chapter-12/nihon-no-supa-desu-yo, chapter-13-extras/koko-ni-imasu-a, chapter-14/kuremasu-exception, chapter-14/karimasendeshita` — then `preflight clean`. All 29 units of that book carry `meta.done === true` (probe over every `chapter-*/cards.json`), and preflight filters `!i.excluded`, so those 7 clips are shipping. SKILL.md:405-406 and references/audio-pipeline.md say a marker-stuck card should be regenerated or hand-trimmed "rather than ship audible nonsense"; scripts/preflight.mjs:164 downgrades it to "heuristic, so a note rather than a failure".
allFindings.recommendation: Two changes. (a) Make marker-stuck a FAILURE for any not-yet-done unit and a note only for already-done ones — the rule the prose states, applied at the moment it is still cheap. (b) Give the duplicate-targets line a persistable acknowledgement (a per-book `preflight-ack.json` listing reviewed group keys) so the count that prints is *unreviewed* groups; a `·` line that has printed non-zero on every run since it was written carries no information, which is exactly how the 3-lessons-missing-from-dedup and isStageOwnedCard incidents in LIMITATIONS.md read. Separately, triage the 7 named clips — they are in a live collection now.

allFindings.title: The review watcher is 40 lines of prose shell retyped four times per chapter, carrying four hard-won bug rules as prose
allFindings.evidence: .claude/skills/build-anki-deck/SKILL.md:56-136 — an 80-line section whose payload is two shell snippets the agent must reproduce correctly on every gate. The four rules it encodes were each learned from a real incident: absolute `RUN` path (a relative one after a `cd` made every poll throw MODULE_NOT_FOUND, :89-98), separate readability probe with no `2>/dev/null`, artifact-freshness rather than flag-only checking after gate 2 (:99-118), and a bounded wait with a stated timeout. It is executed 4× per chapter (2 units × 2 gates); for the 15-chapter book already built that is ~60 hand-transcribed copies. Drift is already visible inside the snippet itself: the gate-2 example hardcodes `APKG=<bookDir>/<book-slug>.apkg` while Step 6 six screens later says the file is `deck.apkg` (see generalist-2), so the copy that is right and the copy that is wrong sit in the same file. Commits ea7a5f7/597a6e6 ("Stop the review watcher from failing silently") and 853ad23 ("stop watching the flag instead of the artifact") are both fixes to this prose.
allFindings.recommendation: Check in `scripts/await-review.mjs <runDir> --gate 1|2 [--timeout 30m] [--book-dir <dir>]`: resolves the run dir to an absolute path itself, fails loud if cards.json is unreadable, polls `meta.reviewed`/`meta.done`, for gate 2 additionally compares `resolveDeckPathForDir(bookDir)` mtime against cards.json (reusing src/deck/deckFileName.js so the filename can never drift again), prints a sparse heartbeat to stdout, and exits 0/1/2/3 with the same semantics the prose defines. SKILL.md then keeps the *judgment* (arm a watcher, tell the user, never set the flag yourself) and drops the transcription. This is the clearest "mechanize opportunistically" win in the repo: it removes zero judgment and four failure modes.

allFindings.title: `prepare` runs five LLM passes; SKILL.md and PIPELINE.md both document four — the number-readings pass is undocumented and overloads the `uncertain` badge
allFindings.evidence: src/cli/commands/prepare.js:225-258 runs a fifth pass after cross-lesson notes: `findUnreadableNumbers` → `ctx.fillNumberReadings` (src/cards/numberReadings.js, prompt docs/number-reading-prompt.md, its own `claude -p` call). SKILL.md:312-326 lists exactly four ("Translate, Fill-in-the-blank enrichment, Semantic de-dup, Cross-lesson notes") and SKILL.md:514 repeats the four-item list; `grep -rn 'number-reading|numberReading' docs/PIPELINE.md` returns nothing. The pass also logs "filled N card(s), each flagged uncertain so you check the counter" (prepare.js:248) — but references/card-authoring-rules.md defines `uncertain` as "the extractor flagged it as possibly premature or already taught", so at gate 1 the same badge now carries two unrelated meanings with no way to tell them apart.
allFindings.recommendation: Add the fifth pass to SKILL.md's ordered `prepare` list and to PIPELINE.md's stage walkthrough (it is the pass that produces the `reading` field card-authoring-rules.md devotes a whole section to, so its absence is a real navigational hole). Separately, either give the machine-filled cards a distinguishing `reviewNote` (cheap, matches how semanticDedup already explains itself) or a distinct flag, so a reviewer at gate 1 knows whether "Uncertain" means "maybe premature" or "check this counter".

allFindings.title: Stale model comments claim a Haiku pass; no doc states the real per-pass model/effort or the serial spawnSync cost
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js:83 — "The only per-item judgment call this makes is category assignment, via a small batched Haiku pass" — but that module calls `defaultRunClaude` with no `scopeEnvPrefix`, so src/util/runClaude.js:7-8 resolves `claude-sonnet-5` / effort `medium`; and :10 in the same file says `BATCH_SIZE = Infinity` ("one call for the whole lesson"), so "small batched" is wrong twice over. src/corpus/epubLlmExtract.js:7 also reasons about "prose commentary … from Haiku specifically". Cost picture nobody documents: runClaude.js:69 uses `spawnSync`, so every pass is serial and blocking, each with a 10-minute ceiling and one retry (:56-62); a chapter is two units × ~5 prepare passes plus the assemble-side extraction/conventions/taught-index/forward-flag/pedagogical-sort passes, i.e. roughly 15-20 serial `claude -p` invocations before any human sees a card.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the two comments, then add a single table to docs/PIPELINE.md: pass → module → prompt file → model/effort → env override → batched? → typical wall-clock. Idea #13 in the ideas inbox asked for exactly this inventory a month ago and it is still open. It is also the cheapest way to make the pinning auditable: today the only way to answer "what model runs the extraction?" is to trace `scopeEnvPrefix` through runClaude's three-level `firstSet`.

allFindings.title: .bak convention has no pruning and silently collides; stale review-*.html artifacts contradict SKILL.md's own claim that they don't exist
allFindings.evidence: 330 `.bak` files / ~10 MB under output/ (`find output -name '*.bak' | wc -l`); `output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana/chapter-5/` alone holds 22, e.g. `cards.json.pre-scene.bak`, `.pre-enhance.bak`, `.pre-hint.bak`, `.pre-jumble.bak`, `.pre-romanize.bak`. The convention is mandated by SKILL.md:440 ("Back the file up first (`<file>.pre-<reason>.bak`, the convention the migrations use)") but has no naming uniqueness and no retention rule — references/card-authoring-rules.md explicitly warns that re-running enhance-card-notes.mjs "overwrites their `.pre-enhance.bak` backups", i.e. the restore point the convention exists to create is destroyed by the second run of the same tool. Separately the same run dirs still contain `review-corpus.html`, `review-translate.html`, `review-audio.html` from a removed feature; nothing in src/ writes those names any more, while SKILL.md:624 asserts "there are no per-stage HTML review artifacts" and audio-pipeline.md repeats it.
allFindings.recommendation: (a) Make the backup helper stamp the filename (`<file>.pre-<reason>-<YYYYMMDDHHmm>.bak`) so a second run of a tool can never clobber the first run's restore point, and add a `scripts/prune-baks.mjs` (keep newest N per unit) the way anki-backups/ pruning already works (references/deliver.md:386-389 documents that precedent, including the 780 MB incident that motivated it). (b) Delete the three stale `review-*.html` per unit, or the doc claim is falsifiable by any agent that runs `ls` — and an agent that Reads `review-corpus.html` would be acting on a months-old card set.

allFindings.title: IDEAS.jsonl is four weeks stale and several rows describe work that has since shipped
allFindings.evidence: .harness/tracking/IDEAS.jsonl holds 13 rows, newest `capturedAt` 2026-07-19T23:19:52Z against today's 2026-08-14 — no capture in ~4 weeks despite ~40 commits in that window. At least four rows are already built: #5 "Manual/interactive corpus entry flow" is the shipped `assemble --words` path (src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js, SKILL.md Step 2); #10 "Extraction: build cards from fill-in-the-blank examples" is src/cards/fillInBlank.js + docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md; #9/#11 (bracket-free variants, Cartesian variant picker) are src/audio/variants.js's comma × brackets product with the dashboard Generate modal, described in references/audio-pipeline.md; #13's inventory is answerable now. Meanwhile TASKS.json has exactly one non-done task (T011), so the backlog is effectively empty and the inbox is the only queue.
allFindings.recommendation: Run the convert-ideas sweep, but reconcile-first: any row whose described feature now exists should be dropped, not converted, or the sweep will author tasks to rebuild shipped work. Rows #8 (validate lesson discovery across several EPUBs) and #12 (two specific bad JBP cards) are the two that still have real value — #8 in particular is the documented mitigation for the biggest known cliff (the parser is proven on one book). Worth a per-row `supersededBy` field or a one-line staleness check in the capture skill, since a month-old inbox will keep re-accruing this.

allFindings.title: Zero tests for scripts/ — including the two checks the recent frontier promoted to the pre-review safety net and the two --apply mutators
allFindings.evidence: `ls test/` shows anki, audio, cards, cli, corpus, deck, docs, model, review, server, support, translate, util — there is no `test/scripts/`. 13 files / 1,653 LOC under scripts/ are untested wiring, including scripts/preflight.mjs (175 L) and scripts/validate-decks.mjs (60 L), both npm-wired and both positioned by SKILL.md:119-125 and :559-567 as the gate that must pass before a human sees a unit; scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs and scripts/extras-order.mjs, which MUTATE signed-off units under `--apply`; and scripts/deliver-to-anki.mjs, which touches the live collection. Their underlying logic modules ARE tested (test/cards/extrasTools.test.js, test/deck/shippableCards, test/model), so the untested surface is exactly the wiring — which is where finding generalist-5 (templates never enumerated) and generalist-6 (marker-stuck downgraded to a note) both live.
allFindings.recommendation: Add `test/scripts/preflight.test.js` and `validateDecks.test.js` that build a tiny fixture output root (books + courses + a template + one deliberately-broken unit of each kind) and assert on exit code and which units were reported — three fixtures would have caught both. Given `/output` is gitignored these are pure temp-dir tests, so they belong in `npm run ci` unlike the commands themselves. Do NOT test the `--apply` mutators against real dirs; test their pure planners and keep the mutation a thin wrapper.

allFindings.title: A foreign book's .apkg sits inside the course output dir, and the course is missing lesson-1
allFindings.evidence: `ls output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/` shows `japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana.apkg` alongside the legitimate `nihongo-101-course-n5.apkg`, plus `lesson-0`, `lesson-2`, `lesson-3` — no `lesson-2`-preceding `lesson-1`. `resolveDeckPathForDir` (src/deck/deckFileName.js:67-73) computes the right name from the dir path so builds and the deliverer are unaffected, but SKILL.md Step 7 tells the user "File → Import in Anki, select the book/course-level `deck.apkg`" — a user or agent picking "the .apkg in the course folder" has a 50% chance of importing an entire foreign 2,009-card book into a 241-card course, a fresh import into a collection that is studied daily.
allFindings.recommendation: Remove the stray file, and harden Step 7 to name the package via `resolveDeckPathForDir` rather than "the .apkg in the folder" (which also fixes generalist-2's Step 7 instance). Optional cheap guard: have preflight warn on any `.apkg` in a collection dir whose name is not `deckFileNameForDir(dir)`. Separately, confirm whether the missing `lesson-1` is intentional — `nextLessonNumber` will happily hand out 4 next and leave the hole permanent.

allFindings.title: Collision audits are per-book, but the learner studies one collection — 47 cross-deck target dupes and 10 uncued ambiguous English prompts ship today
allFindings.evidence: scripts/extras-collision-audit.mjs:18-35 resolves a single <book-dir> and globs only ^(chapter|lesson)-N(-extras)?$ inside it; scripts/preflight.mjs runs the same findCollisions per dir. Probe across output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana (1,914 live cards) + output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5 (236 live cards), both delivered to the same live collection: 47 shared targets with different glosses (おはようございます 'Good morning.' vs 'Good morning'; イギリス 'United Kingdom' vs 'UK'; ちゅうごくじん 'Chinese (person)' vs 'Chinese Person'), and 10 shared English glosses with different targets — 'Nice to meet you.' → はじめまして vs よろしくおねがいします, 'Yes' → ええ vs はい, 'Bag' → ふくろ vs かばん, 'This one' → これ vs こちら. Within a single book the same probe finds 0 uncued members, so the doctrine works; only its scope is wrong.
allFindings.recommendation: Mechanizable, no agentic judgment needed for DETECTION: teach preflight.mjs a collection-wide mode that loads every unit under output/epubs/* and output/courses/* (or, better, every deck listed in an anki-delivered.json) into one findCollisions call and reports cross-deck groups separately from in-book ones. Keep the FIX agentic (merge-vs-cue is a judgment about the source material, exactly as the in-book audit already argues). Also add a line to references/card-authoring-rules.md §'A cue is mandatory on an English-gloss or target collision' saying the deck boundary is not the interference boundary — Anki interleaves every deck the learner studies that day.

allFindings.title: A note's two directions get consecutive due positions and the shipped deck config disables sibling burying — the second direction is answered from working memory
allFindings.evidence: src/deck/collection.js:526-529 — `for (let ord = 0; ord < 2; ord++) { insertCard.run(cardId, noteId, deckId, ord, nowSeconds, position); position++; }` gives Recognition and Production of the same note adjacent new-card positions. src/deck/collection.js:392-401 ships `new: { bury: false, ..., order: 1, perDay: 20 }` and `rev: { bury: false, ... }`. Nothing in .claude/skills/build-anki-deck/**, docs/ or README.md mentions bury, siblings, deck presets or new-card limits (grep for bury/sibling/perDay/preset returns only unrelated 'sibling unit' prose).
allFindings.recommendation: Two cheap, scheduling-safe changes. (1) Flip `new.bury` and `rev.bury` to true in buildDconf — this only affects a fresh .apkg import, never existing scheduling. (2) Interleave positions so the two ords of one note are not adjacent (e.g. emit all ord=0 for a unit, then all ord=1, or offset ord=1 by the unit size) — new-card order only, no id or guid change. Because the AnkiConnect path never applies dconf, also add one line to references/deliver.md telling the owner to enable 'Bury new siblings' / 'Bury review siblings' on the preset his book decks use; that is the only place a delivered deck can get it.

allFindings.title: Every note unconditionally generates both directions — there is no way to ship a recognition-only or production-only card, which is what makes the leaky-scene tension cost real reps
allFindings.evidence: src/deck/collection.js:526 hardcodes two cards per note; `req: [[0,'any',[0]],[1,'any',[2]]]` (collection.js:317-320) makes generation depend only on Target/English being non-empty, and both are required on every card. Consequence in the live deck: に ships 6 cards whose Recognition fronts are all the bare string に, disambiguated by scenes that are near-paraphrases of the answers ('marking a point in time' → 'At, in, on (particle)'; 'marking where someone is heading' → 'To (particle, indicates direction of movement)'). LIMITATIONS.md:1373-1388 documents this as an accepted leak. Same shape for the 22 'Nth of the month' recitation cards in chapter-7 and the counter series.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a per-card `direction`/`recognitionOnly`/`productionOnly` flag and gate it in the templates, which Anki supports natively: prefix each qfmt with a conditional on a new field (e.g. `{{^NoRecog}}…{{/NoRecog}}`) so an empty front suppresses card generation. Author-side selection stays agentic (only a human/LLM can say 'this scene leaks, drop the Recognition direction'). NOTE the ordering dependency: this cannot reach the live collection until learner-4 is fixed, and suppressing a direction on an already-delivered note leaves a live orphan card (learner-10) — so ship it with a suspend path, not silently.

allFindings.title: The deliverer force-syncs fields and CSS but has no path to ADD a template — the 'two delivery paths can never drift' guarantee is false for any card-design change that adds a direction
allFindings.evidence: src/anki/deliver.js:216-232 has an explicit add-missing-field loop (`client.modelFieldAdd(...)` plus `modelFieldReposition`), but src/anki/deliver.js:234-248 computes `tmplChanged` from `!live || live.Front !== t.qfmt || live.Back !== t.afmt` and then calls `updateModelTemplates` with a map that includes the unknown name — AnkiConnect's updateModelTemplates only rewrites templates that already exist by name; there is no createTemplate/modelTemplateAdd call anywhere in the repo (grep). Removal is likewise unhandled. The comment at src/deck/collection.js:162-166 claims the shared CARD_TEMPLATES constant means 'the two delivery paths can never drift'.
allFindings.recommendation: Either (a) add a template-add path (AnkiConnect `modelTemplateAdd`, guarded and reported like `addedFields`, with a loud warning that N new cards will be generated for every existing note — new cards only, existing scheduling untouched, so it is red-line-safe), or (b) if adding templates is deliberately out of scope, make that explicit: detect a spec template with no live counterpart and FAIL the deliver with 'this note type gained a card template; add it by hand in Anki first', instead of pushing an update whose behavior is undefined. Fix the overclaiming comment at collection.js:162-166 either way.

allFindings.title: Nothing in the pipeline ever renders an actual card face — every review gate is a table, so face-level defects are only discoverable after they are being studied
allFindings.evidence: output/epubs/.../chapter-5/review-corpus.html headers are `# | English | Category | Target | Reading (spoken) | Flags | Note` — scene and hint are not even columns. The dashboard (src/review/deckViewChrome.js:275-277) stacks scene above hint in one shared 'hint-col' cell with a title tooltip. Neither surface applies CARD_TEMPLATES or BASE_CSS from src/deck/collection.js:167-261. The 'answerable alone' and 'scene must not reveal the answer' rules (references/card-authoring-rules.md:191-282) are precisely questions about the rendered FRONT, and the reviewer never sees one.
allFindings.recommendation: Cheap and highly mechanizable because the templates are already single-source: add a card-face preview (a per-card flip toggle in the dashboard, and/or a `review-faces.html` artifact) that renders the real qfmt/afmt with the real CSS for BOTH directions, populated from cards.json. This is the highest-leverage change for card quality per line of code — it turns 'is this scene leaking?' from a doctrine the agent must simulate in its head into something the human sees at Gate 1.

allFindings.title: The prompt is the smallest text on the card — Target/English render bare at 20px while the answer renders at 26px bold
allFindings.evidence: src/deck/collection.js:173 and :183 emit `{{Target}}` / `{{English}}` with no wrapping element or class; the only size they get is `.card { font-size: 20px }` (collection.js:194-200). The back wraps the answer as `<div class="answer">` at `font-size: 26px; font-weight: 600` (collection.js:214-218). So the kana string the learner must actually decode on the Recognition front is 20px, and the identical string shown as an ANSWER on the Production back is 26px bold. `languageFontCss` (src/deck/fontLibrary.js:68-73) also applies the Japanese webfont to `.card` wholesale, so the English gloss, notes and hints all render in it too.
allFindings.recommendation: Wrap both prompts in `<div class="prompt">` and give `.prompt` the same 26px/600 treatment as `.answer` (or larger for the target-script side). Scope the language font to a `.target`/`.prompt` class rather than `.card` so Latin text keeps a Latin face. Both are single-source edits in collection.js and propagate to the live collection on the next deliver (CSS and template text ARE force-synced — see deliver.js:234-255 — unlike template addition).

allFindings.title: Back-of-card note and front hint/scene text fail WCAG AA contrast in light mode
allFindings.evidence: src/deck/collection.js:224-233 — `.note-back { font-size: 14px; color: #888888 }` gives ~3.9:1 on white, and `.hint-front { font-size: 13px; color: #9a9284 }` gives ~3.1:1; AA for text under 18pt requires 4.5:1. `.pron` (#555555, ~7.5:1) is fine, and the night-mode overrides at collection.js:243-261 are all comfortably above AA (#a3a09a on #2c2c2e ≈ 5.4:1). So the defect is light mode only — and the hint/scene is the one thing on the front the learner needs BEFORE answering.
allFindings.recommendation: Darken `.note-back` to ~#5f5f5f and `.hint-front` to ~#6f6858 (both keep the visual hierarchy while clearing 4.5:1), or bump the two to 15px/14px. One-line CSS change in the single-source BASE_CSS; reaches the live collection on the next deliver via updateModelStyling.

allFindings.title: Fill-in-blank cards are not cloze drills — they ship as whole-sentence translation pairs, some 95 characters and three clauses long, with same-frame siblings that differ only in a proper noun
allFindings.evidence: 127 live `fillInBlank` cards across the book; src/cards/fillInBlank.js:159-190 stores the COMPLETED sentence as `target`/`english` — no blank survives into the card. Real examples in chapter-1: 'Nice to meet you. I am Brown of the Bank of London. I look forward to working with you.' → はじめまして。ロンドンぎんこうのブラウンです。よろしくおねがいします (a 3-sentence Production card), and `fib-c1-confirm-hoffman` / `fib-c1-confirm-brown` are the same frame with the proper nouns swapped. A frame-normalizing probe (proper nouns → X, digits → N) finds 12 frames of 3+ cards covering 64 live cards. 31 live cards have English ≥60 chars.
allFindings.recommendation: Two things, both authorable in docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md and enforceable in preflight.mjs. (1) A length ceiling on the PRODUCTION face: a drill longer than ~one clause should either be split (the split rule already exists at references/card-authoring-rules.md:180-183 for Q&A pairs — extend it to multi-sentence drills) or shipped Recognition-only once learner-3 lands. (2) A mechanical near-sibling check: group drills by proper-noun/digit-normalized English and warn when a frame has 3+ members, so the extras/dedup pass sees what semanticDedup's per-lesson view misses (the 6-member 'X he is X' frame spans chapter-1 and chapter-1-extras).

allFindings.title: The Reading field is populated on 136 cards and shipped into Anki but rendered by neither template — the learner never sees the intended kana reading of a numeral target
allFindings.evidence: src/deck/collection.js:28 declares the field, :461-463 populates it ('stored, not yet rendered by the templates'), and it appears in neither qfmt nor afmt (collection.js:167-191). Live example: `taoru-o-yonmai-kudasai` ships target タオルを４まいください with reading タオルをよんまいください; the Recognition front shows a raw Arabic numeral in an otherwise all-kana deck and the back never states よんまい. The only place the counter reading surfaces is the romaji Pronunciation ('taoru o yon-mai kudasai'), which trains romaji dependence — and is exactly the crutch that breaks the moment the kanji era arrives, which is the stated reason the field exists.
allFindings.recommendation: Render `{{Reading}}` on the BACK of both templates when it differs from Target (Anki has no field-comparison conditional, so either gate on a separate populated-only field or simply always show it — it is only set on 136 cards). This is a two-line template change that ships to the live collection via updateModelTemplates. Doing it now also de-risks the kanji migration, which is the one scenario where a Reading-less Recognition card becomes genuinely unanswerable.

allFindings.title: A card excluded after delivery is never suspended — the learner keeps drilling a card they explicitly killed, forever
allFindings.evidence: src/anki/deliver.js:441-444 collects `r.orphaned` for every abid-tagged note whose card id left the corpus, and scripts/deliver-to-anki.mjs:93 prints '⚠ orphaned in Anki (kept)'. Nothing suspends, tags or buries it. SKILL.md:446-447 states the consequence plainly ('reports it and never deletes it, so removing it is a manual step'). 95 cards in the JBP book are currently `excluded`; any of those excluded after the 2026-08-14 delivery are live cards with live scheduling.
allFindings.recommendation: Suspending is not deleting — it preserves the card, its interval and its revlog, and is one click to reverse, so it does not touch the owner's red line the way deletion would. Add an opt-in `--suspend-orphans` to deliver-to-anki.mjs that calls AnkiConnect `suspend` on the orphans' cards and adds a marker tag (e.g. `abid-orphan`), reported exactly like the current list. This also unblocks learner-3 and learner-11, both of which produce orphans as a side effect of the fix.

allFindings.title: The LIMITATIONS entry on degenerate uncued pairs is stale — two of its three examples no longer exist, and the third is now cued
allFindings.evidence: .harness/custom/docs/LIMITATIONS.md:1379-1385 states that three pairs 'were left with no scene at all' and 'still show identical Recognition fronts with different expected answers': です ('To be' vs 'Is / am / are'), ばん ('Evening' vs the number suffix), ばんごはん ('Dinner' twice). Probing the live corpus: です has exactly one live card (chapter-1, 'To be (copula)'), ばんごはん has exactly one (chapter-8), and ばん's two cards BOTH carry scenes ('the time of day' / 'labelling something by its number'). The duplicates were evidently merged/excluded and the entry was never updated, so it now overstates the deck's defect load and points a future reader at a fix that is already done.
allFindings.recommendation: Update or close the entry (the 'When to revisit' remedy — merge each pair into one card with a combined gloss — appears to be what actually happened). More generally: LIMITATIONS entries that assert a live-data fact ('three pairs still ship uncued') are the ones that rot; where the fact is checkable, cite the script that checks it (extras-collision-audit / preflight) rather than freezing a count, so a stale entry is caught by running the audit instead of by re-deriving it.

allFindings.title: ~1,900 hand-curated audio clips exist but are never the QUESTION — the deck has no listening direction
allFindings.evidence: All 1,914 live cards have an `audio` file (probe: zero live cards without one), each one auditioned through the variant/trim/manual-cut review described in references/audio-pipeline.md:70-108 at real ElevenLabs cost. In src/deck/collection.js:173 `{{Audio}}` sits on the Recognition FRONT beside the Target it voices (so it is reinforcement, never a test) and at collection.js:189 on the Production BACK (after the answer). No template makes audio the prompt.
allFindings.recommendation: A third 'Listening' template (front `{{Audio}}` + `{{Scene}}`, back Target + English + Pronunciation) would be near-free in content terms and is the biggest available gain in what the deck actually trains — but it triples the daily load on an already ~4,300-card collection, so it belongs behind the same per-card direction flag as learner-3 (opt in for sentences, skip for recitation series), and it cannot ship at all until learner-4 gives the deliverer a template-add path. Flagging as low severity because it is an enhancement, not a defect; noting it because the audio investment is currently under-monetized as pure decoration.

allFindings.title: Injected BOOK_CONVENTIONS countermands the extraction rules with no precedence rule — verified content loss
allFindings.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:11-13 injects {{BOOK_CONVENTIONS}} near the TOP, ~135 lines before the rules it can conflict with, with only "apply it alongside (not instead of) the general guidance below" — which never says who wins a conflict. docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:146-152 says the EXERCISES section is a card source and that a paradigm table introduced by _"repeat the verbs below and memorize their forms"_ is reference material to "Extract in full"; :126 says reference charts rendered as images are extraction targets. The cached conventions for the only real book (.anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/conventions.md, §"Exercise Section Markers (skip these)") says the opposite twice and by name: "Verb/adjective conjugation tables are sometimes rendered as images inside EXERCISES — treat these as exercise material to skip", and lists "ch. 32 Page_117_Image_0013.jpg (あります/います conjugation table)" under "still exercise material". EMPIRICAL: chapters/32.xhtml:474 is verbatim "Repeat the verbs below and memorize their forms—present and past, affirmative and negative" followed by that image; I read the image — a 2×4 grid (あります/ありません/ありました/ありませんでした, います/いません/いました/いませんでした). output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana/chapter-12/cards.json contains ZERO of those forms as cards (only なにもありません / だれもいません, which come from drill e.g.-lines). Timestamps: conventions.md 14 Jul, docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md 9 Aug — nothing invalidates the cached conventions when the prompt's policy changes. The conventions prompt itself seeds the conflict: docs/epub-book-conventions-prompt.md asks for "what does a practice exercise or drill section look like, that should be SKIPPED rather than extracted".
allFindings.recommendation: Three changes, all prompt-side and all compatible with staying agentic. (a) Move the {{BOOK_CONVENTIONS}} block AFTER the extraction rules and add an explicit precedence sentence: conventions are authoritative about MARKUP/where things are, never about WHAT to extract; on any conflict the rules above win. (b) Reword docs/epub-book-conventions-prompt.md so it asks the conventions pass to describe drill markup structurally without prescribing skip/extract policy, and to classify reference-tables-inside-exercises as reference. (c) Mechanize a staleness link: store the extraction-prompt hash alongside conventions.md and warn (not block) when the prompt changed after the conventions were generated, so a re-run is a decision rather than an oversight.

allFindings.title: The dialogue ban (Step 1) and the worked-example requirement (Step 2) are mutually unsatisfiable
allFindings.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:174 is absolute: "Do not extract dialogue lines, reactions, or recap sentences, even ones that seem useful — treat the whole dialogue as off-limits". docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:186-190 then requires "the corpus contains at least one full example sentence that actually uses that form in context" for every Grammar & Function Words item, and says "a line of a dialogue that contains the form all satisfy the requirement, and you must NOT duplicate it" — but a dialogue line was removed from the corpus by :174, so it satisfies nothing the learner will ever see, and :190 even directs the model to "Check the SPEAKING PRACTICE / dialogue sections specifically". EMPIRICAL: in the reviewed corpus .anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/corpora/32.json, item 10 `nihon-no-supa-desu-yo` / にほんのスパですよ is a verbatim TARGET DIALOGUE line (chapters/32.xhtml:31) — extracted in violation of :174, evidently to give the particle よ (item 9) its worked example. Item 64 インドのどこですか likewise comes from the SPEAKING PRACTICE dialogue (:775-786). The ban's cost is also undone downstream: output/.../chapter-12-extras/cards.json re-mines the same dialogue (どようびにエマさんとにっこうにいきます, おおきいおてらやじんじゃがあります, …).
allFindings.recommendation: Resolve the conflict explicitly rather than leaving the model to arbitrate. Narrow :174 to "do not extract the dialogue wholesale as a script" and add a stated exception: a dialogue line MAY be extracted when it is the only in-chapter demonstration of a function word from Step 2, marked with a reviewNote naming the form it illustrates. Then delete the misleading "a line of a dialogue … satisfies the requirement" clause in Step 2 (it is only true if the exception exists). Keep the judgment agentic; the fix is removing an impossible constraint, not adding a rule.

allFindings.title: Placeholder rules have no branch for discontinuous patterns — a 〜 shipped into the live deck
allFindings.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:52 "**Never leave a placeholder character in the final `target`.**" and :57 "an unresolved placeholder character is never a valid `target`" — the hardest constraint in the prompt. It then offers exactly TWO branches (:54 the morpheme itself → strip; :55 phrase-level pattern → fill). Chapter 32's vocabulary table (chapters/32.xhtml:706) prints a DISCONTINUOUS circumfix pattern: だれも…〜ません ("no one"), which fits neither branch. The model fell through and copied it verbatim: corpora/32.json item 54 `dare-mo-masen-no-one` has target "だれも…〜ません", carrying both a 〜 and an ellipsis; it passed both gates. Scanning all 15 reviewed corpora, this is the only 〜-in-target survivor (1/1,083 items) — rare, but rare-and-shipped is exactly the class preflight exists for. Compare: extraction-time misses of the Numbers rule (:44) DO get repaired downstream — corpora 22.json/23.json have 9 digit-bearing targets with no `reading`, yet zero such cards survive into output/, because src/cards/numberReadings.js catches them.
allFindings.recommendation: (a) Prompt: add a third placeholder branch for discontinuous/bracketing patterns (X…〜Y) — resolve BOTH slots into one natural utterance (だれも いません) and record the source spelling in reviewNote; state that '…' is a placeholder marker too, alongside 〜/～/~. (b) Mechanize: preflight.mjs should assert /[〜～~]/ never appears in a shipped `target`. The prompt already declares this absolute, so it is a one-line deterministic check with no judgment in it — precisely the 'catch X before the review gate' pattern the recent commits pursue.

allFindings.title: Only two env scopes exist, each bundling passes of wildly different difficulty and blast radius
allFindings.evidence: src/util/runClaude.js pins claude-sonnet-5 / effort medium for every call. Only two scopeEnvPrefix values exist repo-wide: src/translate/runClaude.js:13,24 ("ANKI_BUILDER_TRANSLATE") and src/corpus/epubLlmRunClaude.js:15 ("ANKI_BUILDER_EPUB_LLM"). EPUB_LLM therefore covers, on one knob: chapter extraction (agentic multi-file + image read; misses are structurally invisible — SKILL.md:283 "Nothing downstream can notice what was never extracted"), the whole-book conventions pass, the taught index, forward flags, fill-in-blank mining, and the pedagogical sort. TRANSLATE covers translation, romanization eval, cross-lesson notes, number readings, semantic dedup, and lesson-word category assignment. The blast radii are not comparable: pedagogicalSort.js:71-90 fails open to the original order and can never add/drop/duplicate an item; semanticDedup only ever excludes fillInBlank cards, reviewer-visible and restorable; forward flags are advisory and the prompt explicitly biases toward false positives (docs/epub-forward-flag-prompt.md "a wrongly-flagged item just costs the reviewer a moment's glance"); lesson category assignment fails open to "Other". None of those need Sonnet-medium; extraction and cross-lesson notes are where quality is irreversible. Nothing in the repo sets either scope pair today, so every pass runs the same default.
allFindings.recommendation: Give each wrapper its own scopeEnvPrefix (one-line change per call site; keep the two legacy pairs as fallbacks so nothing breaks). Then, per pass: RAISE extraction to effort high (and consider it for the conventions pass) — it is the only pass whose failure mode is silent and unrecoverable, and it is agentic, which is where effort actually buys reading discipline; KEEP Sonnet-medium for translate, cross-lesson notes, fill-in-blank mining, number readings (the number-reading prompt itself argues 'a plausible-but-wrong reading is worse than no card'); LOWER forward flags, pedagogical sort, semantic dedup, and lesson-word categorization toward Haiku — each is either mechanically validated, fails open, or is explicitly designed around cheap false positives. This is per-pass tuning, not mechanization of judgment; the red line is untouched.

allFindings.title: The heaviest single model call (whole-book conventions) has an honor-system coverage check, while its sibling pass proves mechanical verification works
allFindings.evidence: docs/epub-book-conventions-prompt.md asks one call to Read all {{CHAPTER_COUNT}} chapter files IN FULL plus open images, then self-report gaps in a "## Coverage" section. For the only real book that is 57 files (.anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/chapters/ has 1..57) plus 729 cached images, inside src/util/runClaude.js's 10-minute hard timeout with one retry at the same budget — so a book that legitimately needs longer can never produce conventions at all, and there is no partial-progress path. The output duly self-certifies: conventions.md §Coverage claims "All 57 chapter files were read in full … No chapter was left partially read", which is unverifiable and is exactly the SILENT DEGRADATION signature catalogued in .harness/custom/docs/LIMITATIONS.md. By contrast the taught-index pass, reading the same 57 files, IS verified: docs/epub-taught-index-prompt.md states "This completeness is verified mechanically: a response missing any listed chapter number is rejected outright", and src/corpus/epubTaughtIndex.js:83-88 actually enforces it against the spine list.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a cheap mechanical coverage assertion to the conventions prompt in the taught-index's style: require a per-chapter line in §Coverage carrying a verbatim short quote from a deterministic anchor in that file (e.g. the chapter's <title> text), and have analyzeBookConventions() check each quote against the cached xhtml, failing loudly on a mismatch. That verifies reading happened without constraining what the pass concludes. Separately, consider batching the pass over chapter ranges with a merge step so the 10-minute ceiling stops being a silent quality cap, and raise its effort (see promptengineer-4).

allFindings.title: SKILL.md and extras-pass.md both assert the pipeline never sees images — it does, by design
allFindings.evidence: SKILL.md:280-283: "Every stage of the pipeline reads the stripped-out plain text, so any teaching material the publisher shipped as a picture … is invisible to all of it". references/extras-pass.md:129 heading: "First, look at the chapter's IMAGES (the pipeline never has)", and :135 "Every stage upstream of you works on text". Both are false for the extraction stage: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:121-131 is a dedicated §Images section instructing the model to resolve each relative to the chapter file and open it with its Read tool, and src/corpus/epubArchive.js:577-591 exists solely to make that work ("The image-aware extraction prompt … tells the model to … open it directly — so any referenced image has to actually exist on disk at that resolved location"). I verified path resolution: chapters/32.xhtml:477 references ../images/9781568366333_9781568366340_Page_117_Image_0013.jpg and that exact file is present in .anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/images/. The conventions prompt also opens images and conventions.md has a per-chapter "Image-Embedded Content" list naming ch.32's images by filename. So the manual sweep SKILL.md:286-289 prescribes (grep , unzip from the .epub) re-derives, by hand and from the archive, information that already exists on disk in two places.
allFindings.recommendation: Correct the claim in both files: the extraction and conventions passes DO read images; the residual risk is that they were told to skip some (see promptengineer-1) or under-read at effort medium. Then replace the unzip/grep recipe with the artifacts that already exist — point at .anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/images/ and at conventions.md's per-chapter image list — and reduce the human step to auditing the images conventions.md already flagged for that chapter. This keeps the judgment agentic while removing a per-chapter, repeated, misdirected chore; more importantly, the wrong diagnosis is why the real cause (the conventions/extraction conflict) was never fixed.

allFindings.title: SKILL.md contradicts itself on when Step 3b runs (after Gate 1 vs after Gate 2)
allFindings.evidence: SKILL.md:367: "**Run this for every chapter/lesson, right after the base unit passes Gate 1.**" But SKILL.md:60-61 tells the watcher-driven agent "generate the audio after gate 1, and after gate 2 run the extras pass, or the merge", and the arc diagram at SKILL.md:142-143 places it after Mark done: "`assemble` → **corpus review** → `audio` → **audio review** → **Mark done**  ↳ then **Step 3b** builds `chapter-N-extras`". Two of three say gate 2, the section that owns the step says gate 1. For an orchestrating agent this is a real fork: starting extras at gate 1 means authoring the sibling unit against a card set that can still change during the audio gate (SKILL.md:437 explicitly permits field edits and exclusions on a done unit, and exclusions change what collides), and references/extras-pass.md's duplicate/collision audits are computed against the base unit.
allFindings.recommendation: Pick one and state it once, with the reason. The arc diagram's ordering (after Mark done) is the safer reading given that exclusions at gate 2 change the base card set the extras audits diff against; if gate 1 is genuinely intended, say explicitly that extras must be re-audited if the base unit changes during gate 2. Delete the losing phrasing rather than softening it — an orchestrator prompt with two timings will pick whichever it read last.

allFindings.title: SKILL.md prescribes a vocabulary-diff "script" that does not exist
allFindings.evidence: SKILL.md:299-310 makes the vocabulary diff a required build step and is explicit that it is not a read-through: "The check is a script, not a read-through: pull every `Japanese word` + `English gloss` pair out of the chapter text and report any whose word appears in no card's `target`." It even specifies the expected false-positive class precisely — "A word the book prints with optional parts, `(お)てら`, will not string-match the card `おてら`" (and that is a real case: chapters/32.xhtml:95 prints (お)てら, corpora/32.json ships おてら). No such script exists: scripts/ contains clean-audio, deliver-to-anki, enhance-card-notes, extras-collision-audit, extras-duplicate-check, extras-order, jumble-number-runs, migrate-deck-numbering, preflight, restore-anki-backup, split-front-hint, strip-restatement-notes, validate-decks — none does a vocabulary diff, and grepping scripts/*.mjs for voca/vocab returns nothing. So the most mechanizable check in the whole flow is re-improvised by the agent on every chapter, with no consistency between chapters.
allFindings.recommendation: Write it: a scripts/vocab-coverage.mjs taking a chapter xhtml + a run dir, parsing <table class="voca"> rows (including td.sub sub-rows, which docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:140 already treats as headwords) and reporting glosses whose target string appears in no card, with the (お)X optional-prefix case normalized away. Wire it into preflight.mjs for EPUB units. This is pure mechanization of a check the skill already defines deterministically — it takes nothing away from the agentic extraction, it just stops a known silent-miss class from depending on the agent remembering.

allFindings.title: Extraction prompt's output contract is stated once at the top and never restated; parser tolerance was tuned for a model no pass runs
allFindings.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:25 states "Respond with ONLY a single JSON array (no markdown fences, no prose before or after)" — clear, but it is line 25 of 205, and the prompt ENDS (:204) on a paragraph about false-friend notes, so the last thing the model reads before generating is content guidance, not the output contract. src/corpus/epubLlmExtract.js:6-14 documents the resulting tolerance: a ```json fence around the whole response, and "from Haiku specifically — prose commentary before a fenced block", plus a first-[-to-last-] fallback. That Haiku attribution no longer describes any deployed pass — every EPUB-family call resolves to claude-sonnet-5 (src/util/runClaude.js:7) and nothing sets ANKI_BUILDER_EPUB_LLM_MODEL — so the tolerance is calibrated against a configuration that no longer exists, and the bare first-[-to-last-] fallback would silently mis-slice a response whose prose happens to contain brackets.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a two-line closing section to the extraction prompt restating the contract verbatim ("Output the JSON array now. No fences, no prose, nothing after the closing ]"). Recency is nearly free and is the cheapest way to stop paying for parser tolerance. Keep the fence-stripping (it is harmless), but refresh the comment to say which model actually produced each observed deviation, and consider logging when a deviation path fires so drift is visible rather than absorbed.

allFindings.title: A whole content class — numbered picture-caption vocabulary lists — has no rule in the extraction prompt
allFindings.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:138 covers "Every headword in a VOCABULARY block" and :140 its indented sub-rows; :123-131 covers images; :136 covers key sentences. Nothing covers the book's WORD POWER pattern: a numbered caption list of bare target-language words with NO gloss beside them (chapters/32.xhtml:255-258 ①うけつけ ②ゆうびんきょく ③かいぎしつ ④ちゅうしゃじょう; :269-278 ten hotel-room items), where the accompanying voc-box glosses only SOME of them. EMPIRICAL: the two labels with no voc-box gloss in list II — れいぞうこ (:270) and はな (:278) — were nonetheless extracted, each carrying a hand-written gloss plus reviewNote "Numbered item ② / ⑩ in the WORD POWER …" and uncertain:true (corpora/32.json items 32 and 18). That is exactly the right call, but the prompt supplies no rule for it; the model reached it by inference. I am a much stronger model than deployed Sonnet-medium, so this recovery should not be assumed to generalize — and this content class is common (conventions.md documents WORD POWER as a recurring section across nearly every lesson chapter).
allFindings.recommendation: Add a short rule under "What to extract": a numbered/labelled caption list (illustration sets, diagram labels, floor plans) is a vocabulary block — extract every label; where a label has no gloss in the accompanying table, supply the gloss yourself, set uncertain:true and name the list in reviewNote. That is three sentences and it converts an inference into an instruction, which is where prompt effort pays best.

allFindings.title: The note-field taxonomy is duplicated across three documents with drift already visible
allFindings.evidence: The same scene/hint/note/reviewNote spec is written out three times: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:33-40, docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md (rules 4-5 and the field-by-field list), and .claude/skills/build-anki-deck/references/card-authoring-rules.md:185-215. Drift is already present: the extraction prompt's heading says "**Three note fields — keep them strictly separate.**" and is immediately followed by FOUR bullets (scene, hint, note, reviewNote), while card-authoring-rules.md:187 correctly says "**Four note fields**". docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md's field list describes `reading` as "set it only when it differs from `target` (rule 7)" — but rule 7 is "Natural sentence-case English"; the digit/reading rule is rule 10. card-authoring-rules.md:215 does cross-reference docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md, so the intent to have one source of truth exists, but the text is still copied.
allFindings.recommendation: Fix the two concrete errors now (Three→Four; rule 7→rule 10). Then reduce duplication where it is safe: card-authoring-rules.md is read by the orchestrating agent and the prompts are read by pass models, so some restatement is justified — but the canonical wording should live in one file with the others quoting a named section, and test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js (which already pins placeholders and output contracts) is the natural place to pin a checksum or a required phrase so a hand edit in one copy fails loudly.

allFindings.title: Pedagogical-sort prompt documents an input field that is never sent, and omits two that are
allFindings.evidence: docs/pedagogical-sort-prompt.md §Input Format lists "`notes` (string, optional): any extra context." The renderer sends no such field: src/corpus/pedagogicalSort.js:33-39 maps items to { id, english, target, category?, hint?, scene? } — `notes` is never produced anywhere in the schema (the fields are note/scene/hint/reviewNote), and `hint`/`scene`, which ARE sent, are undocumented in the prompt. The model is therefore told to look for context that never arrives and given context it was not told about. Low impact because sort output is a permutation that fails open (pedagogicalSort.js:71-90 appends omitted items and can never add/drop/duplicate), but it is the same silent-placeholder class that test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js was written to prevent — that test pins {{PLACEHOLDERS}} only, not the documented item-field schema.
allFindings.recommendation: Replace `notes` with the actual optional fields (`hint`, `scene`) and say what each means for ordering (a scene often marks an answer half that should follow its question). Cheap generalization: extend test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js to assert that each prompt's documented input-field names are a subset of the keys its renderer actually emits — that catches this whole class mechanically without constraining prompt content.

allFindings.title: NCX navPoints with attributed <navLabel>/<text> are silently dropped, shifting every lesson ordinal
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:394-405 — `/\s*([^<]*)<\/text>/i` requires literally `` and `` with NO attributes and no nested markup; on failure the loop `continue`s with no `log()` call (the `log` callback is threaded into listExternalChapters but only ever used at line 507 for unresolved hrefs). NCX legally allows `xml:lang`/`dir` on both elements, and `..` occurs in real conversions. This is the live path for EPUB2 books: my probe of the Betrayer EPUB returned `source: "ncx"`, not `nav`.
allFindings.recommendation: Tolerate attributes (`<navLabel\b[^>]*>\s*<text\b[^>]*>`) and strip inner tags from the label like parseNavXhtmlToc already does; and route every skipped navPoint through the existing `log` callback so a dropped entry is visible at `--list-lessons` time. Fully mechanizable, pure function, no judgment involved.

allFindings.title: Spine files the nav never names are silently absorbed into the preceding lesson's range
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:528-534 computes `lastChapterNumber = next.spinePosition - 1`, so any spine file with no nav entry is folded into whatever entry precedes it, with no signal. Probed on Betrayer: entry [3] "The Horus Heresy" = spine 4-6 (spine 5 is DRAMATIS PERSONAE, spine 6 an epigraph), entry [33] "About The Author" = spine 37-38 (spine 38 is an empty page), entry [35] = spine 40-41. On JBP, entry [56] = spine 56-57. Worse, spine 1 (titlepage.xhtml) precedes the first nav entry and is unreachable by `--lesson` entirely — and `describeChapter(book,1)` returns "Cover", identical to nav entry [1]'s label, so building it via `--chapter-number 1` yields a unit whose chapterLabel collides with nav entry [1] and therefore maps to the SAME Anki deck via unitDeckSegments.
allFindings.recommendation: In `--list-lessons`, print each entry's spine range together with how many of those files the nav actually named (e.g. `spine 4-6 (2 files not named by the TOC)`), and log the same during assemble before the paid extraction. Purely informational — the agent still decides. Also report spine files that fall before the first nav entry as an explicit 'unreachable via --lesson' line.

allFindings.title: classifyLesson is English-and-"Lesson N"-only; SKILL.md filters the user's menu on it
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubLessons.js:18-31. Probe on Betrayer: 0/35 entries classify as `lesson`, 32/35 as `other`. Probed misclassifications on other shapes: "Acknowledgements"/"Appendixes"/"Indexes" → other (the `\b` after `acknowledge?ment`/`appendix` is defeated by the plural); "第1課 あいさつ", "Leçon 1 : Bonjour", "Lektion 3", "Capítulo 2", "Chapter 4: Verbs", "1. Greetings" → all other; "Link to Audio for Exercises" → quiz (JBP entry [7], confirmed in the live probe). SKILL.md:184 says "offer the `lesson`-typed entries as options" — on Betrayer that offers an empty list; on JBP it hides real teaching content. The owner already worked around this by hand: output/epubs/.../chapter-0/cards.json has chapterNumber 11, chapterLabel "Frequently Used Expressions" — an `other`-typed entry.
allFindings.recommendation: Change SKILL.md to present ALL nav entries with `type` as an annotation/sort hint, never as a filter, and to say explicitly that on a non-English or non-"Lesson N" book every entry will read `other` and that is expected. Keep classifyLesson as-is (it is honestly documented as a heuristic) — the defect is the skill doc trusting it as a gate.

allFindings.title: Nav-label parsing defects flow uninspected into live Anki deck names (entities, ruby, tag concatenation)
allFindings.evidence: Label → src/cli/commands/assemble.js:311-312 `corpus.meta.chapterLabel` → src/deck/deckPath.js `unitDeckSegments` → src/anki/deliver.js:100 `ankiDeck`. decodeHtmlEntities (epubArchive.js:272-276) handles only amp/lt/gt/quot/#39, so probed labels keep raw text: "Lesson 3: Don’t Go" → deck segment `Don’t Go`; "Leçon 1 : Bonjour" survives verbatim. Tag stripping at line 353 is a bare `replace(/<[^>]+>/g,"")`: a ruby label `漢かん字じ` probes to "漢かん字じ" (reading interleaved into the word), and `Lesson5` probes to "Lesson5", which then also defeats deckPath.js's GROUPED_LABEL regex. JBP contains ZERO `` in any of its 57 spine files, so this path has never been exercised on the one book the parser is proven on — yet ruby is near-universal in Japanese-published textbooks.
allFindings.recommendation: Decode numeric/hex entities and a broader named set; drop `<rt>`/`<rp>` CONTENT (not just the tags) before stripping; insert a space when stripping inline elements. Critical caveat for red line 2: chapterLabel is the delivery key, so shipping this fix RENAMES existing decks — it needs the same migration treatment as the legacy deck-shell cleanup already in deliver.js:283-296, or it must apply to new books only.

allFindings.title: Multiple nav entries pointing at one spine file collapse silently — a fragment-addressed TOC loses lessons with no warning
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:515-522: consecutive entries resolving to the same spine position are dropped by a bare `continue`, no `log()`. The docstring calls this "deliberate, deterministic" — but it is invisible to the caller. resolveHrefToSpinePosition (line 433) strips fragments, so a book whose 20 lessons live in one XHTML addressed as `body.html#lesson3` presents as a handful of entries; selecting one then hands the entire multi-lesson file to a single extraction call as one 'lesson'.
allFindings.recommendation: Log each collapse through the existing callback and surface a count in `--list-lessons` (`[4] spine 12: Lesson 4  (3 further TOC entries point into this same file)`). That single line converts a silent whole-class failure into something the agent sees before spending a paid pass; fragment-aware slicing can stay out of scope.

allFindings.title: Nav order is assumed monotonic in spine order; a non-monotonic TOC yields inverted and overlapping lesson ranges
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:529-534 computes each range purely as `[own, next-1]` with no ordering check. If nav lists entries out of spine order (cover/TOC after content, interleaved back matter — common in converted EPUBs), an entry gets `lastChapterNumber < firstChapterNumber`, and a later entry's range overlaps an earlier one, feeding the SAME spine file into two different lessons. The inverted case degrades quietly rather than throwing: extractChapterRangeToFile:687 DOES throw on last<first, but assemble.js:290 only calls it when `lastChapterNumber > chapterNumber`, so an inverted range silently becomes a single-file extraction; `--list-lessons` also hides it (assemble.js:148-151 only prints a range when last>first).
allFindings.recommendation: Validate monotonicity in listExternalChapters and warn loudly (naming the offending entries) rather than silently normalizing; clamp `last` to `>= first`. Mechanizable, ~6 lines, and covered by a fixture test.

allFindings.title: Zip-slip: image extraction writes to join(destDir, src) with no containment check
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:637-643 — `const localDest = join(destDir, src); writeFileAtomic(localDest, ...)`. `src` comes straight from the chapter HTML (`` / ``) with only `isLocalRelativePath` filtering (blocks `scheme://` and `data:`, not `../`). src/util/atomicWrite.js:writeFileAtomic does `mkdirSync(dirname(destPath), {recursive:true})`, so the escaping path is created, not rejected. The archive lookup at line 628 normalizes to the same escaping path, and a crafted zip can carry a central-directory entry literally named `../../..`, so both sides match. The threat is concrete, not theoretical: the hostile sample I was pointed at is a libgen download.
allFindings.recommendation: After computing localDest, `resolve()` it and reject anything not under `resolve(destDir)`; log the skip like a dangling ref. Five lines, no behavior change for legitimate `../images/x.png` refs that stay inside the book's cache dir.

allFindings.title: DRM detection covers only zip-level encryption; Adobe ADEPT books parse "successfully" into ciphertext
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:50-54 checks general-purpose bit 0, which catches zip-password encryption. The DRM actually shipped by retailers (Adobe ADEPT) leaves the zip unencrypted and declares encrypted resources in META-INF/encryption.xml — `grep -rn 'encryption' src/` returns zero hits, so nothing reads it. Such a book yields chapters that inflate to binary noise, extractChapterToFile writes them, and analyzeBookConventions (a whole-book paid pass) is handed 40+ files of garbage before anything looks wrong. Contrast with the two shapes that DO fail loudly and have tests (test/corpus/epubArchive.test.js:711, :730).
allFindings.recommendation: Parse META-INF/encryption.xml and throw a clear 'DRM-protected' error ONLY when an encrypted `<CipherReference URI>` names a spine document — IDPF/Adobe font obfuscation uses the same file on perfectly readable books and must not false-positive. Deterministic and testable.

allFindings.title: XML scanners have no comment/CDATA awareness — a commented-out nav anchor becomes a phantom lesson and shifts every ordinal
allFindings.evidence: findTags/findTagOccurrences/NAV_A_TAG_PATTERN (src/corpus/epubArchive.js:102, 308, 337) run over raw text. Probed: `` yields a real entry `"DELETED Lesson"`. The same applies to a commented-out `` in the OPF manifest. A phantom nav entry does two things at once: it shifts every `[number]` that `--lesson N` accepts, and it steals a range boundary from its neighbour.
allFindings.recommendation: Strip `<!--...-->` and `<![CDATA[...]]>` spans before scanning (one preprocessing function shared by all the scanners). Cheap, safe, and matches the existing 'hand-rolled scanner, hardened case by case' philosophy already documented at line 96-101.

allFindings.title: No size or shape guards on the whole-book passes — a large book blows the 10-minute LLM timeout with a misleading error
allFindings.evidence: src/corpus/epubBookConventions.js:59-72 materializes EVERY spine file to disk and lists ALL paths in one prompt; src/corpus/epubTaughtIndex.js does the same. On JBP that is 57 files including two ~24k-char glossaries (measured). Nothing caps spine count, per-chapter size, archive size, or image count, and runClaude is pinned to a 10-minute timeout with 1 retry — so a 300-file or image-heavy book fails as a timeout with no hint that the book's shape was the cause, after having already dumped every image into .anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a mechanized shape report (spine count, total stripped-text bytes, image count, largest chapter, nav source) printed by `--list-lessons` and before the first paid pass, with a WARN above thresholds derived from JBP. Advisory only — the agent decides whether to proceed, so red line 1 is untouched.

allFindings.title: The entire hostile-EPUB shape space is untested; the fixture builder only emits well-formed nav
allFindings.evidence: test/support/epubFixtures.js emits a minimal conformant OPF/nav (per-item `properties`/`mediaType` are optional extras, lines 96-106). Grep across test/corpus/*.js finds zero tests for: ruby labels, numeric/hex entities in labels, comments/CDATA, NCX labels with attributes, duplicate-href nav entries, non-monotonic nav, unnamed spine files inside a range, path-escaping image srcs, non-UTF-8 chapters. The only two adversarial tests that exist (:711 encrypted bit, :730 ZIP64) cover the two paths that already fail LOUDLY — i.e. testing is inversely correlated with silent-degradation risk, which is this project's documented recurring failure signature.
allFindings.recommendation: Add one fixture case per silent shape above. These are pure functions over in-memory zips — fast, deterministic, and they encode the project's own current frontier goal ('catch X before the review gate'). Highest value per line of test code anywhere in the repo.

allFindings.title: Text-poor / image-only chapters have no mechanized signal; the image sweep is 100% agent diligence
allFindings.evidence: Measured stripped-text length vs `` count per JBP spine file: #11 = 94 chars / 7 images (and it IS a built unit — output/epubs/.../chapter-0 is chapterNumber 11 'Frequently Used Expressions'), #57 = 48 chars / 5 images, versus ~6-8k chars for normal lesson files. docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:123-131 tells the model to open images, and extractReferencedImages handles both `` and the SVG-wrapped scanned-page idiom — but nothing anywhere measures whether a selected range is mostly picture. A fixed-layout or scanned textbook therefore extracts to a thin, plausible-looking corpus rather than an obvious failure.
allFindings.recommendation: Print per-spine-file text length and image count for the selected range at assemble time and warn when text density is low ('this unit is mostly images — extraction depends entirely on reading them'). Deterministic measurement, agentic response — exactly the mechanize-opportunistically shape.

allFindings.title: Nav discovery is too narrow, so books that HAVE a TOC report 'no navigation document'
allFindings.evidence: isolateNavToc (src/corpus/epubArchive.js:322-335) requires the attribute to be literally named `epub:type`, and resolveNavSource (line 456) requires the manifest item to carry `properties="nav"`. A conformant EPUB3 that binds the OPS namespace to a different prefix (`ops:type="toc"`), or uses `role="doc-toc"`, or omits the manifest `properties` flag, falls through to `[]` — and with no NCX the CLI prints 'no navigation document found — use --chapter-number <spine index>' (assemble.js:141-144), which is a confidently wrong diagnosis that pushes the user onto raw spine indices for a book that has a perfectly good TOC.
allFindings.recommendation: Add a last-resort sweep: any XHTML manifest item containing a `<nav>` whose `*:type` token list includes `toc` (prefix-agnostic) or whose `role` is `doc-toc`. Keep the current tiers first so proven behavior is unchanged.

allFindings.title: The test suite writes into the LIVE .anki-builder library — proven by a stray book-hash directory
