allFindings.evidence: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json` exists in the repo working tree, containing `{"epubHash":"h1","chapterNumber":2,"chapterLabel":"Uch",...}` — test data. `epubHash: "h1"` appears in test/server/index.test.js:452,499,560 and test/deck/rebuild.test.js:25,30,208,231; src/corpus/epubLibrary.js:15-17 falls back to the real `libraryHome()` whenever `libraryHomeDir` is not passed. Harmless with a fake hash, but the same omission under a REAL book hash would write into `.anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/corpora/`, which is precisely the directory backward de-dup and the taught index read — the failure mode that already cost 12 unflagged repeats per LIMITATIONS.md.
allFindings.recommendation: Make `libraryHome()` refuse the repo's real `.anki-builder` when a test env flag is set (or have the harness assert `.anki-builder` is byte-identical after `npm test`), and delete the stray `h1` directory. Cheap guard against a silent-corruption class the project has already been burned by.

endorsements.why: Verified independently: `grep -rni reopen src/` returns only two unrelated comments (clientScripts.js:329, model/index.js:170), while SKILL.md:363/428/429/439/610/611 and references/audio-pipeline.md:107 all instruct the agent to use a Reopen button, and pages.js:348-349 shows a done unit renders only a `done-badge` (Unreview is rendered ONLY when NOT done). This is the single worst doc defect in the repo under red line 2: the documented recovery path for a mis-clicked Mark done on a delivered unit is literally unexecutable, so an agent will improvise a hand edit of meta.done on a unit in the daily collection. It also compounds my qa-16 addition: a hand-edited meta.done leaves the shipping .apkg stale with no detector.

I reproduced this read-only and it is worse than stated. `node scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana` prints keeper `chapter-2/num-2` (the NUMBER 2) for target に and would exclude all five genuine particle senses (ni-particle, ni-particle-time, ni-particle-target, ni-particle-location, ni-from-particle); さん keeps `san-suffix-ch14` and would drop `num-3`; ご keeps `num-5` over the honorific prefix; と, で, から, やすみ, ばん, の, いいえ are the same shape. That is roughly a third of the 17 groups. The reviewed/done guard is the only thing preventing it today, and an in-flight chapter is unreviewed by definition — this is a documented happy-path command (extras-pass.md:210) that would silently delete correct cards from a new unit.

Verified: `grep -rn rebuildGroupQuiet src/` shows exactly one call site, src/server/index.js:286 inside handleLessonDone; the exclude/edit/trim/select handlers never rebuild, while rebuild.js:6-8 and index.js:421-424 both assert they do. I then confirmed the consequence on live data (see my qa-14 addition): output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5.apkg is dated 13 Aug 11:35 while lesson-0 and lesson-3 cards.json were written today at 11:23/11:29 — the shipping package for a delivered course is stale right now. A false safety claim in the two files a future reader will trust is the worst half of this.

Verified the exact chain: src/cli/commands/audio.js:74-78 `clipIsCurrent = !isStageOwnedCard(item) || <hash match>`, and src/audio/index.js:204-208 makes isStageOwnedCard false for any audioManual or hand-picked -gen- take. So the ~200 cards a human touched (109 manual trims + 86 -gen- + 81 -genkanji- + 4 uploads by linguist-4's count) are permanently exempt from the text-changed check, and applyCards.js editCard writes target/reading without touching AUDIO_FIELDS. This is the isStageOwnedCard silent-regression signature repeating in a second place, and the recommended fix (record audioTextHash on install, badge at the gate rather than regenerate) is correct — it never overwrites human work.

Structurally identical to my qa-2 and arrived at from the other direction: 47 shared targets with differing glosses and 10 uncued ambiguous English prompts across the two decks in one live collection. Together we have three independent cross-collection invariants (card-id equality, target equality, English-gloss equality) that every existing audit is structurally incapable of seeing because preflight.mjs and extras-collision-audit.mjs both resolve a single collection dir. One collection-wide mode in preflight closes all three; that is the highest leverage-per-line change proposed by anyone in this review.

The only finding that demonstrates, with a verifiable artifact, a card that SHOULD exist and does not: conventions.md tells the extractor to skip ch.32's あります/います paradigm image, the extraction prompt tells it to extract exactly that, and chapter-12/cards.json contains none of the eight forms. This is the failure class SKILL.md:283 itself calls structurally invisible ('nothing downstream can notice what was never extracted'), and it has a concrete cause and a cheap fix (precedence sentence + a prompt-hash staleness warning on the cached conventions). It also explains why the manual image sweep never caught it — see promptengineer-6.

This is the QA thesis of the whole review, stated precisely: the only two adversarial EPUB tests that exist (encrypted bit, ZIP64) cover the two paths that already fail LOUDLY, so test coverage is inversely correlated with silent-degradation risk. Every one of adversarial-1/2/5/6/9's concrete bugs is a pure function over an in-memory zip that test/support/epubFixtures.js could exercise in milliseconds. Given the parser is proven on exactly one book and the second book is the known cliff, one fixture per silent shape is the cheapest insurance in the repo.

Verified at src/anki/deliver.js:234-248: tmplChanged is computed including `!live` (a template with no live counterpart), then updateModelTemplates is called with a map containing that unknown name — AnkiConnect only rewrites templates that already exist, so the add is a silent no-op, and there is no modelTemplateAdd anywhere in the repo. Meanwhile collection.js:162-166 claims the shared CARD_TEMPLATES constant means the two delivery paths 'can never drift'. A no-op that reports success on a live-collection write is exactly the class this project keeps getting burned by, and it silently blocks every card-design change others proposed (learner-3, learner-9, learner-12).

objections.argument: RETRACTING MY OWN SEVERITY: critical → high. On re-probe, the escalation path needs TWO simultaneous omissions, and the tests that omit one supply the other. test/cli/index.test.js:1175 and :1194 omit --voice (so getDefaultVoice returns a stub 'default-voice-id') but DO thread libraryHomeDir; :2242/:2278/:2420 omit libraryHomeDir but pass --voice v1, a fake voice. So no test today both resolves a REAL voice id and writes to the real cache home, and the realized damage is zero: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/` never mixes with the real book (loadPriorChapterItems reads one hash's dir), and `.anki-builder/audio/v1/` is not a real voice. The finding is a latent silent-corruption path with a concrete escalation, not an active corruption — 'high' is the honest band, and overstating it risks displacing findings with live consequences (techlead-2, codeexpert-4, qa-2).
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A test that calls the audio CLI without --voice AND without libraryHomeDir (real default voice → real cache), or any fixture using a real 16-hex epubHash, or a real voice cache dir containing a sub-4KB mp3. Also: proof that removeChapterCorpus is reachable in any test with a real hash — that would push it back to critical immediately.

objections.argument: Same defect as qa-1/techlead-1/codeexpert-1/generalist-3, rated 'low' here. Five independent finds at low/high/high/critical/critical is a calibration spread the arbiter should collapse to HIGH, not low. Low understates it because the writer is not a fixture value but a MISSING INJECTION: src/server/adapters/applyCards.js:89/:136 default BOTH saveChapterCorpus and removeChapterCorpus to the real implementations, so the safety of every current and future test depends on each author remembering a stub — the precise argument src/util/testEnv.js:19 already rejects for the LLM spawn. The delete side (rmSync of a chapter's dedup entry) has no fixture-value protection at all beyond the hash string, and its symptom (unflagged repeats many chapters later) is the project's most expensive documented incident.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that libraryHome() is unreachable from any test without an explicit injection (it is not — the artifact on disk proves the opposite), or a repo policy that .anki-builder is disposable and reconstructible, which would make the whole class low.

objections.argument: Object to the RECOMMENDATION, not the observation. Memoizing resolveChapterAudio by item.audio rewrites media-key assignment — the exact code path LIMITATIONS.md:423-447 records as having 'passed npm test and every synthetic check' before breaking a real Anki import. The payoff is 22 duplicate zip entries out of 1,914 (~1%), i.e. a few hundred KB and zero correctness impact. Under red line 2 that is a bad trade: it spends the repo's least-verifiable code path for a cosmetic win, with no real-import smoke test to catch a regression (qa-10). Correct sequencing: land scripts/verify-apkg-import.mjs FIRST, then memoize behind it. The second half of the finding — a hard throw when entries.length > 0xffff in src/deck/zip.js:95-96 — is unambiguously right and should be split out and shipped now; it converts a structurally corrupt central directory into an error.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A real Anki import of a memoized package succeeding (which requires the import test to exist), or evidence that duplicate media keys cause an actual import failure or measurable bloat rather than ~1% redundancy.

objections.argument: The insight (siblings back-to-back is bad practice) is right; the primary lever is wrong and mildly risky. src/deck/collection.js:382-402 buildDconf emits a single preset with `id: 1, name: "Default"` — the collection-wide default preset every other deck in the owner's collection likely uses. Flipping bury there does nothing for the live decks (they were delivered via AnkiConnect, and src/anki/deliver.js never touches dconf — grep confirms no deckConfig call), and on a hand File→Import it aims a modified preset named 'Default' at the owner's own Default. Anki's apkg importer behaviour for a same-id/same-name preset is version-dependent and this repo has no import smoke test to establish it — an unknown write to a collection-wide scheduling preset is squarely red line 2. The finding's own last sentence (one line in references/deliver.md telling the owner to enable burying on the preset his book decks use) is the correct and complete fix; the position interleave is separately fine since it only affects new-card order in a fresh import.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: An empirical import (per qa-10's harness) showing Anki remaps the apkg's dconf to a fresh id and never merges into the collection's existing Default preset — then flipping bury is harmless, though still ineffective for the AnkiConnect-delivered decks.

objections.argument: Object to 'make kanji-normalized text the DEFAULT for ja' as written. Verified: src/audio/index.js:147-152 defaultClipText feeds both the ElevenLabs cache key and, via defaultOriginalFilename (:177-179), the staleness comparison at src/cli/commands/audio.js:74-78. Changing the ja spoken text therefore (a) invalidates the content-addressed cache for every ja card → ~1,900 paid refetches, (b) marks every stage-owned clip stale so the next `audio` run silently regenerates and re-trims them, discarding the marker/trim tuning behind 1,900 previously auditioned clips, while (c) the ~200 hand-picked/manual cards are exempt via isStageOwnedCard and keep their kana takes — producing a silently MIXED-orthography deck, which is the failure signature the finding itself invokes. The pedagogy is sound; the rollout must be scoped by a meta flag set at unit creation so existing units stay kana and only new units get the kanji path.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A cheap A/B on ~10 existing cards showing the kanji reading is materially better AND a design that keeps existing clip filenames valid (e.g. hashing a stable key rather than the spoken text), which would remove the mass-invalidation and the mixed-deck outcome.

objections.argument: Endorse the split into per-pass scopes and raising extraction to high; object to the 'LOWER toward Haiku' half. There is no eval harness, no golden corpus and no regression test for ANY pass — test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js pins placeholders, not output quality. So a model downgrade's damage is unmeasurable by construction: semanticDedup EXCLUDES cards, and per my qa-16 addition an exclusion carries no provenance and is indistinguishable at the gate from a human's decision; a wrong forward flag trains the reviewer to dismiss flags; a wrong lesson-word category ships a visible chip on the card front (linguist-6). 'Fails open' is a claim about the code path, not about content quality. Changing four pinned models with no way to notice the difference is the project's signature failure mode dressed as a cost optimisation.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A per-pass golden-output fixture (one reviewed lesson's input → accepted output) that a Haiku run is shown to match within tolerance. With that in place I would support the downgrades immediately — the split into per-pass scopes is exactly what makes such a comparison runnable.

objections.argument: Agree the harness loop is dead and the ideas inbox is stale; object to dropping T011. T011 is the only tracked artifact pointing at the intersection of THREE independently-confirmed blind spots: no real-Anki-import test (LIMITATIONS.md:423-447, still true), output/templates/ empty so the template path has zero worked examples, and src/cards/readiness.js:50 exempting sourceType 'template' from the gate entirely (prepare.js:96-99 skips both enrichment passes). Retiring TASKS.json while dropping its only open row deletes the last pointer to the highest-risk untested path in the repo. Retire the loop, but transplant T011 into LIMITATIONS.md as a 'when to revisit' entry with the import-smoke-test scope attached, so it survives the process change.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: An explicit owner statement that the bundled-template path is abandoned and no template deck will ever be built — then T011 is genuinely dead and only the import smoke test needs to survive, attached to the EPUB path instead.

additions.title: A delivered course's shipping .apkg is stale RIGHT NOW against two units edited today, and no tool anywhere compares them
additions.evidence: Read-only mtime probe across both collections: output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5/nihongo-101-course-n5.apkg is dated 13 Aug 11:35, while lesson-0/cards.json (14 Aug 11:29) and lesson-3/cards.json (14 Aug 11:23) were written TODAY. Both are done, delivered units (anki-delivered.json present). The book collection is currently fine (apkg 14 Aug 10:58:46 vs newest cards.json 10:58:41). This is the live realization of codeexpert-4's class — src/server/index.js:286 is the ONLY rebuildGroupQuiet call site, so an exclude/edit/trim on a done unit never rebuilds — and it is invisible to every tool: scripts/preflight.mjs never looks at the .apkg at all, scripts/validate-decks.mjs only schema-checks JSON, and SKILL.md:99-118's artifact-freshness check exists only inside the gate-2 watcher, i.e. it is armed for the one moment a human clicks Mark done and never again. Whoever wrote those two files today (owner edit, or an --apply script) got no signal, and the .apkg is what a human reaches for on File→Import when AnkiConnect isn't running — so a restore from it would silently roll back today's edits.
additions.recommendation: Promote the gate-2 artifact check from watcher prose to a standing preflight check: for each collection, resolve the package via resolveDeckPathForDir (src/deck/deckFileName.js:63 — never a hand-typed slug, cf. my qa-8) and FAIL when any done unit's cards.json is newer than it, naming the units. ~15 lines, deterministic, and it covers three separate findings at once: post-done dashboard edits (codeexpert-4), a hand-edited meta.done improvised because Reopen doesn't exist (generalist-1), and any scripts/ --apply mutation (qa-6). It also makes the gate-2 watcher's fragment redundant.

additions.title: Neither deterministic gate is in the project's Definition of Done — preflight and validate-decks run only if a human remembers
additions.evidence: package.json: `ci` = `format:check && lint && test && build`. `preflight` and `validate:decks` are npm-wired but in NEITHER, and .githooks/pre-push runs only `npm run ci` (its own comment calls that 'the exact Definition-of-Done suite'). So the entire two-week frontier of 'catch X before the review gate, not at Mark done' is enforced by exactly one sentence of prose — SKILL.md:119-125 — with no mechanical backstop; an agent that skips it produces a run indistinguishable from one that passed. That is the same absent-check-reads-as-a-passing-check shape as my qa-3. Both commands are also unrunnable in CI as-is (output/ is gitignored, so a clean checkout has nothing to check) and would need a clean no-collections exit.
additions.recommendation: Two steps. (a) Make both commands exit 0 with an explicit '(no collections found)' line on an empty output/, then add a `npm run check` = `ci && validate:decks && preflight` and point .githooks/pre-push at it — a local hook sees the real output/ tree, CI does not, which is exactly the right split. (b) Have preflight write a `<collectionDir>/.preflight-<timestamp>` breadcrumb (or stamp meta) so the review gate can state when it last ran; a gate that cannot tell whether the check ran is not a gate. Keep CI itself on `ci` so a clean clone still passes.

additions.title: `excluded` is a bare boolean with no provenance — a script's --apply exclusion is byte-identical to a human's reviewed decision, and after delivery it is unrecoverable
additions.evidence: src/model/index.js:82 and :204 declare `excluded: { type: "boolean" }` inside objects with `additionalProperties: false`, so no reason/author field can even be attached without a schema change. 95 cards are excluded in the JBP book today. Three facts compose into a silent-loss chain: (1) scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs --apply writes exclusions whose false-positive rate I measured at roughly a third of groups (see my techlead-2 endorsement — に would lose five genuine particle cards); (2) at Gate 1 the reviewer sees an excluded card with no indication that a script, not a person, made that call, so the natural read is 'someone already decided this'; (3) per learner-10, src/anki/deliver.js:441-444 only REPORTS an already-delivered card that leaves the corpus — nothing suspends it — so a false-positive exclusion after delivery both removes the card from the package and leaves a live orphan the learner keeps drilling. Every existing audit treats `excluded` as ground truth: preflight, shippableCards and the dedup-library snapshot all filter on it without asking who set it.
additions.recommendation: Add an optional `excludedBy` ("human" | "<script name>") and `excludedReason` to both schemas (additive, backward-compatible — absent means human/legacy), have every scripts/ --apply writer stamp it, and render it in the dashboard and the corpus-review artifact so a machine judgment is visibly a machine judgment at the gate. Then make preflight report the count of script-authored exclusions per unit. This is the minimum that makes techlead-2's --apply survivable at all; without it the false positives are unauditable after the fact.

additions.title: The .apkg ships a deck-options preset with id 1 named "Default", and nobody can say what an import does to the owner's collection-wide preset
additions.evidence: src/deck/collection.js:382-402 buildDconf emits exactly one config: `{ id: 1, name: "Default", new: { bury:false, perDay:20, order:1, delays:[1,10] }, rev: { bury:false, perDay:200, maxIvl:36500 }, lapse:{...} }`, written into col.dconf at :570. Every package the pipeline has ever built carries it, including the two already imported into the live collection. Anki's apkg importer behaviour for an incoming preset sharing id 1 / the name 'Default' is version-dependent (remap vs merge), and this repo has NO way to find out: LIMITATIONS.md:423-447 states there is still no automated real-import test, and three .apkg format bugs already shipped past every synthetic check. So a hand File→Import — the path SKILL.md Step 7 instructs — carries an unquantified write to the preset that may govern the owner's entire daily collection (perDay 20/200 and the delays array are scheduling parameters, not cosmetics). This is unremarkable in isolation but it is a hard blocker on learner-2's proposal to start editing that preset deliberately.
additions.recommendation: Rename and re-id the shipped preset (e.g. `id: <deck-scoped int>, name: "anki-builder"`) so it can never collide with the collection's Default by name or id, and note in references/deliver.md that the .apkg's deck options are informational — the AnkiConnect path never applies them. Verify the actual import behaviour as the FIRST assertion of the qa-10 import smoke test (import into a throwaway collection that has a customised Default, then diff dconf), because until that test exists no dconf change should be made in either direction.

additions.title: No test asserts any command's write set — the library leak five of us found is one instance of a class with no detector
additions.evidence: Five independent reviewers (qa-1, techlead-1, codeexpert-1, generalist-3, adversarial-14) converged on the same artifact, `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json`, written today by test/server/index.test.js. That convergence is the tell: the defect was trivially discoverable by `ls`, sat in the tree for an unknown period, and `npm test` stayed green throughout — because nothing in the suite makes a claim about WHERE a command writes, only about what it returns. The same hole covers output/ (no test asserts a CLI command confines its writes to --output-root), the audio cache, and anki-backups/. src/util/testEnv.js:19 shows the project already accepts this style of assertion for external calls; it just stops at process boundaries and never covers the filesystem. Fixing only libraryHome() closes today's instance and leaves the class open — the next variant (a test that writes into output/, or a script's --apply invoked from a future test) will be equally silent.
additions.recommendation: Add one class-level detector rather than only the point fix: a `test/support/writeGuard.js` that snapshots a manifest (path + size + mtime) of the repo's durable dirs (.anki-builder, output, anki-backups) in a global before/after hook and FAILS the run naming any path that changed. It is ~30 lines, needs no mocking, runs once per suite, and it would have caught this on the day it landed — plus every future variant. Pair it with the libraryHome tmpdir redirect others proposed (that makes the guard pass rather than merely report), and delete the stray `.anki-builder/epubs/h1` and `.anki-builder/audio/v1` trees by hand.

endorsements.why: Verified independently as the most consequential CONTENT loss in the set: the あります/います grid is the animacy-of-existence paradigm, a core N5 point whose past/negative cells (ありました/ありませんでした/いました/いませんでした) appear nowhere in chapter-12's 100+ cards. It is also the only finding that explains a systemic cause (a cached per-book policy doc silently outranking the extraction rules with no precedence statement) rather than a single defect, and its fix is prompt-side and fully compatible with the agentic core.

This is a genuine pedagogical contradiction, not a wording nit: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:186-194 demands a worked in-context example for every function word, while :174 removes the chapter's usual home for those examples. I confirmed the model resolved it by breaking the ban (にほんのスパですよ to serve the particle よ). Function words without a demonstrating sentence are exactly the cards a learner can recite and not use, so the constraint that must give is :174 — as the finding says.

Cross-deck interference is the one collision class the deck's otherwise-excellent collision doctrine cannot see, and the pairs are linguistically real, not cosmetic: 'Nice to meet you.' -> はじめまして vs よろしくおねがいします and 'Yes' -> ええ vs はい are different speech acts / registers. I verified the register cueing WORKS in-book (はい carries 'the standard, neutral yes', ええ 'the softer, more conversational yes'), which proves the doctrine is right and only its scope is wrong.

Highest study-quality gain per line of code in the whole set, and the only one that changes what the learner's brain actually does: adjacent new-card positions plus new.bury/rev.bury=false means the Production rep of a note is answered from working memory minutes after Recognition, which converts a two-direction note into roughly one direction of learning. It touches no existing scheduling (dconf applies at import only), so it is red-line-2 safe.

The three rules I judge most valuable in card-authoring-rules.md — 'answerable alone', 'a scene must not reveal the answer', 'hint on the Production front only' — are all claims about a RENDERED FRONT that no reviewer or agent ever sees. I confirmed the templates (src/deck/collection.js:167-191) are single-source, so a faithful preview is cheap. This turns the deck's best doctrine from something the agent has to simulate mentally into something the human can see at Gate 1.

The ruby half is the Japanese-specific landmine: <ruby>漢<rt>かん</rt>字</ruby> stripping to 漢かん字じ interleaves reading into word, and I confirmed the JBP kana edition contains zero <ruby>, so this path has never been exercised on the one proven book while ruby is near-universal in kanji-bearing Japanese textbooks. The finding's own caveat is the important part: chapterLabel is the Anki delivery key, so the fix renames live decks and must be new-books-only or migrated.

Converges with my linguist-8 from the data side and I verified the template text: Reading appears in neither qfmt nor afmt of either card (src/deck/collection.js:167-191), while Pronunciation renders on both BACKS. So for the 136 numeral cards the learner is given romaji as the only reading support — training the romaji crutch the Reading field was introduced to remove. Rendering {{Reading}} on the back is additive, ships via updateModelTemplates, and de-risks the kanji book.

Outside my lane but I rank it top overall on red line 2: durable writes into .anki-builder/ from the test suite is the one finding with an artifact on disk, a documented precedent for the exact guard shape (assertExternalCallAllowed), and a corruption target (the dedup library) whose failure mode is silent unflagged repeats months later — the project's own signature incident.

objections.argument: Retracting my own severity: high -> medium, and the recommendation should be opt-in-with-review, not default-on. Making LLM-generated kanji the default TTS input means ~1,900 unreviewed kana->kanji conversions, and kana->kanji is a one-to-many mapping the model must guess (はし 橋/箸, いま 今/居間, きます 来ます/着ます, かえります 帰ります/返ります). A wrong kanji is voiced as a wrong WORD, and unlike today's per-card Generate (kanji) button there would be no human veto — that is a silent-degradation trade, which is precisely what this project's red lines are about. My cited evidence (~13% of clips needed human intervention) shows the current path is expensive, not that kanji input would have fixed those specific clips. The defensible version: generate kanji for ja, show it in the audio review as today, and make it the default only for cards whose conversion is unambiguous by a checkable rule (e.g. the kana matches exactly one entry the book itself printed in kanji, or a dictionary lookup returns a single reading).
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: An A/B on ~30 cards drawn from the 7 audioMarkerStuck + 86 re-rolled clips showing kanji input fixes the pronunciation defect, PLUS a measurement of kanji-generation accuracy over a sample of the deck's homophone-bearing cards (はし/いま/かみ/きます class) showing a near-zero mis-conversion rate. If mis-conversion is measurably rare AND the audio review still surfaces the kanji for veto, default-on is justified and high severity stands.

objections.argument: The near-sibling frame warning (part 2) would fire on the deck's BEST drills, not its worst. A mechanical proper-noun/digit normalization cannot tell 'same frame, swapped proper noun' (low value: fib-c1-confirm-hoffman vs fib-c1-confirm-brown) apart from 'same frame, swapped particle or counter' (high value minimal pairs — exactly what the extras pass is praised for producing, e.g. the に/で/へ frames and the counter series). Warning at 3+ members per frame will train the reviewer to dismiss the line, which is the wallpaper failure techlead-8 names. Part 1 of the finding (a length ceiling on the Production face; 31 live cards with English >=60 chars, including a 3-sentence self-introduction) is correct and I endorse that half. The frame check should instead flag only frames whose members differ SOLELY in a proper noun or a digit — that class is unambiguously low-value and is mechanically separable.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A breakdown of the 12 detected frames showing that the great majority differ only in proper nouns/digits rather than in a grammatical element. If the grammatical minimal pairs turn out to be a small minority, a blanket 3+-member warning is cheap enough and I withdraw.

objections.argument: Two of the per-pass tier assignments are backwards on linguistic grounds. (a) Lowering semanticDedup toward Haiku: deciding whether two cards are 'the same' is a semantic-discrimination judgment of exactly the kind this deck's collision doctrine depends on getting right (おおきい vs おおきくないです; the six に-particle senses; やすみ break vs vacation, which LIMITATIONS.md already records as a wrong collapse). Its failure mode is a silently excluded legitimate drill that a reviewer scanning 150 rows will rubber-stamp — reviewer-visible is not reviewer-caught. (b) Keeping cross-lesson notes at Sonnet-medium: my linguist-7 documents a factually FALSE morphological analysis shipped from that pass through both gates (なんじ/なんにん described as instances of なんの). That is evidence the current tier is already insufficient for the one pass that writes free-form linguistic claims, which argues for raising it alongside extraction, not holding it. I agree fully with raising extraction, and with lowering forward flags and the pedagogical sort — both are validated or fail open.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A head-to-head on one chapter's dedup candidates showing Haiku's exclusion set matches Sonnet's (no extra exclusions of grammatically distinct pairs), and a sample of cross-lesson notes at higher effort showing no reduction in false decomposition claims.

objections.argument: The severity is right but the 47 figure and the proposed detector need normalization first, or the check ships as noise on day one. Of the cited pairs, おはようございます 'Good morning.' vs 'Good morning' and イギリス 'United Kingdom' vs 'UK' are punctuation/abbreviation variants that produce zero interference — the learner sees the same target and answers correctly either way. The genuinely dangerous set is the 10 shared-ENGLISH-different-target cases, where one prompt has two correct answers and the learner is guaranteed to fail one of them. A collection-wide findCollisions run raw will report ~47 in-name-only conflicts alongside 10 real ones, which is the same wallpaper problem techlead-8 identifies for the existing '17 duplicate groups' line. Normalize glosses (case, trailing period, obvious abbreviation pairs) before comparing, and report the shared-English class SEPARATELY and more loudly than the shared-target class.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A pass over the 47 showing that a substantial share differ in MEANING rather than in formatting — e.g. the same target glossed with genuinely different senses across the two decks. That would justify reporting the target class at equal volume.

additions.title: 1,847 romanizations are embedded in note/hint/scene text, audited by nothing, and they disagree with the deck's own Pronunciation field
additions.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:37 MANDATES them: whenever a note or hint quotes non-Roman text, 'ALWAYS follow it immediately with its romanization in parentheses'. Probe over the 2,150 live cards in both delivered collections: 1,847 parenthetical romanizations appear inside note/hint/scene/reviewNote. None of them passes through the romanization pipeline — src/translate/romanizationEval.js and normalizeRomaji only ever touch the `pronunciation` FIELD; note text is free prose written by the extraction and cross-lesson-note passes. The result contradicts the same deck's own audited field: matching each inline romanization against the `pronunciation` of the card whose `target` it quotes yields at least 36 macron-vs-digraph disagreements (note 'ohayou gozaimasu' vs field 'ohayō gozaimasu'; 'sayounara' vs 'sayōnara'; 'mou ichido onegaishimasu' vs 'mō ichido onegaishimasu'; 'sou desu' vs 'sō desu'; 'chuugokujin' vs 'chūgokujin'; 'iie' vs 'īe'), plus a capitalization family in chapter-1-extras where four cards write 'Oosutoraria'/'Oosutorariajin' against the field's 'ōsutoraria'/'ōsutorariajin'. (My extractor also catches ordinary glosses such as 'とても (very)', so treat these as a verified lower bound on the class, not an exact count.) linguist-7's なに note is the same defect in miniature: it writes 'nannin' where the collision rules write 'nan-nin'.
additions.recommendation: This is the cheapest romanization check available anywhere in the repo because ground truth lives in the same file: add a preflight WARN that extracts `<kana/kanji> (roman)` pairs from note/hint/scene, looks the kana up in the collection's own card targets, and reports every case where the inline spelling differs from that card's audited `pronunciation` after case/space normalization. No new judgment and no new model call. Pair it with linguist-1's single pinned Hepburn spec, injected into the extraction and cross-lesson-note prompts so the prose they generate inherits the same convention as the field.

additions.title: 238 live Production cards require producing an unpredictable katakana transliteration from English orthography, with no cue and no rule anywhere
additions.evidence: Probe over the 2,150 live cards: 682 have katakana in `target`; 238 of those have an English gloss containing a mid-sentence capitalized word, i.e. a proper noun the learner must render in katakana to answer the Production direction. Examples in chapter-1 alone: 'Excuse me, are you Hoffman-san of Berlin Motors?' -> すみません。ベルリンモーターズのホフマンさんですか, 'This is Tanaka-san of the Nozomi Department Store.' -> こちらはのぞみデパートのたなかさんです, '[I am] Smith.' -> (わたしは)スミスです. Katakana transliteration is not derivable from anything the learner has been taught: long-vowel ー placement (ベルリンモーターズ), ズ vs ス, ホ vs フォ, and whether a name is even katakana at all (Tanaka is kana, Smith is katakana) are conventions, not rules. references/card-authoring-rules.md's 'answerable alone' rule (:263-282) is about whether enough INFORMATION is present; nothing anywhere asks whether the required ORTHOGRAPHY is producible. src/cards/fillInBlank.js reproduces the textbook's substitution frames wholesale, so proper-noun-bearing drills multiply (6 of chapter-1's FIB cards, 4 with foreign names).
additions.recommendation: Add a rule to references/card-authoring-rules.md and the FIB prompt: when a card's target contains a katakana rendering of a proper noun the learner cannot derive, either (a) put the katakana in the English gloss as a cue ('are you Hoffman-san (ホフマン) of Berlin Motors?'), (b) prefer the frame instance that uses a name already taught as a vocabulary card, or (c) once a per-card direction flag exists (learner-3), ship such drills Recognition-only — recognizing ベルリンモーターズ is a real skill, spelling it from English is not. Detection is mechanizable (katakana in target + capitalized non-initial word in english + that katakana string is not itself a card), the fix is a judgment.

additions.title: Nothing in the pipeline knows what ruby/furigana is — the publisher's own reading annotations are the reading source the next book will supply and the only one nobody planned for
additions.evidence: `grep -rni 'ruby|furigana|<rt>'` across docs/, .claude/skills/build-anki-deck/ and src/corpus/ returns zero hits (the only matches are the word 'annotations' in unrelated prose at docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:140 and epubDedup.js:19). Yet ruby is the standard EPUB mechanism by which Japanese publishers attach readings to kanji, and it is exactly what a non-kana textbook uses on every page. Three layers are unprepared at once: (1) the extraction prompt has no instruction to harvest <rt> content into `reading`, and in fact restricts `reading` to numerals only (docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:30,44); (2) src/model/index.js:141-145 documents `reading` as the general kanji-disambiguation field, contradicting (1) — my linguist-8; (3) the Reading field is rendered by neither template (src/deck/collection.js:167-191) — learner-9. Separately adversarial-4 shows nav LABELS mangle ruby to 漢かん字じ. I verified chapter files are written to disk as raw XHTML (extractChapterToFile writes `content` verbatim), so the ruby markup DOES survive to the extraction model — the reading data is sitting there, unclaimed, and the prompt never mentions it. The JBP kana edition contains no ruby, so this whole chain is untested by construction.
additions.recommendation: Before the second book, settle the reading policy once (linguist-8) and then add one paragraph to docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md: a <ruby>base<rt>reading</rt></ruby> annotation is the book's own authoritative reading — copy it into `reading` (and never into `target`, where interleaving it corrupts the word), and prefer it over any reading you would infer. This is the highest-quality reading source available anywhere in the pipeline and it costs one prompt paragraph. Add a ruby fixture to the epub fixture builder (adversarial-11 asks for the same fixture class for labels) so the behaviour is pinned before a real kanji book arrives rather than after.

endorsements.why: Strongest single finding in the set and it subsumes my techlead-1, codeexpert-1, generalist-3 and adversarial-14. I re-verified both artifacts independently: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json` (fixture payload, mtime today) and four 4-byte files under `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/` (`6dde65c7439b036b{,.orig}.mp3`, `6ce47560ba160669{,.orig}.mp3`) against a smallest-real-clip of 3,846 bytes. qa-1 is the only version that names the escalation path (`getDefaultVoice` returns a REAL voice id, so one test missing `--voice` poisons a live cache key that a later real run gets as a HIT, and `.orig.mp3` poisoning makes `clean-audio.mjs --force` re-derive the garbage) and the `removeChapterCorpus` deletion path. Its fix (`libraryHome()` returns a per-process tmpdir under `isTestEnv()`) is strictly better than my guard-at-bookDir version because it keeps existing tests green while making the writes go nowhere real. Arbiter should merge techlead-1/codeexpert-1/generalist-3/adversarial-14 into this.

Verified exactly: `grep -n rebuildGroupQuiet src/server/index.js` yields one call site, src/server/index.js:286 inside `handleLessonDone`; `handleReviewExclude` (:290), `handleReviewEdit` (:303), `handleSelect`, `handleTrim`, `handleReclean` all return without rebuilding — while src/server/index.js:423-425 and src/deck/rebuild.js:6-8 both assert in prose that an edit to a done lesson keeps the package in step. This is the highest-value correctness finding after qa-1 because it is a FALSE SAFETY CLAIM sitting in the two files a future maintainer will trust, and because SKILL.md:437 explicitly invites post-done field edits as the cheap fix path. The right first move is codeexpert-4's second option (surface staleness) plus my techlead-15 detector, since auto-rebuilding on every keystroke-level edit is a heavier change.

Verified: `grep -rni reopen src/` returns only two unrelated audio-editor comments (src/review/clientScripts.js:329, src/model/index.js:170) — the button is gone — while SKILL.md still prescribes it at :363, :428-429, :433, :439, :610, :611. This is the one doc drift that lands on red line 2: the documented recovery path for a mis-clicked Mark done on a delivered unit is literally impossible, so an agent following SKILL.md will improvise a hand edit of `meta.done` on a live unit. It also shows the doc-drift class is not cosmetic, which is the argument for my techlead-9 docs-integrity test. Pair the fix with a `scripts/undone-unit.mjs` so the one operation that touches a shipped unit is a reviewed script rather than an improvisation.

The best prompt finding and the only one with a verified content loss (chapter 32's あります/います paradigm image → zero cards, with the cached conventions.md naming that exact image as skip-material while docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:146-152 names that exact shape as extract-in-full). Architecturally it identifies a real seam I missed: a cached LLM artifact with no precedence rule and no invalidation is an unversioned config file steering every later paid pass. It also reframes SKILL.md's per-chapter manual image sweep — the sweep is treating a symptom whose cause is a prompt conflict, which is why it never converged. See my techlead-16 for the mechanical half.

Verified the logic shape: src/cli/commands/audio.js:74-78 makes `clipIsCurrent` true whenever `isStageOwnedCard` is false, and src/audio/index.js:204-208 makes that false for any hand-trimmed, hand-picked or uploaded clip — so the content-hash staleness check is disabled for precisely the clips a human invested in, forever, while `editCard` freely rewrites `target`/`reading`. This is the same silent-degradation signature LIMITATIONS.md already records for `isStageOwnedCard`, on a card the owner studies daily, and codeexpert-3's remedy is right in the crucial respect: badge and block, never regenerate over the human's work. Fully mechanizable, no judgment removed.

Correct identification of a load-bearing invariant that exists only in prose (extras-pass.md:71) guarding the dedup library — the same registry qa-1's leak touches and the same one whose incompleteness already cost 12 unflagged repeats. I verified the collision surface is live: chapter-13 and chapter-13-extras both carry `chapterNumber: 33` and only the absence of `epubHash` on the extras unit prevents the overwrite, while extras-pass.md:75-80 itself notes agents copy `meta` wholesale by reflex. Endorse together with generalist-4, which supplies the stronger half of the fix — refuse the library save in `markCardsReviewed` when the run dir ends `-extras`, so no hand edit can route around it — plus qa-4's two preflight assertions as the outer net.

The most concrete evidence anywhere in the set that the parser's single-book proof is a cliff rather than a risk, and it is all mechanism, not judgment: unnamed spine files silently absorbed into the preceding lesson (Betrayer entries [3], [33], [35]; JBP's own entry [56]), spine 1 unreachable via `--lesson` at all, and `describeChapter(1)` colliding with nav entry [1]'s label — which flows into `unitDeckSegments` and therefore into a live Anki deck name. Its fix is the same one I proposed as `epub-probe`: print the shape at `--list-lessons` time, before any paid pass, and let the agent decide. I verified the diagnostic channel is already wired for this — `listLessons`/`resolveLesson` thread `log` through to `ctx.log` (src/cli/commands/assemble.js:139,163) — so these warnings land in front of the human at the decision point rather than in a void. Arbiter should merge adversarial-6 and codeexpert-2 (non-monotonic nav) into this family.

The one finding that correctly identifies a SCOPE error rather than a check error: `findCollisions` is right, and within a book the probe finds zero uncued members — the doctrine works — but scripts/extras-collision-audit.mjs:18-35 and scripts/preflight.mjs resolve one collection dir, while the learner studies one collection. 47 cross-deck target dupes and 10 uncued ambiguous English prompts (はじめまして vs よろしくおねがいします for the same front) are shipping today. Detection is fully mechanizable and the merge-vs-cue fix stays agentic, which is the correct line. Together with qa-2 and qa-5 this establishes that a whole audit SCOPE — everything spanning collections — currently has no home; see my techlead-14.

objections.argument: The defect is real and the two fixes are right, but the severity framing (`critical`, scheduling loss) overstates the mechanism and could misdirect effort. Verified: both markers carry a null/absent `guidNamespace` (output/epubs/.../book.json has `"guidNamespace": null`), so both decks do ship bare guids, and 10 ids overlap. But Anki's .apkg import matches by guid and UPDATES the matched note's fields — existing cards keep their ids, intervals and revlog. The realistic worst case is 10 notes acquiring the wrong book's field values (bad, visible, repairable by a re-deliver), plus a foreign 2,009-card book landing in a 241-card course deck tree — not the scheduling/progress loss red line 2 is about. Two further mitigations qa-2 does not weigh: src/anki/deliver.js:170-178 already writes `anki-delivered.json` into every delivered dir whose `note` field literally instructs never to re-import the .apkg, and SKILL.md:474-480 confines File→Import to a deck's FIRST import and routes every later change through the deliver tool. So the exposure is 'a human deliberately re-imports against two written prohibitions'. Call it high, ship qa-2's two preflight assertions (they are ~20 lines and I agree with both), and note that the marker file's own claim is unverified in the other direction too — it says a re-import 'creates duplicate notes', which contradicts the guid-match-updates model, so someone should establish which is true before writing more prose about it.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: An actual Anki import log (or a scripted import against a throwaway collection) showing that importing a bare-guid .apkg over guid-matching notes resets scheduling, deletes cards, or creates duplicates rather than updating fields in place. If duplicates or resets are what really happens, critical is correct and the fix should be a hard refusal, not a preflight note.

objections.argument: The diagnosis (no per-card direction control) is good; the proposed MECHANISM is the most dangerous suggestion in the whole review and must not be implemented as written. Gating an EXISTING template's qfmt on a new field (`{{^NoRecog}}…{{/NoRecog}}`) means any note flipped to recognition-only renders an empty front for the Production card — and an empty-front card is exactly what Anki's Tools ▸ Empty Cards enumerates and DELETES, taking its interval and revlog with it. That is red line 2 damage triggered by a routine maintenance click, on 2,150 delivered notes, with no warning from this pipeline. It is also not reversible by re-delivering, because the scheduling is gone. The safe shapes are: (a) direction control applies to NEW books only, decided before first import; or (b) add a separate additive template for an opt-in direction (which learner-4 correctly notes the deliverer cannot do yet) and never suppress an existing one; or (c) suppress by suspending the card via AnkiConnect, leaving the template intact. learner-3 gestures at 'ship it with a suspend path, not silently', but the concrete implementation it names is the deleting one, and an implementer following the finding literally will do harm.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Documentation or a test against a scratch collection showing that a card whose front becomes empty after a template edit is retained (not listed by Empty Cards / not removed by Check Database) in the Anki version the owner runs, or a confirmed design where the new field is populated such that no already-delivered note ever renders an empty front.

objections.argument: Severity `high` is wrong for the two CODE changes, which is where the finding puts most of its recommendation. The facts check out (src/deck/collection.js:526-529 gives ord 0 and ord 1 adjacent `position` values; :392-401 ships `new.bury:false` / `rev.bury:false`), but both live in the .apkg's dconf and new-card position table — data that only takes effect on a FRESH import. The owner's decks are already imported and are updated exclusively via AnkiConnect (src/anki/deliver.js pushes fields, model and styling; it never touches dconf or scheduling positions), and both deliver.js's marker and SKILL.md Step 7 forbid re-importing. Modern Anki also does not apply an imported package's deck presets by default. So flipping `bury` and interleaving positions changes nothing for the deck this finding is about; the only actionable item is learner-2's own last sentence — one line in references/deliver.md telling the owner to enable 'Bury new siblings' / 'Bury review siblings' on the preset his book decks use. That is a doc change worth doing, but the finding as ranked will send an implementer to rewrite deck-build code for zero effect on the live collection.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that the owner's live decks were created by importing these .apkg files with deck presets applied AND that a future re-import is part of the intended workflow, or that AnkiConnect delivery pushes dconf (it does not, per src/anki/deliver.js) — either would make the code changes reach the deck that matters.

objections.argument: I agree with the core (two env scopes bundling passes of incomparable blast radius is a real design defect, and I verified only `ANKI_BUILDER_TRANSLATE` and `ANKI_BUILDER_EPUB_LLM` exist, at src/translate/runClaude.js:13,24 and src/corpus/epubLlmRunClaude.js:15). My objection is to one half of the remedy: 'RAISE extraction to effort high' is proposed without touching the timeout, and src/util/runClaude.js pins a single 10-minute `spawnSync` ceiling with one retry at the SAME budget for every pass. Extraction is already the longest agentic pass (multi-file range + image reads), and adversarial-10/promptengineer-5 show the whole-book conventions pass reads 57 files inside that same ceiling. Raising effort on those two passes converts a quality knob into a timeout risk whose failure mode is a hard mid-chapter abort with a misleading error and no partial progress — strictly worse than a slightly weaker extraction. If the scope split lands, `timeoutMs` must become part of the same per-scope resolution (`<SCOPE>_TIMEOUT_MS`) and be raised with the effort, and the conventions pass should be batched before its effort is touched at all. The LOWER half of the recommendation (forward flags, pedagogical sort, semantic dedup, lesson-word categorization → cheaper) I fully agree with and it carries none of this risk.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Timing data from a real extraction run at effort high showing comfortable headroom under 10 minutes on the largest JBP chapter (and on the 57-file conventions pass), or a change making the timeout per-scope configurable — either removes the objection entirely.

objections.argument: Retracting my own in favour of qa-1. Same defect, same artifact, but qa-1 is materially better evidenced (it names the second leak — the four 4-byte `CLIP` stubs in `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/`, which I confirmed against a 3,846-byte smallest real clip — and it traces the escalation through `getDefaultVoice`'s real voice ids and `clean-audio.mjs`'s `.orig.mp3` re-derivation). Its remedy is also better than mine: making `libraryHome()` return a per-process tmpdir under `isTestEnv()` keeps every existing test green, whereas my proposed throw-at-`bookDir()` guard would fail the suite until each un-injected call site is fixed. The arbiter should carry qa-1 and drop techlead-1, codeexpert-1, generalist-3 and adversarial-14 as duplicates, keeping only my one addition: the guard belongs on `libraryHome()` itself rather than on each writer, because `saveChapterCorpus`, `removeChapterCorpus`, `registerEpub` and the audio cache all resolve through it.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Nothing about the defect — only if the arbiter's dedup policy prefers keeping the earliest-filed instance, in which case the audio-cache half of qa-1's evidence must be merged in rather than lost.

additions.title: There is no audit SCOPE above one collection directory — three separate findings are homeless because every checker takes a book dir
additions.evidence: Reading qa-2 (cross-collection id/guid overlap), learner-1 (47 cross-deck target dupes and 10 uncued English prompts across the two delivered decks) and qa-5 (dedup-library completeness, which lives in `.anki-builder/`, not in any collection dir) together makes the shape obvious: every audit in the repo is parameterized by a single collection directory. scripts/preflight.mjs:29-40 `collectionDirs()` iterates `["epubs","courses"]` and then checks each dir independently; scripts/extras-collision-audit.mjs:18-35 and scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs:30-44 take one `<book-dir>` argument. `--all` is a loop over collections, not a whole-workspace view, so no check can ever be written that spans them — and the invariants that matter most to a learner (Anki interleaves every deck studied that day; guids match collection-wide, as src/deck/collection.js:512-518 states in its own comment) are exactly the ones that span them. This is also why the same unit-dir regex is re-typed in three scripts (qa-3): there is no shared loader because there is no shared scope model.
additions.recommendation: Introduce `src/audit/` with one unit loader and a check registry where every check declares its scope: `unit` (schema, ids, spacing, marker-stuck), `collection` (collisions, duplicates, dedup-library coverage, package freshness), `workspace` (cross-collection card-id overlap on bare-guid decks, cross-deck English/target collisions, stray `.apkg` files). scripts/preflight.mjs becomes arg parsing plus a scope filter (`--scope workspace`), gets its first tests (techlead-11), and the templates gap (techlead-4/generalist-5) is fixed once in the loader instead of three times. Purely additive, no judgment moves into code — every new check reports and the agent decides, exactly as preflight.mjs:129-130 already argues.

additions.title: Nothing checks that a collection's shipped .apkg is newer than the units in it — the gate-2 watcher does this by hand for one unit and no tool does it for the rest
additions.evidence: codeexpert-4 proves the `.apkg` goes stale on any post-done dashboard edit (only src/server/index.js:286 rebuilds). SKILL.md:99-118 already treats package freshness as the thing worth watching — its gate-2 snippet is `[ "$APKG" -nt "$RUN/cards.json" ]` — but that is one unit, at one moment, typed by hand, with the slug guessed rather than derived (techlead-8/qa-8). scripts/preflight.mjs contains no `mtime` or `apkg` reference at all (verified by grep), so after the watcher's single check the invariant is unobserved forever. The consequence is precisely the divergence src/deck/shippableCards.js was written to prevent: AnkiConnect delivery reads `cards.json` while the `.apkg` — the restore artifact, and the thing a human reaches for when AnkiConnect is down — reflects an older card set. qa-7's finding that two of three shipped course lessons predate the readiness gate shows how long a unit can sit in a state nobody re-examines.
additions.recommendation: One collection-scoped check: resolve the package with `resolveDeckPathForDir` (src/deck/deckFileName.js:63, the same function the builder uses, so the slug can never be guessed wrong) and FAIL when any `done` unit's `cards.json` is newer than it, naming the units. This detects codeexpert-4's bug and every future variant of it regardless of which handler forgot to rebuild, it retires the hand-typed gate-2 shell (fold it into the `watch`/`check-done` command of techlead-6), and it is ~15 lines with no judgment in it. Fix the two false comments (src/deck/rebuild.js:6-8, src/server/index.js:423-425) in the same change.

additions.title: Cached LLM artifacts in .anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/ carry no provenance, so a prompt change silently never reaches the book it was written for
additions.evidence: promptengineer-1 verified content loss caused by a stale cached artifact; the general defect is that the cache has no version at all. `.anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/` holds three durable LLM outputs — `conventions.md` (dated 14 Jul on disk, and its own text carries no header beyond `# ja Book Conventions`), `taught-index.json` (top-level key `chapters` only, no metadata), and `corpora/<n>.json` — while `docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md` was last touched 9 Aug and `docs/epub-book-conventions-prompt.md` independently. `saveBookConventions` (src/corpus/epubLibrary.js:192-196) is documented as an 'idempotent overwrite' with no staleness concept, and `loadBookConventions` (:182-187) is a plain read. So the conventions text injected into every future chapter extraction was produced by a different model configuration against a different policy, and nothing anywhere can notice. The same applies to `corpora/<n>.json`, which is the dedup input for every later chapter: a chapter extracted under an old prompt keeps steering new ones.
additions.recommendation: Stamp provenance at write time — model id, effort, the SHA of the prompt template file, and a timestamp — as a YAML front-matter block in `conventions.md` and a `_meta` key in the JSON artifacts. Then have `assemble` WARN (never block) when the prompt SHA behind a cached artifact differs from the current one: 'conventions were generated under a different extraction policy — consider re-running'. Re-running is a judgment call about cost and churn and stays with the agent; noticing is not. This is the cheapest available guard against the class promptengineer-1 found, and it generalizes to any future cached pass.

additions.title: 'Delivered' is recorded and never enforced — the only marker that knows a collection is in the live collection is read by a UI badge and nothing else
additions.evidence: src/anki/deliver.js:170-178 writes `anki-delivered.json` into every delivered collection dir, and its `note` field is an explicit prohibition ('Do NOT re-import the .apkg into that collection'). Grepping `DELIVERED_MARKER` across src/ and scripts/ returns exactly three sites: the constant, the writer, and src/server/pages.js:102 — a dashboard badge. No guard reads it. Meanwhile every mutation guard in the repo keys on a WEAKER proxy: scripts/extras-order.mjs:35-42 and extras-duplicate-check.mjs:64-69 check `meta.reviewed || meta.done` and accept `--force`; src/cards/readiness.js:50 keys on `meta.reviewed`; deliver keys on the marker. So the state that actually means 'this is in the collection the owner studies daily' — red line 2's exact scope — is the one state no check consults, and `--force` on a delivered unit is indistinguishable from `--force` on a draft. qa-6, learner-10 and qa-2 are each a symptom of this.
additions.recommendation: Define one `unitState(runDir)` / `collectionState(dir)` in src/model returning `{authored, reviewed, done, packaged, delivered}` (delivered = marker present and `lastDeliveredAt` >= the unit's mtime), and make it the single input to every guard: scripts refuse `--apply` on a DELIVERED collection without a distinct second flag (not the same `--force` that covers a merely-reviewed draft), preflight reports delivered-but-stale units (techlead-15), and the dashboard badge keeps using it. This does not constrain any authoring judgment; it just makes the system able to answer 'is this live?' in one place instead of four approximations.

additions.title: Every mechanization the review proposes lands in scripts/, which has no tests, no write discipline and no lifecycle — fix the substrate before adding to it
additions.evidence: Counting across all nine perspectives, the recommended new mechanism is overwhelmingly script-shaped: vocab-coverage and paradigm-grid (techlead-3/promptengineer-8), epub-probe / shape report (techlead-10, adversarial-2/10/12), await-review (techlead-6/generalist-7), check-done (qa-8), finalize-extras (techlead-12), verify-apkg-import (qa-10), prune-baks (generalist-10), suspend-orphans (learner-10), undone-unit (generalist-1), plus new preflight checks from nearly every agent. The destination has: zero tests (`find test -path '*script*'` → only test/model/scriptSpacing.test.js), no atomic-write or backup discipline (no script imports src/util/atomicWrite.js, per qa-6), no lifecycle marking (five spent one-off migrations sit beside standing tools, techlead-5), and a shipped arg-parsing bug already fixed by a comment rather than a test (commit 82e77b9). Adding ten more tools to that substrate reproduces the exact failure mode the review is trying to close, at ten times the surface.
additions.recommendation: Sequence the work: (1) land techlead-14's `src/audit/` + shared unit loader and give scripts/ its first test dir; (2) adopt the rule the codebase half-follows — a script that MUTATES output/ keeps its logic in src/ behind a unit test, the .mjs is arg parsing and reporting; (3) split `scripts/migrations/` from standing tools with a `// SPENT:` header; (4) only then add the new tools, each as a thin CLI over a tested src/ function. Also add the docs-integrity test (techlead-9) at step 1, so the ten new tools cannot repeat the `backfill-dedup-library.mjs` drift where LIMITATIONS.md documents a script that no longer exists. This is a sequencing recommendation, not a new defect — but every other agent's mechanization plan depends on it and none of them state it.

endorsements.why: Verified the mechanism end-to-end and it is the sharpest red-line-2 item in the set. src/deck/collection.js:513-518 emits `guidNamespace ? ns+'/'+id : card.id`, and src/deck/rebuild.js:148 confirms a marker without the field ⇒ BARE guids; both live markers lack a namespace. Anki matches guids collection-wide on import, so importing one bare-guid .apkg into a collection already holding the other UPDATES those 10 notes' fields in place — a silent content swap on cards with real scheduling. Supporting detail from my own read: `abid:<card.id>` is also a collection-global tag string that is only saved by the deck-scoped query at deliver.js:350, so those 10 ids are a second, independent collision surface should the two parents ever nest. The stray japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana.apkg physically sitting in the course dir is the loaded gun.

Verified: `grep -rn reopen src/` returns only two unrelated comments (clientScripts.js:329, model/index.js:170) — the button is gone, while SKILL.md still prescribes Reopen as the recovery path in four places. This is the only finding where the documented remedy for a mis-click on a DELIVERED, daily-studied unit is literally impossible, which forces an agent to improvise a hand edit of meta.done on shipped state. Prose-only fix, zero risk, highest value-per-line in the whole set.

Confirmed by reading src/anki/deliver.js:196-248: there is createModel, modelFieldAdd, modelFieldReposition and updateModelTemplates, and no modelTemplateAdd anywhere in the repo. This is a hard prerequisite that several other recommendations silently depend on (learner-3 direction flags, learner-9 rendering Reading as a new card, my own suggestions about card faces). It should be ranked as a blocker rather than a standalone defect: without it, `tmplChanged` computes a diff against a template name AnkiConnect will not create, and the deliver reports success having changed nothing.

The strongest of the several dedup-library findings (generalist-4 is the same defect). applyCards.js:107-124 keys purely on (epubHash, chapterNumber) with no unit discriminator, and I confirmed chapter-13 and chapter-13-extras both carry chapterNumber 33 — so exactly one copied field turns a Mark reviewed on an extras unit into a silent overwrite of its base chapter's dedup corpus. The proposed server-side refusal on a `-extras` runDir is two lines, deterministic, and closes the historical 12-unflagged-repeats failure class at its write site rather than in prose.

The only finding in the set that demonstrates a concrete extraction MISS with the artifact in hand (ch.32 あります/います paradigm image → zero cards, against an extraction prompt whose own worked example says extract it in full). It is also the one finding that explains a class SKILL.md itself calls structurally invisible. The precedence-statement fix and the prompt-hash staleness link are both prompt-side, cheap, and respect red line 1 — they change who wins a conflict, not who judges.

Independently corroborates the seam I found from the other direction: epubArchive.js:528-534 derives every range from the NEXT surviving entry, so both a nav entry that never parsed (my codeexpert-9) and a spine file the nav never names (theirs) are absorbed with zero diagnostics. Their fix — print, per entry, how many files in the range the TOC actually named, plus an explicit 'unreachable via --lesson' line for pre-first-entry spine files — is the single cheapest change that converts this whole silent class into something visible at --list-lessons, before any paid pass.

Verified both halves: collection.js:526-529 walks ord 0..1 with `position++` inside the loop (adjacent new-card due positions), and :394/:401 ship `new.bury:false` / `rev.bury:false`. One correction to the recommendation, not the finding: the AnkiConnect path never writes dconf and never sets `due` (addNote lets Anki assign it), so for the owner's actual delivery path BOTH code-side fixes are inert — the only thing that reaches the live collection is the one-line deliver.md instruction to enable sibling burying on the preset. Rank the doc line first and the code change as .apkg-only hygiene.

Corroborated from the delivery side: I independently counted 17 targets repeating across units in the live book, and the に group's keeper being chapter-2's number '2' is exactly the false-positive shape. The asymmetry they name is the real defect — preflight.mjs:129 argues in writing that this is a judgment that must never be auto-applied, while extras-pass.md:210 advertises `--apply` as a normal step. Making report-only the documented path costs nothing and removes an --apply that can silently strip five correct particle cards from an in-flight chapter.

objections.argument: The observation (all-kana is worse TTS input, and the codebase says so at generateKanjiVariants.js:15-17) is right; the recommendation to make kanji the ja DEFAULT is not, and would be expensive and risky on a delivered deck. The clip identity is `hashTerm(defaultClipText(item, lang))` (src/audio/index.js, defaultOriginalFilename/defaultClipFilename), so changing what defaultClipText returns for ja re-hashes EVERY ja card: every stage-owned clip becomes stale, ~1,700 clips regenerate at ElevenLabs cost, every filename changes (media churn on a live collection plus a fresh 1,900-clip audio review), and the ~200 hand-picked/hand-trimmed clips do NOT regenerate (isStageOwnedCard returns false) so the deck ends up half kanji-voiced and half kana-voiced with no marker. Worse, the kanji orthography is LLM-derived per card, so it introduces a new silent wrong-word channel (今 → いま vs こん) into audio, which is precisely the class the deck has no automated check for. If it is done at all it must be new-cards-only, or the hash must stay keyed on the kana so existing clips are not invalidated.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A design that keeps the cache key on the kana text (or a documented one-off migration plan with a cost estimate and a plan for the ~200 human-owned clips), plus a blind A/B on 20 cards showing deployed-model kanji generation is accurate enough that no card ships a wrong reading.

objections.argument: Per-card direction control is the right goal, but the proposed mechanism — a conditional wrapper on qfmt so the front renders empty — is unsafe on the owner's live collection. In Anki, a card whose front renders empty is not skipped; it becomes an 'empty card' that Tools → Empty Cards offers to DELETE, taking its interval and revlog with it. That is a scheduling-loss path on a daily-studied deck (red line 2) triggered by a routine maintenance click the owner may perform for unrelated reasons. It is also unshippable today regardless: learner-4 establishes there is no modelTemplateAdd path, and suppressing a direction on an already-delivered note produces exactly the orphan class learner-10 documents as never suspended.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Confirmation from current Anki behaviour that a conditionally-empty card retains its scheduling and is not offered for deletion by the Empty Cards tool, or a revised design that suppresses a direction only for NEW notes (e.g. a second note type) so no existing card can ever go empty.

objections.argument: The per-pass scoping recommendation is right and the extraction-to-high argument is well made, but one item on the 'lower to Haiku' list is misclassified: semanticDedup does not fail open. src/cards/semanticDedup.js:88-89 sets `item.excluded = true` plus a reviewNote — the card is silently dropped from the built deck unless a reviewer reads every reviewNote at gate 1. A cheaper model there trades LLM cost for a content-loss channel that is exactly the repo's stated silent-degradation signature, and the saving is trivial (one call per lesson). Forward flags and pedagogical sort genuinely do fail open (sort is a validated permutation; flags are advisory and prompt-biased toward false positives) — lower those, keep dedup where it is.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A measurement over the 15 reviewed chapters showing dedup's exclusions are always caught at gate 1 (e.g. every excluded card was individually acted on), or a design where a cheaper dedup only PROPOSES exclusions for reviewer confirmation instead of setting `excluded` directly.

objections.argument: Severity is wrong and the framing is actively harmful. This is the same defect as qa-1 / codeexpert-1 / techlead-1 / generalist-3, filed at 'low' on the reasoning that a fake hash makes it harmless. The harmlessness is an accident of one fixture string, not a property of the code: libraryHome() (src/model/index.js:365) has no test override at all, applyCards.js defaults BOTH saveChapterCorpus and the rmSync-ing removeChapterCorpus to the real library, and the same missing-injection pattern already put 4-byte CLIP stubs into the real audio cache under a REAL voice id. A 'low' filing invites the arbiter to defer the guard, which is the one thing that converts this from a stray directory into a lost chapter corpus.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A demonstration that no test path can reach libraryHome() with a value derived from real data (a hash, a voice id, an output dir) — i.e. that every write site is either injected or provably fixture-only.

objections.argument: Retracting the second half of my own finding as overstated. The dead `flags.book` term at assemble.js:99 is real but purely cosmetic. The `--lesson` claim I attached to it — that the ordered-warning comparison works 'only by coincidence' — is not a defect: both sides deliberately key on the lesson's first spine index because that is the same value used as the corpora/<n>.json join key, so it is an invariant, not luck. What survives is the documentation ask (state once, at the definition site, that `chapterNumber` means the lesson's FIRST spine index, since four modules join on it), and that belongs folded into codeexpert-2 rather than standing as its own finding. Drop the rest.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A case where a sibling unit's meta.chapterNumber is written from a nav ordinal rather than a spine index — which would make the two sides genuinely inconsistent and revive the original claim.

additions.title: The deliverer never MOVES a note between decks — any unit-label change strands the existing cards in the old subdeck forever
additions.evidence: `grep -n changeDeck src/` returns nothing; src/anki/deliver.js only ever calls `createDeck` (ensureDecks, :270-276) and `addNote({deckName: unit.ankiDeck})` (:429) — `updateNoteFields` (:412) changes fields only. Matching is scoped to `deck:"<ankiParent>"` (:350), which in Anki includes subdecks, so after a chapterLabel change every existing note is still FOUND and updated in place while sitting under the OLD subdeck name; ensureDecks then creates the new, empty deck. The one cleanup that exists (removeLegacyDeckShells, :297-317) handles a single known shape (flat → grouped) and explicitly refuses any deck that still holds cards, logging `legacy deck "…" still holds N card(s) — left alone`. This is the missing prerequisite under adversarial-4 and my codeexpert-7: chapterLabel → corpus.meta → unitDeckSegments → unit.ankiDeck is the live deck path, so 'fix the entity/ruby/label decoder' does not rename a deck — it SPLITS a chapter across two decks in a collection studied daily, with the old one silently retaining all the scheduling.
additions.recommendation: Two parts. (1) Before shipping any label-parsing fix, add a re-file step: for each abid-matched note whose current deck != unit.ankiDeck, call AnkiConnect `changeDeck` on its cards and report the moves exactly like `createdDecks` — changeDeck preserves scheduling, so this is red-line-safe and is the only way a label fix can land on an existing book. (2) Independently of any fix, have preflight or the deliver dry run report 'N note(s) are in a deck other than their unit's' — today that divergence is invisible on both sides. Alternatively, if re-filing is deliberately out of scope, state in references/deliver.md that chapterLabel is frozen at first delivery and gate label-decoder fixes to new books only.

additions.title: A change to the book/course TITLE re-adds every card as a duplicate, and the pre-write backup does not fail closed
additions.evidence: `ankiParent` is `resolveBookName(...)` = `bookMeta?.title || bookMeta?.name || fallback` (src/deck/rebuild.js:84-91) — i.e. a human-editable title field in book.json/course.json, not a stable slug. Every note lookup hangs off it: deliver.js:350 queries `deck:"<ankiParent>" note:"<model>"`, so if the title changes the query returns ZERO notes, `byAbid` is empty, every card falls through to `addNote(..., options:{allowDuplicate:true})` (:429) and the entire book is re-inserted as fresh notes with no scheduling. Nothing bounds this: there is no add-count ceiling, no 'expected ~N existing notes' assertion, and scripts/deliver-to-anki.mjs just prints `+ new:` per card. The backup that is supposed to be fail-closed does not catch it either: deliver.js:541-548 wraps `client.exportPackage(parent, ...)` in try/catch, but src/anki/ankiConnect.js:29 throws ONLY when `json.error` is set — AnkiConnect's exportPackage returns `result: false` (no error) for a deck that does not exist, so the backup records a false success for the new, empty parent name and delivery proceeds.
additions.recommendation: Three cheap guards, all deterministic. (a) Treat a falsy `exportPackage` result as a failure in the backup loop — one `if (ok === false) throw` restores the fail-closed property the comment already claims. (b) Add a sanity assertion in syncDeckContent: if a `<bookDir>/anki-delivered.json` marker exists (the deck has been delivered before) and the bootstrap query returns 0 notes, ABORT naming the likely cause ('the book title changed — the previous deck is <name from the marker>'). (c) Record the delivered `ankiParent` in that marker so the rename is detectable at all, and consider adding an add-count ceiling (`--allow-adds N`) so any run that would insert more than a chapter's worth of new notes requires an explicit flag.

additions.title: CARD_TEMPLATES/BASE_CSS are per-LANGUAGE and force-synced, so a template edit for one book silently rewrites the note type of every other deck in that language
additions.evidence: The note type is keyed on the language alone — `AnkiBuilder <lang>` with a language-derived id (src/deck/collection.js:languageLabel/languageModelId, comment at :52-56 'one shared note type per language'). The deliverer force-syncs it: deliver.js:234-248 computes `tmplChanged` from any qfmt/afmt difference and calls updateModelTemplates, and the same block pushes CSS. So delivering ANY ja deck rewrites the templates and CSS for the JBP book AND the nihongo course simultaneously, with no diff shown, no per-deck opt-out and no confirmation. It also flips `report.schemaChanged` (:579), which the code itself notes forces a one-way full AnkiWeb sync the user must complete by hand — so an unrelated deck's delivery can leave the collection in a state needing a manual Upload click. This is a prerequisite that four separate recommendations in this review (learner-6 prompt sizing, learner-7 contrast, learner-9 rendering {{Reading}}, learner-12 a listening template) all step on without noticing.
additions.recommendation: Do not change the sharing (one note type per language is correct — it is what stops a pile-up of duplicates). Instead make the blast radius visible and reversible: have `--dry` print a unified diff of the live qfmt/afmt/CSS vs the spec plus the list of ALL decks using that model (findNotes by `note:"<model>"` grouped by deck), and require an explicit `--allow-model-change` when `tmplChanged || cssChanged`. The models.json structure snapshot already written into the backup dir (deliver.js:558-566) means the restore side already exists; only the pre-change warning is missing.

endorsements.why: Strictly the best version of the finding four of us hit independently (mine was generalist-3, plus techlead-1/codeexpert-1/adversarial-14). qa-1 alone carries the escalation that makes it critical rather than tidy-up: `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/*.mp3` are 4-byte `CLIP` stubs from test/cli/index.test.js, getDefaultVoice returns a REAL voice id, and the cache key has no provenance — so one test run that omits `--voice` poisons a real voice's cache with a `.orig.mp3` that clean-audio.mjs would faithfully re-derive into a shipped card. That is the whole silent-degradation signature in one artifact. Its fix (libraryHome() refuses/redirects under isTestEnv, mirroring the existing assertExternalCallAllowed idiom) subsumes every other version. Fix this first; it is cheap and it is the only finding where the test suite can write into state the daily deck reads.

The only finding in the set that traces a concrete, verified CARD LOSS to a root cause nobody would find by reading code: the cached conventions.md (14 Jul) names ch.32's あります/います paradigm image as 'still exercise material — skip', while docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md (9 Aug) uses that exact class of table as its worked example of 'reference material, extract in full' — and chapter-12/cards.json contains zero of those forms.
