It also identifies a structural hazard my docs-drift lens missed entirely: a CACHED LLM artifact is injected into a later prompt with no precedence rule and no invalidation when the prompt changes. That is a per-book, permanently-silent quality cap. The precedence sentence and the prompt-hash staleness warning are both cheap and neither touches the agentic core.

Verified independently: SKILL.md:280-283 says 'Every stage of the pipeline reads the stripped-out plain text' and extras-pass.md:129 says 'the pipeline never has [looked at images]', while docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md has a dedicated §Images section instructing the model to resolve each and open it with Read, and src/corpus/epubArchive.js:577-591 exists solely to make that resolution work. This matters beyond accuracy: it is the diagnosis that kept the real cause (promptengineer-1) hidden, and it mandates a per-chapter human chore justified by a false premise. Highest-value doc correction in the set after my own generalist-1.

Verified: SKILL.md:367 says run Step 3b 'right after the base unit passes Gate 1', while :60-61 ('after gate 2 run the extras pass') and the arc diagram at :142-143 (extras follows Mark done) say gate 2 — two against one, inside one file. For an orchestrating agent this is a real fork with a real consequence: gate-2 exclusions change the base card set that the extras duplicate/collision audits diff against, so starting at gate 1 silently invalidates those audits. One-line fix, and it is the kind of self-contradiction that my generalist-2 shows this file accumulates because nothing lints it.

Verified: `rebuildGroupQuiet` has exactly one caller (src/server/index.js:286, handleLessonDone) while src/deck/rebuild.js:6-8 and src/server/index.js:421-424 both assert an edit to an already-done lesson rebuilds too. This lands directly on the seam SKILL.md's whole gate-2 procedure is built on ('watch the artifact, not the checkbox') and on my generalist-1: SKILL.md now tells the agent to hand-edit fields on a done unit, and the shipping .apkg silently goes stale. A false safety claim in the two files a future reader trusts is worse than the missing rebuild.

The single best second-book finding, and its fix lives in my area: SKILL.md:184 tells the agent to 'offer the `lesson`-typed entries as options', and on the probed hostile EPUB 0/35 entries classify as `lesson` — the agent offers an empty menu. classifyLesson is honestly documented as a heuristic; the defect is the skill doc promoting it to a gate. The owner has already hand-worked-around it once (chapter-0 is the `other`-typed 'Frequently Used Expressions'). Change the doc to present all entries with `type` as an annotation, never a filter — free, and it removes the most likely first-five-minutes failure of book #2.

Verified src/deck/collection.js:394/401 (`new.bury: false`, `rev.bury: false`) and :526-529 (the two ords of one note get adjacent new positions). It is the only finding in the whole set about how the deck is actually STUDIED daily rather than how it is built, the fix is scheduling-safe by construction (dconf applies to a fresh import only; position order affects new cards only), and it is one flag plus one line in references/deliver.md for the AnkiConnect path which never applies dconf. Highest study-value-per-line-changed in the set.

Both techlead-3 and promptengineer-8 found it; techlead-3 covers both missing scripts (vocabulary diff AND paradigm audit) and correctly notes extras-pass.md:153-169 encodes ~15 lines of real matching rules (predicate position after が/は/も/に, exclude longer forms of the same paradigm) as prose that the agent re-implements from memory every chapter. This is the same class as my generalist-7 (the review watcher): a fully deterministic check written out as prose and hand-re-derived per unit. It is also the check guarding the failure mode SKILL.md itself calls structurally invisible ('nothing downstream can notice what was never extracted'), so per-chapter variance in how it is re-improvised is exactly the wrong place for variance.

objections.argument: RETRACTING MY OWN as a weaker duplicate. generalist-3 says the leak is 'benign because h1 is not a real hash'. qa-1 shows it is not benign: the same missing-injection pattern in test/cli/index.test.js has already written 4-byte `CLIP` stubs into `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/`, and getDefaultVoice returns real voice ids, so the audio-cache variant of this bug can poison a real voice with no fake-hash safety net. My recommendation (a libraryHomeDir parameter threaded through startDeckServer) is also the wrong shape — it relies on every future test remembering to pass it, which is the failure that produced the artifact. qa-1's version (libraryHome() itself refuses or redirects under isTestEnv, mirroring assertExternalCallAllowed) is correct. Drop generalist-3, keep qa-1.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Nothing — this is a retraction in favour of a strictly stronger finding with the same fix. If anything I would want qa-1's fix widened to cover `output/` writes too, not narrowed.

objections.argument: The mechanized checks are right and I want them, but 'critical' overstates the harm and mis-prices it against red line 2. Anki's .apkg importer matches notes by guid and UPDATES the matching note in place — it does not move the note's cards to the incoming deck and does not reset scheduling. So the worst case for the 10 colliding ids is: 10 existing notes get their fields overwritten with the other deck's text (visible, and recoverable — deliver.js:536-560 snapshots each parent deck as .apkg plus models.json before every run), plus ~2,000 foreign notes added to the collection. That is loud and reversible, not the silent scheduling/progress loss red line 2 is about. Compare qa-1, where a poisoned cache entry ships audible garbage with no signal at all. Rank qa-2 high, below qa-1 and codeexpert-4.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A demonstration (or Anki source/docs citation) that an .apkg import whose incoming note carries a matching guid but a DIFFERENT notetype id either duplicates the note, re-homes its existing cards into the incoming deck, or resets due/ivl. If a mid mismatch on a guid hit causes anything other than an in-place field update or a skip, this is critical and I withdraw the objection.

objections.argument: The EOCD uint16 throw is a good idea and should ship. The media memoization should NOT — at least not now. This is the exact code path whose last 'obviously reasonable' change (the `${chapterIndex}-${mediaIndex}` key scheme) produced an .apkg that Anki's importer rejected outright while passing every test and every synthetic check (src/deck/index.js:28-38 documents this at length; LIMITATIONS.md:423-447 says there is still no automated real-import test). The payoff is 22 redundant zip entries out of 1,914 — well under 1 MB on an 11 MB package — against re-entering a path with a proven history of silent format bugs and zero real verification. Sequence it strictly after qa-10's scripts/verify-apkg-import.mjs exists, or drop it.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A real Anki import of a memoized package (a `media` map where two keys map to the same filename, or one key referenced by two notes) importing cleanly with all audio playing — i.e. qa-10's verifier existing and passing. Then it is a fine cleanup.

objections.argument: I agree the harness loop is dead and should be retired (outcomes.jsonl stops 2026-07-13 against 535 commits), and my generalist-11 says the same about IDEAS.jsonl. But 'mark T011 dropped' is the wrong half. T011 ('build a real travel deck + verify in Anki') is the ONLY written pointer at the template path, and three of us independently found that path is the least-exercised surface in the repo: output/templates/ is empty (mine, generalist-5), preflight never enumerates it (generalist-5, techlead-4), and src/cards/readiness.js:50 exempts sourceType==='template' from the readiness gate entirely (qa-7, qa-10). Retiring the loop should MOVE T011's content into LIMITATIONS.md or the skill's own backlog, not delete it — otherwise the retirement quietly erases the record of the biggest untested path, which is the same silent-degradation shape the rest of this review is about.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: The owner stating that the template path is deliberately abandoned and that only EPUB/course sources will ever be built — in which case dropping T011 AND deleting the template branches from src/cli/commands/prepare.js and readiness.js is the honest move, not just dropping the task.

objections.argument: Making kanji-orthography TTS the DEFAULT for ja is the one recommendation in this set that could silently degrade the existing 1,914-clip corpus. Two mechanisms: (a) it changes speechText for every ja card, and per codeexpert-3 the staleness chain (isStageOwnedCard, src/audio/index.js:204-208) exempts every hand-trimmed / hand-picked / uploaded clip from the text-changed check — so the ~200 clips the owner personally auditioned (109 manual trims, 86 re-rolls, 81 genkanji, 4 uploads) would keep their old audio while every untouched clip silently re-generates against different input, leaving a corpus with two provenances and no record of which is which; (b) the kanji orthography is itself LLM-generated, so a wrong kanji choice (は/わ, 一日 ついたち vs いちにち, counter readings) produces confidently wrong audio for a KANA deck where the learner cannot detect the error from the card face. The right shape is the one that already exists — generate the suggestion, show it in the audio review, let the human accept — plus surfacing it automatically instead of behind a per-card button.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A blind A/B on ~20 clips (kana input vs kanji input) showing the kanji path clearly better, PLUS a stated migration plan proving existing hand-touched clips are untouched and the mixed-provenance corpus is recorded. With both, flip the default for NEW cards only.

objections.argument: PARTIAL RETRACTION OF MY OWN recommendation. I recommended deleting the stale review-corpus/translate/audio.html artifacts from every unit dir. Having since confirmed that /output (422 MB) and /.anki-builder (292 MB) are both gitignored and untracked with no backup anywhere (see gen-14 below), I withdraw the 'delete' half: those files are unversioned forensic snapshots of what a reviewer actually signed off on, and deleting them is an irreversible mutation of unbacked state to make a doc claim true. Fix the doc instead (SKILL.md:624 should say 'stale review-*.html files may exist in older unit dirs; nothing writes them now — do not read them'), and let any deletion wait behind a snapshot. The .bak stamping half of the recommendation stands and is more urgent than I rated it.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A backup/versioning mechanism for output/ existing (gen-14), after which deleting genuinely dead artifacts is fine and I would re-raise it.

objections.argument: The single shared UNIT_DIR_PATTERN / listUnitDirs is right and I endorse that half. But 'make preflight FAIL on any directory that contains a cards.json and does not match' will fire on legitimate structure the moment preflight learns templates: a template unit lives at output/templates/<name>/<lang>/ and contains a cards.json that can never match /^(chapter|lesson)-\d+(-extras)?$/ (generalist-5, techlead-4). Shipped as a FAIL, this makes `npm run preflight` red for a whole legitimate source type and trains the operator to ignore it — the same wallpaper failure as the report-only lines that have never been zero. Make it a REPORT line ('N unit-shaped dirs not covered by any check') until the shapes preflight recognises are complete, then promote it.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: preflight's unit loader covering the templates shape first (techlead-4's recommendation); once every legitimate shape is recognised, a hard fail on the residue is correct and I withdraw this.

additions.title: Every irreplaceable artifact in this project is gitignored, untracked, and has no backup — and half this review's recommendations mutate or delete inside it
additions.evidence: Verified: .gitignore lines 7-11 exclude BOTH `/output` and `/.anki-builder`, and `git ls-files output` / `git ls-files .anki-builder` return NOTHING — 422 MB of output/ (1,914 delivered cards across 29 hand-reviewed units, ~2,173 auditioned clips, 330 .bak files) and 292 MB of .anki-builder/ (140 MB audio cache; 152 MB epubs, holding the 15 human-reviewed corpora/<n>.json that ARE the backward-dedup library, conventions.md, taught-index.json, 727 cached images) exist in exactly one place on one disk, in no version control, with no snapshot. `anki-backups/` is also gitignored, is auto-pruned (src/anki/deliver.js:111-160, keep-recent + one per older week, written after a 780 MB incident), and backs up the LIVE ANKI COLLECTION — not output/, not the library. So the one thing with a backup is the one thing that can be rebuilt from the others, and the months of human review that cannot be rebuilt has none. Now compound it with what this review already established: the test suite writes into that state (qa-1, artifact on disk today); scripts/extras-duplicate-check.mjs:90 and extras-order.mjs:69/78 rewrite units with bare writeFileSync, no atomic write, no backup, no post-validate, and `--force` lets them do it to a `done` unit (qa-6); and the ONLY restore point is the `.pre-<reason>.bak` convention that card-authoring-rules.md itself documents as self-overwriting on the second run of the same tool (generalist-10). A single bad `--apply` sweep, a mistyped `rm`, or a disk failure loses the corpus, and with it the ability to correct or rebuild a deck the owner studies daily.
additions.recommendation: This is the prerequisite for most of the rest of this review, not a parallel item. (a) Put the small, irreplaceable half under version control TODAY: output/**/{cards.json,corpus.json,*.json markers} plus .anki-builder/epubs/*/{corpora,conventions.md,taught-index.json} are a few MB of JSON — either un-ignore exactly those globs (keeping audio/, images/, *.apkg, *.bak ignored) or add `scripts/snapshot-state.mjs` writing a timestamped tarball of them beside anki-backups/ with the same prune policy that already exists. (b) Route every scripts/ --apply write through writeFileAtomic + backupFileOnce + validate (qa-6). (c) Stamp .bak filenames so a second run cannot clobber the first restore point. (d) Sequence every destructive recommendation in this review — deleting .anki-builder/epubs/h1, the test-stub mp3s, the stale review-*.html, the stray course .apkg, .bak pruning — AFTER (a). Red line 2 is about not losing the owner's daily-study work; the deck files and the review that produced them are that work, and they are currently one command from gone.

additions.title: Nine reviewers propose ~15 new preflight checks onto a tool with no severity policy, no acknowledgement mechanism, and no tests — that converts the one deterministic gate into wallpaper
additions.evidence: Across this review, preflight is the recommended home for: cross-collection duplicate ids (qa-2), the -extras epubHash guard (qa-4, generalist-4), dedup-library completeness (qa-5), done-but-ungated units (qa-7), meta-vs-marker agreement and numbering gaps (qa-11), corpus/cards drift (qa-12), a romaji style lint (linguist-1), the 'answerable alone' audit (linguist-10), a 〜-in-target assertion (promptengineer-3), cross-deck collisions (learner-1), a near-sibling frame check (learner-8), templates coverage (generalist-5, techlead-4), stray .apkg names (qa-2, generalist-13), and a vocabulary diff (promptengineer-8, techlead-3). Today the tool has six checks, and TWO of its report-only lines have never once been zero — `· duplicates 17 target group(s)` and `· audio 7 clip(s) flagged marker-audible`, both shipped and both followed by `preflight clean` (my generalist-6; techlead-8 independently). It also has zero tests (generalist-12, techlead-11, qa-6), so a check that silently matches nothing is indistinguishable from a check that passes — qa-3's exact signature. Adding fifteen more report lines to that base produces a screen of permanent notices before a review link, which is how the operator learns to scroll past the one line that is new.
additions.recommendation: Do the policy work BEFORE the checks, in this order: (1) three declared tiers — FAIL (blocks handing over a review link), ACK (report + a per-collection `.preflight-accepted.json` written only by an explicit `preflight --accept`, so the printed count is UNREVIEWED instances, techlead-8's design), INFO (coverage/shape reporting that never fails); (2) preflight prints a coverage header — how many collections, units and unit-shaped-but-unmatched dirs it actually looked at — so 'clean' can never mean 'I did not look' (generalist-5); (3) `test/scripts/preflight.test.js` over a tmpdir fixture root with one deliberately-broken unit per kind, so a new check is proven to fire before it is trusted; (4) each new check declares its tier in one line at the top of the file. Then land the checks, cheapest-and-FAIL-tier first: -extras epubHash guard, 〜-in-target, dedup-library completeness, cross-collection ids, stray .apkg name. My generalist-6's marker-stuck promotion should be FAIL-for-not-yet-done / ACK-for-done under this scheme.

additions.title: LIMITATIONS.md is the project's real planning artifact and its 55 entries have no status field — entries that assert live-data facts have already rotted into false ground truth
additions.evidence: Verified: `.harness/custom/docs/LIMITATIONS.md` has 55 `## ` entries and ZERO `Status:` markers; the stated schema (line 8) is What / Why / Impact / When-to-revisit — there is no field for 'resolved', 'superseded', or 'last verified'. techlead-7 shows this file is where the work actually gets steered (83 commits, newest 2026-08-13, against a harness loop dead since 2026-07-13). Three independent rot instances surfaced in this review: LIMITATIONS.md:900-916 documents `scripts/backfill-dedup-library.mjs`, deleted in commit 991d0cb (techlead-5); :1379-1385 asserts three degenerate uncued pairs 'still show identical Recognition fronts', and probing the live corpus shows two of the three no longer exist and the third is now cued (learner-11); :495-517 repeats across four lines the same false 'Haiku pass' claim as the src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js:83 comment (qa-13, generalist-9). Everyone in this review — and every future agent — treats this file as ground truth about what is known and already decided, so a false entry is worse than a missing one: it closes a question that is actually open (the backfill entry) or opens one that is closed (the uncued pairs).
additions.recommendation: Add two lines to the entry schema and backfill them lazily, not in a big sweep: `**Status:** open | resolved <commit> | superseded by <entry>` and, for any entry asserting a fact about live data, `**Verified by:** <command>` naming the script that re-derives it (`node scripts/extras-collision-audit.mjs <book>`, `node scripts/preflight.mjs --all`) instead of freezing a count in prose — learner-11's idea generalized. Then a cheap docs-integrity test (techlead-9's shape) asserts every `scripts/*.mjs` path mentioned in LIMITATIONS.md, docs/, README.md or .claude/skills/ exists on disk, which catches the deleted-script class mechanically. Fix the three known-rotten entries while adding the field.

additions.title: The per-chapter image sweep SKILL.md mandates re-extracts, by hand from the .epub, artifacts that are already on disk in two places
additions.evidence: SKILL.md:286-289 prescribes `grep -o '<img[^>]*>' <chapter>.xhtml` then `unzip -o -j <book>.epub '*<ImageName>*' -d <scratchpad>/imgs`, framed as costing 'about thirty seconds', and calls it 'a required step of every EPUB build'. But src/corpus/epubArchive.js already extracted them: `.anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/images/` holds 727 files (verified), placed there precisely so the extraction prompt's Read-the-image instruction resolves (epubArchive.js:577-591), and the chapter XHTML is cached at `.anki-builder/epubs/<hash>/chapters/<n>.xhtml` — the snippet's `<chapter>.xhtml` never says where that is, so the agent must first find it. On top of that, conventions.md already carries a per-chapter 'Image-Embedded Content' list naming that chapter's images by filename (promptengineer-1's evidence). So the mandated chore duplicates work already done and paid for, using a slower path, on every chapter of every book — and per promptengineer-6 its stated justification ('every stage reads the stripped-out plain text') is false. This is the single most repeated hand-transcribed procedure in the workflow after the review watcher (generalist-7).
additions.recommendation: Rewrite the sweep against the artifacts that exist: point at `.anki-builder/epubs//images/` and at the chapter's entry in conventions.md, and reduce the human step to auditing the images conventions.md already flagged for this chapter plus any `` in the cached chapter file that conventions.md did not mention. If a helper is wanted, it is three lines of glob — `scripts/chapter-images.mjs ` printing each referenced image's resolved cache path and whether conventions.md names it — which is pure mechanism; the judgment (load-bearing vs decoration, by POSITION not filename, SKILL.md:291) stays exactly where it is. Do this together with promptengineer-6's correction and promptengineer-1's precedence fix, or the sweep keeps compensating for a cause that is never addressed.

additions.title: Sequencing: the five fixes worth doing first, and the order they must go in — several popular recommendations are actively unsafe until earlier ones land
additions.evidence: This review produced ~70 findings; roughly 40 of them recommend mutating output/ or .anki-builder/, adding a preflight check, or changing the shipped note model. Three ordering constraints are load-bearing and none of the individual findings state them. (1) Every 'delete the stray X' recommendation (qa-1's .anki-builder/epubs/h1 and the stub mp3s, my generalist-10's review-*.html and .bak pruning, qa-2/generalist-13's stray course .apkg) operates on state with no version control and no backup (generalist-14, verified: both trees gitignored and untracked, 714 MB total). (2) Every 'add a preflight check' recommendation lands on a tool with no severity tiers, no acknowledgement file, and no tests, whose two existing report-only lines have never been zero (generalist-15). (3) Every card-model change (learner-3 direction flags, learner-9 rendering {{Reading}}, learner-12 a listening template) is blocked on learner-4: the deliverer force-syncs fields, templates and CSS but has NO template-add path, so a design change that adds a card direction cannot reach the live collection at all — and a change that removes one produces orphans that are never suspended (learner-10).
additions.recommendation: If only five things get fixed, in this order. FIRST, generalist-14 (a): version-control or snapshot the few MB of JSON that is the human review — everything destructive in this review waits behind it. SECOND, qa-1: make libraryHome() refuse or redirect under isTestEnv, so `npm test` can never write to the dedup library or the audio cache again (cheapest critical fix in the set; the artifacts are on disk today). THIRD, the two silent-corruption guards that are two lines each and need no policy: the `-extras` epubHash refusal in markCardsReviewed (qa-4 / generalist-4) and the rebuild on post-done dashboard edits, or deletion of the two comments claiming it happens (codeexpert-4). FOURTH, the SKILL.md truth sweep as ONE commit — the Reopen flow that no longer exists (generalist-1, red line 2: the documented recovery path for a mis-clicked Mark done is impossible), deck.apkg → <slug>.apkg (generalist-2), the false image claim (promptengineer-6), the Step 3b timing fork (promptengineer-7), the fifth prepare pass (generalist-8), classifyLesson as annotation not filter (adversarial-3) — plus a one-line docs lint in npm run ci so the next drift fails a test instead of a chapter. FIFTH, mechanize the two prose procedures that are retyped per unit and per chapter: scripts/await-review.mjs for the watcher (generalist-7 / techlead-6 / qa-8, four hard-won bug rules currently carried as shell prose) and scripts/vocab-coverage.mjs for the diff SKILL.md already describes deterministically but which does not exist (techlead-3 / promptengineer-8). All five are edges: not one of them removes a judgment call from the agentic core.

endorsements.why: The only finding in the whole set that proves CARDS THAT SHOULD EXIST DON'T. From the study seat that is the worst possible defect: a bad card is visible and fixable at a gate, a missing あります/います paradigm is invisible forever — I verified chapter-12 ships zero of those forms. Precedence between cached conventions and the extraction prompt is a two-line prompt fix with the largest content payoff available.

This is the defect I would actually feel daily and could not diagnose: the clip says one thing, the card says another, and the exemption is permanent for exactly the ~200 cards a human hand-trimmed or hand-picked (109 manual trims + 86 -gen- + 81 -genkanji- in the live book). The recommendation is right in refusing to regenerate over the human's work — badge and block at the gate. Pairs with linguist-4.

Endorsed over its four duplicates (codeexpert-1/techlead-1/generalist-3/adversarial-14) because only qa-1 traces the path that reaches my EARS: 4-byte `CLIP` stubs in `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/`, a cache keyed only by (voice, model, textHash) with no provenance, real voice ids from getDefaultVoice, and clean-audio.mjs faithfully re-deriving a poisoned .orig.mp3 into a shipped card. Silent-degradation, live-collection-adjacent, fully mechanizable.

`--apply` here would DELETE teaching content from my deck: the keeper for に is the NUMBER 2, so five particle-sense cards get excluded, and the same for さん (keeper = the number 3) and ご. The extras doc advertises it as a normal step. This is the one script in the repo whose documented happy path actively degrades the study experience, and preflight already states the correct policy for the identical judgment.

`pronunciation` renders under a 'Says' label on the back of BOTH directions of all 2,150 cards, so per-batch coin-flips (`-san` vs `san`, `yuubinkyoku` vs `yūmei`, terminal periods 100% in ch-2-extras and 0% in ch-6..13) are a learner-facing inconsistency on every single review. Pinning one Hepburn spec plus a WARN-level lint is cheap and touches no judgment.

The mechanized half of my learner-5: 27 shipped cards whose English starts with a pronoun stand-in and carry no scene ('It's the 3rd floor.', 'It's about ten minutes.') are unanswerable-alone in production and I fail them daily for the wrong reason. The doc even names the audit; WARN-level in preflight is exactly right since some hits are legitimately producible.

Audio is on the front of every Recognition card, so TTS quality is a per-review experience, not a build detail. The codebase already knows kanji orthography voices better and buries it behind a per-card button — 13% of clips needed human intervention. Making kanji the default TTS input while kana stays on display is the single biggest audio-quality gain per line changed, and it keeps the human veto.

Red line 2, directly: SKILL.md documents Reopen as the recovery path for a mis-clicked Mark done on a unit that is already in my live collection, and the button does not exist. An agent following the doc will improvise a hand edit of meta.done on a delivered unit. Documentation drift is normally low-severity; this instance is not.

objections.argument: RETRACTING HALF OF MY OWN FINDING. The dconf half is probably inert. Every deck row ships `conf: 1` (src/deck/collection.js:340) and buildDconf emits preset id 1 named 'Default' — on .apkg import Anki will not silently overwrite the user's existing Default preset (deck-preset import is opt-in in the modern importer, and both live decks were delivered via AnkiConnect, which never applies dconf at all, src/anki/deliver.js). So flipping new.bury/rev.bury in buildDconf would change nothing for this owner's collection and risks looking like the problem was fixed when it wasn't. The surviving, actionable parts of learner-2 are (a) the one-line note in references/deliver.md telling the owner to enable Bury new/review siblings on the preset his book decks use — that is the ONLY place a delivered deck can get it — and (b) the position interleaving at collection.js:526-529, which is real for a fresh import but also inert if the owner's preset uses random new-card order. Downgrade this finding to medium and reframe it as a documentation/deck-preset item, not a code fix.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A demonstration that importing one of these .apkg files into a collection that already has a 'Default' preset actually rewrites that preset's bury flags (e.g. Anki version + import-dialog screenshot showing deck presets applied by default), or confirmation that the owner's book decks use a preset created by an .apkg import rather than the collection default.

objections.argument: The CHECK is right and I endorse building it; the CRITICAL severity overstates the harm. I probed all 10 shared ids: 9 are byte-identical in both target and english (`pen`/ペン/Pen, `beef`/ぎゅうにく/Beef, …) and only `scarf` differs (chapter-14 スカーフ vs lesson-3 マフラー, both glossed 'Scarf'). Because both packages ship BARE guids, an .apkg import MATCHES those guids and updates the notes in place — Anki preserves cards, intervals and revlog on a guid match — so the realistic worst case is one course note silently having its answer changed from マフラー to スカーフ, plus a re-import of JBP over itself. That is real silent degradation and worth a preflight failure, but it is not scheduling or progress loss, which is what 'critical' should be reserved for under red line 2. Recommend high, and recommend the check report id-collisions-with-DIFFERING-content separately from harmless identical ones so the signal is not 90% noise on day one.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that Anki's .apkg importer creates duplicate notes (or resets scheduling) rather than updating in place when an incoming guid already exists in the collection — or a larger set of differing-content collisions once a third deck lands, which would move this back toward critical on volume alone.

objections.argument: Lowering the PEDAGOGICAL SORT toward Haiku is the one item in that ladder I would not do. The sort decides the order new cards are introduced, i.e. the actual teaching sequence I experience — and the 'fails open' safety net (pedagogicalSort.js:71-90) only catches a malformed or incomplete permutation, not a well-formed but pedagogically bad one. A degraded ordering is a valid permutation, passes every mechanical check, is never diffed by any tool, and shows up at gate 1 only as a table the reviewer would have to re-derive from scratch to fault. That is the project's exact silent-degradation signature. The rest of promptengineer-4 (raise extraction to high; lower forward flags, which are explicitly biased toward cheap false positives; keep translate/notes/number-readings) I agree with.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A side-by-side of one chapter sorted by Haiku vs Sonnet-medium showing no pedagogically meaningful difference (question/answer pairs adjacent, prerequisites before dependents, number runs handled), or the addition of a mechanical ordering check that would actually fault a bad-but-valid permutation.

objections.argument: Overstated as a defect and the proposed experiment carries a regression risk the finding does not price in. Appending ？ before the 。 changes the TTS input text for 328 delivered cards, which changes their content hash, which regenerates and re-delivers clips that currently work — at ElevenLabs cost — for an unproven prosody gain. More importantly the trim heuristic is calibrated on the silence gap the 。 produces (ttsMarker.js's own measurement: 1.12s with 。 vs 0.24s without); inserting a ？ immediately before it changes that boundary, and 7 clips are ALREADY flagged marker-audible. The ja-only scope of MARKED_LANGUAGES is worth recording in LIMITATIONS as the finding says; the か-question change should be gated on a fresh-card-only trial, never a bulk regeneration of shipped audio.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: An audition of 5-10 newly generated か-final cards showing both a clearly rising contour AND a measured end gap within the current trim tolerance, plus confirmation the change would be applied to new cards only rather than regenerating the 328 delivered ones.

additions.title: The category chip is an unaudited cue on 100% of card fronts — and on 86% of cards it is the ONLY thing on the front besides the word itself
additions.evidence:
Sparked by linguist-6's observation that the chip renders on both fronts. src/deck/collection.js:173 and :183 both open with `{{#Category}}
{{Category}}
{{/Category}}`. Probe over the 2,150 live cards in the two delivered collections: 2,150 of 2,150 have a category (chip always renders), while only 296 have a `scene` and 86 a `hint` — 1,854 cards (86%) have NO scene at all. So on the overwhelming majority of Recognition fronts the entire visual is: an uppercase category chip, the bare target, and the audio button. On a Target→English card that chip is a real answer cue — 「おいしい」 + FOOD, 「ぎゅうにく」 + FOOD narrows the retrieval task far more than any `scene` the collision doctrine would ever permit (references/card-authoring-rules.md is explicit that a cue must not reveal the answer). Nothing audits it: preflight's collision check considers `scene`/`hint` only, the review table has a Category column but reviews it as metadata, and the leaky-scene entry in LIMITATIONS.md:1373-1388 never mentions the chip. On the Production front the same chip is near-harmless (the English gloss already implies the category), so the asymmetry is one-sided. Secondary: 207 live cards are category `Other`, so the chip is contentless noise on ~10% of reviews, and `.cat-chip { color: #a08a5a }` on white (collection.js:234-240) is ~3.3:1 at 11px — below WCAG AA, same class of defect as learner-7.
additions.recommendation: Drop `{{Category}}` from the RECOGNITION qfmt and keep it on the Production front and both backs — a one-line template edit that force-syncs to the live collection via updateModelTemplates (deliver.js:234-248), costs nothing, and removes an uncontrolled cue from 2,150 fronts. It also makes linguist-6's taxonomy work cheaper: an `Other` chip that only appears on the Production front, where the English gloss carries the meaning anyway, stops being a visible defect. If the owner wants the chip kept on Recognition as an intentional aid, then say so explicitly in card-authoring-rules.md and make the collision doctrine account for it — right now the deck applies a rule about cues to `scene` while shipping a stronger uncontrolled cue above it.

additions.title: The note type declares and renders an Image field that is populated on 0 of 2,150 cards, while the extraction pass already reads and caches every book image — the highest-value card type for concrete nouns is fully plumbed and unused
additions.evidence:
Sparked by promptengineer-10 (numbered picture-caption vocabulary lists) and adversarial-12 (text-poor, image-heavy chapters). src/deck/collection.js:179 and :188 both render `{{#Image}}
{{Image}}
{{/Image}}` on the back of each direction, and Image is a declared field on every note. Probe: zero live cards in either collection have an `image` value. Meanwhile the plumbing to fill it exists — src/corpus/epubArchive.js's `extractReferencedImages` caches every referenced image into `.anki-builder/epubs//images/` (729 images for this one book, verified present), the extraction prompt already instructs the model to open them (docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:121-131), and conventions.md carries a per-chapter 'Image-Embedded Content' list. The content this would serve is exactly the class promptengineer-10 found unruled: JBP's WORD POWER numbered illustration sets (chapters/32.xhtml:255-278 — reception desk, post office, meeting room, car park; ten hotel-room objects), all concrete nouns currently taught as kana→English word pairs. For a daily studier, a picture prompt for a concrete noun is the one card design that trains the target word without routing through English at all, and it is the standard remedy for exactly the interference the collision doctrine keeps patching with prose cues (かばん vs ふくろ both glossed 'Bag' — a picture disambiguates where a scene sentence cannot).
additions.recommendation: Scope this as a small, opt-in extension rather than a pipeline change: allow the extraction/extras pass to set `image` on a card whose source is a labelled illustration, copy the cached image into the deck media alongside the audio (src/deck/index.js already owns the sequential-media-key invariant — the image must join the same counter, never a parallel one), and MOVE `{{Image}}` from the back to the Recognition/Production FRONT for such cards so it is a prompt rather than decoration. Two caveats that must be respected: (a) publisher images are copyrighted — this is a personal deck, but it is worth a one-line note in card-authoring-rules.md; (b) it cannot be retrofitted to delivered notes without the field-sync path, which deliver.js:216-232 already handles for fields (unlike templates — learner-4), so this one IS deliverable today.

additions.title: Exactly one of the ten cross-deck id collisions has DIFFERING content — スカーフ vs マフラー both glossed 'Scarf' — which is simultaneously the deck's clearest interference pair and the only note an .apkg import would actually corrupt
additions.evidence: Refines both qa-2 and my learner-1 with a content diff neither did. Probe over the 2,150 live cards: of the 10 ids shared by output/epubs/japanese-for-busy-people-book-1-kana and output/courses/nihongo-101-course-n5, nine are byte-identical in target AND english (`pen`/ペン/Pen, `file`/ファイル/File, `beef`/ぎゅうにく/Beef, `beer`, `small`, `white`, `black`, `restroom`, `camera`) — harmless on both axes. The tenth, `scarf`, is chapter-14 スカーフ 'Scarf' vs lesson-3 マフラー 'Scarf', neither carrying a scene or hint. So the same English prompt has two different expected answers in one collection with no cue — the exact condition references/card-authoring-rules.md declares mandatory to cue — AND it is the one note whose fields an .apkg import would silently rewrite via the shared bare guid. Nine identical twins are also a study defect of their own kind: two notes, four cards, same content, both delivered, so the learner reviews ペン/Pen twice forever with no dedup possible because the audits are per-book.
additions.recommendation: Three separable actions, in ascending cost. (1) Cue the scarf pair now — マフラー is a winter neck scarf, スカーフ a light/head scarf; a one-word scene on each is a hand edit to two cards.json entries and reaches the collection on the next deliver. (2) Make qa-2's proposed cross-collection id check classify by content: identical-content collisions are a duplication note, differing-content collisions are a failure — otherwise the check ships 90% noise on its first run and becomes wallpaper (techlead-8's point). (3) The nine identical twins are the argument for the collection-wide collision mode in learner-1: they are not id bugs, they are the same word taught twice in two products the learner studies from the same queue, and only a collection-wide view can see them.

additions.title: Scene and hint are typographically identical unlabeled grey lines, so on a Production front the learner cannot tell 'here is the situation' from 'here is part of the answer'
additions.evidence:
src/deck/collection.js:183 — the Production qfmt renders `{{#Scene}}
{{Scene}}
{{/Scene}}{{#Hint}}
{{Hint}}
{{/Hint}}`: two different fields, the same class, no label, stacked with nothing between them. The Recognition back (collection.js:176) reuses the same `.hint-front` class for `{{Hint}}` directly under the answer, so one visual treatment carries three different meanings across the note type. Every other semantic field on the card DOES get a label — `.field-label` renders 'Answer', 'Says', 'Note' (collection.js:174-178). 13 live cards currently have both scene and hint, so today's impact is small; it grows with exactly the cue-adding work the collision doctrine mandates, and the dashboard already blurs the same distinction (src/review/deckViewChrome.js:275-277 stacks them in one shared 'hint-col' cell), which means neither the reviewer nor the learner ever sees them as distinct things.
additions.recommendation: Give the two fields distinct treatment in the single-source templates — e.g. keep `.hint-front` for the scene (situation, italic) and add a `.cue-front` for the hint with a small label, or simply prefix the hint with a `.field-label`. This is a CSS+template edit that force-syncs to the live collection on the next deliver. Worth doing BEFORE any bulk cue-adding pass lands, so the new cues arrive already distinguishable; also worth mirroring in the dashboard cell so what the reviewer approves matches what I see.

endorsements.why: I verified both legs independently and they are worse than stated. docs/translate-prompts.md:363-373 documents a full counter-hyphen paragraph AND the example output `rok-kai`; src/translate/romanizationEval.js:66-73 contains NO hyphenation bullet and its example output is `rokkai` — the shipped prompt teaches the opposite of its own documentation. Separately docs/number-reading-prompt.md:46 ships `nisen nijūgonen ni` as a worked example while the same prompt injects JA_COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE (src/translate/languageRules.js:12-16, injected at :36) which forbids exactly that fusion. A worked example that contradicts an injected rule is the single most reliable way to make a model ignore the rule, so this is the direct prompt-level cause of the 209-vs-fused split linguist-1 measured in the live deck.

Four agents found it; qa-1 is the version with the full escalation path traced (real voice ids in src/audio/voiceLibrary.js, cache key with no provenance, clean-audio.mjs faithfully re-deriving the poisoned .orig.mp3). I confirmed the artifacts on disk: `.anki-builder/epubs/h1/corpora/2.json`, and `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/` holding four 4-byte files sitting one directory away from the three real voice caches (3JDquces8E8bkmvbh6Bc, gPPH6SLdL8XSX6GNJ40G, xHIzJ4zBhlGcvJscsdON). This is the only finding in the whole set where an ordinary `npm test` can reach state the live deck is built from.

SKILL.md is a prompt, and this is the worst prompt bug in it: it instructs the orchestrating agent to use a control that does not exist (`grep -rni reopen src/` is empty), on the one path that touches a delivered, daily-studied unit. An agent following an impossible instruction improvises — and the improvisation here is a hand edit of meta.done on a shipped unit. Note the aggravating detail generalist-1 found: commit aa1d150 ADDED Reopen prose after the button was removed, which means the doc is drifting away from the code, not toward it.

Independently corroborates my promptengineer-8 and extends it with the paradigm audit, which I had not checked. Both are cases where SKILL.md says 'write it as a script, not a read-through' — i.e. the doc itself has already ruled that this is mechanism, not judgment — and then supplies no script, so a throwaway with different matching rules gets re-derived every chapter. That is the cleanest possible mechanize-opportunistically win: red line 1 is explicitly about extraction judgment, and a coverage diff is not judgment.

This is a SKILL.md prompt defect misfiled as a parser one, and it is the most likely cause of a bad second-book run. SKILL.md:184 says 'offer the `lesson`-typed entries as options'; classifyLesson (src/corpus/epubLessons.js:18-31) is English-and-'Lesson N'-only, so on the hostile book 0/35 entries qualify and the agent offers an empty menu. The owner's own data already shows the workaround: output/epubs/.../chapter-0 was built from an `other`-typed entry ('Frequently Used Expressions'). The fix is one sentence of prompt (present all entries, type is an annotation not a filter) and costs nothing.

This explains why my whole class of findings is unfixable by review alone. references/card-authoring-rules.md:191-282, docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md and docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md all state rules ABOUT THE RENDERED FRONT ('answerable alone', 'a scene must not leak the answer'), and no surface in the pipeline — not review-corpus.html, not the dashboard — ever applies CARD_TEMPLATES. Both the authoring model and the human reviewer are asked to simulate a face neither has seen. A face preview is the highest card-quality return per line in the repo and it makes several prompt rules verifiable instead of aspirational.

Correct and cleanly fixable in the layer the repo already built for it. src/translate/languageRules.js:1-6 explicitly exists so that 'never Japanese prose leaks into a Spanish run', and romanizationEval.js:24-32 then hardcodes sokuon/kana failure modes and ろっかい/こんにちは exemplars for all seven configured languages. Showing a Hindi run two Japanese examples is not a cosmetic flaw: few-shot examples dominate a short instruction, so the model is being anchored on the wrong task.

The strongest evidence-per-claim finding outside my lane, and it is a scope bug in the doctrine rather than in the cards: the collision rules in card-authoring-rules.md are excellent and hold at 0 uncued members WITHIN a book, while 10 uncued ambiguous English prompts ship across the two books the owner studies in one collection ('Nice to meet you.' → はじめまして vs よろしくおねがいします). Detection is mechanizable with the existing findCollisions over a wider input set; the merge-vs-cue decision correctly stays agentic.

objections.argument: The second half is factually wrong and its recommendation is already implemented. generalist-8 says the number-readings pass overloads the `uncertain` badge 'with no way to tell them apart' and recommends 'give the machine-filled cards a distinguishing reviewNote'. src/cards/numberReadings.js:116-118 already does exactly that: `item.uncertain = true; item.reviewNote = item.reviewNote ? \`${item.reviewNote} | ${REVIEW_NOTE}\` : REVIEW_NOTE;` — and card-authoring-rules.md:206 defines reviewNote as precisely the gate-1-only field that says why a card is uncertain, so the reviewer sees the distinction at the moment it matters. The FIRST half of the finding (SKILL.md:312-326 and PIPELINE.md list four prepare passes when five run) is correct and worth fixing on its own; the badge-overload half should be dropped so it does not consume a doc edit and, worse, prompt someone to add a redundant second flag to the card schema.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A live card whose only provenance is `uncertain: true` with a reviewNote that does not name the number-reading pass, i.e. a case where REVIEW_NOTE was not appended — or a screenshot of the dashboard at gate 1 showing that reviewNote is not surfaced next to the Uncertain badge.

objections.argument: Severity is understated at 'low' and the reasoning that makes it low is the wrong test. adversarial-14 argues the leak is 'harmless with a fake hash'. Harm here is not whether the CURRENT fixture collides — it is that the write is unguarded, so harm is decided by whichever fixture hash a future test happens to pick. qa-1 traced the second, live channel that adversarial-14 missed entirely: `.anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/` holds four 4-byte `CLIP` files from test/cli/index.test.js, and getDefaultVoice (src/audio/voiceLibrary.js:6-7) returns REAL voice ids, so one test that omits `--voice` on a `ja` lesson writes stub bytes under a real voice's content-addressed key and a later real run takes a cache HIT. I confirmed the three real voice dirs sit beside `v1` in the same cache root. Five agents reported this; if the arbiter averages the severities, an understated 'low' with an explicitly reassuring rationale is the one input that can drag a critical to medium.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A guard I missed — e.g. libraryHome() or the ElevenLabs cache path already refusing writes under isTestEnv(), or every audio test injecting a fake voice id — which would make the fixture-hash accident the only exposure and justify 'low'.

objections.argument: Overstated in its harm claim. The title says the FIB prompt 'teaches an invalid category' and that a wrong one is 'silently rewritten'; I probed every live card in both collections and every single `category` value is a member of src/model/categories.js — zero instances of 'Travel', so the snap at fillInBlank.js:170 has never had to fire on this. The prompt also already carries the correct instruction at docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md:109 ('reuse one of the categories already present on the lesson's cards'), which is what the model actually followed; the bad value lives only in the illustrative Output Format JSON. Fix the example and add the enum to the cards schema — both cheap and right — but this should not be ranked alongside defects with demonstrated output damage, and 'the snap silently rewrites' should not be recorded as a bug: snapping to a category the lesson actually has IS the designed fail-safe and is better than shipping an out-of-enum value into a deck template that renders the chip.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Any shipped card in output/ whose category is not in CATEGORIES, or a fillInBlank log line showing the snap firing on a real build (which would prove the prompt's example is actually steering the model, not just sitting in the doc).

objections.argument: Retracting the sharper half of my own finding. I claimed the parser's tolerance 'was tuned for a model no pass runs' and implied the first-[-to-last-] fallback is a live mis-slicing risk. On reflection the risk framing is wrong in a way that could cause harm if acted on: the fallback only runs after the strict parse and the fence strip have both failed, and removing or tightening tolerance in a pipeline whose only alternative is a failed paid pass trades a rare mis-slice for a common hard failure. What survives is only the cheap, purely additive part: restate the output contract in a closing line of docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md (currently stated once at :23-25 of 205 lines, with the prompt ending on false-friend prose at :204), and refresh the stale 'from Haiku specifically' attribution in src/corpus/epubLlmExtract.js:6-14 to name the model that actually produced each observed deviation. Do not touch the tolerance itself.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A logged instance of the first-[-to-last-] fallback producing a wrong slice on a real chapter (prose containing a bracket before the array), which would justify tightening rather than only restating the contract.

additions.title: The two widest-reach prompts live in code, outside the editable-template regime and outside the only prompt test — and their documentation has already drifted
additions.evidence: Eleven prompts, two regimes. Nine are Markdown templates in docs/ rendered at runtime by src/util/promptTemplate.js (`renderPromptTemplate` call sites: cards/crossLessonNotes.js:100, cards/fillInBlank.js:62, cards/semanticDedup.js:25, cards/numberReadings.js:31, plus corpus/epubLlmPrompt.js and the conventions/taught-index/forward-flag loaders, each carrying the same comment: 'Lives in docs/ (not src/) so it stays a plain, human-editable template'). test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js pins the placeholder set and output contract for exactly those files. The remaining four are string-concatenated inside modules — `grep -rln '# Task:' src/*/*.js` returns src/translate/index.js, src/translate/romanizationEval.js, src/corpus/lessonCorpus.js, src/audio/kanjiOrthography.js — and docs/translate-prompts.md is a HAND-MAINTAINED TRANSCRIPT of two of them, not a template (it is the one docs/*.md file the test does not know about). It has already drifted: docs/translate-prompts.md:363-373 documents a full counter-hyphen paragraph and an example output `rok-kai`, while src/translate/romanizationEval.js:66-73 has no hyphenation bullet and outputs `rokkai`. So translation and romanization — the two passes that touch EVERY card in every deck, and the ones linguist-1 measured drifting per unit — are the only prompts a human cannot edit without a code change, the only ones with no automated contract, and the only ones whose documentation is a copy rather than the source.
additions.recommendation: Move `buildRomanizationPrompt` and the translation prompts into docs/romanization-prompt.md / docs/translate-prompt.md rendered through renderPromptTemplate, injecting LANGUAGE_PROMPT_RULES fragments as placeholders exactly as fill-in-blank already injects {{COUNTER_HYPHEN_RULE}} — that single move fixes linguist-1 (one pinnable style spec), linguist-2 (per-language fragments instead of hardcoded Japanese) and linguist-3 (one source for the hyphen rule) at once, and brings them under promptTemplates.test.js. If the move is deferred, the minimum is a test asserting docs/translate-prompts.md contains the string the builder actually emits, so the transcript cannot silently diverge again. kanjiOrthography.js and lessonCorpus.js should follow the same rule.

additions.title: The category rule has no branch for the worked-example sentences Step 2 asks for — the direct cause of linguist-6's 44 mis-categorized sentence cards
additions.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:180 gives one rule: pick the category matching the item's TOPIC 'not its grammatical role', a vocabulary word and a sentence about the same topic get the same category, and 'Use `"Grammar & Function Words"` for particles/conjunctions/question markers'. Ten lines later, Step 2 (:186-196) instructs the model to ensure every Grammar & Function Words item has a full example SENTENCE demonstrating it, and to author one where the chapter has none. Nothing anywhere says which category that sentence takes. The two readings are equally supported by the text — 'it demonstrates a particle, so Grammar & Function Words' vs 'its topic is a pen, so Other/Everyday' — and linguist-6 measured the consequence: 44 sentence-length cards sit in Grammar & Function Words (これはペンですか, いいえ、ちがいます, ちょっとまってください), which is why that bucket is 170 cards while `Other` is 222. Because the category chip renders on the FRONT of both templates (src/deck/collection.js:173,183), the ambiguity is learner-visible on every one of those cards.
additions.recommendation: Add one sentence to the §'Assigning category' block resolving it explicitly, and make it the same rule in both directions: a Step-2 worked example takes the category of the FORM it demonstrates (Grammar & Function Words), because that is what makes it findable next to the bare particle card it exists to serve — or takes its content topic, if the owner prefers. Either choice is defensible; the defect is that the prompt states neither. Whichever is chosen, add it as a worked counter-example (これはペンです → X) since the current text's only example points the other way. This should be settled before linguist-6's proposed new categories are added, or the new buckets inherit the same ambiguity.

additions.title: No prompt ever shows the authoring model what a card actually looks like — scene/hint rules are stated as constraints on a face the model has never seen
additions.evidence: The field semantics are entirely defined by prose about rendering: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:33-40 and card-authoring-rules.md:185-215 say `scene` is context shown on BOTH faces while `hint` is a nudge shown only on the Production front, and card-authoring-rules.md:263-282 requires every answer card to be 'answerable alone'. The actual rendering contract lives in src/deck/collection.js:167-191 (Recognition qfmt = Target + Scene + Audio; Production qfmt = English + Scene + Hint; both afmt add Pronunciation/Reading/note-back) and appears in NO prompt — `grep` for qfmt/afmt/template across docs/*.md returns nothing. So the model authoring the field is told the RULE about the face but never shown the face, and two consequences follow that other agents measured independently: learner-9's Reading field is populated by the number-reading prompt and rendered by neither template (136 live cards), and learner-3/LIMITATIONS.md:1373-1388's leaky-scene class on particle cards, where a scene like 'marking a point in time' is a near-paraphrase of the answer 'At, in, on (particle)' — a defect that is obvious on a rendered front and invisible in a JSON row.
additions.recommendation: Add a compact ~8-line 'What your fields become' block to docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md and docs/fill-in-blank-prompt.md, generated from CARD_TEMPLATES rather than retyped (a {{CARD_FACES}} placeholder rendered from src/deck/collection.js keeps it from drifting the way promptengineer-11's duplicated field taxonomy already has), showing both fronts and both backs with a filled example. This is the prompt-side half of learner-5: the human gets a rendered preview, the model gets the template. It also makes the leak test statable in one operational sentence the model can actually apply — 'if you can guess the answer from the Recognition front alone, the scene leaks' — instead of an abstract rule.

additions.title: The extraction contract has no back-channel: a chapter the model could not read produces the same output shape as an empty one
additions.evidence: docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:23-25 fixes the response as 'ONLY a single JSON array' of card objects. There is no field, no envelope and no side file in which the model can say 'this chapter is almost entirely images', 'I could not open image X', or 'this file looks like front matter'. The only expressible failure is a shorter array — and SKILL.md:283 itself states the consequence: 'Nothing downstream can notice what was never extracted'. The per-item `uncertain`/`reviewNote` channel (:118-120) only covers items that DO exist, so it cannot represent an absence. Two live confirmations: taught-index.json for the only real book records `teaches: []` for chapters 2 and 3 ('Hiragana', 'Katakana') — the kana-chart chapters, which are image-only, so the pass reported nothing and nothing distinguishes that from 'read it, nothing taught'; and adversarial-12 measured spine file 11 at 94 chars of text against 7 images while it IS a built unit. Contrast docs/epub-taught-index-prompt.md, which requires a per-chapter entry and whose completeness src/corpus/epubTaughtIndex.js:83-88 rejects outright when a chapter is missing — the same pass family already proves an envelope with a coverage requirement works.
additions.recommendation: Change the extraction contract to an envelope — `{"items": [...], "coverage": {"imagesOpened": ["", ...], "imagesSkippedAsDecorative": [...], "concerns": ""}}` — and make the parser accept both shapes so nothing breaks (src/corpus/epubLlmExtract.js already tolerates three deviations, so one more branch is free). Then mechanize the cheap half: assemble already knows every `` the chapter references (src/corpus/epubArchive.js:613-643 resolves and caches them), so it can diff the referenced set against `imagesOpened` and print a WARN naming any image the model never accounted for, before the human sees the review link. The judgment stays entirely with the model; what changes is that 'I did not look' becomes expressible and therefore visible.

additions.title: Cached whole-book LLM artifacts carry no provenance — no prompt version, model, effort or date — so any prompt or pinning change silently reuses output built under the old one
additions.evidence: .anki-builder/epubs/1fab0f99d1195ad9/ holds conventions.md (19.8 KB, generated 14 Jul) and taught-index.json (29.8 KB, 11 Aug), both consumed as inputs to later paid passes — conventions.md is injected verbatim into every chapter extraction as {{BOOK_CONVENTIONS}} (pinned by test/docs/promptTemplates.test.js as a required placeholder) and into both forward-flag prompts. The only manifest is book.json, whose entire content is `{"title", "slug"}` — no model, no effort, no prompt hash, no generation date beyond the filesystem mtime. docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md was last modified 9 Aug, i.e. its EXERCISES policy changed nearly a month AFTER the conventions text that contradicts it was cached, and nothing anywhere noticed (this is the mechanism behind promptengineer-1's verified content loss). The exposure grows under two changes already proposed in this review: promptengineer-4's per-pass effort split would leave a book's conventions built at medium while extraction runs at high, and any fix to promptengineer-1's conventions prompt wording would leave every existing book on the old text forever, since the pass only re-runs when the file is absent.
additions.recommendation: Write a sibling `<artifact>.meta.json` when caching conventions.md and taught-index.json: prompt file path + sha256 of the rendered template, resolved model and effort, generation timestamp, and the chapter count read. Then warn (never block, never auto-regenerate — a rebuild is a paid pass and a judgment call) at the top of assemble when the current prompt hash or pinned model differs from the cached one, naming what changed. Roughly 25 deterministic lines, no new dependency, and it converts the single most expensive silent-staleness class in the pipeline into one line of output the agent can act on.

endorsements.why: The only finding in the set that can destroy scheduling on the owner's daily collection, and I verified its mechanism end to end: output/epubs/.../book.json has "guidNamespace": null, readGuidNamespace (src/deck/rebuild.js:149-165) returns null for a course.json with no field, and src/deck/collection.js:518 then emits the bare card.id as the note guid. Anki matches guids collection-wide, so the 10 shared ids between the two delivered decks are a live .apkg-import hazard, and a foreign 11 MB japanese-for-busy-people .apkg is physically sitting in the course dir waiting to be double-clicked. Both proposed checks are pure reads and cost nothing.

Supersedes my own adversarial-14 with the evidence I lacked. I confirmed .anki-builder/audio/ holds four real voice dirs (3JDquces8E8bkmvbh6Bc, gPPH6SLdL8XSX6GNJ40G, xHIzJ4zBhlGcvJscsdON) beside the test-created v1/eleven_v3/*.mp3 4-byte CLIP stubs, and src/cli/commands/audio.js:100-108 falls back to getDefaultVoice — i.e. one CLI test fixture with targetLanguage ja and no --voice writes stub bytes into a REAL voice's content-addressed cache, where a later real run gets a cache hit and ships silence. That is a concrete, one-line-away corruption of delivered audio, not a hypothetical.

Verified and it corrects a misdiagnosis I was also operating under. src/corpus/epubArchive.js:659-663 hands the model the RAW chapter xhtml (content, not stripped) and extractReferencedImages materializes every referenced image at the exact resolved path; docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:121-131 is a dedicated section telling the model to open each one. So SKILL.md:280-283 ("Every stage of the pipeline reads the stripped-out plain text") and extras-pass.md:129 ("the pipeline never has") are both false for the extraction and conventions passes. Getting this right matters beyond the doc fix: it means image gaps are a PROMPT/conventions problem (promptengineer-1) plus a shape-measurement problem (my adversarial-12), not an architectural blindness.

The correct architectural verdict and the best single carrier for almost every EPUB fix in this review. Swapping in an EPUB library would trade two explicit, tested, LOUD rejections (ZIP64, encrypted bit) for generic ones and buy nothing against the actual failure mode, which is downstream convention-bound code (deckPath.js's GROUPED_LABEL, classifyLesson). scripts/epub-probe.mjs is exactly where my adversarial-2 (unnamed spine files), -5 (collapsed duplicate hrefs), -10 (shape report) and -12 (text-vs-image density) should land: one read-only command, zero LLM/TTS spend, agent still decides.

Independent confirmation of my adversarial-6 with the downstream half I did not trace: assemble.js:339 passes lastChapterNumber (the INVERTED, smaller number) to flagForwardConcerns, so epubForwardFlags.js:162 treats the lesson's own spine files as 'later chapters'. That turns a nav-ordering quirk into wrong forward flags on top of silent truncation, and --list-lessons hides the inversion because assemble.js:148-152 only prints a range when last>first. Fix is ~6 lines plus a fixture.

The only PROVEN content loss on the one book the whole pipeline is validated against, and the mechanism generalizes: a cached, undated conventions.md outranks a prompt that was edited a month later, with no precedence statement and no staleness link. Ties directly to my new adversarial-17 — the conventions cache, the chapter cache and the images are all immutable and keyed only on file bytes, so this defect is frozen into the existing book until someone deletes the directory by hand.

Red-line-2 exposure created purely by doc drift: SKILL.md prescribes Reopen → change → Mark done as the recovery path for a delivered, daily-studied unit, grep -rni reopen src/ returns nothing, and unmarkCardsReviewed hard-refuses while done. An agent following the skill will find no button and improvise a hand edit of meta.done on a shipped unit. The proposed scripts/undone-unit.mjs (backup + clear + rebuild) is the right shape: one reviewed operation instead of an improvisation.

Same scope bug as qa-2 on a different axis and it is already costing daily reps: the audits are structurally per-book (extras-collision-audit.mjs resolves a single <book-dir>; preflight runs findCollisions per dir), but the learner studies one interleaved collection, so 'Nice to meet you.' → はじめまして vs よろしくおねがいします ships uncued. Detection is fully mechanizable (one findCollisions call over every delivered collection); the merge-vs-cue decision correctly stays agentic.

objections.argument: Retracting my own severity. I filed the .anki-builder test leak as LOW on the reasoning that epubHash 'h1' is a fake hash and therefore harmless. qa-1 and codeexpert-1 have the evidence I missed: the same missing-injection pattern also reaches the AUDIO cache, where src/cli/commands/audio.js:100-108 resolves a REAL ElevenLabs voice id via getDefaultVoice when --voice is omitted, and the cache key is (voice, model, textHash) with no provenance — I confirmed 4-byte CLIP stubs sitting in .anki-builder/audio/v1/eleven_v3/ next to three real voice directories. A silent cache hit on a poisoned key ships a broken clip into a delivered, daily-studied deck, and scripts/clean-audio.mjs would faithfully re-derive it from the equally poisoned .orig.mp3. This is critical, not low; the correct fix is the guard qa-1 describes (libraryHome() refusing the real dir under isTestEnv, mirroring assertExternalCallAllowed).
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A test-suite-wide assertion that libraryHome() is always overridden in tests, or proof that every audio CLI test passes an explicit non-real --voice AND that no fixture can reach getDefaultVoice with a real language code.

objections.argument: Partially retracting my own framing. I bundled ruby mangling with entity decoding at HIGH severity on the premise that text stripping mangles ruby before the pipeline sees it. That premise is wrong for the pass that matters: extractChapterToFile writes the RAW xhtml and the extraction model reads it directly (verified: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:659-663, docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:121-131), so <ruby>漢<rt>かん</rt></ruby> reaches the model intact and it can read the reading correctly. The ruby defect is confined to (a) nav LABELS that contain ruby — uncommon in a TOC — and (b) any agent-side stripping the skill prescribes. The load-bearing half of the finding is entity decoding (independently confirmed by codeexpert-7: HTML_ENTITIES covers only 5 names, and a label flows verbatim into the Anki deck name), which stands at high. Net: treat adversarial-4 as MEDIUM overall with the ruby component demoted to a label-only concern, so effort goes to decodeHtmlEntities rather than to a ruby-aware stripper nothing currently needs.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A pass that hands the model stripped text rather than a file path, or a real Japanese textbook EPUB whose nav labels carry ruby.

objections.argument: Endorse the split-the-env-scopes half; object to the 'LOWER forward flags, pedagogical sort, semantic dedup and lesson categorization toward Haiku' half. The justification is that these passes are 'mechanically validated' or 'fail open' — but that validation is STRUCTURAL, not qualitative. reorderByIds (src/corpus/pedagogicalSort.js:73-90) guarantees only that no item is added, dropped or duplicated; whether the sequence actually puts atoms before molecules is exactly the pedagogical judgment nothing can check, and a bad order is invisible at gate 1 (the reviewer sees a table, not a curriculum). Category assignment failing open to 'Other' is not free either — the category chip renders on the FRONT of both templates (src/deck/collection.js:173,183) and 'Other' is already the second-largest bucket (linguist-6). There is no eval fixture anywhere in the repo for any pass, so a tier downgrade's quality cost is unmeasurable by construction — which is this project's documented signature failure (silent degradation) applied deliberately, on a deck studied daily, to save cents. Sequence it: build the per-pass eval fixture first, THEN downgrade what the fixture shows is safe.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: A checked-in eval fixture (a pinned chapter with a human-approved reference ordering / category assignment) showing Haiku output within tolerance of Sonnet-medium on those passes.

objections.argument: The goal (per-card direction control) is right; the proposed MECHANISM is a red-line-2 hazard on the already-delivered collection. Gating a template's qfmt on a conditional so it renders empty does not remove a card in Anki — it turns every existing card of that template into an EMPTY CARD, and Anki's own Tools → Empty Cards maintenance action DELETES empty cards together with their review history. The owner runs a live collection daily and Empty Cards is a routine housekeeping click, so a silent 'these cards now render blank' state is one maintenance run away from permanent scheduling loss on cards that were never meant to be deleted. learner-3's 'ship it with a suspend path' does not cover this, because suspension does not stop a card being empty. Safer sequencing: make the direction flag affect NEW builds only (skip generating the note's second card at build time in src/deck/collection.js:526, which is a build-side decision, not a template conditional), and for already-delivered notes change nothing — or suspend, and explicitly document that the template must NOT be made conditional on a live note type.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Documentation or a test showing that the Anki version the owner runs leaves conditionally-empty cards intact under Empty Cards, or a delivery path that suspends-and-tags before the template change lands.

objections.argument: The diagnosis (four independent copies of the unit-dir regex; a non-matching dir is silently skipped) is right and worth fixing. The proposed remedy — 'make preflight FAIL on any directory that contains a cards.json or corpus.json but does not match' — would, if applied today, fail preflight on every template unit: scripts/validate-decks.mjs:29-38 documents that template units live at templates/<name>/<lang>/ and carry cards.json, and that path matches no (chapter|lesson)-N pattern. So qa-3's hard failure collides head-on with generalist-5/techlead-4, which want preflight to START covering templates. Ordering matters: first export one listUnitDirs that KNOWS all three shapes (unit, extras, template), then make the unmatched-dir case a report line, and only promote it to a failure once the known shapes are all enumerated. Otherwise the first person to build the template path — the only open backlog task — hits a red preflight for a legitimate layout and learns to ignore it.
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Confirmation that template units are intended to be out of preflight's scope permanently, in which case the failure should be scoped to the epubs/courses roots explicitly rather than to 'any dir with a cards.json'.

objections.argument: Object to part (a) only — 'make marker-stuck a FAILURE for any not-yet-done unit'. scripts/preflight.mjs:169 downgrades it to a note precisely because it is a heuristic, and the observed rate is 7 clips out of ~2,173 (0.3%). Hard-failing a gate on a heuristic with a non-zero false-positive rate, at the exact moment the agent is trying to hand over a review link, is how a --force habit gets established — and this repo already shows where that leads (extras-duplicate-check.mjs's reviewed/done guard is bypassable by --force, techlead-2). Part (b) of the same finding is the better answer applied to BOTH lines: persist an acknowledgement, print 'N accepted, M new', and fail only on M > 0. That gives the loud signal without teaching anyone to override the gate. (techlead-8 proposes exactly this and should be merged with generalist-6.)
objections.evidenceThatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that audioMarkerStuck has a near-zero false-positive rate on this book (e.g. all 7 flagged clips audited and all genuinely audible), which would make it a reliable enough signal to hard-fail.

additions.title: Two chapters in different directories referencing the same relative image filename silently overwrite each other's image — the model then reads the WRONG picture
additions.evidence: PROBED, read-only, in the scratchpad. Built a fixture EPUB with spine files OEBPS/text/a.xhtml (src="img.png" → OEBPS/text/img.png, bytes "IMAGE-FROM-TEXT-DIR") and OEBPS/b.xhtml (src="img.png" → OEBPS/img.png, bytes "IMAGE-FROM-ROOT-DIR"). Ran extractChapterToFile for chapter 1 then chapter 2 into one chapters/ dir: after ch1 the on-disk chapters/img.png read IMAGE-FROM-TEXT-DIR; after ch2 the SAME file read IMAGE-FROM-ROOT-DIR. No log line fired. Cause: src/corpus/epubArchive.js:637-643 computes localDest = join(destDir, src) — keyed on the RELATIVE src, not on the archive path — and writes unconditionally. Chapter 1's cached xhtml is still there and is treated as an immutable, complete extraction (isCachedChapterFile, line 599-606), so it now points at chapter 2's image forever. The code comment at :639-642 justifies the unconditional write with "the bytes are a pure function of the EPUB, so last-writer-wins is harmless" — my probe shows they are a pure function of the ARCHIVE PATH, not of the destination path, so that argument does not hold and the concurrency safety it claims is also unsound. Impact is now known to be real rather than cosmetic: promptengineer-6 established (and I verified) that the extraction model actually opens these files as content sources, so a swapped image is swapped card content, silently. OEBPS/Text + OEBPS/Images layouts (Sigil, InDesign, many publisher toolchains) are exactly where this fires; the one proven book is flat, which is why it has never been seen.
additions.recommendation: Place images under a per-chapter-directory subpath (or hash the archive path into the name) so two archive paths can never share a destination; at minimum, before writing, compare bytes with any existing file at localDest and log(`[epub] image name collision: ${archivePath} overwrote a different image at ${localDest}`) — the log callback is already threaded in and already used for dangling refs at :633. Fully deterministic, ~5 lines, and a fixture test is the probe above. Add it to the same fixture batch as adversarial-11.

additions.title: Scanned/fixed-layout books referencing an external .svg page wrapper get the wrapper copied but not the raster it points at
additions.evidence: extractReferencedImages (src/corpus/epubArchive.js:618-643) scans ONLY the chapter's own markup, via IMG_SRC_PATTERN and SVG_IMAGE_HREF_PATTERN, and does not recurse into anything it copies. The comment at :610-612 says the SVG-wrapped scanned-page idiom is handled — and it is, for the INLINE case ( and page012.svg internally references page012.png, copies only the .svg; the raster never lands on disk. The model then Reads an SVG whose href dangles, gets no page content, and — because docs/epub-extraction-prompt.md:131 explicitly blesses "If you open an image and it turns out to be decorative, that's a fine outcome" — records that as a legitimate empty result. No log fires, because from extractReferencedImages' point of view the referenced file WAS found. This is precisely the image-only/scanned textbook class my adversarial-12 measures but cannot see the cause of.
additions.recommendation: When a copied asset is an .svg (or has image/svg+xml media-type), re-run the same href scan over its bytes and copy what it references, resolving relative to the SVG's own archive directory. ~10 lines reusing the existing pattern and the existing dangling-ref log. Alternatively, if recursion is judged out of scope, log every copied .svg so the shape report (adversarial-10 / techlead-10's epub-probe) can flag 'this unit's images are SVG wrappers — verify the pages rendered'.

additions.title: The whole EPUB cache is immutable and keyed only on file bytes — no parser or prompt fix in this review will ever apply to the existing book, and there is no clear command
additions.evidence: chapterCachePath (src/corpus/epubLibrary.js:88-90) is bookDir(epubHash)/chapters/<n>.xhtml and isCachedChapterFile (epubArchive.js:599-606) treats any non-empty file as a COMPLETE extraction; extractChapterToFile/extractChapterRangeToFile return early on a cache hit, so extractReferencedImages never re-runs and its dangling-ref log never re-fires. conventions.md and taught-index.json are the same: written once, keyed on the hash, never re-derived (promptengineer-1 measured conventions.md at 14 Jul vs an extraction prompt edited 9 Aug). I grepped for a version/generation marker in src/corpus/epubLibrary.js — there is none — and for any clear/purge/--refresh path in src/cli/index.js and assemble.js — there is none; the only rmSync in the library module is removeChapterCorpus (line 131). Consequence for this whole review: fixing decodeHtmlEntities, the comment/CDATA scanner, the NCX label regex, the image collision (adversarial-15), or the conventions/extraction precedence conflict changes NOTHING for hash 1fab0f99d1195ad9 — chapter 16 of the same book, built next week, will be extracted from the same stale cached bytes and the same stale conventions, and the operator has no supported way to find out or to force a re-derive short of deleting a directory by hand under .anki-builder/, which also holds the corpora/ dedup library he must NOT delete.
additions.recommendation: Two mechanizable pieces, neither touching the agentic core. (1) Put a small integer CACHE_VERSION alongside the parser (bumped whenever extraction/image resolution changes) into the cache path or a sidecar, so a fixed parser re-derives instead of silently reusing. (2) Ship `anki-builder epub cache --clear <hash> [--chapters|--conventions|--taught-index]` that refuses to touch corpora/ — so the one destructive operation on the library is a reviewed command with a guard rather than an improvised rm -rf next to the dedup registry (which is the exact adjacency that already cost 12 unflagged repeats). Also print the cache's provenance (generated-at, parser version, prompt hash) in the shape report so 'this book was extracted under the old rules' is visible before a paid pass.
